chapters.title: Chapter 501: Pictures [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The cerulean liquid hit Silas’s throat like a stream of molten lead mixed with liquid nitrogen.
The chemical heat of it was terrifying... It was like swallowing a fistful of burning phosphorus.
’I can’t believe there are people who actually drink for fun...’
But deep within his chest, the Gold Core gave an angry violent spin.
VUUUM.
A golden microscopic wave of pure mana swept through his digestive tract like an automated firewall.

The ninety-two percent spiritual solvent was violently neutralized, converted into harmless mountain spring water and expelled through his pores in a barely perceptible wisp of steam that drifted from the collar of his coat.
Silas slammed his empty horn onto the table with a crisp clack.
Beside him, Thor was not quite so lucky.
The God of Thunder had chugged the entire horn in four massive throat-bulging swallows.
"Ah~"
She slammed her vessel down an eighth of a second after Silas with her chest heaving and a victorious grin beginning to form on her lips—
And then, her expression locked.
Her storm-blue eyes widened until they were completely round as the pupils contracted into microscopic dots.
Her pale skin instantly turned an alarming violent shade of neon magenta, spreading from her jawline down to the swell of her chest.
GURGLE!
A strange high-pitched whistling noise like steam escaping an over-pressurized boiler hissed through her clenched teeth.
’Again I can’t understand the people who do this for fun I swear.’
Thor slowly turned her head toward Silas. Her lips moved, trying to form a word... perhaps a curse or perhaps a plea for roasted meat but only a tiny pitiful squeak emerged.
’...Cold...’ Thor’s eyes rolled straight back into her skull, revealing pure whites.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The towering immortal God of Thunder folded at the waist like a felled oak, her upper body crashing forward onto the pine table.
Her face buried straight into a platter of cold mashed tubers with her massive arms sprawling out across the wood as she was dead to the world.
THUD!
A single snore tore from her throat, rattling the iron platters.
HROOOOO-SNK!
Dead silence gripped the mess hall.
Silas stood tall with his dark coat pristine and his golden ringed blue eyes clear and sharp as diamonds, not a single hair out of place.
He reached up, casually wiping a stray drop of blue liquid from his lower lip with his thumb, completely unaffected.
"DOWN IN ONE!" Thora shrieked, hopping onto the bench and throwing her hands into the rafters! "THE BLONDE GIANT HAS FALLEN! THE LORD STANDS UNBROKEN!"
"YEEEEEEEEEAH!"
The barracks exploded into a frenzy of adoring cheers.
"Lord Silas! Pour some for us!" Brenda squealed, shoving her wooden tankard across the table with flushed cheeks.
"My Lord, over here! Give me a drink from your hands!" Sarah cried out, elbowing her way through the press of bodies.
"Feed us some of that boar meat, my Lord! Please!"
Silas chuckled warmly with the stern mask completely melting away as he leaned over the table, taking up a carved wooden pitcher and filling their cups one by one.
He sliced tender strips of peppered meat with a knife, feeding them directly onto the platters of the eager blushing women who practically squirmed under his attentive gaze.

Looking around at the crowded hall... at Brenda laughing with her mouth full, at Helen grinning with a foam mustache, at the Princess giggling helplessly as she tried to balance a bone on the sleeping Thor’s ear.
A deep protective warmth settled beneath his ribs.

’I’ll make sure to reward you...’ Silas thought, his smile softening with unshakeable affection. ’All of you... Every single woman who bleeds for this banner. You deserve the best this world has to offer.’
Over by the dark recessed archway near the western entrance of the mess hall, partially concealed behind a heavy velvet curtain, Morwenna stood in tense silence.
The Pirate Queen had slipped into the hall unnoticed twenty minutes ago.
She was still dressed in her dry leather trousers and a dark woolen coat with her messy black hair tied back with a strip of frayed hemp rope.
Her eyes were narrowed to slits, and held securely in her calloused hands was the enchanted runic camera.
She had stalked into the barracks with a singular purpose... Revenge.
Eluned had humiliated her.
Eluned had captured her completely naked, dripping with soap suds, and had framed the photograph for the entire Keep to see.
Morwenna’s pirate pride demanded retribution and right now, sitting across the hall, the target was fully ripe for the plucking.
Eluned was magnificently plastered.
The Goddess was currently slumping sideways across the bench, her green robes sliding off one pale shoulder.
Her lips were parted in a loose undignified pout, her tongue poking slightly out the corner of her mouth as she attempted to feed a roasted carrot to an empty wooden flagon.
It was an expression of divine stupidity.

’This is it,’ Morwenna thought, her fingers trembling with vicious anticipation as she slowly raised the camera to her eye. ’If I capture this shot... if I print her looking like a drooling tavern wench and pin it over the main gatehouse... she will never look me in the eye again. The weed will finally bend the knee.’
She lined up the lens through the heavy smoke as her finger hovered over the glowing shutter rune.
And then... her gaze drifted three inches to the left. Silas was standing right beside the slumped spirit.
He was leaning over the table, his dark hair falling across his forehead, laughing warmly at something Brenda had just shouted.
The orange firelight from the hearth washed over his sharp handsome features, softening the look that usually hardened his eyes.
’Captain looks warm...’
Morwenna’s breath caught in her throat.
Her finger froze over the rune as a sudden jolt of heat struck her chest, blooming outward until her cheeks burned with a deep furious blush.
Her hands trembled against the brass casing.
She looked at the drooling green-haired spirit which was a guaranteed victory in their petty war then she looked back at Silas’s smile.
’It’s a no-brainer,’ Morwenna thought, her heart slamming against her ribs with an intensity that terrified her.
She shifted her boots, adjusting her stance in the shadows as she smoothly pivoted the lens away from Eluned, centering the frame dead on Silas.
CLICK-FLASH!
A brilliant pulse of white light flared through the smoke, catching Silas mid-laugh as he turned toward the western wall.
WHIRRRR-ZIP!
From the slot of the enchanted apparatus, a thick square of glossy photographic paper slid out smoothly.
Morwenna snatched the paper from the air, waving it frantically to accelerate the chemical development.
The image cleared in real-time.
It was stunning.
Silas was captured in razor-sharp clarity, the firelight dancing in his blue eyes, his smile natural and devastatingly handsome, framed by the bustling warmth of his soldiers behind him.
"It’s wonderful..." Morwenna whispered under her breath, a soft smitten smile curling the edges of her lips as she traced the edge of the paper with her thumb. "It really is a wonderful pictu—"
GRIP!
Two large hands suddenly slid around her waist from behind.
"EEP!"

Morwenna’s entire body went rigid as iron as her instincts flared with her right hand instinctively snapping down toward Tidebringer at her hip, her muscles coiling to execute a violent spinning elbow check...
"Find what you were looking for, Morwenna?"
The deep voice murmured directly against the shell of her ear, sending an agonizingly sweet shiver cascading straight down her spine.
Morwenna instantly deflated with the murderous tension evaporating into a puddle of flustered panic as she recognized the voice.
"C-captain!" Morwenna stammered, frantically trying to twist around in his grip, but his hands remained firmly anchored to the narrow curves of her hips.
Silas leaned his chin over her shoulder with his blue eyes glancing down at the fresh photograph clutched in her trembling fingers.
A teasing smirk spread across his face.
"Well, look at that," Silas whispered, his warm breath tickling her earlobe. "You took one of me? Lurking behind curtains in the dark... what a shameless little stalker you are, Morwenna."
An apocalyptic shade of purple-red detonated across Morwenna’s face.
She frantically tried to shove the photograph into her coat pocket with her boots stomping against the stone floor in mortification.

"I AM NOT STALKING YOU!" Morwenna hissed, her voice cracking into an undignified squeak as she struggled against his hold. "The lighting was optimal! And I wanted to take a picture! I’m not a stalker!"
"Right. You’re not a stalker," Silas chuckled, not believing a single syllable, his fingers giving her waist an affectionate squeeze that made her squeak again.
"What’s that? Are we taking pictures?!"
A melodic slurred voice chimed from the side.

Eluned stumbled out of the shadows, swaying like a willow tree in a gale with her green hair completely disheveled as she practically threw her upper body onto Silas’s chest, pushing herself between him and the blushing pirate.

"Come on! Let’s take one together!" Eluned whined, her arms winding around Silas’s neck as she glared blearily at Morwenna. "Give me that camera, you salt-crusted barnacle! We need a proper portrait!"
"Get your sticky weed-hands off my lens!" Morwenna snapped defensively, holding the camera high overhead.
"I can take it!"
The Princess suddenly trotted over from the long table, her cheeks bright red and a heavy wooden tankard dangling from one hand while she reached eagerly for the brass device.
"I know how to operate cameras!" the Princess declared proudly, hiccuping softly. "Let me take the picture!"
"Wait, I want in!" Brenda’s voice rang out from across the hall.
"Me too! Move over, rookies!" Helen shouted.
Within thirty seconds, the quiet place was completely swarmed.
All of the women present, which was almost every woman in Blessed Land crowded together in an enormous chaotic semicircle, hell even Kaelia was here.

Silas was shoved dead-center into the middle of the mass... Eluned clinging tightly to his left arm with a dopey affectionate grin, Morwenna standing stiffly at his right with her arms crossed and her face still burning red, and the Princess happily balancing on her tiptoes just behind his shoulder.

The dwarven smiths shoved their way to the front, kneeling on the floorboards with their tankards held high, while the other girls piled onto benches behind them, flashing peace signs, flexing their biceps, and sticking their tongues out in drunken joy.
Silas looked at the sea of smiling, flushed faces surrounding him, let out a soft laugh, and threw his arms around the shoulders of the women closest to him, offering the camera a wide grin.
Across the room, the unconscious Thor suddenly gave a massive snort.
SNK-ROOOOM!
The God of Thunder’s eyes snapped open. Sensing a moment of glory, she launched herself off the table.
She snatched the enchanted camera from the woman’s hands, set the mechanical timer rune with a heavy flick of her thumb, and mounted it atop a stack of empty ale kegs twelve paces back.
BEEP-BEEP-BEEP.
The runic shutter began to pulse with rapid blue light but Thor didn’t run back to the group with the Princess... she teleported there.
KRA-FLASH!
In an imperceptible fraction of a microsecond, a streak of blue lightning detonated across the floor.

Before the timer could hit zero, Thor materialized directly beside Silas, ducking her frame down and locking her thick muscular hand firmly around his right fingers with an enormous boar-grease-covered grin.
FLASH!
The camera illuminated the entire hall in an explosion of pure white radiance.
ZOOOOOM!
Thor’s hand blurred again.

With the terrifying god-like reflexes of an apex warrior, she shot across the room like a bullet, snatching the camera out of the air right as the vibration of the shutter shook it loose from the kegs.
She caught it cleanly against her chest, skidding across the stones on her knees with a boisterous roar.
"GWAHAHAHAHA! PERFECT TIMING!"
The girls cheered wildly, crowding around the kneeling thunder god as the enchanted photographic paper slowly slid out of the lower tray.
Thor held it up to the torchlight.
It was an incredible shot...
The garrison of Blessed Land was captured in vibrant breathtaking detail.

The blazing hearths, the smoke drifting through the rafters, the tankards raised in triumph, and the women smiling with genuine unshakeable happiness around their black-haired Lord, whose presence anchored the entire hall.
Silas looked down at the paper, a deep, quiet pride swelling within his chest.
’It’s a very good picture...’
The following morning broke with a cold unforgiving stillness.

The heavy blizzards that had picked up throughout the previous night had finally dissipated, leaving behind an iron-gray overcast sky that hung low and suffocating over the jagged peaks of the Umbral Basin.
Fine powdery flakes of white snow drifted lazily through the sub-zero air, dusting the black slate battlements and settling across the broad gravel yard of the Keep.
’I really hate this snow...’
Sitting tall and motionless atop the reinforced leather saddle of Valkyrie in the center of the snowy courtyard was Silas.
The Lord was fully clad in his heavy winter combat ensemble... dark fitted void-iron lamellar armor layered over thick insulated wool, his coat cinched tight by a wide leather weapon harness.
Across his lap rested the radiant golden mythril blade with its sheath cold to the touch.
’Still this is my Tier 3 Mythril Longsword... my first weapon heh, been a while...’
His Gold Core hummed with steady power as a thin barrier of warmth radiated off his skin to melt the falling snowflakes before they could touch his hair.
Standing beside Valkyrie’s muscular flank was Kaelia.
The head of the Keep’s Culinary Haven looked like an anxious fretting wife.
Her dark hair was neatly pinned beneath a warm woolen cap with her breath rising in trembling plumes of white mist as she hoisted three massive lacquer-sealed transport containers into the air.

"My Lord, please take these," Kaelia urged, her eyes pooling with genuine fretful worry as she looked up at him. "I stayed up through the night preparing them... There are thirty-six individual meal rations inside. Roasted mountain venison sealed in clarified tallow, steamed winter tubers seasoned with spirit-salt, dense honey-seed traveler’s bread, and six vacuum-sealed jars of concentrated bone broth. It will keep for weeks without freezing!"

chapters.title: Chapter 502: Departing From Blessed Land [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas looked down at the towering stack of containers with a warm reassuring smile curving his lips.

"Kaelia," Silas chuckled softly, reaching out and resting a heavy, gloved hand atop her wool cap, giving her an affectionate pat. "We’re mounting an extraction strike, not marching to the edge of the world but I appreciate it. Your cooking is the only reason this territory functions."
VUUUM!

Silas tapped into his spatial inventory and a shimmer of azure mana washed over the lacquer boxes, instantly dematerializing the three heavy containers and filing them into the stabilized pockets of his personal storage.
"See? Safe and sound," Silas assured her, withdrawing his hand. "We’ll be back before the week is out so keep the hearths stoked and the garrison fed."
"May the gods watch over your blade, Lord Silas," Kaelia murmured, offering a deep respectful bow before stepping back toward the heated portico. ’I really really really want to kiss him...’
Silas turned his head, letting his blue eyes sweep across the strike detachment assembled in the snow behind him.
It was a small formation as every single woman present had been chosen for extreme mobility or strategic versatility.
Mounted side-by-side upon two Blessed Wolves were Eluned and Morwenna.
The Goddess was clad in a traveling ensemble of dark emerald wool lined with white ermine fur with her long silver green hair braided tightly down her spine to keep it out of the wind.
She was casually conversing with the Pirate Queen, who sat slouched in her saddle with her heavy cutlass resting across her pommel with a rare relaxed smirk playing across her face.
The mutual hostility from the previous day seemed to have settled into a strange comfortable truce born of respect and perhaps the lingering aftershocks of too much dwarven stout.
A few paces to their left sat Aeliana.
The high-elf secretary was dressed in a pristine white high-collared shirt and fitted charcoal traveling trousers, tucked securely into knee-high riding boots.
Her striking silver-gold eyes flicked nervously across the snowy battlements, her small porcelain hands gripping the reins of her mount so tightly her knuckles were white.
She looked visibly jittery.
Silas understood her tension completely.
For a while, Aeli had been the secondary Lord so she was feeling a bit shy, Silas was sure once they were in the field she would calm down.
Beside Aeliana sat Kadi.
The Sand Mage was equally restless.
Dressed in her desert silks reinforced with lightweight steel plates, Kadi’s dark braids whipped in the icy wind.
She kept shifting in her saddle, checking the leather straps on her weapon belts with sharp twitchy movements.
She hadn’t been part of the primary mining crews yesterday, having spent the entire day nursing Talira through her draconic mana fever.
Being thrust directly into a strike team heading for the northern trenches had set her nerves on edge.
Positioned near the center of the formation was Aurelia.
The Saintess of the Argent Flame looked breathtakingly regal.
She sat tall atop her mount... the notoriously arrogant Blessed Wolf draped in light armor.
Despite the bitter chill, she wore no heavy furs as the imperceptible halo of the Argent Flame humming within her soul kept the air around her warm and fragrant.
Sensing Silas’s gaze, Aurelia turned her head, offering him a serene confident smile that instantly settled the nervous energy rippling through the ranks.
Riding alongside Aurelia was the Princess.
The royal maiden was bundled in a heavy fur-lined traveling mantle, her small hands fussing nervously with the leather buckles of her riding harness.
On her shoulder pauldron sat the obsidian bird, its beady eyes sharp and alert, acting as the living compass for the mission.
And rounding out the rear of the detachment were Tasmin and Thor.
Tasmin sat low in her saddle, cloaked in liquid shadows that seemed to swallow the gray morning light with her twin void-daggers resting securely in reverse-grip sheaths along her thighs.
Thor, however, had completely commandeered Titan... the Alpha of the original Blessed Wolf pack.
The Alpha was currently lying flat on its belly in the snow, letting out a series of tiny whimpering chuffs.

The towering blonde God of Thunder was sitting cross-legged across its broad shoulders, laughing boisterously as she aggressively scratched behind the beast’s ears with enough divine force to shake its entire skull.
"Gwahahaha! Who is a good mountain dog?! You are! Yes, you are!" Thor roared merrily, rubbing the Alpha’s snout until its tongue flopped sideways in submissive defeat.
Silas chuckled, shaking his head at the sight.
"Leave the poor beast alone, Thor. He needs his dignity to lead the charge."
Even Valkyrie was giving him weird looks...
CLANK-CLANK!
Heavy steel-toed footsteps echoed across the slush as the person marching toward them was Thora.
The dwarven forge master was bundled in a heavy leather shearling coat, her breath huffing in short bursts as she carried an enormous, iron-banded wooden crate in her arms.
"Hold your reins! Nobody moves an inch until you take these!" Thora barked, dropping the crate into the snow with a dull thud.
She kicked the lid open with her boot, revealing eight heavy folded cloaks of an entirely unfamiliar textile.
The fabric was stunning.

It possessed a deep midnight-black hue that seemed to absorb ambient light, woven from ultra-dense fibers, but layered throughout the weave was a shimmering microscopic network of liquid silver that caught the morning sun like a web of stars.
Silas dismounted, stepping through the snow to pick up the top garment.
The cloak was surprisingly lightweight, but the moment his fingers brushed the fabric, it felt a bit strange.
"What is this material, Thora?" Silas asked, rubbing the dense weave between his thumb and forefinger.

"The finest armor my foundry has ever produced, my Lord," Thora beamed proudly, crossing her thick arms over her chest. "The primary weave was crafted by our tailor using the synthetic material you brought back from your last supply run to the human world on Earth but that’s just the base. I took four hundred pounds of virgin Sil-Graves Silver, liquefied it in the plasma crucibles, and drew it into microscopic hair-thin runic threads."
She pointed a calloused finger at the silver webbing running through the dark wool.

"Those silver threads are woven directly into the structural lattice of the polymer," Thora explained. "It possesses dispersion so you could take a high-velocity siege bolt dead to the chest, and the impact would spread across the entire surface of the cloak like water hitting an anvil. Furthermore, Sil-Graves Silver is naturally immune to breaking apart and it also can keep you warm and protect from spells... It is the ultimate personal defense!"
Silas looked down at the masterpiece of synthetic engineering and magical metallurgy, a slow impressed smile spreading across his face.

"Incredible work, Thora," Silas said genuinely, reaching out and resting his palm atop the dwarf’s head, giving her rough hair a firm affectionate ruffle. "You’ve outdone yourself. Blessed Land’s industry is unmatched..."

Thora’s pale cheeks instantly flushed a brilliant, flustered pink. She coughed aggressively into her fist, swatting his hand away with a mumbled grumble, though her eyes were shining with dwarven pride.
"Hmph! Just make sure you bring it back without monster guts caked into the silver threads! Dry cleaning high-tier alloy is a nightmare!"
Silas took the cloaks, walking down the line and distributing them to the strike team.
Eluned draped hers gracefully over her shoulders, the midnight fabric contrasting beautifully with her emerald hair.

Morwenna ran her thumb over the silver weave with a quiet, appreciative whistle, while Aeli and Kadi fastened their brooches with visible relief, the protective weight immediately easing their morning jitters.
Silas fastened his own cloak around his neck, letting the silver-threaded wool fall over his armor like a shadow.
They were entering the forbidden depths of the Umbral Basin as the northern trenches were populated by Tier 4 and Tier 5 monsters.
In a zone like that, there was no such thing as being too prepared as the stronger they were, the better their chances of survival.
’Though I’m not sure we’re going to die... It’s not like we’re going to pick a fight with the monsters there.’ Silas thought.
They were going for the goddess, and if they were attacked on the way, what did they have to do... Just kill a few beasts right?
Silas turned his gaze toward the front, standing near the Spirit trees with her massive Titan’s Cleaver strapped across her back, was Brida.
Silas had debated taking her along.
Her raw physical power and devastating shockwave attacks were unmatched among his vanguard but high-tier expeditions required cold discipline.
More importantly... a territory could not be left leaderless.
Behind Tasmin and Aeli... Brida was the next in line for operational authority.
She possessed the respect of everyone, the combat instincts of a veteran officer, and an unshakeable loyalty to his person.
Silas trusted her with his life, and he trusted her with his home.
Brida marched forward with her heavy boots crunching into the permafrost, stopping three paces before Silas.
She snapped her right fist against her chestplate in a sharp immaculate military salute.
CLANG!
"Brida," Silas addressed her. "Are the defenses prepared?"

"All sectors secure, my Lord!" Brida reported loudly, her amber eyes burning with fierce, disciplined focus. "The northern and southern walls are fully manned. Furthermore, every single recruit and officer on the line has been stamped with the Genesis Runes across their knuckles..."
She raised her right gauntlet, showing the intricate glowing green runes etched into the metal plates over her fingers.
"If any monster attack occurs, the girls can trigger an immediate cellular regeneration surge to stabilize fatal wounds and kill their opponents. We are locked down tight."
Silas looked at her steady, unblinking gaze, letting out a soft satisfied breath.
"Thank you, Brida," Silas said softly. "I’m sorry you have to stay behind while we march north. I know how much you wanted to swing your cleaver today..."
Brida lowered her salute.
Her fierce battle-hardened expression softened as a sudden emotional warmth rose in her eyes.
She took a step forward, closing the distance, and wrapped her strong armored arms around Silas’s torso in a fierce tight embrace.
THUD.
Her cheek pressed against the thick wolf fur of his collar with her breath warm against his neck.

"Do not apologize, my Lord," Brida whispered. "To be trusted with your walls... to be trusted with your home while you walk into the dark... there is no greater honor for a woman . I am honored that you thought of me for this position so I swear upon my blood, not a single pebble will be displaced from Blessed Land while you are gone."
Silas smiled gently, wrapping his arms around her broad shoulders and returning the hug with firm reassuring pressure.
He leaned back slightly, looked into her glowing amber eyes, and pressed a soft lingering kiss directly onto her forehead.
SMOOCH!
Brida froze as her breath completely hitched in her throat.
Her eyes dilated, and a furious wave of crimson exploded across her cheeks, traveling all the way down to her collarbone.
"Ahem~"
From the saddle of her mount three paces away, Eluned cleared her throat with an exaggerated pointed cough as her emerald eyes narrowed into a jealous squint.
Silas chuckled, releasing the trembling woman and stepping smoothly back toward Valkyrie.
He vaulted into the saddle with fluid grace, settling his boots into the stirrups.
He pulled the heavy, silver-threaded hood over his dark hair, shadowing his face, leaving only the piercing golden-blue gleam of his eyes visible beneath the brim.
He drew the golden blade three inches from its scabbard, the raw mana flaring along the steel like a sunburst.
SHING!
"Strike detachment!" Silas roared. "Form standard wedge! Eyes sharp and pace steady! Forward march!"
HOWOOOOOOOOOL!
The Blessed Wolves answered with a unified bone-chilling howl that shook the snow from the eaves.
Pounding across the frozen gravel, the eight mounts surged forward, tearing through the inner courtyard.

They shot past the towering Spirit Trees, their silver-furred bodies moving with terrifying effortless speed, before thundering through the massive opened iron gates of Blessed Land, heading straight into the lightless frozen horrors of the northern Umbral Basin.
KRRRRRR-CLANG.
Behind them, the colossal iron-banded gates groaned on their massive hinges, swinging shut with a concussive final boom that sealed the territory tight.
Left standing alone in the center of the quiet snow-dusted courtyard, Brida remained completely motionless.
The cold wind whipped her hair across her face, but she didn’t feel the chill.
Her forehead was burning as if branded by a holy flame.
Her cheeks were a radiant shade of beet-red and her breath was coming in short gasps that plumed into the morning air.
Slowly, almost unconsciously, her hand drifted down from her chestplate with her trembling fingers pressing gently between her thighs through the thick fabric of her leather breeches.
A grin split across her flushed face.
’He kissed me...’ Brida thought with her heart slamming against her ribs like a berserker’s war drum. ’Right on the forehead... in front of the entire squad...’
Her fingers twitched, pressing a fraction firmer against her crotch as her mind began to spiral into wild sinful fantasies.
’He left me in charge... I am the temporary Lord of Blessed Land... which means... technically... I am the Lord’s acting wife right now...’
She swallowed hard, looking back toward the towering silent expanse of the Keep.
’Will it be okay... if I sneak into his private chambers... wrap myself in his unwashed bedsheets... and use Master’s smell to get it off...?’
A soft breathless moan escaped her parted lips as a shiver of ecstasy rippled through her spine.
She turned on her heel with her boots practically floating across the snow as she marched eagerly toward the Keep’s entrance, her eyes glazed with lewd anticipation.
’Best day...’ Brida purred inwardly, hugging herself tightly. ’...EVER~!’

chapters.title: Chapter 503: Operation: Save The Beast Goddess [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Snow exploded into fine powdery plumes behind eight pairs of driving hindquarters as the Blessed Wolves tore through the frost-crusted drifts.
The concussive thud-thud-thud of padded paws hammering against petrified shale sounded like heavy artillery firing at a steady tempo.

The biting wind of the Umbral Basin screamed past Silas’s ears, whipping the fur trim of his coat against his jaw but the micro-current of heat circulating beneath his collar kept the sub-zero air from biting into his lungs.
Up ahead, low in the saddle of her mount, Tasmin raised her left arm with her black leather gauntlet cutting cleanly through the freezing gale.
"Boundary in three hundred meters!" she called back, her raspy voice carrying sharply over the howling squalls. "Decelerating to column order!"
Riding bareback atop Titan with her long legs casually flanking the Alpha wolf’s ribs, Thor blinked her storm-blue eyes.
The divine warrior tilted her head, her blonde locks whipping into a golden halo around her broad muscular shoulders.

"Boundary?" Thor echoed, her voice booming over the rush of the wind without an ounce of strain. "What boundary? We’ve been running across cold gravel for an hour, Silas! Has the dirt changed flavors?"
Beside Aurelia’s wolf, the Princess sat upright in her saddle, her gloved fingers tightly gripping the reins.
Her azure eyes were wide, darting between the towering dark conifers lining the ridgeline and the horizon where the mountain peaks jagged into the bruising clouds.
"Is it a perimeter ward?" the Princess asked, her tone carrying a breathless, girlish thrill. "Like a demarcation line? A defensive threshold from an old war?"
She looked thoroughly enamored with the concept, sitting with her back straight, fully leaning into the feeling of an elite deployment.
To someone who had spent her entire sheltered existence locked behind palatial balconies and formal tea rooms, the terminology sounded like something pulled straight out of a modern thriller.
"Hehe~"
From the head of the column, Silas let out a slow frosty breath, watching the white vapor dissipate over Valkyrie’s twitching silver ears.

"Nothing that poetic," Silas said, pulling slightly on the leather straps to bring the pace from a thundering dead sprint down to a controlled ground-eating lope. "The ’Boundary’ is just the term we stamped on the maps back at the Keep. It marks the outer perimeter of our territorial reconnaissance limit... Up to that stone ridge fifty paces ahead, my women have scouted, cleared, and mapped every fault line, cave mouth, and diamond vein."
He pointed a gloved hand toward a massive fissure running horizontally across the valley floor, where two split granite pillars stood like broken teeth jutting from the permafrost.
"Once we step past those pillars," Silas continued, "we’re off the map so none of us have set foot beyond that line."
From the front, Tasmin pulled her mount parallel to Valkyrie, flashing a crisp confident thumbs-up over her shoulder.
"We pass the perimeter at the gorge my Lord... Past this, we’re walking on virgin soil."
Silas reached down, patting Valkyrie’s thick muscular neck with a gloved palm. The Blessed wolf let out a deep rumbling chuff of acknowledgment, her golden harness humming softly against her chest.

’It would be simple to just unleash Thor,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes drifting back to the blonde demigoddess who was currently trying to see if she could catch falling snowflakes on her tongue while balancing on the Alpha’s back. ’We could hand the bird to her, tell her to ride the lightning, and she’d cover forty miles in ten seconds... She could drop out of the stratosphere, crack the Forever Ice with a celestial shockwave, throw the Beast Goddess over her shoulder, and be back at the Keep before lunchtime.’
He mentally shook his head, clamping down on the thought before it could take root.
’No. Bad habit...’
Thor was an incredible combat asset which was an overwhelming wall of divine muscle and atmospheric devastation, but she wasn’t his soldier.
She wasn’t bound to his territory and she wasn’t a registered Hero of Blessed Land.
She was a wandering divine entity who had essentially hitched a ride with the royal girl because the royal girl kept her belly full of prime pork and sweet dwarven ale.
When the Princess’s week expired and she returned to Earth, Thor would walk right out behind her. And who was to say she would ever step foot in this basin again?

’I can’t let the territory become reliant on an outside god,’ Silas reminded himself with his jaw setting firmly. ’Relying on borrowed power dulls your own edge... The moment you build your operational framework around a weapon you don’t own, you’re already writing your own obituary.’
Maybe during the next Hero summoning, the world would grant him a flight-capable aerial deity of his own.
But until then, they moved on their own legs, measured their own steps, and solved their own problems.
As the pack crested the gravel ridge, the granite pillars loomed over them, casting long lightless shadows across the snow.
Silas drew Valkyrie to a complete halt, turning his head to look back at the Princess’s mount.

"From here on out," Silas announced, his voice dropping into a disciplined tone that carried across the eight riders. "We follow the bird’s navigation... We’re taking the paths of least resistance, routes with minimal monster packs but keep your eyes wide... I want to study their migration patterns. All those monsters and shapeshifters that keep leaking south toward our side are bleeding out from this sector. I want to know what’s pushing them."
Aurelia nodded serenely, her golden eyes scanning the jagged timberline with quiet vigilance.
"Understood, Lord Silas."

"I have the rear flank," Morwenna added, her dark gray eyes sharp as flint beneath her heavy traveling cloak and her fingers resting lazily against the silver pommel of Tidebringer. "Nothing slips through my draft, Captain."
On the Princess’s shoulder, the obsidian bird let out a sharp clicking clack of its scythe-beak.
The moment Valkyrie’s front paws crossed the imaginary line between the two shattered pillars, the avian launched into the freezing air with an explosive beat of its dark wings.
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP!
The bird surged forward, leveling off ten feet above the snowdrifts, banking hard into a sharp sweeping ninety-degree right turn that cut straight into a dense forest of black-barked pine.
"Follow it!" Silas ordered, nudging his heels into Valkyrie’s flanks.
The Blessed Wolves surged forward as a cohesive unit, vaulting the horizontal rock fissure and diving headfirst beneath the suffocating canopy of the northern tree line.
The interior of the northern forest was different from the light airy woodlands surrounding the southern borders of Blessed Land.
Here, the trees did not grow straight... they twisted like petrified bone, their charcoal-black branches tangling overhead in a dense suffocating web that choked out nearly all daylight.
The sub-zero wind that howled across the open plains died to a sinister stagnant hush, broken only by the crunch of heavy paws and the unsettling drip of dark moisture falling from dead needles.
The deeper they pressed into the lightless grove, the heavier the atmospheric pressure became.
It was an oppressive crawling sensation... the distinct feeling of cold hostile eyes pressing against the back of one’s neck from every shadow.
The bark of the trees was scored with grotesque, unnatural claw marks, and the smell of snow was tainted by the coppery tang of dried blood and stagnant swamp water.
Silas exhaled a slow, controlled breath with the skin along his arms prickling.
’There are dozens of them,’ Silas thought, his eyes tracking the micro-movements of the dead brush thirty yards to his left. ’They aren’t hunting yet so my guess is that they’re observing...’
He reached into his tunic, lightly tapping his collarbone with his thumb.
FZZT!
From beneath the dark silver-threaded weave of his cloak, a warm, radiant crimson sphere drifted out into the frigid air.
Kael-Drin popped into existence with a cheerful melodic chime that sounded like tiny glass bells.
The fist-sized spirit hovered around Silas’s neck, its translucent ruby shell pulsing with tiny flecks of pure gold mana.
Feeling the cold malignant stares lingering in the dark pines, the spirit’s core suddenly flared with sudden protective heat, tiny sparks of crimson fire dancing along its surface.

"Easy, Kael-Drin," Silas murmured softly, raising a single finger to let the warm sphere bump gently against his knuckle. "Keep it quiet. Don’t broadcast our heat signature unless I tell you to light them up."
The spirit’s pulsing stabilized, letting out a soft obedient hum as it settled down against his right shoulder, resting beneath the heavy hood of his cloak like a radiant warm brooch.
Silas turned his head slightly toward Eluned, who was riding smoothly to his left with her emerald braid resting neatly over her shoulder.
"Elu," Silas asked quietly, his voice barely carrying past their mounts, "are we even remotely close to the trench?"
Eluned closed her eyes for a brief second, her consciousness dipping into the soil beneath the permafrost, probing the dormant root systems of the basin.
When she opened her emerald irises, she offered a slow reluctant shake of her head.

"Not yet, my love," Eluned replied, her melodic voice laced with quiet caution. "The signature of the Forever Ice is vast, but it lies deep within the geological rift... We must penetrate at least fifteen miles further into the basin’s core before we reach the descent lip."
From overhead, banking low through a gap in the twisted black boughs, the obsidian bird let out a harsh sound.
"SQUAWK! Krrr-caw!"
"Tch. Even further, huh," Silas grunted, pulling his fur collar tighter against his throat.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, expanding the spiritual perception anchored within his Mythic Gold Core.
The golden mana circulated outward in an invisible spherical pulse, sweeping across the dark forest floor.
Within a three-hundred-meter radius, he picked up forty distinct biological signatures.
Most were low-tier scavengers... blind burrowing abominations hiding beneath the roots, waiting for scraps.
But lingering just at the edge of his range were larger mana signatures.
’If we can just maintain a clear path, we can reach the lip before dusk,’ Silas analyzed. ’A direct march without burning resources on minor skirmishes is optimal.’
Reality, however, had zero intention of cooperating.
As the pack rounded the moss-rotted trunk of a shattered ironwood, the landscape abruptly shifted.

The crisp freezing air suddenly grew thick and suffocatingly humid. From the hollows between the tree roots, a dense milky-white fog began to bleed upward from the earth, swirling around the wolves’ paws like living creeping tendrils of vapor.
Within seconds, the mist rose to their waists, drastically cutting their visual range down to less than fifteen paces.
"Heads on swivels!" Tasmin’s sharp command sliced through the silence.
The commander dropped her center of gravity, her twin void-daggers sliding from their sheaths with a whispering shing. "Visibility is dropping fast so thermal and shadow signatures are blurring!"
SHSHSHK!
Barely three yards above Silas’s right shoulder, the dead bough of a black pine cracked.
From the swirling white fog, a grotesque sickening projectile lunged through the air straight toward his throat.

It was roughly four feet long... a pale fleshy segmented creature resembling a bloated eyeless earthworm, but its circular maw was lined with five concentric rings of serrated needle-like bone teeth that dripped with clear paralytic mucus.
Silas didn’t even flinch.
CLANG-SHING!
His right arm blurred into a golden arc.
The golden mythril longsword cleared its scabbard with the deafening shriek of drawn steel.
Before the worm’s jaws could snap shut, the radiant blade cleaved cleanly through the center of its segmented body.
SPLAT!
The two severed halves of the monster tumbled onto the snow, twitching violently as dark foul-smelling fluid sprayed across the white crust.
RUSTLE-SNAP-CRACK!
The single strike acted like a tripwire.
All around them, the suffocating canopy of the black pines erupted into violent coordinated motion.
Dozens of the segmented worm-aberrations began dropping out of the branches like disgusting fleshy rain, their circular maws gnashing in high-pitched wet chittering sounds.
"Eep!" The Princess gasped, reflexively drawing her void-iron dagger, bracing herself behind Aurelia’s flank.
"Hold your ground," Morwenna’s dry voice cut through the rising panic.
The Pirate Queen casually reached across her chest, her calloused fingers wrapping around Tidebringer but she didn’t draw the weapon.
Her gray eyes flickered with a cold, lazy glint.
’Heh... let’s look cool.’
She popped the crossguard forward with her thumb by a single solitary inch.
CLICK.
SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING!
An invisible terrifying storm of vacuum blade-air detonated outward from the seam of her scabbard.
To the mortal eye, she hadn’t moved an arm.

But in the space between two heartbeats, hundreds of razor-thin pressurized crescents of oceanic wind-mana spiraled upward in a howling vortex, shredding the space above the column into a butcher’s block.
CHOP-CHOP-CHOP-CHOP!

sentences.text: Snow exploded into fine powdery plumes behind eight pairs of driving hindquarters as the Blessed Wolves tore through the frost-crusted drifts.

The biting wind of the Umbral Basin screamed past Silas’s ears, whipping the fur trim of his coat against his jaw but the micro-current of heat circulating beneath his collar kept the sub-zero air from biting into his lungs.
Up ahead, low in the saddle of her mount, Tasmin raised her left arm with her black leather gauntlet cutting cleanly through the freezing gale.
"Boundary in three hundred meters!" she called back, her raspy voice carrying sharply over the howling squalls.
"Decelerating to column order!"
Riding bareback atop Titan with her long legs casually flanking the Alpha wolf’s ribs, Thor blinked her storm-blue eyes.
The divine warrior tilted her head, her blonde locks whipping into a golden halo around her broad muscular shoulders.
"Boundary?" Thor echoed, her voice booming over the rush of the wind without an ounce of strain.
"What boundary?
We’ve been running across cold gravel for an hour, Silas!
Has the dirt changed flavors?"
Beside Aurelia’s wolf, the Princess sat upright in her saddle, her gloved fingers tightly gripping the reins.
Her azure eyes were wide, darting between the towering dark conifers lining the ridgeline and the horizon where the mountain peaks jagged into the bruising clouds.
"Is it a perimeter ward?" the Princess asked, her tone carrying a breathless, girlish thrill.
"Like a demarcation line?
A defensive threshold from an old war?"
She looked thoroughly enamored with the concept, sitting with her back straight, fully leaning into the feeling of an elite deployment.
To someone who had spent her entire sheltered existence locked behind palatial balconies and formal tea rooms, the terminology sounded like something pulled straight out of a modern thriller.
"Hehe~"
From the head of the column, Silas let out a slow frosty breath, watching the white vapor dissipate over Valkyrie’s twitching silver ears.
"Nothing that poetic," Silas said, pulling slightly on the leather straps to bring the pace from a thundering dead sprint down to a controlled ground-eating lope.
"The ’Boundary’ is just the term we stamped on the maps back at the Keep.
It marks the outer perimeter of our territorial reconnaissance limit...
Up to that stone ridge fifty paces ahead, my women have scouted, cleared, and mapped every fault line, cave mouth, and diamond vein."
He pointed a gloved hand toward a massive fissure running horizontally across the valley floor, where two split granite pillars stood like broken teeth jutting from the permafrost.
"Once we step past those pillars," Silas continued, "we’re off the map so none of us have set foot beyond that line."
From the front, Tasmin pulled her mount parallel to Valkyrie, flashing a crisp confident thumbs-up over her shoulder.
"We pass the perimeter at the gorge my Lord...
Past this, we’re walking on virgin soil."
Silas reached down, patting Valkyrie’s thick muscular neck with a gloved palm.
The Blessed wolf let out a deep rumbling chuff of acknowledgment, her golden harness humming softly against her chest.

’It would be simple to just unleash Thor,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes drifting back to the blonde demigoddess who was currently trying to see if she could catch falling snowflakes on her tongue while balancing on the Alpha’s back. ’We could hand the bird to her, tell her to ride the lightning, and she’d cover forty miles in ten seconds...
She could drop out of the stratosphere, crack the Forever Ice with a celestial shockwave, throw the Beast Goddess over her shoulder, and be back at the Keep before lunchtime.’
He mentally shook his head, clamping down on the thought before it could take root.
’No.
Bad habit...’
Thor was an incredible combat asset which was an overwhelming wall of divine muscle and atmospheric devastation, but she wasn’t his soldier.
She wasn’t bound to his territory and she wasn’t a registered Hero of Blessed Land.
She was a wandering divine entity who had essentially hitched a ride with the royal girl because the royal girl kept her belly full of prime pork and sweet dwarven ale.
When the Princess’s week expired and she returned to Earth, Thor would walk right out behind her.
And who was to say she would ever step foot in this basin again?
’I can’t let the territory become reliant on an outside god,’ Silas reminded himself with his jaw setting firmly. ’Relying on borrowed power dulls your own edge...
The moment you build your operational framework around a weapon you don’t own, you’re already writing your own obituary.’
Maybe during the next Hero summoning, the world would grant him a flight-capable aerial deity of his own.
But until then, they moved on their own legs, measured their own steps, and solved their own problems.
As the pack crested the gravel ridge, the granite pillars loomed over them, casting long lightless shadows across the snow.
Silas drew Valkyrie to a complete halt, turning his head to look back at the Princess’s mount.
"From here on out," Silas announced, his voice dropping into a disciplined tone that carried across the eight riders.
"We follow the bird’s navigation...
We’re taking the paths of least resistance, routes with minimal monster packs but keep your eyes wide...
I want to study their migration patterns.
All those monsters and shapeshifters that keep leaking south toward our side are bleeding out from this sector.
I want to know what’s pushing them."
Aurelia nodded serenely, her golden eyes scanning the jagged timberline with quiet vigilance.
"Understood, Lord Silas."
"I have the rear flank," Morwenna added, her dark gray eyes sharp as flint beneath her heavy traveling cloak and her fingers resting lazily against the silver pommel of Tidebringer.
"Nothing slips through my draft, Captain."
On the Princess’s shoulder, the obsidian bird let out a sharp clicking clack of its scythe-beak.
The moment Valkyrie’s front paws crossed the imaginary line between the two shattered pillars, the avian launched into the freezing air with an explosive beat of its dark wings.
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP!
The bird surged forward, leveling off ten feet above the snowdrifts, banking hard into a sharp sweeping ninety-degree right turn that cut straight into a dense forest of black-barked pine.
"Follow it!" Silas ordered, nudging his heels into Valkyrie’s flanks.
The Blessed Wolves surged forward as a cohesive unit, vaulting the horizontal rock fissure and diving headfirst beneath the suffocating canopy of the northern tree line.
The interior of the northern forest was different from the light airy woodlands surrounding the southern borders of Blessed Land.
Here, the trees did not grow straight... they twisted like petrified bone, their charcoal-black branches tangling overhead in a dense suffocating web that choked out nearly all daylight.
The sub-zero wind that howled across the open plains died to a sinister stagnant hush, broken only by the crunch of heavy paws and the unsettling drip of dark moisture falling from dead needles.
The deeper they pressed into the lightless grove, the heavier the atmospheric pressure became.
It was an oppressive crawling sensation... the distinct feeling of cold hostile eyes pressing against the back of one’s neck from every shadow.
The bark of the trees was scored with grotesque, unnatural claw marks, and the smell of snow was tainted by the coppery tang of dried blood and stagnant swamp water.
Silas exhaled a slow, controlled breath with the skin along his arms prickling.
’There are dozens of them,’ Silas thought, his eyes tracking the micro-movements of the dead brush thirty yards to his left. ’They aren’t hunting yet so my guess is that they’re observing...’
He reached into his tunic, lightly tapping his collarbone with his thumb.
FZZT!

Kael-Drin popped into existence with a cheerful melodic chime that sounded like tiny glass bells.
