chapters.title: Chapter 504: Operation: Save The Beast Goddess [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Every single worm suspended in mid-air was instantly diced into dozens of neat uniform cross-sections.
The pressurized wind sheared clean through the overhanging branches, severing the worms still clinging to the bark before they could even coil their muscles to leap.
THUD-THUD-THUD-SPLAT!
A shower of diced rubbery meat and severed teeth rained down around the wolves’ paws, splashing harmlessly against the ambient mana barriers woven by Eluned’s roots.
Morwenna’s thumb pressed the crossguard back down with a sharp echoing clack.
"Sloppy little leeches," Morwenna muttered, leaning her elbow back against the pommel. "Not even worth drawing the steel..."
Overhead, the obsidian bird let out an urgent shrieking rattle, banking hard to the right, cutting clean through a dense curtain of hanging moss to exit the suffocating hollow.
"Right flank! Keep moving!" Silas barked.
The wolves bounded after the feathered guide, tearing through the moss curtain and bursting out of the low-lying ravine.
Almost instantaneously, the humid foul-smelling white vapor thinned out, replaced once more by the biting clean frost of the high ridges.
The obsidian bird fluttered down to a low-hanging rock shelf, perching on its talons and puffing out its dark chest, letting out an audible rattling wheeze of pure relief.
"Krrr-clack... squawk..."
Silas pulled Valkyrie to a halt, looking back over his shoulder at the pale swirling bank of fog they had just escaped.
"What was that about?" Silas asked, his brow furrowing as he looked up at the bird. "Why the sudden panic over low-tier leeches?"

The bird launched into a frantic sequence of squawks, bobbing its head toward the mist, fluttering its wings in wide circular motions, and then stabbing its beak toward the dirt, mimicking a creeping spreading shadow.
Eluned listened intently, her emerald eyes tracking the bird’s erratic movements before turning to Silas with an informative nod.

"It is a phenomenon of the deep basin," Eluned explained, adjusting the ermine trim of her cloak. "That fog is a manifestation of stagnant necrotic dampness that bleeds from the bogs. Those worm creatures... Corpse-Leeches do not exist as physical entities outside of that specific vapor. They are born from the mist, they feed within the mist, and they dissolve when the mist dissipates. If a monster lingers in the fog for more than a few minutes, the vapor thickens until a lot of them manifest simultaneously, suffocating prey beneath a living tide."
Silas raised his golden longsword, bringing the flat of the blade to eye level.
His blue eyes narrowed.
The thick black ichor that had coated the steel when he cleaved that first worm clean in two... was completely gone.
Not a smudge remained... hell not even a single stain either. The polished mythril was immaculate, reflecting the gray sky like a flawless mirror.

’That’s very weird...’ Silas thought. ’A biological entity that exists only as an extension of an atmospheric anomaly... If the blood doesn’t even leave physical residue, what kind of mutated core is anchoring this basin?’
Again and again, it just proved that the Umbral Basin was very dangerous.
He flicked the sword clean on instinct and slid it back into its scabbard with a crisp clack.
"Let’s keep moving," Silas ordered. "We don’t want to be caught in the open when the sun drops..."
The path dictated by the obsidian bird wound upward along the spine of a jagged black shale ridge, skirting the edges of several plunging drop-offs that vanished into lightless ravines.
For the next two miles, the march was eerily quiet but as they crested the ridge and looked down into the valley below, the terrain flattened into an unavoidable bottleneck.
To the west, the entire valley floor was completely submerged in that same crawling milky-white fog, bubbling like a witch’s cauldron between the jagged rock walls.
’Not only do I hate snow now... I hate the fog too.’
And directly blocking the only clear, frost-crusted path to the east was an enormous sprawling sunken grove.
The trees in this grove were colossal with their roots arching out of the permafrost like the ribcage of an ancient petrified leviathan.
But unlike the quiet forest behind them, the air within this grove was vibrating with the sounds of guttural snarls, clicking mandibles, and the wet tearing of flesh.
Tasmin dropped from her mount, melting into the shadows of a basalt boulder to scout ahead.
She returned thirty seconds later, stepping out of the rock face with a grave focused expression.

"Path is blocked," Tasmin reported quietly, crouching beside Valkyrie’s stirrup. "The western pass is completely saturated with that necrotic fog. We can’t push the wolves through that soup without getting swarmed by the leeches and the eastern grove... is an active monster den."
"What are we looking at?" Silas asked, his hand casually resting on his sword hilt.

"A mixed congregation," Tasmin detailed with crisp, professional efficiency. "Roughly thirty Hound monsters with spines, they’re Tier 2 pack hunters with hardened bone carapaces along their spines and pressurized acid bile. Anchoring the center are four Tier 3 brute abominations that are roughly twelve feet tall with a thick hide and crushing clubs for arms... Haah..."
"Roosting in the upper branches are at least a dozen giant mantises with cloaking carapaces."
Silas analyzed the layout in an instant.

’An unavoidable junction... The fog cuts off the bypass and the grove holds the throat of the pass. If we try to skirt the outer edge, we’ll trigger an ambush from the mantises while the hounds flank our mounts.’
He looked back at his detachment.
Aeliana was gripping her reins with her pointed ears pinned back, her silver-gold eyes wide as she listened to the numbers.
Beside her, Kadi was nervously rolling a handful of fine golden sand across her knuckles with her dark braids trembling slightly in the wind.
Silas looked over at Thor.
The towering God of Thunder was sitting cross-legged atop Titan’s back, her head tilted back, completely unbothered by the impending clash.

In her massive calloused hands, she was holding an enormous, two-foot-wide wooden trencher loaded with thick strips of cold roasted wild boar, heavily seasoned with crushed garlic and black pepper from Kaelia’s morning rations.
She picked up a three-pound slab of succulent meat, shoved half of it into her mouth with savage enthusiasm, and began chewing with loud blissful smacks of her lips.
CHOMP! CHOMP! GULP!

"Mmmph!" Thor grunted, wiping a smear of pork fat from her chin with the back of her forearm, her storm-blue eyes sparkling as she looked down at Silas. "Are we fighting now, Silas? Or are we waiting for the cold to tenderize them? Because this meat is magnificent, and I am not putting it down for a pack of overgrown mangy dogs..."
Silas stared at her for a flat unblinking second with a dry incredulous smirk tugging at his lips.
"Keep eating, Thor," Silas said dryly. "Try not to choke on the bone while we work."
"Gwahahaha! A true god never chokes on glorious meat!" Thor roared happily, ripping another massive bite from the shank with a wet tear.
Silas turned back toward the grove with confidence descending over his features like an iron mask.
"Detachment, dismount..." Silas commanded quietly.
CLINK!
The wolves were anchored to the rear beneath a low basalt overhang with their instincts keeping them silent and still.
Silas stepped into the open snow, drawing the golden longsword from his hip.
SHING!
Beside him, Aurelia drew her silver rapier, the pale holy flame igniting along the slender steel with a gentle fwoosh.
Morwenna drew Tidebringer, resting the broad spine casually against her shoulder pauldron.
Eluned stepped forward with a wooden staff lightly tapping the permafrost, sending a soft green pulse through the soil.

"Standard kill-zone protocols," Silas instructed, his blue eyes locking onto the dark silhouettes shifting between the massive tree trunks fifty yards ahead. "Tasmin, take the high branches and eradicate the mantises before they can dive on our flanks... Aurelia, lock down the hounds with Argent Flame. Elu, root the brutes... Morwenna and I will take the center. Aeli, Kadi... provide perimeter denial and protect the Princess."
"Understood!" the women chorused in disciplined whispers.
"Move."
BOOM!
Silas detonated into motion.
His boots pulverized the shale beneath him, launching him forward in a low sprint that closed thirty yards in a fraction of a second.
The golden longsword flared with sun-bright Gold Core mana, casting long, dancing shadows across the snowy grove.
"GRAAHHHHH!"
The sudden blinding radiance shattered the grove’s stillness.
From the hollows beneath the massive roots, thirty Spine-Hounds violently reacted.

Their mangy gray-skinned bodies were covered in thick jagged plates of external bone armor and their red eyes burned with feral fury as they snapped their jaws, venomous green bile dripping from their serrated teeth.
"WOOOOOOH!" a shriek tore through the air as the pack surged forward like a chaotic gray wave.
WHOOSH!

From the high frozen canopy forty feet overhead, three massive Chitin-Stalkers disengaged their camouflage, dropping from the branches like falling anvils with their eight-foot serrated scythe-limbs cocked to decapitate Silas from above.
SHSHSHK!
"Too slow," a raspy whisper echoed from the empty air above their heads.
Tasmin materialized out of the empty shadow of a high pine.
She rode the liquid darkness like a wave with her twin void-daggers spinning in reverse grips.
SLASH-SLASH-CRUNCH!
In an imperceptible blur of high-velocity assassination, Tasmin executed a mid-air double flip.

Her left dagger drove straight through the neck joint of the first mantis, severing its nerve cluster with a sickening squelch, while her right blade caught the second stalker dead between its faceted eyes.
KRA-CLATTER!

Before the third mantis could even swivel its triangular head, Tasmin wrapped her weighted void-chains around its thorax, yanked violently with her entire core, and hurled the multi-ton insect bodily into the trunk of a dead pine, shattering its carapace into greenish goo.
"Clear above!" Tasmin called out, landing lightly on a high branch with her amber eyes scanning for the next target.
Down on the ground, the wave of thirty Spine-Hounds was barely ten paces from Silas’s boots, their throats expanding as they prepared to unleash a coordinated barrage of pressurized acid.
FWOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A brilliant wall of pure silver-white fire erupted across the snow in a flawless sweeping arc.
Aurelia stepped forward with her silver rapier thrust forward in a crisp, immaculate lunge.
"Cleanse," Aurelia commanded softly, her golden eyes radiant with divine authority.
The Argent Flame burned and judged at the same time as the silver inferno swept through the front fifteen hounds like a holy scythe.
The moment the holy fire touched their corrupt mutated carapaces, the bone armor cracked like brittle glass and the acid in their gullets detonated internally with muffled popping thuds.
"SKREEEEEEE!"
The burning hounds shrieked, collapsing into piles of smoldering white ash before they could even cross the silver line.
From the rear, sitting atop Titan while happily gnawing on a succulent pork rib, Thor raised her flagon of ale, cheering with her mouth completely full.
"Gwahaha! Good form, Saintess! Crisped ’em right up! Needs a bit of garlic salt, though!"
"Focus on your breakfast, Thor! Let them work!" The Princess shouted from the rear guard, waving her wrench in exasperation.
GROOOOOOOOOOOO-RAAAAAAAAH!
A deafening bass-heavy roar tore through the center of the grove, shaking the snow from the high branches.
Crashing through the massive ironwood trunks, completely ignoring the burning hounds, came the four Grave-Gorgers.
The Tier 3 abominations were colossal like Tasmin had described... they were twelve feet of dense slate-gray muscle covered in weeping pustule-ridden tumors.
Their lower jaws split horizontally into three fleshy mandibles, and their massive club-like forearms were dense as solid bedrock, dragging along the snow with terrifying momentum.
The lead brute locked its milky, dead eyes onto Silas, raising both colossal arms high overhead, bringing them down in a brutal ground-shattering pile-driver.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The bedrock shattered and a shockwave of pulverized stone and jagged shale blasted outward in a thirty-foot cone.
’Really slow...’
Silas sidestepped horizontally with terrifying precision as the brute’s stone-hard fist cratered the earth barely an inch from his left shoulder with the pressurized wind whipping his coat.
VUUUM.
"Now my turn."
Silas’s right hand clenched around the hilt of his golden longsword. The dense reservoir of his Mythic Gold Core flared to life, channeling straight through his bicep.
KRA-FLASH!
He executed a clean upward diagonal slash.
The golden mythril blade carved through the air like a laser, meeting the brute’s twelve-inch-thick wrist joint.
CHOP-SPLAT!

The massive rock-hard forearm was severed cleanly off at the joint as a geyser of thick foul-smelling black blood erupted into the freezing air as the Grave-Gorger let out an ear-splitting agonizing bellow.
"Elu! Pin it!" Silas barked without looking back.
CRRR-WHIP!
From the frozen permafrost directly beneath the howling brute’s boots, four colossal emerald roots... thick as ancient oak trunks and wrapped in sharp jade-hard thorns erupted like striking serpents.
The roots wrapped tightly around the monster’s thick legs and torso, violently slamming it down onto its knees with a concussive crunch that cracked its kneecaps!
"Bound, my love!" Eluned’s melodic voice chimed from the perimeter, her green eyes glowing with playful dominance.
Eluned really enjoyed holding back, it was like bullying in a way especially when you knew you were stronger than them.
SWOOSH!
Silas vaulted off the pinned monster’s shoulder with his boots driving into the creature’s skull with enough force to fracture its bone plate.
BANG!
"GRAA—!"
He spun mid-air, bringing the golden blade down in a clean vertical execution strike.
SHING-CRACK!
The golden steel drove straight through the crown of the brute’s head, sinking to the hilt.

The mana of his Gold Core detonated internally, blowing the monster’s nervous system into smoking ash and Silas pulled the blade free with a wet sound, landing lightly in the snow, his eyes instantly tracking the remaining three brutes.
To his left, Morwenna was putting on a masterclass in brutal violence.
’No matter how hard I train... I doubt I’ll be able to reach her level in this life.’
The Pirate Queen was facing down two of the massive Grave-Gorgers simultaneously.

She stood completely relaxed with her feet planted in the red-stained snow and her dark hair whipping across her gray eyes as the first brute lunged forward, swinging its massive club-fist in a horizontal sweep meant to crush her torso.
FWOOM!
Morwenna leaned back by an eighth of an inch with the crushing fist whistling past her nose with the force of a wrecking ball.
"You aren’t even in the sea and you’re this slow?" Morwenna mocked coolly.
CLANG!
Tidebringer flashed.

sentences.text: Every single worm suspended in mid-air was instantly diced into dozens of neat uniform cross-sections.
The pressurized wind sheared clean through the overhanging branches, severing the worms still clinging to the bark before they could even coil their muscles to leap.
THUD-THUD-THUD-SPLAT!
A shower of diced rubbery meat and severed teeth rained down around the wolves’ paws, splashing harmlessly against the ambient mana barriers woven by Eluned’s roots.
Morwenna’s thumb pressed the crossguard back down with a sharp echoing clack.
"Sloppy little leeches," Morwenna muttered, leaning her elbow back against the pommel.
"Not even worth drawing the steel..."
Overhead, the obsidian bird let out an urgent shrieking rattle, banking hard to the right, cutting clean through a dense curtain of hanging moss to exit the suffocating hollow.
"Right flank!
Keep moving!" Silas barked.
The wolves bounded after the feathered guide, tearing through the moss curtain and bursting out of the low-lying ravine.
Almost instantaneously, the humid foul-smelling white vapor thinned out, replaced once more by the biting clean frost of the high ridges.
The obsidian bird fluttered down to a low-hanging rock shelf, perching on its talons and puffing out its dark chest, letting out an audible rattling wheeze of pure relief.
"Krrr-clack... squawk..."
Silas pulled Valkyrie to a halt, looking back over his shoulder at the pale swirling bank of fog they had just escaped.
"What was that about?" Silas asked, his brow furrowing as he looked up at the bird.
"Why the sudden panic over low-tier leeches?"

The bird launched into a frantic sequence of squawks, bobbing its head toward the mist, fluttering its wings in wide circular motions, and then stabbing its beak toward the dirt, mimicking a creeping spreading shadow.
Eluned listened intently, her emerald eyes tracking the bird’s erratic movements before turning to Silas with an informative nod.
"It is a phenomenon of the deep basin," Eluned explained, adjusting the ermine trim of her cloak.
"That fog is a manifestation of stagnant necrotic dampness that bleeds from the bogs.
Those worm creatures...
Corpse-Leeches do not exist as physical entities outside of that specific vapor.
They are born from the mist, they feed within the mist, and they dissolve when the mist dissipates.
If a monster lingers in the fog for more than a few minutes, the vapor thickens until a lot of them manifest simultaneously, suffocating prey beneath a living tide."
Silas raised his golden longsword, bringing the flat of the blade to eye level.
His blue eyes narrowed.
The thick black ichor that had coated the steel when he cleaved that first worm clean in two... was completely gone.
Not a smudge remained... hell not even a single stain either.
The polished mythril was immaculate, reflecting the gray sky like a flawless mirror.
’That’s very weird...’ Silas thought. ’A biological entity that exists only as an extension of an atmospheric anomaly...
If the blood doesn’t even leave physical residue, what kind of mutated core is anchoring this basin?’
Again and again, it just proved that the Umbral Basin was very dangerous.
He flicked the sword clean on instinct and slid it back into its scabbard with a crisp clack.
"Let’s keep moving," Silas ordered.
"We don’t want to be caught in the open when the sun drops..."
The path dictated by the obsidian bird wound upward along the spine of a jagged black shale ridge, skirting the edges of several plunging drop-offs that vanished into lightless ravines.
For the next two miles, the march was eerily quiet but as they crested the ridge and looked down into the valley below, the terrain flattened into an unavoidable bottleneck.
To the west, the entire valley floor was completely submerged in that same crawling milky-white fog, bubbling like a witch’s cauldron between the jagged rock walls.
’Not only do I hate snow now...
I hate the fog too.’
And directly blocking the only clear, frost-crusted path to the east was an enormous sprawling sunken grove.
The trees in this grove were colossal with their roots arching out of the permafrost like the ribcage of an ancient petrified leviathan.
But unlike the quiet forest behind them, the air within this grove was vibrating with the sounds of guttural snarls, clicking mandibles, and the wet tearing of flesh.
Tasmin dropped from her mount, melting into the shadows of a basalt boulder to scout ahead.
She returned thirty seconds later, stepping out of the rock face with a grave focused expression.
"Path is blocked," Tasmin reported quietly, crouching beside Valkyrie’s stirrup.
"The western pass is completely saturated with that necrotic fog.
We can’t push the wolves through that soup without getting swarmed by the leeches and the eastern grove... is an active monster den."
"What are we looking at?" Silas asked, his hand casually resting on his sword hilt.
"A mixed congregation," Tasmin detailed with crisp, professional efficiency.
"Roughly thirty Hound monsters with spines, they’re Tier 2 pack hunters with hardened bone carapaces along their spines and pressurized acid bile.
Anchoring the center are four Tier 3 brute abominations that are roughly twelve feet tall with a thick hide and crushing clubs for arms...
Haah..."
"Roosting in the upper branches are at least a dozen giant mantises with cloaking carapaces."
Silas analyzed the layout in an instant.
’An unavoidable junction...
The fog cuts off the bypass and the grove holds the throat of the pass.
If we try to skirt the outer edge, we’ll trigger an ambush from the mantises while the hounds flank our mounts.’
He looked back at his detachment.
Aeliana was gripping her reins with her pointed ears pinned back, her silver-gold eyes wide as she listened to the numbers.
Beside her, Kadi was nervously rolling a handful of fine golden sand across her knuckles with her dark braids trembling slightly in the wind.
Silas looked over at Thor.
The towering God of Thunder was sitting cross-legged atop Titan’s back, her head tilted back, completely unbothered by the impending clash.

In her massive calloused hands, she was holding an enormous, two-foot-wide wooden trencher loaded with thick strips of cold roasted wild boar, heavily seasoned with crushed garlic and black pepper from Kaelia’s morning rations.
She picked up a three-pound slab of succulent meat, shoved half of it into her mouth with savage enthusiasm, and began chewing with loud blissful smacks of her lips.
CHOMP!
CHOMP!
GULP!
"Mmmph!" Thor grunted, wiping a smear of pork fat from her chin with the back of her forearm, her storm-blue eyes sparkling as she looked down at Silas.
"Are we fighting now, Silas?
Or are we waiting for the cold to tenderize them?
Because this meat is magnificent, and I am not putting it down for a pack of overgrown mangy dogs..."
Silas stared at her for a flat unblinking second with a dry incredulous smirk tugging at his lips.
"Keep eating, Thor," Silas said dryly.
"Try not to choke on the bone while we work."
"Gwahahaha!
A true god never chokes on glorious meat!" Thor roared happily, ripping another massive bite from the shank with a wet tear.
Silas turned back toward the grove with confidence descending over his features like an iron mask.
"Detachment, dismount..." Silas commanded quietly.
CLINK!
The wolves were anchored to the rear beneath a low basalt overhang with their instincts keeping them silent and still.
Silas stepped into the open snow, drawing the golden longsword from his hip.
SHING!
Beside him, Aurelia drew her silver rapier, the pale holy flame igniting along the slender steel with a gentle fwoosh.
Morwenna drew Tidebringer, resting the broad spine casually against her shoulder pauldron.
Eluned stepped forward with a wooden staff lightly tapping the permafrost, sending a soft green pulse through the soil.
"Standard kill-zone protocols," Silas instructed, his blue eyes locking onto the dark silhouettes shifting between the massive tree trunks fifty yards ahead.
"Tasmin, take the high branches and eradicate the mantises before they can dive on our flanks...
Aurelia, lock down the hounds with Argent Flame.
Elu, root the brutes...
Morwenna and I will take the center.
Aeli, Kadi... provide perimeter denial and protect the Princess."
"Understood!" the women chorused in disciplined whispers.
"Move."
BOOM!
Silas detonated into motion.
His boots pulverized the shale beneath him, launching him forward in a low sprint that closed thirty yards in a fraction of a second.
The golden longsword flared with sun-bright Gold Core mana, casting long, dancing shadows across the snowy grove.
"GRAAHHHHH!"
The sudden blinding radiance shattered the grove’s stillness.
From the hollows beneath the massive roots, thirty Spine-Hounds violently reacted.

Their mangy gray-skinned bodies were covered in thick jagged plates of external bone armor and their red eyes burned with feral fury as they snapped their jaws, venomous green bile dripping from their serrated teeth.
"WOOOOOOH!" a shriek tore through the air as the pack surged forward like a chaotic gray wave.
WHOOSH!

From the high frozen canopy forty feet overhead, three massive Chitin-Stalkers disengaged their camouflage, dropping from the branches like falling anvils with their eight-foot serrated scythe-limbs cocked to decapitate Silas from above.
SHSHSHK!
"Too slow," a raspy whisper echoed from the empty air above their heads.
Tasmin materialized out of the empty shadow of a high pine.
She rode the liquid darkness like a wave with her twin void-daggers spinning in reverse grips.
SLASH-SLASH-CRUNCH!
In an imperceptible blur of high-velocity assassination, Tasmin executed a mid-air double flip.

Her left dagger drove straight through the neck joint of the first mantis, severing its nerve cluster with a sickening squelch, while her right blade caught the second stalker dead between its faceted eyes.
KRA-CLATTER!

Before the third mantis could even swivel its triangular head, Tasmin wrapped her weighted void-chains around its thorax, yanked violently with her entire core, and hurled the multi-ton insect bodily into the trunk of a dead pine, shattering its carapace into greenish goo.
"Clear above!" Tasmin called out, landing lightly on a high branch with her amber eyes scanning for the next target.
Down on the ground, the wave of thirty Spine-Hounds was barely ten paces from Silas’s boots, their throats expanding as they prepared to unleash a coordinated barrage of pressurized acid.
FWOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A brilliant wall of pure silver-white fire erupted across the snow in a flawless sweeping arc.
Aurelia stepped forward with her silver rapier thrust forward in a crisp, immaculate lunge.
"Cleanse," Aurelia commanded softly, her golden eyes radiant with divine authority.
The Argent Flame burned and judged at the same time as the silver inferno swept through the front fifteen hounds like a holy scythe.
The moment the holy fire touched their corrupt mutated carapaces, the bone armor cracked like brittle glass and the acid in their gullets detonated internally with muffled popping thuds.
"SKREEEEEEE!"
The burning hounds shrieked, collapsing into piles of smoldering white ash before they could even cross the silver line.
From the rear, sitting atop Titan while happily gnawing on a succulent pork rib, Thor raised her flagon of ale, cheering with her mouth completely full.
"Gwahaha!
Good form, Saintess!
Crisped ’em right up!
Needs a bit of garlic salt, though!"
"Focus on your breakfast, Thor!
Let them work!" The Princess shouted from the rear guard, waving her wrench in exasperation.
GROOOOOOOOOOOO-RAAAAAAAAH!
A deafening bass-heavy roar tore through the center of the grove, shaking the snow from the high branches.
Crashing through the massive ironwood trunks, completely ignoring the burning hounds, came the four Grave-Gorgers.
The Tier 3 abominations were colossal like Tasmin had described... they were twelve feet of dense slate-gray muscle covered in weeping pustule-ridden tumors.
Their lower jaws split horizontally into three fleshy mandibles, and their massive club-like forearms were dense as solid bedrock, dragging along the snow with terrifying momentum.
The lead brute locked its milky, dead eyes onto Silas, raising both colossal arms high overhead, bringing them down in a brutal ground-shattering pile-driver.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The bedrock shattered and a shockwave of pulverized stone and jagged shale blasted outward in a thirty-foot cone.
’Really slow...’
Silas sidestepped horizontally with terrifying precision as the brute’s stone-hard fist cratered the earth barely an inch from his left shoulder with the pressurized wind whipping his coat.
VUUUM.
"Now my turn."
Silas’s right hand clenched around the hilt of his golden longsword.
The dense reservoir of his Mythic Gold Core flared to life, channeling straight through his bicep.
KRA-FLASH!
He executed a clean upward diagonal slash.
The golden mythril blade carved through the air like a laser, meeting the brute’s twelve-inch-thick wrist joint.
CHOP-SPLAT!

The massive rock-hard forearm was severed cleanly off at the joint as a geyser of thick foul-smelling black blood erupted into the freezing air as the Grave-Gorger let out an ear-splitting agonizing bellow.
"Elu!
Pin it!" Silas barked without looking back.
CRRR-WHIP!
From the frozen permafrost directly beneath the howling brute’s boots, four colossal emerald roots... thick as ancient oak trunks and wrapped in sharp jade-hard thorns erupted like striking serpents.
The roots wrapped tightly around the monster’s thick legs and torso, violently slamming it down onto its knees with a concussive crunch that cracked its kneecaps!
"Bound, my love!" Eluned’s melodic voice chimed from the perimeter, her green eyes glowing with playful dominance.
Eluned really enjoyed holding back, it was like bullying in a way especially when you knew you were stronger than them.
SWOOSH!
Silas vaulted off the pinned monster’s shoulder with his boots driving into the creature’s skull with enough force to fracture its bone plate.
BANG!
"GRAA—!"
He spun mid-air, bringing the golden blade down in a clean vertical execution strike.
SHING-CRACK!
The golden steel drove straight through the crown of the brute’s head, sinking to the hilt.

The mana of his Gold Core detonated internally, blowing the monster’s nervous system into smoking ash and Silas pulled the blade free with a wet sound, landing lightly in the snow, his eyes instantly tracking the remaining three brutes.
To his left, Morwenna was putting on a masterclass in brutal violence.
’No matter how hard I train...
I doubt I’ll be able to reach her level in this life.’

FWOOM!
Morwenna leaned back by an eighth of an inch with the crushing fist whistling past her nose with the force of a wrecking ball.
"You aren’t even in the sea and you’re this slow?" Morwenna mocked coolly.
CLANG!
Tidebringer flashed.

chapters.title: Chapter 505: Operation: Save The Beast Goddess [III]
paragraphs: Morwenna didn’t block the attack... she parried the brute’s elbow at an oblique angle, deflecting the multi-ton energy straight into the dirt as the brute overextended, tumbling forward onto one knee.
Morwenna pivoted on her heel with her body twisting like a coiled spring.
SLASH-KRA-CHOP!
Her Tidebringer carved through the back of the monster’s neck like a heated cleaver through butter.
The decapitated head rolled across the permafrost, spraying black ichor in a wide arc before the body even realized it was dead.
"I’m sorry Tide, I have to use you against low-tier mobs... They aren’t even worthy of your blade."

Well it was not like she even had a choice in the matter, it was either that or using another weapon and apart from chains, Tidebringer didn’t really like it when she was using another sword especially when she was being wielded.
’It’s just a sword with a fucking attitude issue...’
The third brute roared, lunging at Morwenna’s blind spot—
FZZZZZZT!
"Hold right there, ugly!" Kadi’s sharp voice rang out.

A roaring torrent of dense pressurized golden sand erupted from Kadi’s outstretched palms, wrapping around the charging brute’s face like a suffocating mask, blinding its milky eyes and ripping through its soft tissues with microscopic abrasive fury.
"GAH?!"
The brute stumbled, swinging blindly—
FLASH!
Aeliana appeared out of thin air directly beside the blinded beast.
The high-elf secretary’s silver-gold eyes were wide with razor-sharp focus as she clapped her slender hands together, releasing a spatial shear right at the monster’s ankle.
CRACK-POP!
The space around the joint violently twisted, snapping the thick leg bone in half like a dry twig.
"GRAHHHHHH!"
The brute crashed into the snow with an earth-shattering thud, howling in agony; however Morwenna walked up calmly and stepped onto the struggling monster’s chest.
"Whining on and on... Your kind really makes me sick."
She drove Tidebringer straight down through its throat with a sickening final squelch.
"And... That’s the last of them." Morwenna smirked, giving her blade a crisp downward flick that flung the black blood cleanly into the snowdrifts.
Up in the trees, the final Chitin-Stalker was attempting to scuttle away through the high branches...
THWIP!
A single, silver-fletched arrow whistled through the freezing air, driven by the Princess’s focused draw.

The arrow struck the mantis dead-center through its jointed wing-casing, pinning it to the trunk as Tasmin dropped down from above a fraction of a second later, her void-dagger severing its head with a clean twist.
Within less than three minutes, the entire grove was silent once more.
Thirty Spine-Hounds, four massive Grave-Gorgers, and a dozen Chitin-Stalkers lay dead with their mutilated corpses littering the red-stained snow.
Back at the edge of the grove, sitting tall atop Titan with grease glistening on her fingers, Thor tossed the clean stripped marrow bone over her shoulder with a satisfied cavern-shaking sigh.
THUMP.

"Ah! That was a splendid show!" Thor declared, wiping her mouth with the back of her sleeve with her belly thoroughly full. "Good footwork, pirate! Nice precision, little elf but you took too long on the big ones! A good lightning bolt would have turned them all into fertilizer before the ale lost its chill!"
"Shut your pie-hole, giantess!" Morwenna snapped back, though her chest was heaving with an adrenaline-fueled smirk as she wiped sweat from her brow. "Some of us actually enjoy the physical workout!"
Silas walked into the center of the grove with his eyes scanning the carnage with calm efficiency as he flicked his longsword clean, sheathing it with a sharp clack.
’That was a clean execution... The team is as good as I thought.’
He looked up at the sky and sighed.
"Haah..."
Gnarled charcoal-black boughs knit together above their heads like a petrified ribcage, blotting out whatever pale daylight managed to filter down through the basin’s bruising sky.
High above, fine flakes of dry mountain snow still sifted through the tangled needles, drifting down in lazy spirals to dust the dark wool of his cloak.
Behind him, the low wet gurgle of dying flesh finally ceased as the last Spine-Hound went limp against the permafrost with its black blood freezing into brittle glassy crusts over the shale.

’We dealt with them cleanly enough,’ Silas thought, resting his gloved palm against the pommel of his sheathed longsword. ’But if every mile in this northern corridor throws a dozen ambush predators across our vector, we’re going to burn half our operational window just scraping marrow off our boots...’
His primary concern wasn’t the physical threat.
Between Thor’s raw devastation, Eluned’s power, Morwenna’s blade, and Aurelia’s cleansing silver fire, these low-tier roaming packs were little more than minor terrain friction.
The true enemy was time lost, momentum bled away, and the relentless creep of the sub-zero basin chill grinding down the mounts.
He wanted this expedition wrapped up speedily.
Every extra hour spent navigating these unmapped gorges was an hour the territory ran without him.
Suddenly, an involuntary shudder traveled up the base of Silas’s neck.
It was not cold.
His Gold Core hummed like a furnace within his chest, washing through his pathways with a golden warmth.
The chill was from a thought.
’Leaving Brida in charge of the entire territory...’
Silas rubbed the bridge of his nose with an uneasy grimace tightening the corners of his mouth.
At dawn, before they crossed the perimeter trench, the decision had seemed impeccably rational.

Brida possessed the undisputed respect of everyone in the territory, she had the operational instincts of a veteran, an unshakeable sense of territorial pride, and an iron grip on the defensive rotations.
Behind Tasmin, she was the natural choice to hold the territory so why did the back of his scalp itch with pure dread?

’Was that actually a terrible idea?’ Silas mused, his eyes narrowing as he stared blankly at the snow. ’Brida is disciplined when steel is clashing but give her twenty-four hours of unsupervised administrative command, an open run of the Keep, and the keys to the master quarters...’
A vivid horrifying mental image flashed through his mind...

Silas could picture himself returning through the southern pass to find the whole Barracks repurposed into a brewery, all of the warriors wrestling in grease in the main courtyard, and the Lord’s private chambers thoroughly ransacked with his spare tunics gathered into an unholy nesting pile.

’I doubt she would burn the walls down,’ Silas reasoned, though the thought brought remarkably little comfort. ’She loves the Keep too much for that but she might turn the residency into a den of sin before I make it back to the gates.’
A sudden fierce urgency took root in his chest.
They needed to find this frozen Goddess, crack the ice, and march south before Brida had time to organize a coup over his linen closet.

"Form up on the center line!" Silas called out, his deep voice slicing through the quiet grove with crisp authority. "Check the wolves’ cinches, clear the gore from your stirrups, and tighten the spacing... We’re moving."
"Understood, my Lord," Tasmin answered from the edge of the clearing.
She was already back in her saddle, her twin void-daggers wiped clean and locked into their thigh holsters with a muffled click.
Overhead, perched on the low branch of a weeping cedar, the obsidian bird let out an impatient metallic squawk.

It snapped its scythe-curved beak, shook the frost from its dark crystalline feathers, and launched into the air with three sharp flaps, banking smoothly toward a narrow ascending rocky ravine that cut northward through the cliffs.
"Bird’s got the scent," Morwenna noted from the flank as Valkyrie arrived.
The Pirate Queen reached up, pushing a stray lock of jet-black hair behind her ear, her cool gray eyes tracking the bird’s flight path through the dense canopy.
Her hand rested comfortably on the pommel of Tidebringer as her posture was fluid despite the freezing squall.
"Looks like it’s funneling us along the high shelf, Captain. Flatter footing, at least..."
"Let’s make use of it," Silas said, nudging Valkyrie forward.
The eight Blessed Wolves fell into an offset column with their broad paws pounding rhythmically against the shale.
For the next mile, the terrain grew increasingly severe.
The twisted pine forest thinned out, replaced by towering walls of black basalt that rose vertically on either side, pinching the trail into a deep corridor of stone and ancient ice.
Yet, as they pressed deeper into the corridor, the light began to fail with alarming speed.
It was not the natural twilight of dusk.
From the cracks between the basalt slabs, that same milky-white opaque fog they had skirted earlier was beginning to pool anew.
It crept out of the fissures in thick lazy ribbons, curling around the wolves’ hocks like freezing water.
With every hundred yards they gained, the ribbons thickened, fusing together into a dense soupy bank that clung to the permafrost, rising rapidly toward their waists.
High above, the obsidian bird suddenly halted its forward glide.

It fluttered erratically, diving down from the mist-shrouded rocks to land heavily upon the Princess’s leather pauldron with its talons digging into the reinforcement as it issued a series of sharp distressed clicks.
"KRR-CLIK! Squawk! Krrr-caw!"
Eluned, riding parallel to Silas, tilted her head.
Her long, emerald-green braid swayed over her shoulder as her eyes flared with a faint luminescence, attuning to the creature’s panicked vibrations.
"Silas," Eluned spoke, her voice filled with seriousness. "The monster says we must stop our advance immediately."
Silas pulled on Valkyrie’s reins, bringing the pack to a smooth halt. "What is it? A territorial pack ahead?"

"The fog," Eluned explained, gesturing with her wooden staff toward the white vapor rapidly rising around their thighs. "According to the bird’s instincts, the necrotic fog in this specific sector operates on an ebb and flow. At this hour, it surges to its peak saturation point across the entire low-lying basin... If we remain exposed on this trail when the peak arrives, the fog will completely blind us, and the boundary will become entirely impassable. It insists we locate an enclosed cavern... something deep within the cliffside and seal the threshold completely so none of this vapor can seep inside."
’I really couldn’t have thought that a Bird would be that smart...’

She turned her gaze up toward the jagged rock walls. "Once the peak crests and burns itself out through the valley vents, the air will clear for several hours so we will have an open unobstructed window to ride straight to the trench without harassment."
Silas sighed, a heavy plume of gray mist puffing into the chill. "Just what we needed. Stalled by bad weather..."
"Why bother hiding in a hole like frightened mice?!"
Thor’s booming voice shattered the quiet of the gorge.
The God of Thunder shifted atop Titan’s broad back, crossing her thick sculpted arms over her chest.
Her storm-blue eyes flashed with restless combative irritation as she glared down at the creeping white mist.

"We are warriors, Silas!" Thor scoffed, her golden locks whipping in the draft. "We have the strength of the earth, the fury of the skies, and blades that can sever mountains! If the fog is thick, I will summon a gale and blow it back to whatever pit spawned it! Why waste time shivering in a cold burrow when we could simply cut through the entire valley?!"
From her saddle between Aurelia and Tasmin, the Princess shrank slightly into the deep wool lining of her cloak.
Her small hands, clad in thick sheepskin gloves, were trembling from the unrelenting sub-zero draft that howled down the canyon.
She had spent the entire morning maintaining a proud stoic royal facade, desperate to prove that she wasn’t a fragile liability to the girls but the truth was simple...
Her limbs were stiff as iron, her ears were burning with frost-nip, and the violent clash in the grove had drained the last remnants of her adrenaline.
She looked up at Thor’s towering defiant silhouette.

’If Thor insists on marching, Lord Silas will keep pushing the line,’ the Princess thought, her mind working frantically through courtly negotiation tactics. ’I need to redirect her but you cannot reason with a storm with logic... you have to offer it a feast.’
The Princess cleared her throat softly, pulling her fur mantle tighter around her slender neck as she leaned toward the thunder deity.

"Lady Thor..." the Princess began, her azure eyes widening with deliberate innocent pleading. "I... I agree that you could effortlessly blow this entire mountain away with your divine thunder. Truly, none of these monsters could stand against you for an instant."
Thor puffed her broad chest out, a proud satisfied grin instantly breaking across her face.
"Gwahahaha! You see, Silas? The little royal knows true majesty when she sees it!"

"However," the Princess continued smoothly, her voice sweet as honey, "if we take shelter in a cavern now, as Lady Eluned suggests... we would finally have the time to sit by a warm hearth and eat properly."
Thor’s grin hitched as her ears twitched.
"Eat... properly?" Thor echoed, her voice dropping down a bit as she was suddenly intensely curious.

"Yes," the Princess nodded, leaning into the trap. "Remember the three massive containers Lady Kaelia packed for Lord Silas this morning? The roasted mountain venison sealed in rich tallow? The thick, herb-crusted loin slices? The warm concentrated bone broth? If we push through the storm, we cannot stop to open the containers... The food will freeze into blocks of ice while we ride but inside a warm cavern... we can lay out the platters, stoke a fire, and eat until our bellies are completely full."

The brute stumbled, swinging blindly—
FLASH!
Aeliana appeared out of thin air directly beside the blinded beast.
The high-elf secretary’s silver-gold eyes were wide with razor-sharp focus as she clapped her slender hands together, releasing a spatial shear right at the monster’s ankle.
CRACK-POP!
The space around the joint violently twisted, snapping the thick leg bone in half like a dry twig.
"GRAHHHHHH!"
The brute crashed into the snow with an earth-shattering thud, howling in agony; however Morwenna walked up calmly and stepped onto the struggling monster’s chest.
"Whining on and on...
Your kind really makes me sick."
She drove Tidebringer straight down through its throat with a sickening final squelch.
"And...
That’s the last of them." Morwenna smirked, giving her blade a crisp downward flick that flung the black blood cleanly into the snowdrifts.
Up in the trees, the final Chitin-Stalker was attempting to scuttle away through the high branches...
THWIP!
A single, silver-fletched arrow whistled through the freezing air, driven by the Princess’s focused draw.

The arrow struck the mantis dead-center through its jointed wing-casing, pinning it to the trunk as Tasmin dropped down from above a fraction of a second later, her void-dagger severing its head with a clean twist.
Within less than three minutes, the entire grove was silent once more.
Thirty Spine-Hounds, four massive Grave-Gorgers, and a dozen Chitin-Stalkers lay dead with their mutilated corpses littering the red-stained snow.
Back at the edge of the grove, sitting tall atop Titan with grease glistening on her fingers, Thor tossed the clean stripped marrow bone over her shoulder with a satisfied cavern-shaking sigh.
THUMP.
"Ah!
That was a splendid show!" Thor declared, wiping her mouth with the back of her sleeve with her belly thoroughly full.
"Good footwork, pirate!
Nice precision, little elf but you took too long on the big ones!
A good lightning bolt would have turned them all into fertilizer before the ale lost its chill!"
"Shut your pie-hole, giantess!" Morwenna snapped back, though her chest was heaving with an adrenaline-fueled smirk as she wiped sweat from her brow.
"Some of us actually enjoy the physical workout!"
Silas walked into the center of the grove with his eyes scanning the carnage with calm efficiency as he flicked his longsword clean, sheathing it with a sharp clack.
’That was a clean execution...
The team is as good as I thought.’
He looked up at the sky and sighed.
"Haah..."
Gnarled charcoal-black boughs knit together above their heads like a petrified ribcage, blotting out whatever pale daylight managed to filter down through the basin’s bruising sky.
High above, fine flakes of dry mountain snow still sifted through the tangled needles, drifting down in lazy spirals to dust the dark wool of his cloak.
Behind him, the low wet gurgle of dying flesh finally ceased as the last Spine-Hound went limp against the permafrost with its black blood freezing into brittle glassy crusts over the shale.

’We dealt with them cleanly enough,’ Silas thought, resting his gloved palm against the pommel of his sheathed longsword. ’But if every mile in this northern corridor throws a dozen ambush predators across our vector, we’re going to burn half our operational window just scraping marrow off our boots...’
His primary concern wasn’t the physical threat.
Between Thor’s raw devastation, Eluned’s power, Morwenna’s blade, and Aurelia’s cleansing silver fire, these low-tier roaming packs were little more than minor terrain friction.
The true enemy was time lost, momentum bled away, and the relentless creep of the sub-zero basin chill grinding down the mounts.
He wanted this expedition wrapped up speedily.
Every extra hour spent navigating these unmapped gorges was an hour the territory ran without him.
Suddenly, an involuntary shudder traveled up the base of Silas’s neck.
It was not cold.
His Gold Core hummed like a furnace within his chest, washing through his pathways with a golden warmth.
The chill was from a thought.
’Leaving Brida in charge of the entire territory...’
Silas rubbed the bridge of his nose with an uneasy grimace tightening the corners of his mouth.
At dawn, before they crossed the perimeter trench, the decision had seemed impeccably rational.

Brida possessed the undisputed respect of everyone in the territory, she had the operational instincts of a veteran, an unshakeable sense of territorial pride, and an iron grip on the defensive rotations.
Behind Tasmin, she was the natural choice to hold the territory so why did the back of his scalp itch with pure dread?

’Was that actually a terrible idea?’ Silas mused, his eyes narrowing as he stared blankly at the snow. ’Brida is disciplined when steel is clashing but give her twenty-four hours of unsupervised administrative command, an open run of the Keep, and the keys to the master quarters...’
A vivid horrifying mental image flashed through his mind...

Silas could picture himself returning through the southern pass to find the whole Barracks repurposed into a brewery, all of the warriors wrestling in grease in the main courtyard, and the Lord’s private chambers thoroughly ransacked with his spare tunics gathered into an unholy nesting pile.

’I doubt she would burn the walls down,’ Silas reasoned, though the thought brought remarkably little comfort. ’She loves the Keep too much for that but she might turn the residency into a den of sin before I make it back to the gates.’
A sudden fierce urgency took root in his chest.
They needed to find this frozen Goddess, crack the ice, and march south before Brida had time to organize a coup over his linen closet.
"Form up on the center line!" Silas called out, his deep voice slicing through the quiet grove with crisp authority.
"Check the wolves’ cinches, clear the gore from your stirrups, and tighten the spacing...
We’re moving."
"Understood, my Lord," Tasmin answered from the edge of the clearing.
She was already back in her saddle, her twin void-daggers wiped clean and locked into their thigh holsters with a muffled click.
Overhead, perched on the low branch of a weeping cedar, the obsidian bird let out an impatient metallic squawk.

It snapped its scythe-curved beak, shook the frost from its dark crystalline feathers, and launched into the air with three sharp flaps, banking smoothly toward a narrow ascending rocky ravine that cut northward through the cliffs.
"Bird’s got the scent," Morwenna noted from the flank as Valkyrie arrived.
The Pirate Queen reached up, pushing a stray lock of jet-black hair behind her ear, her cool gray eyes tracking the bird’s flight path through the dense canopy.
Her hand rested comfortably on the pommel of Tidebringer as her posture was fluid despite the freezing squall.
"Looks like it’s funneling us along the high shelf, Captain.
Flatter footing, at least..."
"Let’s make use of it," Silas said, nudging Valkyrie forward.
The eight Blessed Wolves fell into an offset column with their broad paws pounding rhythmically against the shale.
For the next mile, the terrain grew increasingly severe.
The twisted pine forest thinned out, replaced by towering walls of black basalt that rose vertically on either side, pinching the trail into a deep corridor of stone and ancient ice.
Yet, as they pressed deeper into the corridor, the light began to fail with alarming speed.
It was not the natural twilight of dusk.
From the cracks between the basalt slabs, that same milky-white opaque fog they had skirted earlier was beginning to pool anew.
It crept out of the fissures in thick lazy ribbons, curling around the wolves’ hocks like freezing water.
With every hundred yards they gained, the ribbons thickened, fusing together into a dense soupy bank that clung to the permafrost, rising rapidly toward their waists.
High above, the obsidian bird suddenly halted its forward glide.

It fluttered erratically, diving down from the mist-shrouded rocks to land heavily upon the Princess’s leather pauldron with its talons digging into the reinforcement as it issued a series of sharp distressed clicks.
"KRR-CLIK!
Squawk!
Krrr-caw!"
Eluned, riding parallel to Silas, tilted her head.
Her long, emerald-green braid swayed over her shoulder as her eyes flared with a faint luminescence, attuning to the creature’s panicked vibrations.
"Silas," Eluned spoke, her voice filled with seriousness.
"The monster says we must stop our advance immediately."
Silas pulled on Valkyrie’s reins, bringing the pack to a smooth halt.
"What is it?
A territorial pack ahead?"
"The fog," Eluned explained, gesturing with her wooden staff toward the white vapor rapidly rising around their thighs.
"According to the bird’s instincts, the necrotic fog in this specific sector operates on an ebb and flow.
At this hour, it surges to its peak saturation point across the entire low-lying basin...
If we remain exposed on this trail when the peak arrives, the fog will completely blind us, and the boundary will become entirely impassable.
It insists we locate an enclosed cavern... something deep within the cliffside and seal the threshold completely so none of this vapor can seep inside."
’I really couldn’t have thought that a Bird would be that smart...’
She turned her gaze up toward the jagged rock walls.

"Once the peak crests and burns itself out through the valley vents, the air will clear for several hours so we will have an open unobstructed window to ride straight to the trench without harassment."
Silas sighed, a heavy plume of gray mist puffing into the chill.
"Just what we needed.
Stalled by bad weather..."
"Why bother hiding in a hole like frightened mice?!"
Thor’s booming voice shattered the quiet of the gorge.
The God of Thunder shifted atop Titan’s broad back, crossing her thick sculpted arms over her chest.
Her storm-blue eyes flashed with restless combative irritation as she glared down at the creeping white mist.
"We are warriors, Silas!" Thor scoffed, her golden locks whipping in the draft.
"We have the strength of the earth, the fury of the skies, and blades that can sever mountains!
If the fog is thick, I will summon a gale and blow it back to whatever pit spawned it!
Why waste time shivering in a cold burrow when we could simply cut through the entire valley?!"
From her saddle between Aurelia and Tasmin, the Princess shrank slightly into the deep wool lining of her cloak.
Her small hands, clad in thick sheepskin gloves, were trembling from the unrelenting sub-zero draft that howled down the canyon.
She had spent the entire morning maintaining a proud stoic royal facade, desperate to prove that she wasn’t a fragile liability to the girls but the truth was simple...
Her limbs were stiff as iron, her ears were burning with frost-nip, and the violent clash in the grove had drained the last remnants of her adrenaline.
She looked up at Thor’s towering defiant silhouette.

’If Thor insists on marching, Lord Silas will keep pushing the line,’ the Princess thought, her mind working frantically through courtly negotiation tactics. ’I need to redirect her but you cannot reason with a storm with logic... you have to offer it a feast.’
The Princess cleared her throat softly, pulling her fur mantle tighter around her slender neck as she leaned toward the thunder deity.
"Lady Thor..." the Princess began, her azure eyes widening with deliberate innocent pleading.
I agree that you could effortlessly blow this entire mountain away with your divine thunder.
Truly, none of these monsters could stand against you for an instant."
Thor puffed her broad chest out, a proud satisfied grin instantly breaking across her face.
"Gwahahaha!
You see, Silas?
The little royal knows true majesty when she sees it!"

"However," the Princess continued smoothly, her voice sweet as honey, "if we take shelter in a cavern now, as Lady Eluned suggests... we would finally have the time to sit by a warm hearth and eat properly."
Thor’s grin hitched as her ears twitched.
"Eat... properly?" Thor echoed, her voice dropping down a bit as she was suddenly intensely curious.
"Yes," the Princess nodded, leaning into the trap.
"Remember the three massive containers Lady Kaelia packed for Lord Silas this morning?
The roasted mountain venison sealed in rich tallow?
The thick, herb-crusted loin slices?
The warm concentrated bone broth?
If we push through the storm, we cannot stop to open the containers...
The food will freeze into blocks of ice while we ride but inside a warm cavern... we can lay out the platters, stoke a fire, and eat until our bellies are completely full."

chapters.title: Chapter 506: Kadi’s Time To Shine
paragraphs: Thor stared at the young woman for three agonizing seconds.
Her jaw moved slowly and an audible wet swallow echoed from her throat as she visualized three pounds of glistening, peppered venison tenderloin.

"Well..." Thor grumbled, abruptly uncrossing her arms and scratching the back of her neck with an exaggerated thoughtful scowl. "When you frame it with such strategic foresight... a tactician must know when to conserve fuel. Sitting in a dark cave is an insult to the open sky, but starving a warrior’s stomach is an insult to the cosmos! Silas! I have reconsidered! We take the cave!"
Silas stared at the Princess, an amused impressed smirk tugging at his lips.
The royal woman caught his glance and offered him a tiny conspiratorial wink beneath the rim of her fur hood.
’Clever girl,’ Silas thought. ’She handled that better than the others would have...’
SH-SH-SHK!
A sharp scuttling sound scraped across the loose scree twenty paces up the eastern slope.
From behind a jagged basalt tooth, a mutated six-legged crawler with its pale blind face split into a wet ring of needle-like teeth lunged down the rock face, drawn by the sound of voices.
FZZZZZZT!
Kadi didn’t even turn her shoulders.
The Sand Mage simply flicked her right wrist toward the slope.
From the leather pouches at her hip, a dense pressurized stream of golden mineral sand erupted like high-velocity buckshot.
The sand whipped through the freezing air with the deafening shriek of a drill.
’When doing long range like this... the sand with me is the best.’ She thought.
KRA-CH-CH-CH-CH-PONG!

The abrasive torrent struck the leaping aberration dead in the chest and the hyper-concentrated grit acted like an industrial water-jet cutter, grinding through the creature’s chitin, muscle, and spinal column in less than half a second.
SPLAT!
The pulverized remnants of the beast splashed across the dark rock, dead before the pieces hit the snow.
Kadi closed her fist, drawing the red-stained sand back toward her waist, letting it settle into the pouches with a soft metallic rustle.
Her dark braids swayed as she exhaled a long shaky breath with her knuckles white against her reins.
"I agree with the rest," Kadi murmured, her voice tight with lingering strain.
Her dark eyes were tired with dark circles bruising the skin beneath them.
"We’ve been on high alert since dawn, my Lord. Even an hour to catch our breath and reset our wards will keep our reflexes from slipping..."
From behind them, Aeliana sat stiffly in her saddle.
The high-elf secretary adjusted the silver wire-rimmed spectacles resting on her nose, clearing her throat with an official administrative air.

"Lord Silas," Aeliana began, pulling a small book from her satchel to review their projected march routes, "if we adhere strictly to the logistical projections I drafted, pausing for a forty-five-minute interval will depress our average velocity by sixteen percent... We are currently two hours ahead of the base schedule so if we push through the boundary now, we could theoretically reach the descent threshold before the midnight—"
GURRRRRR-GL-GL-GL-GL!
A loud unladylike rumble tore from Aeliana’s stomach.
The sound was so clear that it echoed off the narrow canyon walls like a distant landslide.
Aeliana froze.

Her sentence died instantly on her tongue and then slowly, a brilliant wave of pure crimson flooded across the high-elf’s pale cheeks, burning all the way up to the slender delicate tips of her long pointed ears.
She clamped both hands over her lower abdomen, shrinking into the collar of her white shirt as her eyes darted desperately down at the wolf’s mane.
"I... that was..." Aeliana stammered, her voice dropping into a humiliated, microscopic squeak. "...an involuntary sound... Lord Silas..."
A muffled snicker broke out from the line.
"Sounds like your stomach wants some roast pork, ears," Morwenna teased, leaning back in her saddle with a wide toothy grin.

"I can easily sustain the march for another twelve hours without caloric intake!" Morwenna declared, turning her gray eyes toward Silas with sharp arrogant pride. "A True woman doesn’t whine about a growling belly... My Tidebringer and I can carve a clean corridor straight through this mist right now, Captain. Nobody protects your blind spots better than me."

"Oh, please," Eluned scoffed melodiously from Silas’s other side, rolling her emerald eyes with dramatic disdain. "A pirate’s crude iron is hardly a substitute for the living primordial power of the World Tree. One word from me, and the deep roots will form a highway that shields our Lord from every foul creature in this trench... If anyone is securing his safety, barnacle, it is his divine wife."

"Wife?!" Morwenna bristled, her jaw tightening as she gripped Tidebringer’s hilt. "Just because you have sex doesn’t mean you’re his wife, you overgrown shrub! Don’t flatter yourself! I was cutting down leviathans while you were still fertilizing moss!"
"Enough," Silas commanded, raising a single hand to cut through the rising storm of divine and nautical bickering.
Both women clicked their tongues, turning their faces in opposite directions with identical childish scowls.
Silas looked past them with his blue eyes settling on the dark undulating wall of white mist gathering at the end of the gorge.
He had been caught in that vapor once before.
"Haah..."
He remembered the sickening weightless horror of it... the way the Corpse-Leeches manifested from empty air, the way the sound died and the absence of physical logic.
If they were swallowed by that fog at its peak, it wouldn’t just be low-tier leeches dropping from the sky.

’I have a terrible feeling about that mist,’ Silas thought, his fingers tightening against Valkyrie’s reins. ’Pushing forward out of stubborn pride is how entire strike teams end up buried under the permafrost.’

"We rest," Silas decreed firmly, leaving zero room for debate. "We find an elevated cavern, dig in, seal the threshold, and wait for this surge to clear. Tasmin, scout the eastern wall and find us an opening that won’t collapse under a strike."

"Already spotted one, my Lord," Tasmin replied, pointing her dagger toward an elevated basalt shelf forty feet above the gorge floor. "Two hundred yards up. A dry fissure mouth with a deep narrow access point and defensible choke, it’s quite perfect for a squad hold."
"Lead the way."
The ascent to the elevated cavern shelf was brutal.

The Blessed Wolves had to dig their iron-shod claws into the icy shale, scrambling up the steep scree slope in a tight disciplined zig-zag pattern while the white fog continued its relentless climb up the canyon floor behind them.
When they crested the shelf, the cavern opening loomed before them.
It was a jagged irregular tear in the solid basalt face, roughly twelve feet wide and fifteen feet high.
The interior was completely pitch-black, exhaling a faint unnatural smell that carried the distinct foul odor of rot.
"Dismount," Silas commanded softly.
THUD! THUD!
The eight riders slid from their saddles into the ankle-deep snow.
Silas closed his eyes, extending the spiritual perception anchored within his Mythic Gold Core.
The invisible golden pulse radiated into the lightless cavern mouth, bouncing off the uneven stone walls and mapping the subterranean space.
’A large main chamber, roughly sixty paces deep with a natural granite ceiling and it’s structurally sound.’
Then, his sensory pulse struck living flesh.
’There are four signatures that are deep in the rear hollow and they’re of Tier 2 energy...’
"We have residents," Silas murmured, his hand dropping toward his weapon belt. "Four hostiles nested near the back wall. Looks like—"
"Allow me, Lord Silas."
Kadi stepped forward.
The Sand Mage’s voice was remarkably steady, though the fine shaking of her hands betrayed the nervous adrenaline coursing through her veins.
She pulled the heavy wool cloak from her shoulders, letting it drape across the pommel of her mount, revealing her dark leather armor and the brass-inlaid rings ringing both of her forearms.
She looked directly into Silas’s blue eyes, a fierce hunger for validation burning in her dark irises.

"You brought me on this strike to pull my weight," Kadi said, her chin lifting with quiet determination. "I didn’t swing a pickaxe in the mines yesterday, and I spent the morning watching the Saintess and the commanders clear the road... Let me clear the den so I will secure the cavern for our squad, my Lord."
Silas studied her face for a quiet second.
"Go," Silas granted with a slow, respectful nod. "Take the room, Kadi. We have your back."
A fierce, grateful spark ignited in Kadi’s eyes. "Thank you, my Lord."
She turned, stepping boldly across the frozen threshold into the pitch-black maw of the cavern.
The moment her leather boots crossed the boundary, the dark interior awakened.
SKREEEEEEEEE-CH-CH-CH!
An ear-splitting metallic screech tore through the cavern, echoing off the stone walls like shattering glass!
From the ceiling of the rear chamber, four shapes detached, crashing onto the granite floor with concussive sounds.
THUD! THUD! THUD! THUD!
They were Basalt Crawlers... they were monstrous arachnid-like horrors roughly the size of warhorses.

Their bodies were encased in thick, jagged plates of petrified black rock that functioned as natural armor and their eight jointed legs terminated in diamond-hard, spear-like points capable of punching through solid steel as their bloated underbellies pulsed with a sickly glowing yellow acid.
"CREEEEEE!" a hiss rattled through the air as the four beasts charged forward in synchronized scuttling.
CLIK-CLIK-CLIK-CLIK-CLIK!

The lead crawler closed the distance in an instant, lunging through the darkness with its two front spear-limbs cocked, thrusting straight toward Kadi’s throat with the speed of an armor-piercing ballista.
FZZZZZZT!
Kadi didn’t retreat an inch as her eyes burned with amber mana.
"Flow," Kadi whispered.
SHSHSH-BOOM!
She didn’t summon sand from her pouches this time, Kadi reached out to the very bedrock beneath her feet!
Her earth mana surged into the stone floor as the solid granite beneath the charging crawler instantly lost its molecular cohesion, grinding down into billions of microscopic sand particles.
’Finally we’re not out in the snow...’
The solid floor transformed into a violent churning quicksand vortex in the span of a single second.
WHOOSH!
The lead crawler’s front legs plunged into the liquid stone.
Its terrifying momentum violently betrayed it as the beast pitched forward, its armored head slamming face-first into the churning sand with an earth-shaking crack.
Before the monster could thrash its limbs, Kadi clapped her hands together.
CLAP!
"Solidify."
The churning vortex of sand instantly crystallized back into solid unbreakable granite.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The crawler’s legs, torso, and lower jaw were permanently fused into the stone floor, trapped in a stone vice that crushed its internal organs under millions of pounds of geological pressure.
The beast shrieked, vomiting a geyser of yellow acid that sizzled uselessly against the cave ceiling!
"First one down," Kadi muttered, her braids whipping as she pivoted on her heel.

The second and third crawlers vaulted over their trapped kin, their massive rock-plated bodies lunging through the air from the left and right flanks with their mandibles wide and dripping with slime.
WHOOSH.
Kadi dropped low, sliding across the dusty floor on her knees.
As she slid between the two airborne monstrosities, she thrust both arms straight upward toward the cavern ceiling.
CRRR-RUMBLE!
"Twin Spire!"

From the solid rock of the ceiling above, two stalactites that were as thick as tree trunks and sharp as needles shattered loose under her magical command, driven downward by the full force of gravity and pressurized earth mana.
THUD-CRUNCH-SPLAT!
The two falling stone pillars impaled both mid-air crawlers simultaneously.
The massive stone spikes drove clean through their armored thoraxes, pinning both writhing shrieking monstrosities dead-center to the cavern floor.
Black ichor and shattered plates of basalt exploded across the walls in a violent sickening display of total dominance.
SKREEEEEEE!
The fourth and largest crawler... a scarred brute nearly twice the size of the others skidded to a halt, its twelve red eyes widening in pure shock.
Realizing it was outmatched, the beast curled its legs, attempting to launch itself backward into the deep shadows of the rear tunnels...
"You don’t leave," Kadi snarled as she extended her right arm with her fingers clawing at the empty air.
From the pulverizing impact zones behind her, clouds of fine pulverized stone dust were hanging suspended in the draft.
Kadi seized that dust and her mana superheated the microscopic particles, converting the cloud into a swirling vortex of molten glass-sand.
VUUUUUUM!
The glowing superheated sand formed an eight-foot serrated crescent blade that hovered above her shoulder, spinning with the deafening high-pitched scream of a turbine engine.
"Sand Sever!"
Kadi brought her arm down in a violent chopping motion.
SHING-BOOOOOOM!
The molten glass crescent tore through the cavern.
It crossed twenty yards in seconds, cleaving cleanly through the fleeing crawler’s armored waist, through its legs, and burying itself four feet deep into the solid granite wall behind it.
THUD-SPLAT!
The two severed halves of the alpha crawler collapsed into the dust, twitching twice before curling into stillness as the cavern fell into ringing silence.
