"Lead the way."
The ascent to the elevated cavern shelf was brutal.

The Blessed Wolves had to dig their iron-shod claws into the icy shale, scrambling up the steep scree slope in a tight disciplined zig-zag pattern while the white fog continued its relentless climb up the canyon floor behind them.
When they crested the shelf, the cavern opening loomed before them.
It was a jagged irregular tear in the solid basalt face, roughly twelve feet wide and fifteen feet high.
The interior was completely pitch-black, exhaling a faint unnatural smell that carried the distinct foul odor of rot.
"Dismount," Silas commanded softly.
THUD!
THUD!
The eight riders slid from their saddles into the ankle-deep snow.
Silas closed his eyes, extending the spiritual perception anchored within his Mythic Gold Core.
The invisible golden pulse radiated into the lightless cavern mouth, bouncing off the uneven stone walls and mapping the subterranean space.
’A large main chamber, roughly sixty paces deep with a natural granite ceiling and it’s structurally sound.’
Then, his sensory pulse struck living flesh.
’There are four signatures that are deep in the rear hollow and they’re of Tier 2 energy...’
"We have residents," Silas murmured, his hand dropping toward his weapon belt.
"Four hostiles nested near the back wall.
Looks like—"
"Allow me, Lord Silas."
Kadi stepped forward.
The Sand Mage’s voice was remarkably steady, though the fine shaking of her hands betrayed the nervous adrenaline coursing through her veins.
She pulled the heavy wool cloak from her shoulders, letting it drape across the pommel of her mount, revealing her dark leather armor and the brass-inlaid rings ringing both of her forearms.
She looked directly into Silas’s blue eyes, a fierce hunger for validation burning in her dark irises.
"You brought me on this strike to pull my weight," Kadi said, her chin lifting with quiet determination.
"I didn’t swing a pickaxe in the mines yesterday, and I spent the morning watching the Saintess and the commanders clear the road...
Let me clear the den so I will secure the cavern for our squad, my Lord."
Silas studied her face for a quiet second.
"Go," Silas granted with a slow, respectful nod.
"Take the room, Kadi.
We have your back."
A fierce, grateful spark ignited in Kadi’s eyes.
"Thank you, my Lord."
She turned, stepping boldly across the frozen threshold into the pitch-black maw of the cavern.
The moment her leather boots crossed the boundary, the dark interior awakened.
SKREEEEEEEEE-CH-CH-CH!
An ear-splitting metallic screech tore through the cavern, echoing off the stone walls like shattering glass!
From the ceiling of the rear chamber, four shapes detached, crashing onto the granite floor with concussive sounds.
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
They were Basalt Crawlers... they were monstrous arachnid-like horrors roughly the size of warhorses.

Their bodies were encased in thick, jagged plates of petrified black rock that functioned as natural armor and their eight jointed legs terminated in diamond-hard, spear-like points capable of punching through solid steel as their bloated underbellies pulsed with a sickly glowing yellow acid.
"CREEEEEE!" a hiss rattled through the air as the four beasts charged forward in synchronized scuttling.
CLIK-CLIK-CLIK-CLIK-CLIK!

The lead crawler closed the distance in an instant, lunging through the darkness with its two front spear-limbs cocked, thrusting straight toward Kadi’s throat with the speed of an armor-piercing ballista.
FZZZZZZT!
Kadi didn’t retreat an inch as her eyes burned with amber mana.
"Flow," Kadi whispered.
SHSHSH-BOOM!
She didn’t summon sand from her pouches this time, Kadi reached out to the very bedrock beneath her feet!
Her earth mana surged into the stone floor as the solid granite beneath the charging crawler instantly lost its molecular cohesion, grinding down into billions of microscopic sand particles.
’Finally we’re not out in the snow...’
The solid floor transformed into a violent churning quicksand vortex in the span of a single second.
WHOOSH!
The lead crawler’s front legs plunged into the liquid stone.
Its terrifying momentum violently betrayed it as the beast pitched forward, its armored head slamming face-first into the churning sand with an earth-shaking crack.
Before the monster could thrash its limbs, Kadi clapped her hands together.
CLAP!
"Solidify."
The churning vortex of sand instantly crystallized back into solid unbreakable granite.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The crawler’s legs, torso, and lower jaw were permanently fused into the stone floor, trapped in a stone vice that crushed its internal organs under millions of pounds of geological pressure.
The beast shrieked, vomiting a geyser of yellow acid that sizzled uselessly against the cave ceiling!
"First one down," Kadi muttered, her braids whipping as she pivoted on her heel.

The second and third crawlers vaulted over their trapped kin, their massive rock-plated bodies lunging through the air from the left and right flanks with their mandibles wide and dripping with slime.
WHOOSH.
Kadi dropped low, sliding across the dusty floor on her knees.
As she slid between the two airborne monstrosities, she thrust both arms straight upward toward the cavern ceiling.
CRRR-RUMBLE!
"Twin Spire!"

From the solid rock of the ceiling above, two stalactites that were as thick as tree trunks and sharp as needles shattered loose under her magical command, driven downward by the full force of gravity and pressurized earth mana.
THUD-CRUNCH-SPLAT!
The two falling stone pillars impaled both mid-air crawlers simultaneously.
The massive stone spikes drove clean through their armored thoraxes, pinning both writhing shrieking monstrosities dead-center to the cavern floor.
Black ichor and shattered plates of basalt exploded across the walls in a violent sickening display of total dominance.
SKREEEEEEE!
The fourth and largest crawler... a scarred brute nearly twice the size of the others skidded to a halt, its twelve red eyes widening in pure shock.
Realizing it was outmatched, the beast curled its legs, attempting to launch itself backward into the deep shadows of the rear tunnels...
"You don’t leave," Kadi snarled as she extended her right arm with her fingers clawing at the empty air.
From the pulverizing impact zones behind her, clouds of fine pulverized stone dust were hanging suspended in the draft.
Kadi seized that dust and her mana superheated the microscopic particles, converting the cloud into a swirling vortex of molten glass-sand.
VUUUUUUM!
The glowing superheated sand formed an eight-foot serrated crescent blade that hovered above her shoulder, spinning with the deafening high-pitched scream of a turbine engine.
"Sand Sever!"
Kadi brought her arm down in a violent chopping motion.
SHING-BOOOOOOM!
The molten glass crescent tore through the cavern.
It crossed twenty yards in seconds, cleaving cleanly through the fleeing crawler’s armored waist, through its legs, and burying itself four feet deep into the solid granite wall behind it.
THUD-SPLAT!
The two severed halves of the alpha crawler collapsed into the dust, twitching twice before curling into stillness as the cavern fell into ringing silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 507: Does He Have Magic Hands?
paragraphs: Kadi stood in the center of the slaughter with her chest heaving and her hands glowing with the dying embers of amber earth mana.
She wiped a bead of sweat from her forehead with the back of her forearm, turned toward the entrance, and snapped a crisp trembling salute toward Silas.
"Cavern secured, Lord Silas!" Kadi called out, her voice proud and ringing with triumph. "Zero hostile signatures remaining!"
Standing at the threshold, Silas smiled warmly.
"Flawless execution, Kadi," Silas said, stepping inside. "That quicksand trap was pure genius. Outstanding work."
A brilliant smile broke across Kadi’s tanned face with her shoulders finally dropping their defensive tension as she beamed under his praise.
"Grab the legs, girls," Morwenna ordered, walking past with a smirk. "Let’s toss this garbage down the cliff before it stinks up the bedroom."
Morwenna and Tasmin grabbed the severed husks of the crawlers, hauling them to the threshold and heaving them over the basalt ledge.
CRASH-THUD-RUMBLE!
The massive carapaces tumbled down the scree slope, vanishing into the rocky gullies below.
Right on cue, a bone-chilling unnatural hiss rose from the bottom of the canyon.
The thick milky-white necrotic fog had finally crested the high shelf.
Like a living wall of blinding white smoke, the mist surged across the rocks, swirling hungrily toward the cavern opening and desperate to pour into the enclosed space.
"Elu! Seal the door!" Silas commanded.
"With pleasure, my love," Eluned replied, stepping gracefully to the cavern mouth.
She drove the base of her living wooden staff into the stone threshold.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
From the solid granite of the cavern entrance, dozens of massive roots erupted outward.
The emerald wood coiled together, expanding and intertwining in a dense, multi-layered weave that completely bricked up the twelve-foot opening in less than two seconds.
Thick moss and hardened bark filled every microscopic seam, locking the barrier into an airtight living wooden wall.
SZZZZZZZZT!
On the other side of the wood, the necrotic fog slammed against the barrier.

A muffled wet sound like thousands of microscopic leeches scraping their teeth against hard bark hissed against the exterior, but not a single wisp of the foul white vapor could penetrate Eluned’s sacred wood.
Inside, the cavern was completely sealed. It was safe, dry, and insulated from the freezing horrors of the basin.
The cavern was dark, but that darkness lasted only a fraction of a second.
Aurelia stepped forward, drawing her silver rapier two inches from its sheath.
She closed her eyes, her lips moving silently as she focused the power humming within her soul.
FWOOSH!
A sphere of pure silver-white flame... roughly the size of a melon ignited above her palm.
With a gentle flick of her wrist, she lofted the orb toward the ceiling, anchoring it in mid-air near the center of the chamber.
The Argent Flame burned without smoke and without consuming fuel as it bathed the entire granite cavern in a soft holy luminescence that was warm and comforting.
"Ah..." The Princess let out a soft trembling sigh of bliss as she pulled her heavy traveling hood down. "It’s so warm..."
"Let’s get comfortable," Silas said, unbuckling the heavy silver clasp of his midnight cloak.
He pulled the heavy silver-threaded garment over his shoulders, laying it flat across a clean raised stone shelf near the rear wall.

Reaching into his spatial inventory, Silas withdrew a dozen thick insulated woolen sleeping mats and woven fur blankets, spreading them out across the flat floor to create a wide communal resting area around the floating holy flame.
The eight Blessed Wolves were already settling down with their golden bodies curling into the corners of the cavern with deep contented grunts.
Silas walked over to Valkyrie and Titan as well as the rest of them, looking down at the magnificent beasts

"They hauled us through miles of sub-zero drifts and fought through two ambush lines," Silas noted, his voice carrying genuine affection for the mounts. "Not only do we have to keep them full, but they must be properly hydrated. Frozen snow damages their digestive lining if they eat too much of it."
VUUUM!
Silas tapped his storage again.
Eight massive heavy iron platters materialized in the air, landing softly on the cavern floor before the resting wolves.
Each platter was piled high with massive three-pound slabs of raw beast meat, marrow-rich femur bones, and dried liver chunks.
The wolves’ ears instantly perked up, their dark eyes widening with ecstatic gratitude.
Silas raised his right hand, channeling a gentle current of pure water mana from his core.
SPLASH-SHHHH!
Clear pristine water cascaded from his fingertips, filling eight secondary stone basins to the brim with fresh lukewarm moisture.
"Eat up, guys," Silas smiled, reaching down to scratch Titan behind his scarred ears.
The Alpha wolf let out a muffled rumbling whine of pure adoration, leaning its head hard against Silas’s chest as his wet nose snuffled against his tunic.
Valkyrie nudged in from the other side, her long pink tongue giving Silas’s cheek an affectionate sandpaper-rough swipe that nearly knocked him off balance.
"Hey, easy, easy!" Silas chuckled warmly, shrugging off the beasts as they began tearing into the meat with savage crunching of bone. "Eat your dinner, you big mutts."
Silas turned back toward the center of the camp.
The seven women had already shed their heavy cloaks and weapons, sitting together across the woven wool mats in the warm silver light of Aurelia’s flame.
Silas walked over, sitting cross-legged near the center of the circle.
With a brief flick of his sovereign storage, he retrieved the three massive lacquer containers Kaelia had prepared that morning, popping the airtight seals with a satisfying hiss.
POOF!
The rich mouth-watering aroma of roasted mountain venison, melted marrow butter, garlic tubers, and steaming spiced bone broth flooded the cavern.
A collective involuntary chorus of soft gasps and stomach rumbles rippled through the circle.
"Oh, blessed ancestors..." Kadi groaned, leaning forward with her hands on her knees with her eyes locked onto the succulent meat. "That smells like heaven."
Before Silas could even reach for a serving spoon, a slender fragrant weight settled heavily against his left side.
Eluned slid her arms around his bicep, pressing her soft, emerald-robed body against him, resting her chin comfortably atop his shoulder.
Her long green hair spilled across his chest like liquid silk, her emerald eyes looking up at him with half-lidded shameless adoration.
"Silas..." Eluned purred softly, her sweet voice tickling his ear. "My hands are so terribly cold from weaving that massive root wall... I don’t think I can hold a fork. Feed me? Please, hubby?"
Silas looked at her, he was aware that a Goddess didn’t feel temperature, but the sweet pleading look in her jade eyes made it impossible to refuse.
’Just don’t get hard...’
"You’re completely shameless, you know that?" Silas murmured with a soft smirk.
He picked up a polished wooden fork, speared a thick succulent piece of pepper-crusted venison glistening with savory tallow, and brought it to her lips.

Eluned parted her soft rosy lips, letting out a delicate trembling sigh of pure satisfaction as she took the meat into her mouth, chewing slowly with her eyes closed, humming a melodic tune of pure bliss.
"Mmmph... divine..." Eluned sighed, nuzzling her cheek deeper into his neck.
Sitting across from them, Morwenna’s jaw worked silently.
The Pirate Queen had been quietly reaching for a wooden bowl, but watching Eluned receive the Lord’s personal attention made something fiercely possessive snap in her chest.
She set her bowl down with a sharp clack.
Her cheeks flushed with an embarrassed pink, her gray eyes narrowing as she looked sideways at Silas.

"Hey... Captain," Morwenna muttered, clearing her throat aggressively as she crossed her legs on the mat. "If the weed gets hand-fed just for growing a few sticks... my sword arm is practically paralyzed from carving those brutes in the grove. Fair is fair on a flagship."
Silas raised an eyebrow, amused by the normally ruthless pirate’s sudden stubborn shyness.
"Is that so, Morwenna?" Silas teased.

"Aye," Morwenna grumbled, looking away toward the cave wall, though her lips parted slightly in clear anticipation. "Protocol demands the quartermaster be sustained... That’s how I did it on my ship."
Silas chuckled, spearing a golden-brown roasted tuber soaked in bone broth and leaning across the mat.
He brought the food to her lips.
Morwenna took the bite, her eyes fluttering shut as the savory buttery heat exploded across her tongue.
"Mm~"
A tiny muffled moan escaped her throat before she could catch herself, her cheeks instantly igniting into a deep furious crimson as she chewed frantically, hiding her face behind her black fringe.
"Tch... not bad..." Morwenna whispered, though the goofy smitten smile on her lips betrayed her completely.
Tasmin shifted quietly on her knees.
The dark-haired woman leaned forward, her amber eyes wide and surprisingly earnest as she looked straight at Silas.
"Lord Silas," Tasmin requested, her voice unusually soft. "I require sustenance from command as well."
Silas smiled, slicing a tender strip of loin and feeding her directly.
Tasmin ate it with graceful precision, her eyes softening with a rare peaceful warmth that completely erased the cold look on her face.
Aeliana and the Princess exchanged a wide-eyed flustered glance.
The high-elf secretary adjusted her spectacles, her fingers trembling as she gathered her courage.
"L-Lord Silas... if it wouldn’t be... an administrative imposition..."
"Open up, Aeli," Silas offered warmly, holding out a steaming piece of venison. "Right, Nice spectacles too."
Aeliana leaned forward, taking the bite with a delicate nibble, her long pointed ears twitching with an ecstatic blushing flutter that made her look ten years younger.
’Not only did my Lord feed me but my Lord said he liked the spectacles too...’ Aeli thought, at this point, he had to put a baby in her.
Beside her, the Princess could no longer contain herself.
Gathering every ounce of her royal courage, she leaned her frame toward him, her azure eyes shimmering with breathless excitement.
"Lord Silas... me too, please!"
Silas chuckled, feeding the royal a delicate morsel of honey-glazed root bread.
The Princess clapped her hands together, letting out a joyful muffled squeak of pure happiness as she chewed, feeling included in the inner circle.
Then came Kadi.
The Sand Mage crawled forward on the mat, her dark eyes completely uninhibited, trembling with lingering exhaustion from her solo clash with the crawlers.
"My Lord... please," Kadi breathed huskily.
Silas brought a thick cut of savory venison to her mouth.
The moment the meat touched her tongue, Kadi let out an audible breathless moan.
"Ahhn..."
She closed her eyes, her entire body shuddering with an intensely sweet physical relief as she swallowed. "It’s... it’s so good, Lord Silas... another bite... please..."

Silas fed her a second piece, and another breathless, trembling whimper escaped her lips, her cheeks burning with an intoxicating blissful heat that made Morwenna cough into her fist in sudden embarrassment.
Watching this entire spectacle from the edge of the mat was Thor.
The towering God of Thunder sat cross-legged, a wooden flagon of stout resting between her knees.
Her wild blonde locks hung loose around her shoulders, and her storm-blue eyes were wide with genuine childlike bafflement as she watched Silas hand-feed seven different women.

’What is going on here?’ Thor wondered, scratching her chin with a thick calloused finger. ’They are all groaning and squirming like they were struck by a high-tier blessing... Is there... a different kind of magic when someone feeds you? Does food taste sweeter from the hand of a Lord?’
The curiosity became too much to bear.
Thor leaned her massive sculpted frame forward, casting a colossal shadow over the central mat.
She poked Silas in the shoulder with a finger thick as an iron rail.
"Silas," Thor rumbled, her voice surprisingly earnest. "Feed me a bite."
The entire circle fell dead silent.
Silas paused, looking up at the towering immortal warrior. "You want me to feed you, Thor?"

"Aye!" Thor nodded vigorously, her wild hair bouncing. "I must conduct an empirical evaluation... These women are whimpering as if you’re feeding them ambrosia plucked from the cosmic tree so give me a piece of that boar tenderloin! Let me see what magic lies in your fingers!"
Silas let out an amused breath, picking up a substantial four-ounce cut of prime roasted meat with the carving fork.
He raised it toward the towering deity.
"Alright. Open up."
Thor leaned down, opening her mouth wide, and clamped her teeth over the meat, swallowing it in a single massive chomp.
CHOMP! GULP!
Thor froze.
She closed her eyes, smacking her lips thoughtfully, searching her divine soul for the ethereal spark.
She opened her eyes, blinking.
"Well?" Silas asked with a smirk. "Did you feel the cosmic magic?"
"No," Thor answered bluntly, scratching her nose. "It tastes like salted boar... Excellent boar, mind you, but there is zero divine enchantment."
She paused, looking down at Silas’s calm handsome face, the way his golden ringed blue eyes held hers without an ounce of fear or hesitation, the easy warmth radiating off his hands.
A strange unfamiliar warmth suddenly tugged at the corner of Thor’s chest.
She looked down at her heavy flagon of dwarven ale, then slid it across the mat, nudging it against his knee.

"However..." Thor grunted, a rare smirk breaking across her rugged beautiful face as she tilted her head back, "it isn’t a bad feeling to have someone wait on me for once. Hold the flagon, Silas... Feed me the ale."
Silas chuckled, picking up the heavy wooden vessel and tilting the rim against her lips.
Thor drank deeply, swallowing the cold, frothing stout with loud gulps as Silas held the weight steady.
GLUG! GLUG! GLUG!
She let out a massive satisfied sigh, wiping a stray drop of foam from her lip with the back of her wrist, looking down at him with a deep quiet contentment in her storm-blue eyes.
’Aye...’ Thor thought, settling her massive shoulders back against the stone wall. ’It truly isn’t bad to be fed... I wouldn’t mind if that person was Silas every day...’

The Sand Mage crawled forward on the mat, her dark eyes completely uninhibited, trembling with lingering exhaustion from her solo clash with the crawlers.
"My Lord... please," Kadi breathed huskily.
Silas brought a thick cut of savory venison to her mouth.
The moment the meat touched her tongue, Kadi let out an audible breathless moan.
"Ahhn..."
She closed her eyes, her entire body shuddering with an intensely sweet physical relief as she swallowed.
"It’s... it’s so good, Lord Silas... another bite... please..."

Silas fed her a second piece, and another breathless, trembling whimper escaped her lips, her cheeks burning with an intoxicating blissful heat that made Morwenna cough into her fist in sudden embarrassment.
Watching this entire spectacle from the edge of the mat was Thor.
The towering God of Thunder sat cross-legged, a wooden flagon of stout resting between her knees.
Her wild blonde locks hung loose around her shoulders, and her storm-blue eyes were wide with genuine childlike bafflement as she watched Silas hand-feed seven different women.
’What is going on here?’ Thor wondered, scratching her chin with a thick calloused finger. ’They are all groaning and squirming like they were struck by a high-tier blessing...
Is there... a different kind of magic when someone feeds you?
Does food taste sweeter from the hand of a Lord?’
The curiosity became too much to bear.
Thor leaned her massive sculpted frame forward, casting a colossal shadow over the central mat.
She poked Silas in the shoulder with a finger thick as an iron rail.
"Silas," Thor rumbled, her voice surprisingly earnest.
"Feed me a bite."
The entire circle fell dead silent.
Silas paused, looking up at the towering immortal warrior.
"You want me to feed you, Thor?"
"Aye!" Thor nodded vigorously, her wild hair bouncing.
"I must conduct an empirical evaluation...
These women are whimpering as if you’re feeding them ambrosia plucked from the cosmic tree so give me a piece of that boar tenderloin!
Let me see what magic lies in your fingers!"
Silas let out an amused breath, picking up a substantial four-ounce cut of prime roasted meat with the carving fork.
He raised it toward the towering deity.
"Alright.
Open up."
Thor leaned down, opening her mouth wide, and clamped her teeth over the meat, swallowing it in a single massive chomp.
CHOMP!
GULP!
Thor froze.
She closed her eyes, smacking her lips thoughtfully, searching her divine soul for the ethereal spark.
She opened her eyes, blinking.
"Well?" Silas asked with a smirk.
"Did you feel the cosmic magic?"
"No," Thor answered bluntly, scratching her nose.
"It tastes like salted boar...
Excellent boar, mind you, but there is zero divine enchantment."
She paused, looking down at Silas’s calm handsome face, the way his golden ringed blue eyes held hers without an ounce of fear or hesitation, the easy warmth radiating off his hands.
A strange unfamiliar warmth suddenly tugged at the corner of Thor’s chest.
She looked down at her heavy flagon of dwarven ale, then slid it across the mat, nudging it against his knee.
"However..." Thor grunted, a rare smirk breaking across her rugged beautiful face as she tilted her head back, "it isn’t a bad feeling to have someone wait on me for once.
Hold the flagon, Silas...
Feed me the ale."
Silas chuckled, picking up the heavy wooden vessel and tilting the rim against her lips.
Thor drank deeply, swallowing the cold, frothing stout with loud gulps as Silas held the weight steady.
GLUG!
GLUG!
GLUG!
She let out a massive satisfied sigh, wiping a stray drop of foam from her lip with the back of her wrist, looking down at him with a deep quiet contentment in her storm-blue eyes.
’Aye...’ Thor thought, settling her massive shoulders back against the stone wall. ’It truly isn’t bad to be fed...
I wouldn’t mind if that person was Silas every day...’

chapters.title: Chapter 508: Entries From The Past? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The cavern was filled with the quiet contented murmur of shared laughter as well as the deep breathing of the resting wolves.
The Princess sat cross-legged near the edge of the woven mat with her small belly delightfully full of warm venison and broth.
Her boots were unlaced as her tired toes were warming pleasantly in the ambient glow of Aurelia’s floating holy flame.
As she leaned back on her hands, her right palm pressed against a strange hard protrusion beneath the thick wool fabric of the mat.
CRUNCH!
The Princess frowned softly.
"What is that...?"

Thinking it was a stray piece of sharp basalt scree that had been overlooked when Silas laid out the bedding, she reached her gloved hand beneath the edge of the blanket with her fingers curling around the cold rigid object to pull it free.
Her fingers closed around long jointed cylinders and then she pulled her hand out.
"Eee—"
The sound died in the Princess’s throat and her azure eyes widened in paralyzing horror.
Held in her trembling palm... was a human hand.

It was completely lacking any sort of flesh... the ivory bones were stained a deep mottled yellow with age, the joints locked in a petrified claw-like rigor mortis, covered in a thin brittle crust of centuries-old ice.
"KYAAAAAAAAAAH!"
The Princess shrieked, violently flinging the skeletal appendage across the cavern floor.
CLATTER-CLATTER-THUD!
The bones bounced across the stone, coming to a halt right in the center of the circle, landing squarely in the light of the Argent Flame.
"Hostiles?!" Morwenna was on her feet in an instant with her hand snapping to Tidebringer’s hilt.
"Form up!" Tasmin’s void-daggers cleared their holsters with a deadly hiss!
"Wait, hold your steel!" Silas commanded, raising a hand as he stood up.
He walked over to the shivering Princess, placing a firm palm on her shoulder, feeling her smaller frame trembling violently.
"Breathe, Princess... You’re safe. It’s not an attack."
"I-It was a hand!" the Princess stammered, pointing a shaking finger at the center of the mat. "A dead person’s hand under my blanket, Lord Silas!"
Silas stepped over to where the skeleton piece had rolled, kneeling down beside the yellowed bones.
The rest of the squad gathered around in a tight, cautious circle... Eluned, Aurelia, Aeliana, and Thor all peering down at the macabre discovery.

"It’s ancient," Silas observed, picking up a twig to turn the bones over without touching them directly. "The marrow inside the radius is completely petrified so it’s obvious this person died centuries ago."
"Look there," Kadi pointed, her sharp eyes catching a detail in the light. "Tucked into the curled fingers... The hand was holding something when it froze."
Silas leaned closer.
Clamped tightly within the curled bony grip of the petrified fingers was a small, tightly rolled cylinder of ancient wax-treated parchment.
The wax seal had cracked into flakes of red dust, but the dense vellum had somehow survived the damp sub-zero centuries of the cavern.
Using the tip of his dagger, Silas carefully pried the brittle bone fingers apart.
SNAP!
The dry finger bone broke away with a soft crack, releasing the rolled paper.
Silas picked it up, feeling the dry brittle texture between his calloused thumbs.
"Aeliana, bring the light closer," Silas murmured.
The high-elf secretary knelt beside him, holding up a small polished brass reflector that focused the holy rays of Aurelia’s flame onto the parchment.
Silas gently unrolled the stiff vellum.

The paper was in terrible condition as large portions of the surface were rotted through with black mold, and decades of freezing condensation had caused the ancient iron-gall ink to bleach and fade into illegible ghostly smudges.
It was written in the form of fragmented disconnected log entries like a desperate journal scrawled in the dark by a trembling dying hand.
Silas squinted, his blue eyes tracing the broken faded lines, reading the legible fragments aloud to the silent watching squad.

"Let me see... Not everything is okay here but I’ve seen one... [ENTRY: 44]... the tremors did not cease... the breach at the lower shaft has widened... we were fools to think the [] could be bargained with..."
Silas paused with his finger trailing across an entire sentence that had been dissolved into a dark greasy water stain.
"...[ENTRY: 46]... Beasts... they are not wild... they move with divine intent... Her wrath has turned the northern canyons into an abattoir... but the cold... the unnatural cold came from behind..."
"Beasts?" Morwenna echoed with her brow furrowing deeply. "The Goddess of Beasts?"
Silas continued reading, his voice dropping into a somber steady rhythm.

"...[ENTRY: --]... a clash of primordial horrors... Beasts and Ice fighting against each other... the heavens shattered... the frost did not fall from the sky, it erupted from the deep crust... strong... very..."
Another massive scorched tear ran across the center of the vellum, obliterating three whole paragraphs.
The next visible entry was jagged, written in violent frantic scratches.

"...not a battle... a slaughter... Ice... the glacier swallowed the entire place... they did not freeze, their souls were suspended in the crystal... a lot of people died... thousands in the span of a single breath... the screaming stopped when the whiteout descended..."
The air in the cavern seemed to drop by ten degrees as the women listened in dead silence with the weight of the ancient tragedy hanging heavy in the warm light.
Silas reached the very bottom of the paper where the final entry was barely two lines, scrawled right before the writer’s hand had locked in death.

"...fled to the upper shelf... the mist is leaking through the stone... no escape... do not look for the treasure... the seal was never meant to hold her... the seal was meant to contain the []... beware the deep mines..."
The text abruptly terminated.
The last stroke of the ink trailed off the edge of the vellum in a long, erratic scrape, where the dying expeditioner had collapsed onto the basalt floor.
Silas lowered the paper, staring down at the faded, disconnected words.

"Beasts and Ice fighting each other..." Silas muttered, his tactical mind racing through the fragments. "Thousands of people dead in an instant. A freeze that erupted from the crust, not the sky and a warning... about the deep mines?"

"It doesn’t make sense," Tasmin whispered, her arms crossed over her chest as she stared at the bones. "If the Forever Ice was forged to seal the Goddess of Beasts... why does the log describe the ice fighting against her? And what were thousands of humans doing in the deep northern trenches centuries ago?"
"The mines," Morwenna pointed out with her gray eyes dark and serious. "The letter ended with the mines. Whatever was down there... people were digging for it before the basin fell into darkness."
Eluned stood motionless, her emerald eyes locked onto the ancient parchment with a deeply troubled shadow crossing her divine features.
"Silas..." Eluned spoke softly, her voice barely a whisper against the crackle of the flame. "The entity trapped in that trench... may not be the only thing waiting for us beneath the ice."
Silas slowly rolled the brittle vellum back up, securing it carefully within the interior pocket of his tunic.
He looked toward the sealed root wall, listening to the muffled relentless scraping of the necrotic fog outside.
His blue eyes hardened into cold resolve.
"Whatever is down there," Silas declared, his voice echoing cleanly off the granite walls, "we crack the ice, we take the goddess, and we find out the truth."
The rolled vellum in Silas’s hands felt like thin layers of brittle slate.

His gloved thumbs pressed down along the edges to prevent the parchment from curling back into its long-held cylinder, and every time the fiber flexed, tiny flecks of black iron-gall ink flaked away into the woven fabric of the floor mat.
Beside him, the Argent Flame hung motionless in the cavern’s vault.
Aurelia’s holy fire threw clean, cast-silver light into every crack in the granite, making the shadows behind the stacked crates sharp as cut glass.

The yellowed hand bone that the Princess had hurled lay resting on its knuckles four feet away, looking less like a terror from the deep and more like an abandoned chisel forgotten by an uncaring mason.
Silas took in a lungful of the dry, pine-scented air that the silver fire produced.
He let it out slowly with his shoulders dropping half an inch inside his dark coat.

’So people were breaking rock down here before the borders were even marked,’ he thought, his blue eyes drifting back to the fragmented script. ’Long before Aeli’s original Lord came here and centuries before my core ever touched an altar.’
He had known the Umbral Basin had an appetite.

The geography itself had the feel of a place that had swallowed several successive civilizations without bothering to chew but finding a hand clutching a warning about deep shafts was an entirely different matter.

’Does this mean every strike we’ve driven into the shale is sitting on an ancient tomb?’ he wondered, the strategist in him immediately calculating risk ratios. ’If the mines are cursed, we’re digging our own basement into a furnace...’
He shook his head with the fur collar of his traveling cloak brushing his jaw.

’No. The letter specifically pointed downward... "Deep mines" and "Lower shafts". What Thora’s teams have opened so far are mere surface scratches... quarries and open-pit faults barely twenty fathoms into the limestone. If there’s something buried under the deep bedrock that made thousands of armed men die screaming in a single morning, it’s not going to be solved by reading moldy vellum and the only person who would actually know the layout of the basin before the frost locked it down is the one who was there when the glaciers slammed shut.’
The Goddess of Beasts.
The tablet had called her a sovereign presence and the bird’s erratic panic confirmed she was an ancient pillar.
If she was entombed in the deep northern rift, she had watched whatever calamity unfolded before the ice took her limbs.

’I’ll ask her myself when we crack the shell,’ Silas concluded, his fingers rolling the vellum back into its tight crease before sliding it securely into the interior pocket of his tunic. ’Until then, speculation is just dead weight...’
He turned away from the bone, looking toward the living barricade that sealed the mouth of the cavern.
Thick emerald-veined roots of the World Tree were knotted across the entrance like massive intertwined pythons.
They formed a solid petrified wooden plug eight inches thick, completely sealing out the draft.
Through the microscopic gaps between the bark, sickly white threads of moisture clung to the perimeter, twitching like blind maggots.
"Elu," Silas called out, his voice quiet in the hollow stone space. "What’s the mist doing out there?"
Eluned, who was still lounging against his side with her cheek pressed against his bicep, didn’t bother opening her eyes.
Her emerald hair spilled over his forearm, the tips faintly glowing as they tapped into the moisture within the wood.

"It’s swollen to the ceiling of the gorge, Silas," she murmured, her voice thick with lazy warmth. "The pressure is immense... The little leeches from before have multiplied as hundreds of them are writhing in the vapor, and several larger abominations are scraping their bone-plates against my outer bark. They can smell the wolves’ blood through the stone, but they don’t have the weight to split my grain so they’ll blunt their teeth until the cycle breaks."
High on a basalt protrusion near the fire, the obsidian bird let out a sharp sequence of clicks.
It bobbed its crested skull three times, its dark feathers rustling as it tucked its beak back beneath its wing.

"The bird confirms it," Eluned added, shifting her weight so that she was leaning more heavily against Silas’s ribs. "The high tide of the fog lasts three hours, perhaps four... It will churn through the narrow canyons, choke on its own and then sink back into the deep fissures. We have nothing to do but wait."
Silas exhaled, looking around the cavern. "Then we take the downtime. Nobody moves until the air is dry..."
He reached down to the iron platters that had held their meal.
The empty wooden trenchers and bone broth flagons were scattered across the edges of the mats.
With a thought, he summoned a gentle circular current of raw water mana to his fingertips.

A thin film of warm water lifted from his palms, wrapping around the wooden bowls, scouring the grease dried tallow, and marrow remnants from the grain with a soft circular shhhhhk before the moisture was expelled into a small dark crevice near the rear wall.
VUUUM!
The cleaned lacquer containers dissolved into blue light, filed neatly back into his inventory.

’We still have enough salted venison and cakes to feed twenty men for a week,’ he calculated, closing his interface with a silent blink. ’Kaelia over-packed as usual, which means we won’t have to hunt now...’
Around the perimeter of the chamber, the Blessed Wolves took their cue from the silence.
Valkyrie turned two slow circles on the hard floor before collapsing with a heavy floor-shaking whump, resting her chin across her front paws.
Beside her, Titan let out a long shuddering sigh that blew the loose dust away from the wolf’s snout, closing his eyes as his ribcage rose and fell in deep slumber.

chapters.title: Chapter 509: A Game For Cuddles [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas laughed softly beneath his breath, watching the eight silver predators settle down like an oversized pack of hound puppies.
"You all are really cute..."
He leaned back against a smooth slab of basalt, extending his long legs across the fur-lined blankets.
He pulled the heavy, silver-threaded collar of his cloak down around his chest, closing his eyes to let the ambient warmth of Aurelia’s flame settle into his bones.
The cavern was quiet, a bit too quiet for his liking to be honest.
When he opened his eyes again, several pairs of female eyes were locked onto him.
Silas froze.
The space on his left was already occupied by Eluned, who had curled her slender silk-robed legs beneath her and anchored two hands around his forearm.
But the space on his right... a wide empty stretch of soft bearskin blanket was completely unoccupied.
More importantly, the flat broad expanse of his chest was entirely open.
To the exhausted freshly fed warriors trapped in a freezing cavern, that open chest looked like a prime piece of real estate.
Tasmin’s amber eyes flicked from the corner of the mat to his collarbone, her jaw tightening with subtle assessment.
Kadi was nervously adjusting the brass bangles on her wrists, her dark eyes darting toward his boots with an unmistakable hungry intensity.
’Tch... Eluned really is a bitch.’

Beside her, Aeliana sat with her knees pressed tightly together with her silver-gold irises wide behind her wire-rimmed spectacles and her chest rising and falling in shallow rapid breaths as she stared at the fur trim of his coat.
Even the Princess had crept two inches closer across the wool, her cheeks flushed a light peach as she curled a lock of azure hair around her thumb.
The only one who wasn’t currently calculating an approach vector was Thor.
The towering God of Thunder was lying flat on her back three paces away with her boots kicked off and her massive woolen stockings resting against Titan’s furry rump.
Her mouth was slightly open with a tiny comical line of clear drool pooling at the corner of her lips as she stared up at the granite ceiling, her chest heaving in slow massive rhythms.

"Mmmmph..." Thor grunted in her half-sleep, muttering toward the rock. "More salted ribs... Silas, tell the dwarf to bring the four-gallon cask... this cave isn’t half bad... quite comfy, honestly..."
Eluned slowly raised her head from Silas’s arm, her emerald eyes narrowing as she surveyed the competitors circled around the mat.
An incredibly wicked smirk spread across the World Spirit’s porcelain lips.

’Look at her,’ Eluned thought, her gaze lingering on the drooling thunder deity. ’Even after centuries of wandering between dimensions... Thor is still the exact same lumbering oaf as when I first laid eyes on her in the old realms. She has zero feminine cunning but these other girls...’
She sat up, smoothing her green robes over her thighs with an exaggerated graceful rustle.

"Well, well," Eluned chimed, her melodic voice cutting through the heavy silence of the cave. "It seems our Lord is rather cold... Every single one of you is staring at my husband’s chest as if it were a platter of roast quail."
"I am merely observing the defensive posture of our commander’s position," Tasmin rasped without blinking, though her ears twitched.

"I was checking his cloak’s weave," Morwenna lied through her teeth, her black fringe falling over her gray eyes as she crossed her arms over Tidebringer. "Making sure the dwarven alloy wasn’t warping under the heat."
She would have jumped at it but she didn’t want to be called a virgin by Eluned again.
’Even if I’m a bit rude... I want my first time to be lovely.’

"You’re both terrible liars," Eluned purred, tilting her head. "And since I am a benevolent goddess who believes in fair governance, I will not monopolize the Lord’s warmth... I propose a trial. A contest if you will!"
Silas blinked, his composure instantly slipping into deep suspicion.
"Elu, wait, I don’t think we need a—"
"Hush, Silas, the men don’t dictate the terms of the inner pavilion," Eluned interrupted smoothly, waving a pale hand dismissively in his face.
"Aye, pipe down, Captain," Morwenna barked, suddenly leaning forward with sharp competitive fervor. "If there’s a wager on the table, a sailor doesn’t turn it down... What’s the game, weed?"
"A simple game of Root and Stone," Eluned declared, raising her right hand.
From her palm, four tiny smooth wooden blocks of heartwood manifested.
Each block was carved with four distinct elemental runes which were Gale, Tide, Earth, and Ember.

"The rules are simple," Eluned explained, her eyes sparkling with divine mischief. "Each player draws two blocks blind. We place them in the center simultaneously... If your rune counters the opponent’s, you advance one step along the stone grid. If there is a clash, the one who can channel a micro-thread of that exact element to ignite the carving wins the contested ground, for those who don’t have the affinities, you can just pour your mana and it’ll give the same effect. The first one to take the center stone... wins the right to use the Lord as her personal mattress for the remainder of the watch."
"I’m sitting right here," Silas pointed out dryly.
Nobody listened to him.
"A duel of elemental intuition and reaction time?" Aurelia murmured, her golden eyes lighting up with quiet interest. "I see..."
She usually wouldn’t participate in this but honestly Aurelia wanted to check if she was really seductive to someone like their Lord.
"I have excellent manual dexterity," Aeliana whispered, pushing her spectacles up her nose with her mind already mapping the probability combinations of four runes.
"I’m in," Kadi growled, rolling her shoulders like she was stepping into a gladiatorial pit.
"Let’s see your steel, then!" Morwenna grinned savagely, dropping to her knees at the edge of the mat.
From her spot by the Alpha wolf, Thor cracked one storm-blue eye open.
She looked at the seven women huddled around four wooden blocks with deathly white-knuckled seriousness, then glanced at Silas, who was rubbing his temples in utter defeat.

"Gwahahaha!" Thor’s belly laugh rumbled through the cavern, vibrating the dust on the stalactites. "Mortal women are truly terrifying creatures! They face down monsters with cold steel, and now they bicker like wolves over a single scrap of bone! Silas, you are truly a doomed man!"
"Thanks for the support, Thor," Silas muttered.
"Anytime, comrade!" Thor bellowed, resting her chin in her hand to watch the spectacle unfold.
"Round one!" Eluned announced, tossing the blocks onto the center of the blanket.
CLACK-CLACK!
The first clash was between Morwenna and Tasmin.
The Pirate Queen slammed down a Tide block with enough force to make the blanket jump.
THUD!
Tasmin countered with Gale...
"Current breaks before the squall," Tasmin rasped, her eyes narrowing as a wisp of razor-sharp wind curled around her fingernail.
FZZZT!
"Not when the tide has iron in it, shadow-rat!" Morwenna snarled.

Her gray eyes flashed and a microscopic drop of high-pressure sea moisture formed at the tip of her index finger, slamming into the wooden block with a sharp tick that forced Tasmin’s wind to shatter.
"Point to the quartermaster!" Morwenna roared, thrusting her fist into the air!
"That was improper pressure application," Tasmin clicked her tongue, retreating to the rear rank with a dark scowl.
"Next!"
Aurelia stepped forward against Kadi.

The Saintess laid down Ember, her block radiating with a pure immaculate silver warmth that smelled of dried lavender while Kadi slammed down Earth, attempting to smother the flame beneath a micro-barrier of dense sand grit.
CRACKLE!
"Faith does not suffocate beneath dirt, sister," Aurelia whispered.
She really hated talking like that but it pissed people off and if she managed to pull that off then the person could lose their focus.
The holy flame flared, glassing the sand into tiny translucent beads in an instant.
Kadi groaned, throwing her hands up in defeat as Aurelia claimed the square.
"Now... the semi-finals," Eluned purred, stepping forward to face Aurelia herself.
The World Spirit didn’t even drop a block as she simply looked at the remaining pieces, and a tiny living vine erupted from the wood, flipping the Gale rune forward with effortless divine authority.
Aurelia’s Ember clashed against the living wood, but Eluned’s primordial mana was simply too vast as the vine absorbed the heat, blooming into a tiny white flower that settled on the stone.
"My square," Eluned smiled sweetly.
"Your pride will be your undoing, Lady Eluned," Aurelia murmured, though she bowed politely as she yielded the mat. ’It’s just bullying...’
"Which leaves..." Eluned turned her predatory emerald gaze toward the final challenger.
Sitting alone at the edge of the blanket with her knees trembling slightly, was Aeliana.
The high-elf secretary adjusted her wire-rimmed glasses with a shaking finger.
She had never engaged in high-stakes territorial gambling, and standing against an immortal spirit who held authority over the basin’s soil seemed like professional suicide.
"Come along, long ears," Morwenna teased from the sidelines, leaning on her elbow. "Show the weed what that brain can do!"
"You can do it, Lady Aeliana!" the Princess cheered softly, pumping her small fists.
Aeliana swallowed hard with her throat clicking.
She reached into the wooden cup as her slender fingers closed around the final two blocks.
Eluned smiled, confident in her overwhelming elemental reservoir as she placed Tide onto the center slate.
"Tide covers the shore," Eluned declared. "Show me your move, Aeli."
Aeliana looked at the block.
Her mind, which had spent a while cataloging thousands of tons of ore, tracking dimensional frequencies, and calculating spatial drift, didn’t view the blocks as elements.
She viewed them as spatial coordinates...
’If Tide moves along the third axis... then the displacement vector requires a void,’ Aeliana calculated in a microsecond. ’Anything that helps me win.’
She dropped Gale but the moment the wood touched the blanket, Aeliana didn’t summon wind.
POP!
A microscopic paper-thin spatial vacuum opened directly beneath the rune.

The pocket of empty space collapsed inward, creating a tiny pressurized vortex that violently pulled the atmospheric moisture from Eluned’s Tide block, completely desiccating the wood before the World Spirit’s mana could anchor into the grain.
CLACK!
The Tide block went dull with its blue carving fading to gray ash as the cavern went dead silent.
Eluned’s jaw dropped. Her emerald eyes widened until they were completely round.
"That..." Eluned gasped, pointing a shaking finger at the dried block. "That was spatial manipulation! That’s cheating! That wasn’t a wind spell!"

"The rules stated an elemental manifestation to manipulate the carving, Lady Eluned," Aeliana answered softly, her voice remarkably steady as she pushed her spectacles up her nose, though her entire face was rapidly turning the shade of a ripe strawberry. "A spatial vacuum is merely the displacement of atmospheric air so by physical definition, it falls under the Gale quadrant. The center stone belongs to me."
"TCH!" Morwenna clicked her tongue, though an appreciative grin split across her face. "The pen-pusher took the prize! Unbelievable!"
"Hooray!" The Princess squeaked, clapping her hands together.
"Splendid reasoning, Aeliana," Aurelia smiled warmly though inwardly her eye twitched. ’It should have been me...’
Eluned sat frozen, staring at the empty wooden square as if her entire divine lineage had been personally insulted.
Aeliana stood up on trembling legs.

She stepped across the woven mats with her soft leather slippers making no sound against the wool as she reached the edge of the blanket where Silas was leaning against the basalt, stopping right beside his outstretched boots.
She looked down at him, her large golden-rimmed elven eyes shimmering with an agonizing mixture of terror, shyness, and overwhelming desire.
"L-Lord Silas..." Aeliana whispered, her fingers nervously pleating the fabric of her charcoal trousers. "May I... do I have permission to... claim the reward...?"
Silas looked up at his usually composed secretary.
Seeing her standing there, blushing to the tips of her long ears, looking at him like he was the only source of warmth in the entire freezing universe, his heart softened completely.
He reached out, his gloved hand catching her wrist and gently pulling her down toward the blankets.
"Permission granted, Aeli," Silas said softly. "Come here."
Aeliana didn’t just sit.
The moment her knees hit the fur, all the nervous hesitation completely dissolved into pure possessive instinct.
She collapsed forward onto his chest with a soft trembling gasp.
THUD!
She wrapped both of her slender arms tightly around his neck, burying her burning face directly into the crook of his collarbone, inhaling his scent with a desperate breath.
And then, before anyone could blink, Aeliana shifted her lower body.
SWISH!

With the fluid terrifying flexibility that nobody knew an elf was capable of, she threw her right leg completely over both of Silas’s thighs, locking her ankle behind his calf in a fierce iron-clad leg lock that pinned him flat to the stone floor.

She anchored her hips against his waist, curling her entire body over his torso like a living breathing blanket, pressing her soft curves against his armor until not a single millimeter of air remained between them.
PFFFFFT!
Across the mat, Kadi violently spat her mouthful of bone broth straight onto the stone.
"WHAT IN THE DESERT IS THAT?!" Kadi choked, coughing frantically into her fist. "SHE LOCKED HIM DOWN LIKE A RUNAWAY CAMEL!"
Tasmin’s jaw went slack, her void-daggers nearly slipping from her fingers. "That... that is an advanced technique that Brida practiced... Where did Aeli learn ground-grappling?!"
"GET OFF HIM!"
Eluned let out an outraged shriek, launching herself forward across the blankets with her emerald hair whipping wildly.

"LET ME AT THIS ELF! LET ME AT THIS HOMEWRECKER!" Eluned yelled, her pale hands clawing at the air as she tried to drag the elven girl off Silas’s ribs. "SHE DIDN’T JUST TAKE THE BED, SHE BUILT A FORTRESS ON HIS PELVIS!"
Morwenna caught Eluned around the waist from behind, digging her boots into the mat as the screaming goddess thrashed in her grip.

"Calm your roots, you overgrown weed!" Morwenna barked, laughing so hard her ribs ached. "It was your game! You set the stakes, you drew the runes, and the long ear elf outplayed you! Take your loss like a proper captain!"
"I WAS ROBBED!" Eluned wailed, though Morwenna hauled her bodily back to the far side of the mat.

chapters.title: Chapter 510: Monster Horde [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Down on the floor, Silas let out a breathless muffled grunt as Aeliana tightened her grip around his neck.
The high-elf had tucked her nose under his jawline with her breath hot against his throat and her smaller hands clutching the fabric of his coat as if she were drowning at sea.
She was trembling slightly, but the fierce stubborn line of her jaw told him she would rather have her limbs severed than let go of this position.

Silas let out an amused resigned sigh. He brought his arm up, wrapping it securely around Aeliana’s slender waist, his fingers resting gently against the curve of her hip, letting her draw all the heat she needed.
"Comfortable, Aeli?" Silas murmured into her blond hair.
Aeliana gave a tiny frantic nod against his skin and a soft purring hum vibrating in her throat as she closed her eyes, completely dead to the world.
Gradually, the cavern settled back into stillness.
Morwenna eventually forced Eluned to lie down on the adjacent mat, where the Goddess spent twenty minutes muttering curses about unfairness before the heavy warmth of the fire claimed her.
’Elu barely slept...’
Tasmin curled into the shadow of a supply crate, her daggers never leaving her reach.
Aurelia and the Princess lay side-by-side beneath a thick wolf-pelt blanket with their quiet whispers dying down as their breathing synchronized into the gentle rhythm of deep sleep.
’Well riding over such a long period is an experience for them so I’m not surprised.’ Silas thought.
Over by the Alpha wolf, Thor was still awake.
The God of Thunder had rolled onto her side, propping her head up on one thick calloused palm.

Her storm-blue eyes watched the sleeping camp... the way the elven girl clung to Silas, the way the firelight softened the lines on Morwenna’s face and the unshakeable peace that filled this cold lightless hole in the earth.

’I really enjoy my time with them...’ Thor mused, her rugged face softening with an unfamiliar warmth. ’It’s strange. For a long time, I walked between halls of gold and blood. Gods bickering over celestial thrones, titans breaking stars... it was all so loud and so heavy but here... sharing cold pork in a dirt hole, watching mortal women brawl over a sleeping spot... it feels so wonderfully normal.’
She looked at Silas.
The mortal had his eyes closed now with his breathing steady, his hand resting protectively over the elven girl’s spine.
He carried the weight of an entire territory, yet he bore it without the hollow arrogance of the kings she had slaughtered in the past.

’Maybe next time... I will join their foolish block game,’ Thor thought with a quiet, internal rumble of amusement. ’I could easily crush their runes so dragging for Silas’s chest might be an entertaining diversion.’
Then, a sudden dark cloud passed behind Thor’s storm-blue irises as her broad jaw tightened and her teeth clicked together with a sharp suppressed grind.
’Loki...’
The name hung in the back of her divine mind like a venomous needle.
Her sister’s senses were everywhere.
The Trickster had eyes woven into the dimensional fabric of modern Earth, watching the noble families and tracking the movement of divine relics.
Once the Princess returned with her, Loki would take notice and once Loki discovered that Thor had forged an emotional attachment to this mortal... it was only a matter of time before she descended.
Thor’s fingers dug into the basalt beneath her blanket, cracking the stone to dust.

The thought of seeing Silas’s calm eyes glazed over by Loki’s emerald illusions... the thought of seeing him kneeling beneath her sister’s silver tongue with his mind hollowed out into a laughing puppet... it made the thunder in Thor’s blood surge with pure murderous fury.
’How do I prevent her from finding this place...?’ Thor questioned silently, her eyes fixed on his sleeping profile. ’What should I do to shield him...?’
She had no answer as only the quiet crackle of Aurelia’s flame to keep the shadows at bay.
Four hours later, the change came.
It was not a sudden burst of light, but a slow sweeping absence.
Through the thick barrier of Eluned’s root wall, the wet relentless scraping of the leeches began to falter.
The heavy suffocating pressure that had weighed against the stone like deep water gradually thinned, draining away into the lower fault lines of the basin.
The necrotic fog was gone.
Silas opened his eyes with his Gold Core flared to life instantly, sweeping away the cobwebs of sleep with a single cycle of golden heat.
"Aeli," he whispered, gently tapping the high-elf’s shoulder. "Shift’s over, little secretary. Time to move."
Aeliana stirred, letting out a tiny sleepy mumble and her eyelids fluttered open, her silver-gold eyes meeting his at point-blank range.
It took her precisely two seconds to realize that her face was buried in his neck and her legs were still clamped around his thighs in a vice.
"Haah!"
Aeliana scrambled backward so violently she nearly collided with the sleeping Thor.
Her spectacles flew off her nose with her hands flailing as her face turned the color of a blazing forge fire.
"L-L-LORD SILAS!" she squeaked, grabbing her ledger to hide her entire face. "I... my I apologize... the cold was..."
Silas chuckled, pushing himself up to his feet and adjusting his tunic.
"Save the apologies, Aeli. You kept me warm. Pack your bags."

"Up and at ’em, girls!" Morwenna’s voice rang out, her boots already crunching across the stone as she buckled Tidebringer to her hip. "The air’s clean! Let’s get our boots on the trail before the sludge comes back!"
Eluned yawned delicately, stepping to the cavern mouth as she tapped her living staff against the floor.
KRA-CRACK!
The massive interwoven roots uncoiled, retracting smoothly back into the stone frame with a dry wooden hiss.
The late morning air struck them like a physical blow.
It was completely scrubbed of the foul, coppery rot that had choked the gorge earlier.

High above, the tangled black canopy of the forest still partially shadowed the path, but the sky had opened up, dumping silent sheets of powdery white snow that blanketed the crags in pristine ivory.
Silas mounted Valkyrie with fluid grace, pulling the heavy silver-threaded hood of his cloak over his dark hair.
"Strike formation!" Silas commanded. "Tasmin, take point and wolves on my mark!"
HOWOOOOOOOL!
Titan and Valkyrie lunged from the cavern shelf simultaneously, their broad paws pulverizing the snowdrifts as they hit the gorge floor.
The eight Blessed Wolves hit a thundering coordinated dead sprint, their bodies cutting through the powder like high-speed cutters through foam.
All of the girls felt completely refreshed.
The warm venison, the hours of rest, and the relief of escaping the fog had restored their combat edges to razor sharpness.
Riding bareback atop Titan, her blonde locks whipping freely in the freezing wind, Thor let out a broad breathless grin.
’It feels nice...’ Thor thought, her knuckles tightening around the leather reins. ’It feels like... being a soldier.’
For centuries, her existence had been a monotonous cycle of celestial boredom.
Wrestling three-headed cosmic leviathans, shattering void-beasts with a single flick of her hammer... it was so effortless that it had lost all flavor.
It was dull but this... riding in a tight wedge with mortal companions, watching their flanks, feeling the rhythm of the wolves’ breath, the bite of real mountain air...
This was anything but boring! It was magnificent even and it made her feel alive!
Thor grinned wildly, leaning forward over Titan’s muscular neck.
"HYAH!" Thor roared, slapping her heels into the Alpha’s flanks. "Run, beast! Show these mountain crags how the northern skies move!"
Titan let out a thundering roar, surging three paces ahead of the column, breaking the tight wedge formation.
"Thor, check your speed!" Tasmin shouted over the wind, her daggers gleaming as she adjusted her line. "You’re dragging the vanguard’s spacing out! Keep the flanks tight!"
Thor blinked, her triumphant grin instantly withering into a comical sheepish pout.
Her shoulders slumped and her storm-blue eyes dropped downcast toward Titan’s ears like a reprimanded schoolgirl.
"I was merely... going faster..." Thor grumbled beneath her breath.
Silas brought Valkyrie alongside her, glancing at the towering warrior with a warm approving smirk.

"Good pace, Thor," Silas praised, his voice carrying easily over the rushing gale. "Your mount is moving well so just keep him half a stride behind my flank so we don’t trip the formation’s blind spots."
Thor’s eyes widened slightly.
The downcast pout vanished, her lips curving upward into a wide pleased smile that reached her eyes.
’For some reason...’ Thor thought, pulling Titan back into the designated slot with her heart feeling curiously light, ’hearing compliments from this mortal brings a real smile to my face.’
Silas turned his focus back to the horizon, exhaling a quiet relieved breath.
’I can’t feel it anymore,’ he thought, monitoring his internal circuits. ’The crawling oily oppression that came with that necrotic fog is completely gone. The air is clean.’
For the next four miles, the detachment ate up the distance with terrifying efficiency.
The high basalt walls gradually receded, and the suffocating canopy of twisted pines began to thin with the trees growing sparser as the trail approached the lip of a massive geological shelf.
By late evening, the bruised purple-gray sky was beginning to streak with dark crimson at the edges of the jagged mountain horizon.
Suddenly, a low concussive vibration began to shudder through the bedrock beneath the wolves’ paws.
It was not an earthquake.
It was the sound of thousands of tons of living muscle, iron carapaces, and shattered bone grinding against each other.
A deafening chaotic cacophony of guttural roars, shrieking mandibles, and wet rending flesh rolled across the open terrain.
Silas pulled Valkyrie down to a controlled lope, glancing back over his shoulder toward the secretary.
"Aeli! Are we on time?!" Silas called out. "We’re leaving the timberline!"
Aeliana leaned over her wolf’s shoulder with her fingers rapidly tracing the lines across her book.

"We are making good time, Lord Silas!" Aeliana reported loudly. "We are roughly twenty-two minutes behind the schedule due to the rest interval, but our velocity is holding steady! Once we clear this clearing, the descent canyon is less than five leagues north!"

"Eyes sharp, everyone!" Silas commanded with his hand locking firmly around the hilt of his golden longsword. "Listen to those impacts... We have mass movement up ahead. If we can bypass it, we do so. The priority is burning the lost time from our rest, not collecting trophies."
"Agreed!" Morwenna called out from the rear.
The Blessed Wolves crested the final ridge of black shale and every single rider, even the obsidian bird, instantly froze.
"By the stars..." the Princess whispered, her hands flying to her mouth.
Before them stretched an enormous, sunken plateau... a lightless expanse nearly a mile wide, flanked by towering glaciers of blue ice.
The entire basin floor was a churning sea of carnage.
It was like two unstoppably violent tides of monstrosities had collided head-on in the center of the clearing.

On the western side surged a massive horde of pale multi-legged horrors... hundreds if not a thousand of burrowing crawlers, acid-spitting carapaces, and armored centipedes tearing out of the deep earth.

Crashing into them from the east was an equally colossal army of mutated frost beasts... Spine-Hounds the size of horses, horned ice-bears with crystallized claws, and winged carrion-drakes dropping from the clouds.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The sounds of violence were deafening.
Limbs were torn from sockets, carapaces were shattered under multi-ton impacts, and geysers of black, green, and azure blood painted the snow in violent abstract murals of slaughter.
Silas’s blue eyes narrowed to cold slits.

’I’ve only seen this kind of monster volume during the early founding days...’ Silas thought. ’When the territory was still an open beacon and the first waves crashed against our crude palisades. The monsters around the Keep eventually learned to fear our steel but even then... Was it ever this much?’
VUUUM!
Silas analyzed.
His vision swam with rapid data.
[Target Analyzed: Glacial Bone-Shatterer (Tier 4 Boss)]
[Target Analyzed: Abyssal Carapace-Titan (Tier 4 Boss)]
[Target Analyzed: Frost-Gilded Basilisk (Tier 4 Boss)]
Right in the center of the bloodbath, three Tier 4 entities were currently engaged in a three-way brawl.

Two of them resembled large armadillos encased in layered plates of petrified, glowing blue basalt that deflected every blow like solid fortress walls and their spiked tails whipping through the air with enough force to level a building with every swing.

The third was a mutated serpentine monstrosity with six jointed limbs and an armored crown of frozen bone, snapping its jaws shut with concussive cracks that pulverized dozens of lesser beasts into red mist with every strike.
Silas’s jaw tightened.
’Well, damn. Multiple Tier 4s tearing each other apart.’
High above, the obsidian bird fluttered erratically, hovering three feet above Silas’s head.
The power of colliding high-tier mana was rattling its crystalline feathers, making it let out a panicked wheezing series of clicks as it refused to fly into the storm of shockwaves.
"Silas!" Tasmin pointed her dagger toward the eastern perimeter. "Look there! Along the cliff base!"
Silas’s eyes followed her blade.
