chapters.title: Chapter 511: ...Swallowed...?
paragraphs: Because the three Tier 4 titans had dragged the center of gravity into the heart of the plateau, the extreme eastern lip of the clearing... running beneath an overhanging shelf of solid granite was relatively clear.
Only a scattering of bleeding stragglers and minor scavengers were skirting the perimeter.
"We have an opening," Silas said, his voice dropping into razor-sharp focus. "We shouldn’t engage the horde, we ride the wall instead..."
He looked back at the girls.
"We punch through the eastern shelf at maximum velocity and break through to the northern pass."
"What about the stragglers?" Morwenna asked, her gray eyes burning with combative heat as she drew Tidebringer.

"I take point," Silas declared, drawing his golden longsword with a clean shing. "Any beast that steps onto our path gets cut down by my steel... You girls hold the rear and flank lines, keep the Princess covered, and wipe out anything that tries to pursue. Do not decelerate. If you stop, the horde collapses on our flanks."
"Understood!" the women answered in disciplined unison.
"Valkyrie! CHARGE!" Silas roared.
HOWOOOOOOOOOL!
The lead wolf exploded forward.

Valkyrie hit an instantaneous dead sprint with her powerful hindquarters launching her down the shale embankment like a silver missile, creating an immediate fifty-pace gap between Silas and the rest of the formation.
Behind him, the obsidian bird, realizing Silas was carving the path, tucked its wings and shot through the air right beside his shoulder.
"FORWARD!" Morwenna roared, her weapon blazing with heavy-water mana as the seven riders followed in a tight protective wedge behind their Lord.
BOOM!
The sudden radiant intrusion of Silas’s Gold Core immediately drew bloodthirsty attention.

From the churning edge of the horde, three massive eight-legged Grave-Stalkers... their chitinous carapaces dripping with acidic slime spotted the charging wolf and lunged horizontally across the snowdrifts to cut him off!
The obsidian bird let out a terrified shriek, banking wildly to the right.
"Eyes front, bird!" Silas barked! "Hold your line!"
Silas didn’t slow Valkyrie by a fraction of an inch.
VUUUM!
He channeled a surge of dense high-pressure water mana from his core straight into the golden mythril steel of his blade.
The blade began to hum with the deafening, high-pitched scream of a breaking wave.
"Abyssal Sever!"
SHING-FZZZZT!
He executed a clean horizontal flick of his wrist as a razor-thin forty-foot crescent of pressurized aqua energy detonated outward from the blade’s edge.
CHOP-CHOP-CHOP!
The aqua crescent carved through the freezing air at high speed.
It sliced clean through the lead stalker’s armored skull, through the second beast’s torso, and severed the third monster’s front four legs in the span of seconds.
SPLAT!
The three beasts collapsed into the snow, their severed parts skidding across the ice as Valkyrie vaulted directly over their smoking corpses.
"More on the left!" Tasmin shouted from thirty paces behind!
From a high basalt ledge, a cluster of five winged Frost-Gargoyles folded their stony wings, diving toward Silas’s head like falling artillery shells, their talons extended to crush his skull.
Silas didn’t look up as he twisted in his saddle, his core spinning into rotational torque.
He drew ambient moisture from the freezing gale into his lungs, cycled it through his Gold Core, and unleashed the fury of Morwenna’s martial art.
"Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style... Severing Horizon."
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal thirty-foot-wide crescent arc of phantom heavy-water exploded upward from his blade.
The phantom wave hit the diving gargoyles with the concussive, bone-shattering force of an oceanic tsunami.
CRUNCH-CRUNCH-CRUNCH!
The stone-hard gargoyles were violently crushed into pulverized gravel mid-air with their bodies exploding into gray dust before they could even scream.
"And stay down," Silas muttered.
Before the airborne moisture could dissipate, he flicked his left hand toward the falling debris, releasing the next spell.
"Ice Transformation!"
FROOOOO-SH!

The pulverized mist and heavy-water residue instantly flash-froze into a massive twenty-foot wall of crystalline ice spears that slammed down behind Valkyrie’s tail, completely barricading the eastern flank from the main horde.
From the rear of the column, Morwenna watched the colossal ice wall erupt with a sharp, toothy grin.
"Tch! Look at him using my art like he was born on a deck," Morwenna clicked her tongue in arrogant pride with her gray eyes burning. "That’s my Captain for you!"
"Don’t lose your focus, Morwenna!" Kadi shouted from her wolf!

Kadi thrust both hands forward, unleashing a roaring torrent of golden sand that caught three leaping Spine-Hounds in mid-air, shredding their flesh into red ribbons before they could breach the perimeter.
Beside her, Aeliana snapped her fingers, opening a vertical spatial tear that cleanly sheared the heads off two pursuing crawlers with a crisp terrifying snik.
"Flank clear, Lord Silas!" Aeliana reported proudly, her spectacles gleaming in the blood-stained snow.
THUD-THUD-THUD!
Valkyrie cleared the final basalt shelf, bursting cleanly out of the eastern gorge and onto the wide unobstructed snowfields of the northern pass.
The sounds of the clashing monster armies abruptly fell behind them, muffled by the granite wall they had just skirted...
They had made it through.
Silas pulled Valkyrie around in a smooth sweeping turn, bringing the dire wolf to a halt as the rest of the detachment thundered up behind him.
He stood tall in his stirrups, looking down at his seven warrior maidens with a broad radiant smile.
He raised his right hand, flashing them a clean effortless peace sign with two fingers.
The girls caught his gaze and every single one of them smiled back.
Tasmin let out a rare genuine chuckle, raising two fingers in an identical peace sign.
Aurelia offered a gentle smile, mirroring the gesture with her slender hand.
Kadi and Aeliana grinned brightly, flashing their peace signs with flushed triumphant cheeks, while the Princess practically bounced in her saddle.
’Eh... it’s a bit cringe but whatever.’
She did it.
Even Thor, looking at the gesture, threw her head back with a booming laugh, raising two calloused fingers high into the freezing air.
"Gwahahaha! Victory!"
Behind them, five desperate Spine-Hounds managed to scramble over the ice wall, snapping their jaws as they lunged in a frantic pursuit—
SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING!
Morwenna didn’t even turn her head.
She simply brandished Tidebringer in a lazy backhanded arc behind her flank as an invisible crescent of vacuum wind sliced across the trail.
CHOP!
All five hounds were decapitated in a single fluid stroke, their severed heads rolling into the snowdrifts as Morwenna casually slid the blade back into its scabbard with a crisp clack.
"Too slow, you mangy mutts," Morwenna mocked coolly with a triumphant smirk curling her lips. "Go chew on some shale."
She looked back toward Silas, her smirk widening as she raised her hand to return his peace sign.
Silas was still facing away from the trail, looking down at his companions with that warm reassuring smile.
Because he was facing backward... he didn’t notice.
No... it wasn’t a matter of noticing.
It was simply too fast.
SZZZZZZZZZZT!
From the clean empty snow directly beneath Valkyrie’s front paws, a dense plume of milky-white necrotic fog detonated upward like an erupting geyser.
High above, the obsidian bird let out an ear-splitting, shrieking rattle of pure horror.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK! CAW! CAW!"
The whiteout rose in an imperceptible fraction of a microsecond!
Thor’s storm-blue eyes dilated violently as the divine thunder in her veins flared to life with her muscles coiling to launch across the ten paces separating them—
KRA-FLASH!
Before the God of Thunder could take a single step... before Morwenna’s blade could clear the hilt... before Eluned’s roots could even twitch in the soil—
SNAP!
The blinding white vapor collapsed inward with the concussive hollow pop of an imploding vacuum as the fog vanished.
The air was clean once more.
The falling snow continued its lazy silent descent from the gray sky.
Valkyrie was standing alone in the center of the trail with her head lowered, sniffing the disturbed snowdrifts with a confused whimper.
The saddle was empty and Silas... had completely vanished.
’Strange...’
The thought had barely crossed Silas’s mind before the cold seized him.
He had felt the unnatural power of this whiteout before, back when the pale ribbons clung to the basalt slopes, but this was different.
The instant it gathered around his boots, the air didn’t just chill... it liquefied into pure suffocating malice.
Every instinct honed through countless skirmishes screamed that this was an active trap but before his muscles could even coil to kick free of Valkyrie’s stirrups, reality folded.
The snowy pass, the triumphant cheers of the girls, and Morwenna sheathing Tidebringer were ripped away in an imperceptible fraction of seconds.
Light vanished and sound died as his vision was violently submerged in pitch-black void... a spatial dislocation so abrupt it made his inner ear spin and his Gold Core lurch against his ribs.
The sensory blackout lasted only an instant.
FWOOOOOOSH!
Freezing air battered Silas’s face as gravity violently reasserted itself.
He was tumbling through empty space, plummeting out of a lightless ceiling toward jagged frost-bitten ground dozens of feet below.
A frantic fluttering sound cut through the rush of the wind beside his ear.
"SQUAWWWK!"
The obsidian bird was tumbling through the empty air right beside him with its dark crystalline wings flailing in blind panic as it plummeted headfirst.
"Haah... What is this...?"
Silas reacted without a breath of hesitation.
He extended his right arm, snapping his gloved fingers out to create a steady perch.
The bird recognized the lifeline instantly, banking its wings and latching its sharp talons onto his reinforced leather vambrace with a desperate clattering grip.
VUUUM!

With his left hand free, Silas channeled a controlled pulse of atmospheric wind mana through his palm, releasing a foundational burst of [Hurricane Repulsion] downward against the approaching bedrock.
BOOM!
The concussive downward shockwave met the frozen stone floor, decelerating his terminal velocity in an instant.

Silas hit the permafrost in a low three-point crouch with the kinetic dispersion woven into his silver-threaded cloak absorbing the remaining force as a small concussive ring of pulverized frost rippled outward from his boots.
He straightened slowly, his breath steadying into pale quiet wisps and the air here was dead.
It was an enormous cavern, far beneath the surface ridges of the basin as the ceiling was lost in high shadows, but curling across the jagged floor was that same milky-white creeping fog.
It didn’t rush or surge like before... it drifted with the bloated laziness of a well-fed serpent.
"Strange."
The bird gave him a look, was he not bothered about all this?!
Silas looked down at his arm.
The obsidian bird was perched on his wrist, its crested head twitching rapidly, its small beady eyes dilated with unmistakable terror.
"Do you know this specific part?" Silas asked quietly.
The bird bobbed its beak once in a stiff trembling nod but it didn’t flap. It crouched low against his forearm, its crystalline feathers trembling against the cold leather.
Silas turned his gaze outward, letting his eyes adjust to the pale gloom.
As the fog drifted across the uneven stone, the terrain revealed itself as littering the cavern floor in every direction were skeletons.
...Hundreds of them.
They weren’t human bones.

These were the colossal petrified remains of ancient beasts... massive five-yard-wide rib cages arching out of the permafrost like shattered ships, skulls the size of carriages with broken horns, and serpentine spinal columns coiled in frozen agony.
Every single skeleton was hollowed out, their marrow long since dissolved, coated in the pale frosted residue of the necrotic mist.
The bird let out a sharp mournful squawk that rattled off the distant stone pillars.
Silas exhaled a slow frosty breath.
He really didn’t need Eluned to translate the bird’s panic this time as the environmental pressure weighing against his Gold Core told the entire story.
"We’re in the Domain of one of those Tier 5 monsters... and the one behind the fog, right?" Silas murmured.
The bird snapped its beak shut, nodding frantically with its talons digging deeper into his vambrace as if begging him to turn back, find a crack in the wall, and run.
Silas stared into the sprawling graveyard.
A Tier 5 monster huh?
A slow smile crept across Silas’s lips.
SHING!
With a crisp ringing draw of steel, the golden mythril longsword cleared its scabbard, illuminating the creeping white mist with the radiant glow of his Gold Core.
The light cut through the pale gloom, casting long defiant shadows behind the towering rib cages.
"What are we waiting for then?" Silas chuckled. "Let’s go kill it."
He stepped forward, his combat boots crunching steadily through the brittle frost and bone dust as he marched directly toward the deep heart of the fog.
The obsidian bird puffed its feathers, throwing its head back to unleash a high-pitched squawk of pure indignant outrage.
"SQUAWWWWWK! KRR-CLACK! CAW!"
Silas didn’t even look back.
He gave his wrist a sharp dismissive flick, cutting through the bird’s frantic scolding without breaking his stride.
"Shut up, bird," Silas muttered with an amused smirk with his grip tightening around the golden hilt. "Have some balls... We’ve got a monster to hunt."

sentences.text: Because the three Tier 4 titans had dragged the center of gravity into the heart of the plateau, the extreme eastern lip of the clearing... running beneath an overhanging shelf of solid granite was relatively clear.
Only a scattering of bleeding stragglers and minor scavengers were skirting the perimeter.
"We have an opening," Silas said, his voice dropping into razor-sharp focus.
"We shouldn’t engage the horde, we ride the wall instead..."
He looked back at the girls.
"We punch through the eastern shelf at maximum velocity and break through to the northern pass."
"What about the stragglers?" Morwenna asked, her gray eyes burning with combative heat as she drew Tidebringer.
"I take point," Silas declared, drawing his golden longsword with a clean shing.
"Any beast that steps onto our path gets cut down by my steel...
You girls hold the rear and flank lines, keep the Princess covered, and wipe out anything that tries to pursue.
Do not decelerate.
If you stop, the horde collapses on our flanks."
"Understood!" the women answered in disciplined unison.
"Valkyrie!
CHARGE!" Silas roared.
HOWOOOOOOOOOL!
The lead wolf exploded forward.

Valkyrie hit an instantaneous dead sprint with her powerful hindquarters launching her down the shale embankment like a silver missile, creating an immediate fifty-pace gap between Silas and the rest of the formation.
Behind him, the obsidian bird, realizing Silas was carving the path, tucked its wings and shot through the air right beside his shoulder.
"FORWARD!" Morwenna roared, her weapon blazing with heavy-water mana as the seven riders followed in a tight protective wedge behind their Lord.
BOOM!
The sudden radiant intrusion of Silas’s Gold Core immediately drew bloodthirsty attention.

From the churning edge of the horde, three massive eight-legged Grave-Stalkers... their chitinous carapaces dripping with acidic slime spotted the charging wolf and lunged horizontally across the snowdrifts to cut him off!
The obsidian bird let out a terrified shriek, banking wildly to the right.
"Eyes front, bird!" Silas barked!
"Hold your line!"
Silas didn’t slow Valkyrie by a fraction of an inch.
VUUUM!
He channeled a surge of dense high-pressure water mana from his core straight into the golden mythril steel of his blade.
The blade began to hum with the deafening, high-pitched scream of a breaking wave.
"Abyssal Sever!"
SHING-FZZZZT!
He executed a clean horizontal flick of his wrist as a razor-thin forty-foot crescent of pressurized aqua energy detonated outward from the blade’s edge.
CHOP-CHOP-CHOP!
The aqua crescent carved through the freezing air at high speed.
It sliced clean through the lead stalker’s armored skull, through the second beast’s torso, and severed the third monster’s front four legs in the span of seconds.
SPLAT!
The three beasts collapsed into the snow, their severed parts skidding across the ice as Valkyrie vaulted directly over their smoking corpses.
"More on the left!" Tasmin shouted from thirty paces behind!
From a high basalt ledge, a cluster of five winged Frost-Gargoyles folded their stony wings, diving toward Silas’s head like falling artillery shells, their talons extended to crush his skull.
Silas didn’t look up as he twisted in his saddle, his core spinning into rotational torque.
He drew ambient moisture from the freezing gale into his lungs, cycled it through his Gold Core, and unleashed the fury of Morwenna’s martial art.
"Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style...
Severing Horizon."
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal thirty-foot-wide crescent arc of phantom heavy-water exploded upward from his blade.
The phantom wave hit the diving gargoyles with the concussive, bone-shattering force of an oceanic tsunami.
CRUNCH-CRUNCH-CRUNCH!
The stone-hard gargoyles were violently crushed into pulverized gravel mid-air with their bodies exploding into gray dust before they could even scream.
"And stay down," Silas muttered.
Before the airborne moisture could dissipate, he flicked his left hand toward the falling debris, releasing the next spell.
"Ice Transformation!"
FROOOOO-SH!

The pulverized mist and heavy-water residue instantly flash-froze into a massive twenty-foot wall of crystalline ice spears that slammed down behind Valkyrie’s tail, completely barricading the eastern flank from the main horde.
From the rear of the column, Morwenna watched the colossal ice wall erupt with a sharp, toothy grin.
"Tch!
Look at him using my art like he was born on a deck," Morwenna clicked her tongue in arrogant pride with her gray eyes burning.
"That’s my Captain for you!"
"Don’t lose your focus, Morwenna!" Kadi shouted from her wolf!

Kadi thrust both hands forward, unleashing a roaring torrent of golden sand that caught three leaping Spine-Hounds in mid-air, shredding their flesh into red ribbons before they could breach the perimeter.
Beside her, Aeliana snapped her fingers, opening a vertical spatial tear that cleanly sheared the heads off two pursuing crawlers with a crisp terrifying snik.
"Flank clear, Lord Silas!" Aeliana reported proudly, her spectacles gleaming in the blood-stained snow.
THUD-THUD-THUD!
Valkyrie cleared the final basalt shelf, bursting cleanly out of the eastern gorge and onto the wide unobstructed snowfields of the northern pass.
The sounds of the clashing monster armies abruptly fell behind them, muffled by the granite wall they had just skirted...
They had made it through.
Silas pulled Valkyrie around in a smooth sweeping turn, bringing the dire wolf to a halt as the rest of the detachment thundered up behind him.
He stood tall in his stirrups, looking down at his seven warrior maidens with a broad radiant smile.
He raised his right hand, flashing them a clean effortless peace sign with two fingers.
The girls caught his gaze and every single one of them smiled back.
Tasmin let out a rare genuine chuckle, raising two fingers in an identical peace sign.
Aurelia offered a gentle smile, mirroring the gesture with her slender hand.
Kadi and Aeliana grinned brightly, flashing their peace signs with flushed triumphant cheeks, while the Princess practically bounced in her saddle.
’Eh... it’s a bit cringe but whatever.’
She did it.
Even Thor, looking at the gesture, threw her head back with a booming laugh, raising two calloused fingers high into the freezing air.
"Gwahahaha!
Victory!"
Behind them, five desperate Spine-Hounds managed to scramble over the ice wall, snapping their jaws as they lunged in a frantic pursuit—
SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING!
Morwenna didn’t even turn her head.
She simply brandished Tidebringer in a lazy backhanded arc behind her flank as an invisible crescent of vacuum wind sliced across the trail.
CHOP!
All five hounds were decapitated in a single fluid stroke, their severed heads rolling into the snowdrifts as Morwenna casually slid the blade back into its scabbard with a crisp clack.
"Too slow, you mangy mutts," Morwenna mocked coolly with a triumphant smirk curling her lips.
"Go chew on some shale."
She looked back toward Silas, her smirk widening as she raised her hand to return his peace sign.
Silas was still facing away from the trail, looking down at his companions with that warm reassuring smile.
Because he was facing backward... he didn’t notice.
No... it wasn’t a matter of noticing.
It was simply too fast.
SZZZZZZZZZZT!
From the clean empty snow directly beneath Valkyrie’s front paws, a dense plume of milky-white necrotic fog detonated upward like an erupting geyser.
High above, the obsidian bird let out an ear-splitting, shrieking rattle of pure horror.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK!
CAW!
CAW!"
The whiteout rose in an imperceptible fraction of a microsecond!
Thor’s storm-blue eyes dilated violently as the divine thunder in her veins flared to life with her muscles coiling to launch across the ten paces separating them—
KRA-FLASH!
Before the God of Thunder could take a single step... before Morwenna’s blade could clear the hilt... before Eluned’s roots could even twitch in the soil—
SNAP!
The blinding white vapor collapsed inward with the concussive hollow pop of an imploding vacuum as the fog vanished.
The air was clean once more.
The falling snow continued its lazy silent descent from the gray sky.
Valkyrie was standing alone in the center of the trail with her head lowered, sniffing the disturbed snowdrifts with a confused whimper.
The saddle was empty and Silas... had completely vanished.
’Strange...’
The thought had barely crossed Silas’s mind before the cold seized him.

chapters.title: Chapter 512: What Silas Would Want
paragraphs: A solitary gust of sub-zero wind scoured the lip of the northern shelf, whistling through the empty leather stirrups of Valkyrie’s saddle.
The Blessed wolf stood still with her forepaws braced against the permafrost and her ears twitching forward and back in rapid, agitated ticks.
She lowered her broad muzzle, drawing in a long draught of air from the disturbed snow where Silas had stood less than three seconds prior.
There was no coppery scent of torn flesh and there was no spatial residue of warped mana either.
Behind Valkyrie, the detachment hung suspended in the violent momentum of their halted sprint.
The silence lasted only a heartbeat before it fractured.
"Lord Silas!"
The Princess’s voice snapped through the cold like thin crystal breaking on rock.
She scrambled out of her saddle before her mount had even fully settled its hindquarters with her heavy boots catching in the deep snowdrift as she hit the ground running.

Her azure traveling mantle flared behind her, catching on the jagged spurs of black shale, but she tore it free without looking, stumbling toward Valkyrie with both hands outstretched as if she could gather the empty air back into the shape of a man.
"Lord Silas! Where—where did he—" Her fingers clawed through the empty space above the saddle, meeting only the bitter drafts of the basin.
Her breathing hitched, turning shallow and frantic with the color completely draining from her cheeks until she was as pale as the falling powder.
She whipped around, looking at the stone walls, up at the leaden sky, and then down into the sheer drop of the eastern gorge where the remnants of the monster horde still churned.
"He was right here! He held up his hand! He gave the signal! Where did the mist take him?!"
Beside her, Aeliana slid from her mount with her book slipping from her numbed fingers to tumble into the red-stained slush.
The high-elf secretary didn’t bother to retrieve them.
Her slender hands shot up to the frames of her spectacles, shoving them hard against the bridge of her nose as her silver-gold eyes dilated into wide trembling rings.

"S-Spatial displacement..." Aeliana stammered, her voice thin and high-pitched, vibrating with an edge of terror. "The atmosphere didn’t register a rift... there was no fold... I didn’t feel a tear in anything! If he was drawn into a—"
"Quiet down, long ears," Morwenna’s raspy voice cut across the panicked babble like a lead pipe striking gravel.
The Pirate Queen didn’t dismount.
She sat high on her wolf, leaning forward with her black hair whipping across her gray eyes and her calloused fingers remaining firmly wrapped around the hilt of Tidebringer.
She wasn’t scanning the empty air where Silas had been as she was watching the high basalt ridges and the retreating edge of the whiteout.
"Panic burns breath, and breath is what keeps your blood from freezing in this ditch," Morwenna said, her tone level and completely dry. "Look at the mount."
Tasmin, who had melted into a low crouch five paces to the left with her twin void-daggers cocked in reverse grips, flicked her amber eyes toward Valkyrie.
The dire wolf had stopped sniffing the ground.
She wasn’t howling either and she wasn’t throwing her head back in the death-wail that bonded territorial beasts gave when their master’s life-thread snapped.

Valkyrie shook the dry snow from her shoulders with a violent concussive rattle of her harness, let out a deep annoyed snort that blew two neat holes in the snowdrift, and turned her head back toward Eluned.

"The bond holds," Tasmin rasped, though the muscles along her jaw remained coiled like steel cables. "His core hasn’t flickered... If he were bleeding out, the contracts would be burning cold or that’s how I know this stuff works so he’s alive."
"Of course he is," Thor’s booming voice rumbled from Titan’s back, sounding too casual for the sudden disappearance of their commander.
The God of Thunder leaned back against the high pommel of her saddle, folding her massive muscular arms over her leather cuirass.
She watched the Princess’s frantic pacing with an amused, half-lidded squint, completely unbothered by the sub-zero squall that made the other mortals shiver.

"The man survived a slap of mine into the courtyard without losing his balance, and you think a puff of damp northern smoke is going to digest him?" Thor snorted, shaking her blonde mane. "He’s stubborn as an ox and twice as thick-skulled... If whatever swallowed him tries to chew, it’s going to break a tooth so sit down before you twist your ankle, little royal. You’re fluttering like a sparrow in a thunderstorm."

"How can you be so callous?!" The Princess rounded on the giantess, her small fists clenched at her sides with her royal posture completely shattering beneath raw distress. "He is our leader! He brought us into this frozen wasteland, he took the point position to protect us from that horde, and now he is gone! We don’t know where he was dragged! We don’t know what kind of horrors are in that mist! We have to search the gorge! We have to dig into the fissures! We can’t just stand here while he—"
"Princess."
The word was spoken softly, yet it carried an immovable weight that seemed to vibrate straight out of the earth beneath their soles.
Eluned urged her mount forward by two paces.
The Goddess sat with her spine straight, her emerald-threaded traveling cloak falling in neat unhurried folds over her knees.
Her porcelain face was remarkably serene with the glow of her eyes fitting it well.
She reached out with a pale, slender hand, resting her palm gently atop Valkyrie’s silver head.
The wolf leaned into the touch, letting out a low rumbling whimper of acknowledgment.
"Silas gave standing operational protocols before we embarked on this mission," Eluned said. "Do you recall them, Tasmin?"
Tasmin kept her gaze fixed on the northern pass, answering without hesitation.

"Section Four, In the event of command separation, isolation, or unresolvable spatial fracture, all subordinate units are ordered to execute an immediate fighting retreat toward the territorial perimeter... We fall back to the Keep, consolidate with the rest of the girls, and hold the gate until contact is re-established."
"Precisely," Eluned said with a faint, graceful nod. "If the commander is cut off, the squad preserves the asset line and pulls back to the fortress."
The Princess stared at her, her jaw slack with disbelief. "Pull back...? You... you want us to turn around? Leave him behind?! In this cold?!"
Her voice cracked with indignation, tears of frustration prickling at the corners of her azure eyes.

"You claim to be his wife! You spent the entire night curled against his ribs, begging him to feed you with his own hands, and the moment he is taken, you recite protocol like an uncaring court clerk?! You would abandon him here?!"
Aurelia stepped between the trembling Princess and the Goddess, placing a gentle armored hand on the young maiden’s trembling shoulder.
The Saintess’s touch was warm, radiating with the soft glow of the Argent Flame, easing the hysterical shiver running through the girl’s spine.
"Be at peace," Aurelia murmured softly. "Listen to the whole thing before you judge Miss Eluned’s heart."
Eluned didn’t take offense.

She merely offered the Princess an indulgent smile... the look of an ancient entity humoring a frantic child and her emerald eyes sparkled with a strange, amused warmth as she gently stroked Valkyrie’s silver ears.

"You misunderstand me, little royal," Eluned purred, tilting her head toward the dark northern horizon. "I recited his orders merely to acknowledge that he gave them but I have zero intention of obeying them."
Morwenna let out a sharp raspy bark of laughter.
"Knew it. A good sailor knows when to throw the captain’s rulebook into the drink."

"I am ignoring the retreat order completely," Eluned stated, her tone as matter-of-fact as if she were discussing the afternoon tea service. "Silas expects us to be sensible, which is precisely why he won’t be surprised when we are not but more importantly..."
She closed her eyes, raising her chin toward the biting wind.

From the tip of her wooden staff, a translucent green root sprouted, coiling into the frozen air before disintegrating into tiny specks of emerald mana that drifted northward, caught in the currents of the high-altitude squall.

"I can feel her," Eluned whispered, her eyes opening with sharp, divine clarity. "The Goddess of Beasts... The resonance of her slumbering presence in the Forever Ice is quite weak but vibrates through the permafrost, through the dormant root networks that sleep beneath the rock... I do not need that little avian to find the descent path as I can guide us straight to her chamber."

"And what of Lord Silas?" Aeliana asked, her voice still trembling as she retrieved her spectacles from the snow, wiping the slush onto her sleeve. "If we march to the goddess... we are moving away from where he vanished."
Eluned turned to the high-elf, her lips curling into a smile of absolute, unshakable faith.
"Do you really believe that man was taken to be slaughtered?" Eluned asked softly. "Think about who he is..."
She looked back at the six women, her gaze fierce and filled with certainty.

"I have faith in Silas," Eluned declared. "He is not cowering in a dark corner waiting for a rescue party. He is marching forward. In fact... knowing how his pride works when he is left alone, he will likely carve his way straight through whatever abomination rules that mist and arrive at the Beast Goddess’s tomb long before we even reach the descent lip."
The Princess blinked.
The suffocating knot of panic in her chest loosened slightly, replaced by the infectious ironclad confidence radiating from the Goddess.
Morwenna gave Tidebringer’s scabbard a loud echoing smack against her thigh.
"Aye. The weed’s not entirely useless after all... The Captain’s probably cursing our names right now for not keeping up with him since he hates doing manual labor without an audience."
Aeliana let out a quiet huff that sounded remarkably like a chuckle, her shoulders finally dropping from their rigid posture.
"He does prefer to have his drink poured."
Even Kadi, who had been quietly keeping watch on the rear slope, let out a nervous breathless giggle as she dusted the sand from her leather bracers.
"He’s probably looking around for someone to give him a clean towel right now."
The tension that had threatened to tear the squad into paralyzed fragments evaporated into the crisp mountain air.
The women straightened their backs, the discipline and mutual trust they had built over a long time of territorial labor snapping back into place like a drawn bowstring.

"Mount up!" Eluned commanded, taking the vanguard lead alongside Valkyrie. "We move north! Full lope! Keep the spacing tight and your blades loose! If my husband arrives at the prize before us, I will never hear the end of it at the dinner table!"
"HYAH!"
Eight pairs of powerful hindquarters drove into the permafrost simultaneously, launching the pack into a thundering coordinated gallop along the high shelf.
Behind them, three mutated crawl-scavengers attempted to scramble up the scree in pursuit—
FZZZZZT-CRUNCH!
Kadi didn’t even look back.
A sweeping wave of pressurized golden sand detonated from her palm, scouring the rock face and pulverizing the beasts into red mist before they could crest the rise.
"Rear clear!" Kadi shouted, her voice ringing with newfound confidence.
At the head of the column, riding neck-and-neck with Valkyrie, Eluned looked up at the bruised northern sky with her green hair whipping in the gale as she whispered to the wind.
"He’s probably having fun right now..."
SWOOSH!
A razor-thin crescent of pressurized aqua energy cleaved through the lightless gloom with a deafening high-pitched shriek.
SPLAT-CHOP!

A four-foot-wide bloated fog-aberration... resembling a grotesque, multi-segmented leech with eight blind sensory stalks and a circular maw of needle-teeth was sheared cleanly in half along its horizontal axis.
The two severed halves of the monster tumbled out of the air, splashing into the thick creeping carpet of white mist that covered the cavern floor.
Dark oily ichor sprayed across the black shale, sizzling softly against the permafrost before the fluid dissolved into gray foul-smelling vapor.
Silas flicked the golden mythril longsword in a crisp downward arc.
CLACK!
The blade was immaculate, the golden mana radiating from his Mythic Gold Core actively repelling every stray drop of visceral filth before it could touch the steel.
He drew in a slow icy breath with his golden ringed blue eyes gleaming in focus.
’It’s actually a bit fun,’ Silas thought, a wolfish smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.

The Blessed wolf stood still with her forepaws braced against the permafrost and her ears twitching forward and back in rapid, agitated ticks.
She lowered her broad muzzle, drawing in a long draught of air from the disturbed snow where Silas had stood less than three seconds prior.
There was no coppery scent of torn flesh and there was no spatial residue of warped mana either.
Behind Valkyrie, the detachment hung suspended in the violent momentum of their halted sprint.
The silence lasted only a heartbeat before it fractured.
"Lord Silas!"
The Princess’s voice snapped through the cold like thin crystal breaking on rock.
She scrambled out of her saddle before her mount had even fully settled its hindquarters with her heavy boots catching in the deep snowdrift as she hit the ground running.

Her azure traveling mantle flared behind her, catching on the jagged spurs of black shale, but she tore it free without looking, stumbling toward Valkyrie with both hands outstretched as if she could gather the empty air back into the shape of a man.
"Lord Silas!
Where—where did he—" Her fingers clawed through the empty space above the saddle, meeting only the bitter drafts of the basin.
Her breathing hitched, turning shallow and frantic with the color completely draining from her cheeks until she was as pale as the falling powder.
She whipped around, looking at the stone walls, up at the leaden sky, and then down into the sheer drop of the eastern gorge where the remnants of the monster horde still churned.
"He was right here!
He held up his hand!
He gave the signal!
Where did the mist take him?!"
Beside her, Aeliana slid from her mount with her book slipping from her numbed fingers to tumble into the red-stained slush.
The high-elf secretary didn’t bother to retrieve them.
Her slender hands shot up to the frames of her spectacles, shoving them hard against the bridge of her nose as her silver-gold eyes dilated into wide trembling rings.
"S-Spatial displacement..." Aeliana stammered, her voice thin and high-pitched, vibrating with an edge of terror.
"The atmosphere didn’t register a rift... there was no fold...
I didn’t feel a tear in anything!
If he was drawn into a—"
"Quiet down, long ears," Morwenna’s raspy voice cut across the panicked babble like a lead pipe striking gravel.
The Pirate Queen didn’t dismount.
She sat high on her wolf, leaning forward with her black hair whipping across her gray eyes and her calloused fingers remaining firmly wrapped around the hilt of Tidebringer.
She wasn’t scanning the empty air where Silas had been as she was watching the high basalt ridges and the retreating edge of the whiteout.
"Panic burns breath, and breath is what keeps your blood from freezing in this ditch," Morwenna said, her tone level and completely dry.
"Look at the mount."
Tasmin, who had melted into a low crouch five paces to the left with her twin void-daggers cocked in reverse grips, flicked her amber eyes toward Valkyrie.
The dire wolf had stopped sniffing the ground.
She wasn’t howling either and she wasn’t throwing her head back in the death-wail that bonded territorial beasts gave when their master’s life-thread snapped.

Valkyrie shook the dry snow from her shoulders with a violent concussive rattle of her harness, let out a deep annoyed snort that blew two neat holes in the snowdrift, and turned her head back toward Eluned.
"The bond holds," Tasmin rasped, though the muscles along her jaw remained coiled like steel cables.
"His core hasn’t flickered...
If he were bleeding out, the contracts would be burning cold or that’s how I know this stuff works so he’s alive."
"Of course he is," Thor’s booming voice rumbled from Titan’s back, sounding too casual for the sudden disappearance of their commander.
The God of Thunder leaned back against the high pommel of her saddle, folding her massive muscular arms over her leather cuirass.
She watched the Princess’s frantic pacing with an amused, half-lidded squint, completely unbothered by the sub-zero squall that made the other mortals shiver.
"The man survived a slap of mine into the courtyard without losing his balance, and you think a puff of damp northern smoke is going to digest him?" Thor snorted, shaking her blonde mane.
"He’s stubborn as an ox and twice as thick-skulled...
If whatever swallowed him tries to chew, it’s going to break a tooth so sit down before you twist your ankle, little royal.
You’re fluttering like a sparrow in a thunderstorm."
"How can you be so callous?!" The Princess rounded on the giantess, her small fists clenched at her sides with her royal posture completely shattering beneath raw distress.
"He is our leader!
He brought us into this frozen wasteland, he took the point position to protect us from that horde, and now he is gone!
We don’t know where he was dragged!
We don’t know what kind of horrors are in that mist!
We have to search the gorge!
We have to dig into the fissures!
We can’t just stand here while he—"
"Princess."
The word was spoken softly, yet it carried an immovable weight that seemed to vibrate straight out of the earth beneath their soles.
Eluned urged her mount forward by two paces.
The Goddess sat with her spine straight, her emerald-threaded traveling cloak falling in neat unhurried folds over her knees.
Her porcelain face was remarkably serene with the glow of her eyes fitting it well.
She reached out with a pale, slender hand, resting her palm gently atop Valkyrie’s silver head.
The wolf leaned into the touch, letting out a low rumbling whimper of acknowledgment.
"Silas gave standing operational protocols before we embarked on this mission," Eluned said.
"Do you recall them, Tasmin?"
Tasmin kept her gaze fixed on the northern pass, answering without hesitation.

"Section Four, In the event of command separation, isolation, or unresolvable spatial fracture, all subordinate units are ordered to execute an immediate fighting retreat toward the territorial perimeter...
We fall back to the Keep, consolidate with the rest of the girls, and hold the gate until contact is re-established."
"Precisely," Eluned said with a faint, graceful nod.
"If the commander is cut off, the squad preserves the asset line and pulls back to the fortress."
The Princess stared at her, her jaw slack with disbelief.
"Pull back...?
You... you want us to turn around?
Leave him behind?!
In this cold?!"
Her voice cracked with indignation, tears of frustration prickling at the corners of her azure eyes.
"You claim to be his wife!
You spent the entire night curled against his ribs, begging him to feed you with his own hands, and the moment he is taken, you recite protocol like an uncaring court clerk?!
You would abandon him here?!"
Aurelia stepped between the trembling Princess and the Goddess, placing a gentle armored hand on the young maiden’s trembling shoulder.
The Saintess’s touch was warm, radiating with the soft glow of the Argent Flame, easing the hysterical shiver running through the girl’s spine.
"Be at peace," Aurelia murmured softly.
"Listen to the whole thing before you judge Miss Eluned’s heart."
Eluned didn’t take offense.

She merely offered the Princess an indulgent smile... the look of an ancient entity humoring a frantic child and her emerald eyes sparkled with a strange, amused warmth as she gently stroked Valkyrie’s silver ears.
"You misunderstand me, little royal," Eluned purred, tilting her head toward the dark northern horizon.
"I recited his orders merely to acknowledge that he gave them but I have zero intention of obeying them."
Morwenna let out a sharp raspy bark of laughter.
"Knew it.
A good sailor knows when to throw the captain’s rulebook into the drink."
"I am ignoring the retreat order completely," Eluned stated, her tone as matter-of-fact as if she were discussing the afternoon tea service.
"Silas expects us to be sensible, which is precisely why he won’t be surprised when we are not but more importantly..."
She closed her eyes, raising her chin toward the biting wind.

From the tip of her wooden staff, a translucent green root sprouted, coiling into the frozen air before disintegrating into tiny specks of emerald mana that drifted northward, caught in the currents of the high-altitude squall.
"I can feel her," Eluned whispered, her eyes opening with sharp, divine clarity.
"The Goddess of Beasts...
The resonance of her slumbering presence in the Forever Ice is quite weak but vibrates through the permafrost, through the dormant root networks that sleep beneath the rock...
I do not need that little avian to find the descent path as I can guide us straight to her chamber."
"And what of Lord Silas?" Aeliana asked, her voice still trembling as she retrieved her spectacles from the snow, wiping the slush onto her sleeve.
"If we march to the goddess... we are moving away from where he vanished."
Eluned turned to the high-elf, her lips curling into a smile of absolute, unshakable faith.
"Do you really believe that man was taken to be slaughtered?" Eluned asked softly.
"Think about who he is..."
She looked back at the six women, her gaze fierce and filled with certainty.
"I have faith in Silas," Eluned declared.
"He is not cowering in a dark corner waiting for a rescue party.
He is marching forward.

In fact... knowing how his pride works when he is left alone, he will likely carve his way straight through whatever abomination rules that mist and arrive at the Beast Goddess’s tomb long before we even reach the descent lip."
The Princess blinked.
The suffocating knot of panic in her chest loosened slightly, replaced by the infectious ironclad confidence radiating from the Goddess.
Morwenna gave Tidebringer’s scabbard a loud echoing smack against her thigh.
"Aye.
The weed’s not entirely useless after all...
The Captain’s probably cursing our names right now for not keeping up with him since he hates doing manual labor without an audience."
Aeliana let out a quiet huff that sounded remarkably like a chuckle, her shoulders finally dropping from their rigid posture.
"He does prefer to have his drink poured."
Even Kadi, who had been quietly keeping watch on the rear slope, let out a nervous breathless giggle as she dusted the sand from her leather bracers.
"He’s probably looking around for someone to give him a clean towel right now."
The tension that had threatened to tear the squad into paralyzed fragments evaporated into the crisp mountain air.
The women straightened their backs, the discipline and mutual trust they had built over a long time of territorial labor snapping back into place like a drawn bowstring.
"Mount up!" Eluned commanded, taking the vanguard lead alongside Valkyrie.
"We move north!
Full lope!
Keep the spacing tight and your blades loose!
If my husband arrives at the prize before us, I will never hear the end of it at the dinner table!"
"HYAH!"
Eight pairs of powerful hindquarters drove into the permafrost simultaneously, launching the pack into a thundering coordinated gallop along the high shelf.
Behind them, three mutated crawl-scavengers attempted to scramble up the scree in pursuit—
FZZZZZT-CRUNCH!
Kadi didn’t even look back.
A sweeping wave of pressurized golden sand detonated from her palm, scouring the rock face and pulverizing the beasts into red mist before they could crest the rise.
"Rear clear!" Kadi shouted, her voice ringing with newfound confidence.
At the head of the column, riding neck-and-neck with Valkyrie, Eluned looked up at the bruised northern sky with her green hair whipping in the gale as she whispered to the wind.
"He’s probably having fun right now..."
SWOOSH!
A razor-thin crescent of pressurized aqua energy cleaved through the lightless gloom with a deafening high-pitched shriek.
SPLAT-CHOP!

A four-foot-wide bloated fog-aberration... resembling a grotesque, multi-segmented leech with eight blind sensory stalks and a circular maw of needle-teeth was sheared cleanly in half along its horizontal axis.
The two severed halves of the monster tumbled out of the air, splashing into the thick creeping carpet of white mist that covered the cavern floor.
Dark oily ichor sprayed across the black shale, sizzling softly against the permafrost before the fluid dissolved into gray foul-smelling vapor.
Silas flicked the golden mythril longsword in a crisp downward arc.
CLACK!
The blade was immaculate, the golden mana radiating from his Mythic Gold Core actively repelling every stray drop of visceral filth before it could touch the steel.
He drew in a slow icy breath with his golden ringed blue eyes gleaming in focus.
’It’s actually a bit fun,’ Silas thought, a wolfish smirk tugging at the corner of his lips.

chapters.title: Chapter 513: Forces Of The Fog [I]
paragraphs: Back at Blessed Land, his days were consumed by work.
It was necessary work, the foundational labor of building an empire, but it rarely gave him an excuse to simply unleash his core.

He hadn’t stood on an open field with a bare blade and nothing to manage but the trajectory of incoming steel in a while but out here, deep beneath the basin’s crust, there really was nothing to balance.
There was only distance, momentum, and things that needed to be cut down.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK!"
The ear-splitting screech rattled against Silas’s eardrum from barely three inches away.
The obsidian bird, still clamped to his left leather vambrace with a white-knuckled bone-deep grip, flapped its crystalline wings erratically, snapping its scythe-curved beak toward the ceiling.

From the high shadows of an overhanging basalt arch, a second leech... twice the length of the first, its pale rubbery hide covered in weeping bioluminescent yellow boils lunged silently through the air like an uncoiling spring with its maw wide as it was aiming straight for the back of Silas’s neck!
Silas didn’t even turn his head.
His reaction was pure reflex as he stepped half a pace to the left, pivoting on his heel with efficiency.
The lunging monster missed his shoulder by less than two inches with the cold rush of its displacement whipping the fur trim of his coat.
As the beast sailed past, Silas raised his empty left hand, pointing his index and middle fingers directly at its bloated underbelly.
"Currents of the deep, compress and divide," Silas murmured. "Water that shears the stone, form the edge... Abyssal Sever."
There really were times when one wanted to say the chant and right now was a very good example.
SHING!
A five-foot crescent of compressed aqua mana detonated from his fingertips at point-blank range.
SQUELCH-BOOM!

The pressurized water blade didn’t just slice the worm as the hydraulic shock wave expanded inside its rubbery cavity, blowing the entire twelve-foot creature into thousands of tiny shredded chunks of gray meat that rained harmlessly across the stone floor.
"What a weird place..." Silas muttered, lowering his hand and shaking his head.
He looked around, taking in the suffocating scale of the subterranean expanse.
The cavern was colossal... so vast that the jagged tooth-like stalactites hanging from the ceiling were lost in pitch-black shadow hundreds of feet above.
The ground was an uneven wasteland of petrified black shale, broken granite pillars, and fossilized ribcages that curved out of the permafrost like the frames of sunken galleons.
And drifting through it all, thick as curdled milk, was that relentless, unnatural white fog.
It wasn’t rising from the floor like normal swamp vapor... It pulsed instead.
’Eerie shit.’

Every few seconds, a low-frequency atmospheric wave would ripple through the cavern, causing the mist to swirl and thicken, rolling across the stone in lazy tides that reduced visibility to less than twenty paces.

’From what I can gather,’ Silas analyzed, his mind cataloging the environmental anomalies, ’This isn’t just an abandoned cave system... This is an active nesting ground. The domain of that Tier 5 monster that anchors the fog cycle and we’re walking straight down its throat.’
He glanced down at his boots as the mist had risen to his shins, clinging to his trousers like freezing greasy cobwebs.
’The density is increasing the further we march inward which means the core entity is sitting right in the center of this web.’
He let out an exasperated breathy sigh with his brow furrowing as he looked down at his left wrist.
The obsidian bird was trembling violently.

Its beady crystalline eyes were darting from shadow to shadow, its head twitching in rapid paranoid ticks, its claws digging so hard into his reinforced vambrace that the leather was beginning to groove.
"Why the hell am I down here alone with this useless feathered ornament...?" Silas grumbled aloud, his tone sounding thoroughly unimpressed.
He gave his arm a firm annoyed shake, but the bird only squawked in terror and clamped its talons down even harder.

"Seriously," Silas muttered, rolling his eyes toward the ceiling. "If the spatial trap had to grab someone, why couldn’t it take Valkyrie? At least she has teeth... She has four legs, she doesn’t screech in my ear every time a worm drops from the ceiling, and she’s infinitely more useful in a scrap than a paranoid crow."
The bird looked up at him, its crested head tilting as if it understood every single insult, letting out an offended sound.
"Krrr-clack!"
"Don’t give me that look," Silas scoffed, stepping over a shattered rib bone. "You’re supposed to be a divine guide... So far, all you’ve done is use my shoulder as a perch and scream at shadows."
He paused, looking back over his shoulder toward the empty mist behind him.
The immediate silence of the deep cavern made him pause. For a brief second, his thoughts drifted back to the frozen ridge above.
’Did Eluned follow standing orders?’ he wondered, an amused smirk touching his lips. ’Section Four which said immediate retreat to the perimeter and regroup with Brida.’
He gave a soft dry chuckle, shaking his head.
’Not a chance in hell.’
He knew his women far too well.
The Princess would have panicked naturally, but Eluned’s divine arrogance would never allow her to turn her back on the basin, especially with the Beast Goddess’s signature calling to her.
’I’m sure she can sense her about now...’
Morwenna would rather drown in shale than run from a fight, and Tasmin’s loyalty lay with him, not the manual.
They were marching north and he was certain of it.

"We have to reach the center before they do," Silas said, turning his gaze back into the fog and picking up his pace. "If Eluned and Morwenna find that goddess without me, they’ll spend three weeks arguing over who gets the credit for breaking the seal, and Brida will use my absence as an excuse to turn the keep’s courtyard into an open-air wrestling pit..."
On his arm, the obsidian bird blinked its dark eyes.
It looked at the man’s broad unbothered shoulders, the relaxed rhythmic swing of his longsword, and the casual absence of fear in his posture.
The bird let out a bewildered questioning click.
To the avian familiar, this place was a waking nightmare.
It had flown these corridors for a long time, watching great beasts and ancient heroes enter the whiteout only to be hollowed out into bleached bone.
The entity that ruled this deep pit was a terror of the northern fault lines... a nightmare of necrotic hunger and dampness that had choked entire armies in the old wars against monsters.
Yet this mortal man was walking through the slaughterhouse as if he were taking an afternoon stroll through an orchard, complaining about his schedule and mocking the local fauna.

’Why is he so confident?’ the bird wondered, its small chest heaving with nervous clicks. ’Is there some unfathomable power slumbering within his blood? Or is he simply too ignorant to comprehend the horrors waiting in the dark?’
Silas didn’t bother to explain.
He simply walked.
As they pressed deeper into the cavern, the landscape deteriorated into petrified ruin.
The ground sloped steadily downward, descending into a massive sunken amphitheater of jagged stone.
The air grew increasingly thick, so humid and cold that tiny crystals of greasy rime began forming along the edges of Silas’s cloak.
The milky-white fog rose to his waist, swirling in sluggish eddies with every step he took.
Suddenly, Silas halted.
His boots stopped on the edge of a wide circular clearing flanked by six broken granite monoliths.
Within his chest, the Mythic Gold Core gave a gentle pulse, circulating a warm current of golden mana through his ocular nerves.
’Haah... Good...’
He didn’t just use normal vision either, Silas lightly adjusted the moisture balance within his own eyeballs, tapping into his personal adaptation of Morwenna’s Rip-Current Perception.
The world shifted into high-contrast shades of deep navy and luminous aqua.
Through the dense opaque wall of mist, Silas could finally sense distinct mana signatures.
’Seven... eight... nine,’ Silas counted mentally, his hand tightening around the golden hilt. ’Low-tier monsters, but their cores are strange.’
SH-SH-SH-CLICK!
From the top of the broken monoliths twenty paces ahead, several silhouettes shifted in the gloom.
They were Mist-Spitters... grotesque four-legged aberrations that looked like a repulsive fusion between an armored toad and a bloated tick.
Their slate-gray carapaces were covered in weeping, pressurized vents, and their elongated throats were swelling with sickening bubbling sounds.
PHT-PHT-PHT-PHT!
Without a fraction of warning, four of the beasts fired simultaneously.
From their maws erupted a volley of high-velocity crystallized projectiles...
They weren’t acid like Silas expected.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
They were jagged four-inch spikes of petrified bone-ice, launched with the concussive force of crossbows, whistling through the fog straight toward Silas’s chest and throat.
"SKREEEEE!" The bird shrieked, ducking its head beneath Silas’s wrist but Silas didn’t even blink.
He simply shifted his weight onto his back heel, rotating his shoulders by a fraction of an inch.
TICK-TICK-SHING!

Two of the bone-spikes whistled past his ear, severing a single hair from his temple, while the third struck the flat of his golden longsword with a crisp harmless clang, deflecting harmlessly into the ceiling.
Silas raised his left hand, his palm flat against the incoming fourth spike—
FWOOM!
A tiny razor-sharp vortex of compressed wind erupted from his palm... a small pulse of [Hurricane Repulsion].
The miniature atmospheric barrier caught the bone-spike in mid-air, reversing its target in seconds.
THWACK!
The reflected spike shot backward through the mist, driving clean through the eye of the lead spitter.
The beast let out a muffled wet gurgle, toppling backward off the monolith to crash into the shale with a dull thud.
"Annoying little pests," Silas muttered.
BOOM!
He detonated into motion as his boots shattered the permafrost, launching him across the twenty paces in the space between two heartbeats.
The golden longsword blurred into a radiant arc of sun-bright steel.
SLASH-CRUNCH-SPLAT!
In three clean and terrifyingly efficient strokes, Silas cleaved the remaining three spitters from their perches.
The radiant heat-laced Gold Core mana cauterized the wounds instantly, leaving behind neat smoldering cross-sections of monster flesh that collapsed into the fog without a sound.
He landed lightly on the stone with his breath steady and his sword held low.
"Is that all this fog has to offer?" Silas murmured, stepping over a severed leg. "Just an endless conveyor belt of target practice?"
RUMBLE...
As if the cavern itself had heard his insolent challenge, the ground beneath his boots violently shuddered.
The white fog churned into a violent maelstrom as from the dark fissures lining the amphitheater walls, dozens of glowing red and sickly yellow eyes ignited in the mist!
A high-pitched, wet chittering sound echoed off the basalt ceiling, multiplying until it sounded like a roaring river of scuttling limbs.
"HAUUUUUUHAUHAUUUU!"
A horde of at least forty monsters surged out of the shadows.

There were dozens of the segmented Corpse-Leeches writhing through the air, packs of six-legged Bone-Scuttlers tearing across the stone with diamond-hard claws, and heavy acid-bloated spitters ringing the high ledges!
"SQUAWWWWWWWK!"
The obsidian bird lost its mind completely.

It abandoned Silas’s arm, fluttering frantically into the air with its wings beating a desperate retreat toward the highest farthest ceiling stalactite it could reach, perching on a narrow stone spur and trembling so hard its feathers rattled!
Silas looked up at the fleeing bird, letting out an amused mocking snort.
"Coward," Silas muttered.
He turned back toward the incoming tide of monsters, rolling his shoulders with relaxed fluid grace.
’Forty-odd low tiers... and one large presence hiding in the back.’
His [Rip-Current Perception] caught a heavy mana signature lingering just beyond the edge of the horde... a massive silent silhouette moving through the thickest bank of mist with chilling patience.
’A Tier 4 at least... Let’s see what kind of toys this nest breeds.’
"RAHHHHH!"
The front line of twelve Bone-Scuttlers lunged simultaneously, their jagged claws extended to shred him into kindling.
BOOM!
Silas met them head-on as he didn’t retreat an inch and his golden longsword became a spinning wheel of golden light.
CLANG-SHING-CHOP!
The first scuttler was bisected from snout to tail.
Silas spun on his heel, using the rotational torque to drive the flat of his blade into the second beast’s skull, shattering the bone into powder with pure unassisted physical strength.
He vaulted over the falling corpse with his left hand snapping forward—
"[Incineration Ray]!"
ZAP-BOOOOOOM!
A concentrated pencil-thin beam of pure solar fire erupted from his index finger!

The beam punched clean through the chests of four charging beasts in a straight line, superheating their internal fluids until their carapaces exploded from the inside out in violent, concussive pops of smoldering ash!
SHSHSHK!
Silas ducked low, feeling the wind of three jumping leeches whistle over his head!
Without looking, he thrust his blade straight upward into the belly of the first, channeled a burst of heavy-water mana along the spine, and swept the blade horizontally in a wide arc.
"Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style... Severing Horizon!"
KRA-BOOOOOOM!
A thirty-foot crescent wave of phantom heavy-water exploded outward from his stance.
The hydraulic mass hit the swarm like an avalanche, crushing fifteen monsters against the basalt walls in a single earth-shaking impact.
Shattered carapaces and pulverized bone rained down into the rising mist like hail yet, right in the middle of Silas’s follow-through—
SNAP.
The space directly behind Silas’s right blind spot folded and from the dense whiteout, a massive, terrifying shape materialized out of nothingness.
