Morwenna would rather drown in shale than run from a fight, and Tasmin’s loyalty lay with him, not the manual.
They were marching north and he was certain of it.
"We have to reach the center before they do," Silas said, turning his gaze back into the fog and picking up his pace.

"If Eluned and Morwenna find that goddess without me, they’ll spend three weeks arguing over who gets the credit for breaking the seal, and Brida will use my absence as an excuse to turn the keep’s courtyard into an open-air wrestling pit..."
On his arm, the obsidian bird blinked its dark eyes.
It looked at the man’s broad unbothered shoulders, the relaxed rhythmic swing of his longsword, and the casual absence of fear in his posture.
The bird let out a bewildered questioning click.
To the avian familiar, this place was a waking nightmare.
It had flown these corridors for a long time, watching great beasts and ancient heroes enter the whiteout only to be hollowed out into bleached bone.
The entity that ruled this deep pit was a terror of the northern fault lines... a nightmare of necrotic hunger and dampness that had choked entire armies in the old wars against monsters.
Yet this mortal man was walking through the slaughterhouse as if he were taking an afternoon stroll through an orchard, complaining about his schedule and mocking the local fauna.
’Why is he so confident?’ the bird wondered, its small chest heaving with nervous clicks. ’Is there some unfathomable power slumbering within his blood?
Or is he simply too ignorant to comprehend the horrors waiting in the dark?’
Silas didn’t bother to explain.
He simply walked.
As they pressed deeper into the cavern, the landscape deteriorated into petrified ruin.
The ground sloped steadily downward, descending into a massive sunken amphitheater of jagged stone.
The air grew increasingly thick, so humid and cold that tiny crystals of greasy rime began forming along the edges of Silas’s cloak.
The milky-white fog rose to his waist, swirling in sluggish eddies with every step he took.
Suddenly, Silas halted.
His boots stopped on the edge of a wide circular clearing flanked by six broken granite monoliths.
Within his chest, the Mythic Gold Core gave a gentle pulse, circulating a warm current of golden mana through his ocular nerves.
’Haah...
Good...’
He didn’t just use normal vision either, Silas lightly adjusted the moisture balance within his own eyeballs, tapping into his personal adaptation of Morwenna’s Rip-Current Perception.
The world shifted into high-contrast shades of deep navy and luminous aqua.
Through the dense opaque wall of mist, Silas could finally sense distinct mana signatures.
’Seven... eight... nine,’ Silas counted mentally, his hand tightening around the golden hilt. ’Low-tier monsters, but their cores are strange.’
SH-SH-SH-CLICK!
From the top of the broken monoliths twenty paces ahead, several silhouettes shifted in the gloom.
They were Mist-Spitters... grotesque four-legged aberrations that looked like a repulsive fusion between an armored toad and a bloated tick.
Their slate-gray carapaces were covered in weeping, pressurized vents, and their elongated throats were swelling with sickening bubbling sounds.
PHT-PHT-PHT-PHT!
Without a fraction of warning, four of the beasts fired simultaneously.
From their maws erupted a volley of high-velocity crystallized projectiles...
They weren’t acid like Silas expected.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
They were jagged four-inch spikes of petrified bone-ice, launched with the concussive force of crossbows, whistling through the fog straight toward Silas’s chest and throat.
"SKREEEEE!" The bird shrieked, ducking its head beneath Silas’s wrist but Silas didn’t even blink.
He simply shifted his weight onto his back heel, rotating his shoulders by a fraction of an inch.
TICK-TICK-SHING!

Two of the bone-spikes whistled past his ear, severing a single hair from his temple, while the third struck the flat of his golden longsword with a crisp harmless clang, deflecting harmlessly into the ceiling.
Silas raised his left hand, his palm flat against the incoming fourth spike—
FWOOM!
A tiny razor-sharp vortex of compressed wind erupted from his palm... a small pulse of [Hurricane Repulsion].
The miniature atmospheric barrier caught the bone-spike in mid-air, reversing its target in seconds.
THWACK!
The reflected spike shot backward through the mist, driving clean through the eye of the lead spitter.
The beast let out a muffled wet gurgle, toppling backward off the monolith to crash into the shale with a dull thud.
"Annoying little pests," Silas muttered.
BOOM!
He detonated into motion as his boots shattered the permafrost, launching him across the twenty paces in the space between two heartbeats.
The golden longsword blurred into a radiant arc of sun-bright steel.
SLASH-CRUNCH-SPLAT!
In three clean and terrifyingly efficient strokes, Silas cleaved the remaining three spitters from their perches.
The radiant heat-laced Gold Core mana cauterized the wounds instantly, leaving behind neat smoldering cross-sections of monster flesh that collapsed into the fog without a sound.
He landed lightly on the stone with his breath steady and his sword held low.
"Is that all this fog has to offer?" Silas murmured, stepping over a severed leg.
"Just an endless conveyor belt of target practice?"
RUMBLE...
As if the cavern itself had heard his insolent challenge, the ground beneath his boots violently shuddered.
The white fog churned into a violent maelstrom as from the dark fissures lining the amphitheater walls, dozens of glowing red and sickly yellow eyes ignited in the mist!
A high-pitched, wet chittering sound echoed off the basalt ceiling, multiplying until it sounded like a roaring river of scuttling limbs.
"HAUUUUUUHAUHAUUUU!"
A horde of at least forty monsters surged out of the shadows.

There were dozens of the segmented Corpse-Leeches writhing through the air, packs of six-legged Bone-Scuttlers tearing across the stone with diamond-hard claws, and heavy acid-bloated spitters ringing the high ledges!
"SQUAWWWWWWWK!"
The obsidian bird lost its mind completely.

It abandoned Silas’s arm, fluttering frantically into the air with its wings beating a desperate retreat toward the highest farthest ceiling stalactite it could reach, perching on a narrow stone spur and trembling so hard its feathers rattled!
Silas looked up at the fleeing bird, letting out an amused mocking snort.
"Coward," Silas muttered.
He turned back toward the incoming tide of monsters, rolling his shoulders with relaxed fluid grace.
’Forty-odd low tiers... and one large presence hiding in the back.’
His [Rip-Current Perception] caught a heavy mana signature lingering just beyond the edge of the horde... a massive silent silhouette moving through the thickest bank of mist with chilling patience.
’A Tier 4 at least...
Let’s see what kind of toys this nest breeds.’
"RAHHHHH!"
The front line of twelve Bone-Scuttlers lunged simultaneously, their jagged claws extended to shred him into kindling.
BOOM!
Silas met them head-on as he didn’t retreat an inch and his golden longsword became a spinning wheel of golden light.
CLANG-SHING-CHOP!
The first scuttler was bisected from snout to tail.
Silas spun on his heel, using the rotational torque to drive the flat of his blade into the second beast’s skull, shattering the bone into powder with pure unassisted physical strength.
He vaulted over the falling corpse with his left hand snapping forward—
"[Incineration Ray]!"
ZAP-BOOOOOOM!
A concentrated pencil-thin beam of pure solar fire erupted from his index finger!

The beam punched clean through the chests of four charging beasts in a straight line, superheating their internal fluids until their carapaces exploded from the inside out in violent, concussive pops of smoldering ash!
SHSHSHK!
Silas ducked low, feeling the wind of three jumping leeches whistle over his head!
Without looking, he thrust his blade straight upward into the belly of the first, channeled a burst of heavy-water mana along the spine, and swept the blade horizontally in a wide arc.
"Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style...
Severing Horizon!"
KRA-BOOOOOOM!
A thirty-foot crescent wave of phantom heavy-water exploded outward from his stance.
The hydraulic mass hit the swarm like an avalanche, crushing fifteen monsters against the basalt walls in a single earth-shaking impact.
Shattered carapaces and pulverized bone rained down into the rising mist like hail yet, right in the middle of Silas’s follow-through—
SNAP.
The space directly behind Silas’s right blind spot folded and from the dense whiteout, a massive, terrifying shape materialized out of nothingness.

chapters.title: Chapter 514: Forces Of The Fog [II]
paragraphs: It was a Mist-Phantom Chimera which was a Tier 4 predator like he expected.
"Haah!"

The beast was fifteen feet long, its muscular panther-like body covered in interlocking plates of translucent milky-white crystal that completely refracted the ambient light, rendering it nearly invisible in the fog.
Its head was a nightmarish fusion of a feline skull and a serrated snapping turtle, and its long, whip-like tail ended in a massive heavy mace of petrified basalt.
The Tier 4 beast had utilized the dense necrotic mist as a natural cloaking medium, executing a flawless ambush at the exact microsecond Silas completed his sword swing.
WHOOSH!
The stone mace-tail whipped through the air with high speed, aimed directly at Silas’s ribs!
’Fast!’ Silas’s mind registered instantly since he didn’t have the leverage to bring the longsword back across his body.
...So he didn’t try.
Silas simply shifted his center of gravity, tightening his abdominal muscles and letting the furnace of his Gold Core flood his vascular system with protective mana.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!

The stone mace slammed squarely into Silas’s left flank and the force was immense as the concussive shockwave blew the surrounding mist away in a twenty-foot ring, and Silas was hurled laterally through the air with his boots skimming across the permafrost before he dug his heels into the shale, carving two deep smoking trenches into the stone as he came to a halt twenty paces away.
Up on the ceiling stalactite, the obsidian bird let out an ear-splitting screech of pure despair.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK! KRR-CLACK!"

The animal covered its eyes with its wings, fully convinced the mortal had just been crushed into a paste of broken ribs and ruptured organs however down on the floor, Silas slowly lowered his left arm.
He rolled his left shoulder.
CRACK-POP!
The joint popped smoothly.

The silver-threaded wool of his coat was scuffed with gray stone dust, and there was a dull ache along his lower ribs... a light muscular bruise that faded the instant his Gold Core circulated a single wave of restorative golden heat through his marrow.
His bones were completely intact and his stance was rock-solid too.
Silas brushed a fleck of basalt dust from his lapel, his blue eyes locking onto the translucent Tier 4 chimera with a cold unimpressed stare.
"Not a bad swing," Silas noted, his voice sounding calm and level. "Good acceleration. Solid mass behind the pivot but your follow-through is lacking."
The chimera let out a low bass-heavy growl that rattled the stones beneath their boots.
Its translucent crystal plates flared with sickly, pale mana as it realized its fatal strike hadn’t even broken the prey’s skin.
FZZZT!
The beast blurred, melting backward into the thick white mist and attempting to reposition for another cloaked ambush.
"You don’t get to hide twice," Silas said softly.
He didn’t chase it with his feet as he closed his eyes for a fraction of a heartbeat, focusing on the moisture contained within the freezing fog.
’There.’
The chimera’s muscular body displaced forty gallons of atmospheric moisture as it sprinted along the eastern perimeter.
To the naked eye, the fog was an opaque white wall but to Silas’s [Rip-Current Perception], the beast’s trajectory was a glowing electric-blue highway carving through the dark.
SHSHSHK!
The chimera struck again.
It lunged from the ceiling shadows directly above Silas’s head, its massive razor-sharp crystal talons extended to decapitate him in a downward pounce!
Silas didn’t look up and he waited.
...One pace.
...Half a pace.
At the exact second the monster’s claws entered his perimeter—
BOOM!
Silas didn’t parry as he sidestepped with terrifying microscopic precision, letting the massive multi-ton beast crash into the stone floor right beside him.
KRA-CRUNCH!

The impact cratered the granite and before the chimera could recoil or whip its stone tail, Silas stepped forward, driving his heavy leather boot squarely onto the beast’s snout, pinning its massive head into the cracked rock with the concussive weight of an anvil.
SPLAT!
The chimera thrashed violently with its claws tearing deep furrows into the shale, but Silas’s leg was an iron pillar.
"Ice..." Silas commanded with cold authority. "Transformation."
FROOOOO-SH!
Dense high-pressure water mana erupted from the sole of his boot, flooding over the chimera’s skull and forelimbs.
In the span of a single second, the liquid flash-froze into massive, unbreakable blocks of solid glacial ice, permanently locking the Tier 4 monster’s front half into the bedrock.
The beast let out a muffled frantic roar with its hind legs kicking wildly as it tried to shatter the freeze...
Silas raised his golden longsword with both hands, reversing his grip so the tip pointed straight down at the monster’s exposed nape.
"Good effort," Silas said quietly.
SHING-CRACK!

He drove the blade down with the full weight of his Gold Core and the golden mythril steel punched clean through the chimera’s crystal neck plates, severing the thick spinal column, burying three feet deep into the solid granite beneath.
SQUELCH!
A thick geyser of dark viscous monster blood sprayed across the white ice, sizzling softly before the life-force faded.
The chimera’s massive hindquarters twitched violently twice with the translucent crystal plates dulling into brittle milky chalk, before collapsing into stillness.
THUD!
Silas pulled the longsword free with a smooth effortless jerk of his wrists.
The amphitheater fell into ringing silence.

The forty low-tier beasts had been completely eradicated... shredded, burned, and crushed into silent heaps of smoking visceral debris while the Tier 4 apex predator lay dead at his boots, its neck pinned in an eternal block of ice.
Up on the ceiling stalactite, the obsidian bird sat completely frozen.
Its wings were half-unfolded, its beady eyes bulging as it stared down at the lone mortal standing amidst the slaughterhouse.
It had watched the Tier 4 monster sneak the man twice with bone-shattering strikes, fully expecting the human to be ripped into ribbons.
Instead... the man had barely grunted.
He had brushed off a powerful strike like it was a dusting of dry flour, pinned the apex predator with a single boot, and executed it with the casual bored precision of a farmer culling a sick goat.
The bird slowly fluttered down from the ceiling, landing cautiously on the edge of the chimera’s frozen tail.
It looked at the dead titan, then looked up at Silas, letting out a faint bewildered click.
"Krrr... caw...?"

"See?" Silas said, flicking the blood from his blade and sliding it back into its scabbard with a crisp clack. "Told you. There’s nothing to lose your feathers over so now get back on my arm and stop trembling. You’re vibrating like an unbalanced turbine."
The bird didn’t squawk.
It simply hopped onto his leather vambrace, tucking its head low against his wrist in complete humbled submission.
Whatever arrogance the ancient familiar had carried was dead, buried beneath the corpses of forty basin horrors.
Silas stepped over the chimera’s frozen flank, continuing his march toward the deep northern corridor.
’No more mana signatures within five hundred paces,’ Silas noted, his senses expanding through the quiet dark. ’The horde was the perimeter guard. Whatever sits ahead... is alone.’
He walked for another twenty minutes through a rising, narrow basalt flue.

The ground underfoot grew increasingly smooth, worn down by centuries of an unnatural drag as if some colossal monolithic weight had been pulled back and forth across the stone until the shale was polished like black marble.
And then, with terrifying suddenness... the white fog simply died.
It simply terminated along a clean line, as if an invisible spatial wall severed the humid vapor from the chamber ahead.
Silas stepped across that boundary.
The air on this side was dead and completely lacking of heat, moisture, or the coppery stench of blood.
It carried a suffocating stillness as the ceiling opened up into an unfathomable vaulted dome that stretched hundreds of paces into the dark.
And right in the center of the chamber, thirty paces ahead of Silas’s boots...
SZZZZZT!
A sudden howling atmospheric draft detonated outward from the center of the cavern.
The violent rush of air whipped Silas’s dark traveling coat back against his shoulders with his black hair blowing wildly across his forehead, stinging his eyes with dry mineral dust.
From the high, shadowed wall of petrified black ice that filled the far side of the dome...
Two colossal eyelid-like folds of gray leathery skin slowly parted with the sickening wet sound of tearing paper.
SQUELCH.
An enormous circular eye ignited in the dark and it was big... easily twenty feet across, swollen, bulging, and veined with thick black vessels that wept clear viscous slime onto the stone below.
And right in the center of that massive unblinking sphere... sat a flat, horizontal pupil of dull stone-gray.
The pupil didn’t flicker.
It slowly rotated within the socket with an audible wet shluck, locking its dead gaze directly onto Silas’s tiny solitary figure.
Silas stood motionless in the freezing draft with his boots planted firmly on the polished marble shale, staring back at the towering hideous monstrosity.
His face remained completely deadpan but he didn’t draw his sword and he didn’t drop into a combat crouch.
He just stared at the massive slimy orb for five long agonizing seconds with his brow slowly furrowing into an expression of pure disgust.
’What the fuck...’ Silas thought, his lips twitching with distaste as his hair whipped in the howling wind. ’It looks so damn ugly.’
Silas took a deep breath.
He genuinely had no idea what he was supposed to do next.
Across the thirty paces of dead air separating them, the colossal, twenty-foot orb remained embedded in the petrified black ice, perfectly still.
Silas kept his spiritual perception poured into his Gold Core, muscles primed to detonate into an evasive slide or channel an immediate blast of [Hurricane Repulsion].
He waited for the inevitable mental probe, the intrusive phantom hum of a psychological assault, or the telltale heat of an ocular beam charging behind that glassy surface.
...Nothing came.
’Doesn’t she have anything?’
There was no insidious pressure scraping against his consciousness, no surge of hostile mana gathering along the optic nerves, and zero feral malice leaking from its flesh.
The gargantuan organ was simply sitting in its socket, staring directly at him with that flat horizontal pupil.
’What the hell...?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing deeper into baffled annoyance.
He had mentally mapped out an entire multi-phase boss fight the second the ceiling vault opened up.

He had planned the approach angle... Use [Rip-Current Perception] to track the tectonic shifts, drop a blinding burst of [Incineration Ray] straight into the pupil to scorch the optic stem, and follow through with [Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style — Severing Horizon] to shear the surrounding ice wall clean off its foundation.
Yet the giant veiny monstrosity just... sat there and staring.
It was looking less like an apex subterranean predator and more like an overgrown discarded fish head trapped in a frozen gutter.
"You going to throw a beam, or are we having an unblinking contest?" Silas muttered under his breath with his fingers tightening around the golden grip of his sheathed longsword.
He shifted his weight onto the ball of his right foot, preparing to draw steel and initiate the clash himself but before his blade could clear the scabbard, the creature moved.
SCHLUCK.
A sickening wet tremor rippled across the leathery gray skin framing the socket as the entire sphere violently hitched upward by half an inch.

Silas stiffened instantly, locking his center of gravity to the stone, while the obsidian bird on his vambrace clamped its talons down until the leather groaned, letting out a strangled hiss of panic.
Then, the eye did something utterly incomprehensible.
The thick blackened veins webbing the sclera began to pulse rapidly, flushing with a sudden surging heat as the wide gray horizontal pupil dilated, trembling with a slow agonizing spasm.
From beneath the heavy, leathery upper lid, a massive bead of translucent fluid welled up.
It clung to the rim for a fraction of a second before breaking free, cascading down the curve of the eyeball like a falling sheet of glass.
DRIP!
A droplet the size of a carriage wheel broke away from the bottom fold of skin, plummeting through the dead air before slamming heavily against the shale three paces ahead of Silas.
SPLASH!
The fluid struck the stone with a soft hollow shhhk, instantly evaporating into clean odorless vapor that dissolved into the freezing air without leaving a single trace of acid or poison behind.
Silas blinked, his jaw going slack as he lowered his hand half an inch from his pommel.
The leathery folds shuddered again, and a second massive sphere of clear moisture welled up, spilling over the dark rim in an unbroken stream that washed across the blackened permafrost.
The eye wasn’t charging an attack... It was weeping?

’What the hell...?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing deeper into baffled annoyance.
He had mentally mapped out an entire multi-phase boss fight the second the ceiling vault opened up.
He had planned the approach angle...

Use [Rip-Current Perception] to track the tectonic shifts, drop a blinding burst of [Incineration Ray] straight into the pupil to scorch the optic stem, and follow through with [Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style — Severing Horizon] to shear the surrounding ice wall clean off its foundation.
Yet the giant veiny monstrosity just... sat there and staring.
It was looking less like an apex subterranean predator and more like an overgrown discarded fish head trapped in a frozen gutter.
"You going to throw a beam, or are we having an unblinking contest?" Silas muttered under his breath with his fingers tightening around the golden grip of his sheathed longsword.
He shifted his weight onto the ball of his right foot, preparing to draw steel and initiate the clash himself but before his blade could clear the scabbard, the creature moved.
SCHLUCK.
A sickening wet tremor rippled across the leathery gray skin framing the socket as the entire sphere violently hitched upward by half an inch.

Silas stiffened instantly, locking his center of gravity to the stone, while the obsidian bird on his vambrace clamped its talons down until the leather groaned, letting out a strangled hiss of panic.
Then, the eye did something utterly incomprehensible.
The thick blackened veins webbing the sclera began to pulse rapidly, flushing with a sudden surging heat as the wide gray horizontal pupil dilated, trembling with a slow agonizing spasm.
From beneath the heavy, leathery upper lid, a massive bead of translucent fluid welled up.
It clung to the rim for a fraction of a second before breaking free, cascading down the curve of the eyeball like a falling sheet of glass.
DRIP!
A droplet the size of a carriage wheel broke away from the bottom fold of skin, plummeting through the dead air before slamming heavily against the shale three paces ahead of Silas.
SPLASH!
The fluid struck the stone with a soft hollow shhhk, instantly evaporating into clean odorless vapor that dissolved into the freezing air without leaving a single trace of acid or poison behind.
Silas blinked, his jaw going slack as he lowered his hand half an inch from his pommel.
The leathery folds shuddered again, and a second massive sphere of clear moisture welled up, spilling over the dark rim in an unbroken stream that washed across the blackened permafrost.
The eye wasn’t charging an attack...
It was weeping?

chapters.title: Chapter 515: Forces Of The Fog [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The clear heavy fluid cascaded from the lower fold of leathery gray skin with the violent force of an opened sluice gate.
SPLOOSH!
Another massive globule struck the flat permafrost four paces ahead of Silas’s boots, splashing across the polished stone before flashing away into fine odorless steam.
It left no acid bite in the air, no scorch marks on the dark basalt, and no lingering chemical sting.
Yet with every impact, the volume of the weeping eye’s discharge seemed to warp the subterranean pressure of the chamber, turning the stagnant chill into humid air.
Silas took two measured steps backward with the leather soles of his boots grinding small dry chips of shale against the frozen bedrock.
His fingers remained wrapped loosely around the grip of his sheathed longsword with his shoulders loose and his center of gravity dialed directly over his hips.
’The fuck...’
The creature had not expanded its physical frame.
Its internal mana reservoir remained completely flat... it was stil a pool of high-density Tier 5 energy that neither spiked with hunger nor thinned with fear.
It simply hung suspended within the wall of petrified black ice, staring straight forward with that wide twenty-foot horizontal pupil of dull lifeless stone-gray.
’It’s really just crying...?’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing as he tracked another carriage-wheel-sized tear rolling down the bulging sclera.
The concept was completely absurd.
He had crossed blades with different kinds of monsters, but an unblinking twenty-foot eyeball leaking cataracts of clean water like an abandoned child was an entirely new category of bizarre.
’Is it feeling sorry for me? Or does it look at me standing in its nest and pity the meat?’
He swallowed hard as his throat dry against the dead air then the physical laws of the area began to unravel.
Where the falling tears struck the permafrost, the resulting steam did not dissipate into the upper shadows.
It thickened and it curdled.
The rising white vapor grew greasy, pooling outward along the black marble floor in churning milky currents that rapidly swallowed Silas’s shins.
FZZZZZZT!
Silas’s instincts flared before his eyes could even register the shift as he didn’t wait to see what the condensation would do.
With a sharp exhale, he rotated his torso and snapped his left palm downward, channeling a thread of wind mana through his fingertips.
"Hurricane Repulsion!"
BOOM!
A concussive ring of compressed atmospheric force detonated outward from his palm, scything across the stone floor in a flat high-velocity shockwave.
The violent draft blew the creeping white vapor back twenty yards, carving a clean circle of bare dark bedrock around his boots.
Yet the expelled fog didn’t scatter.
Instead of shredding under the gale, the white mist violently twisted upon itself, forming tight vortexes that sucked the humidity of the chamber into churning funnels.
SQUELCH! SQUELCH! SQUELCH!
From the centers of the swirling vortexes, pale rubbery flesh began to knit together out of thin air.
Segmented hides rows of needle-like teeth, and twitching sensory stalks manifested from the fog with sickening rapid-fire speed.
In less than two seconds, eight new Corpse-Leeches dropped onto the stone, their bloated bodies shuddering as they shook the wet rime from their snouts.
Flanking them, three four-legged Mist-Spitters tore their way out of the fog, their armored throats already swelling with high-pressure fluid.
"GRAHHHHHH!"
The newly formed pack didn’t hesitate.
Driven by the blind reflexive impulse of the weeping eye, they lunged forward in a chaotic screeching wave, their claws and mandibles tearing across the stone straight toward Silas’s throat.
Silas drew his longsword with a clean shing.
SLASH-CHOP-CRUNCH!
He stepped inside the reach of the lead leech, his blade cleaving upward through its jaw, through the brain stem, and exiting the top of its skull in a continuous golden arc of light.
Without pausing, he pivoted on his back heel, driving a front kick into the chest of an approaching spitter that caved its ribcage inward and hurled it fifteen yards into the wall.
He backpedaled with his boots skidding across the frost as another five abominations threw themselves at his flanks.
’Fuck.’
A sour irritated taste filled his mouth.
He had spent the last two minutes staring at the eye like a tourist in an art gallery, completely caught off guard by the ridiculousness of a weeping monster.
While he had been standing there wondering about its psychological state, the creature’s passive bodily secretions were literally manufacturing a personal army out of the moisture in the room.
’It’s not sad... It’s an engine. Does that mean it’s useless by itself?’
He raised his left hand, aiming his index finger directly across the cavern toward the center of the giant gray pupil.
"Stop leaking, you ugly bastard," Silas growled.
"[Incineration Ray]!"
ZAP-BOOOOOOM!
A blinding razor-thin beam of pure solar fire detonated from his fingertip, piercing through the dark immediately.
The concentrated heat was enough to melt through a foot of reinforced mythril plate in the blink of an eye.
Yet, five paces before the beam could strike the cornea, the dense wall of fog in front of the socket violently imploded.
SPLAT!
A massive armored monstrosity... a hulking six-legged brute made of condensed petrified fog-ice materialized directly in the path of the beam!
The solar ray struck the beast dead-center in the chest!
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The impact blew a three-foot molten crater through the creature’s torso, incinerating its internal organs and blasting its hindquarters into white ash.
The charred husk tumbled heavily onto the permafrost, completely dead but it had served its sole purpose.
The giant eye behind it remained untouched.
SCHLUCK!
Another colossal wave of tears washed over the leathery lids.

The mist doubled in volume as the cavern floor disappeared entirely under an undulating sea of churning white foam, and from the deep shadows, dozens of new clicking sounds as well as growls and wet shrieks began to multiply with terrifying exponential speed.

’I need to kill it right now,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes hardening into murderous focus. ’If I let it keep crying, it’s going to fill this entire vault until I’m wading through three hundred Tier 3s and Tier 4s with no room to swing...’
He had expected a boss battle.
A physical clash against a terrifying titan where they traded blows until the stone collapsed.
"Haah... Fuck me..."
He hadn’t expected an immovable weeping tumor that acted as an automated summoning gate.
Silas drew in a deep burning draught of the freezing air.
The Mythic Gold Core within his sternum spun into rapid violent rotation, flooding his muscular pathways, tendons, and eyes with dense golden mana.
VUUUM!
On his left shoulder, the obsidian bird looked up toward the ceiling stalactites with its wings twitching as it prepared to abandon ship and fly to safety.
"SQUAWK—"
The avian’s beak snapped shut with a dry choking gasp.

Circling high in the vault, weaving through the jagged stalactites, were four winged abominations... leathery, bat-like horrors with razor-sharp ice beaks that were actively patrolling the upper airspace.
The bird swallowed an audible nervous lump, pulling its crested head down between its wings and digging its talons hard into Silas’s vambrace, realizing there was nowhere to run.
"Told you to have some balls," Silas muttered, shifting his grip on the golden longsword. "Hold on tight."
BOOM!
Silas detonated forward.

He channeled a continuous stream of compressed wind mana beneath the soles of his boots as a [Cyclone Slipstream] that negated the friction of the permafrost and propelled him across the stone at blinding velocity.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The air shrieked behind him as he carved a vacuum corridor straight through the sea of fog.
Three Bone-Scuttlers lunged from his left flank with their jaws wide—
SHING-SHING-SHING!
Silas didn’t even turn his shoulders.
The golden blade blurred in three clean backhanded sweeps, severing their heads before their feet could touch the ground.
’Faster... I have to cross thirty paces before it can spawn another wall.’
WHOOSH!
He reached twenty paces.
He locked his gaze onto the giant weeping pupil, cocking his sword arm back for a devastating rotational strike—
FWUMP!
The giant eye didn’t fire a beam and it didn’t summon an armor plate either. The twenty-foot organ simply... tilted?

With an agile, horrifying elasticity that defied its mass, the leathery gray skin of the socket puckered, and the entire eye shifted four yards to the right along the curved ice wall with the frictionless speed of an oiled piston!
Silas’s strike whistled through empty air!
KRA-CRACK!

The phantom heavy-water edge of his longsword cleaved three feet deep into the bare black ice where the eye had rested half a second prior, sending massive shards of petrified rime exploding outward into the dark!
’It moved?!’ Silas’s eyes widened.
Before he could wrench the blade free, the eye opened wide from its new position on the right wall.
SPLOOSH!
A massive geyser of tears erupted from the socket, flooding across the floor and instantly solidifying into four armored Spine-Hounds that lunged at his exposed back.
Silas didn’t look back.
He released the hilt with his right hand, spun on his heel, and slammed his open palms down into the permafrost.
"Tectonic Rupture!"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOM!
High-tier earth mana flooded the bedrock beneath his gloves!

The solid granite floor violently buckled and a twenty-foot wave of jagged stone spikes tore upward from the ground in an explosive, circular eruption, impaling all four lunging hounds mid-air and shattering their ribcages into fine bloody gravel.
Silas tore his longsword from the ice, vaulting atop one of the freshly raised stone spires.
"You think you’re fast, you overgrown marble?!" Silas yelled, his voice echoing off the ceiling vault.
He leaped from the spire, wind mana detonating behind his shoulder blades to rocket him toward the eye’s new coordinates.
The eye blinked once.
SCHLUCK!
It shifted again as it slid vertically up the ice wall, retreating twenty feet into the shadows near the ceiling arch with the terrifying effortless mobility of an insect skittering across a window.
Silas’s second thrust struck empty stone.
BOOM!
"Third time," Silas snarled, twisting his body mid-air.
He didn’t fall.
He kicked off the vertical ice face with his boots leaving two cracked indentations in the frost, and drove himself straight upward toward the ceiling shadow where the eye had relocated.
VUUUM!
Golden lightning began to crackle along his forearm... Dangerous arcs of electric mana coiling from his Gold Core straight into the steel of his longsword!
"Fulgur Annihilation!"
CRACK-BOOOOOOOOM!
A blinding bolt of golden thunder detonated from the blade, screaming across the ten-foot gap straight for the pupil.
SWISH.
The eye dropped.
The leathery folds detached from the ceiling anchor, letting the twenty-foot mass freefall into the dense fog below like a dropped boulder, dodging the lightning strike by less than three inches.
The golden thunderbolt slammed into the ceiling, obliterating a five-yard section of solid basalt into raining gravel and dust.
Silas landed heavily on the permafrost below with his knees flexing to absorb the impact.
He was breathing hard, not from mana exhaustion, but from frustration.
"Three times," Silas growled, wiping a fleck of rime from his cheek with the back of his glove. "A twenty-foot eyeball with zero legs is dodging me like an oiled eel?"
Was he that slow...?
Across the chamber, forty paces away, the eye surfaced from the sea of white mist.
It didn’t look damaged and it didn’t look tired either.
The gray horizontal pupil stared at him with that same dull empty stillness.
Then, the leathery lids peeled back further than they ever had before.
GURRRRR-GL-GL.
A deep sickening sound rose from the base of the optic socket... This time it was not the clean splash of weeping tears, but a churning of something solid being forced through an opening.
The thick blackened veins across the sclera flared with a violent purplish-black mana.
SQUELCH.
From the lower rim of the eye, beneath the leathery skin, the monster didn’t spit a leech.
...It vomited a man.
’Huh?’
Silas’s boots locked to the stone as his eyes narrowed to pinpoint slits and the figure landed on the frost with a silent and perfectly balanced crouch.
It was roughly six feet tall, humanoid in silhouette, but composed entirely of condensed petrified fog and midnight-blue chitin.
It wore no armor, yet its skin was layered in overlapping razor-thin scales that absorbed the light like a void.
Its face was a smooth featureless mask of polished obsidian, lacking any sort of eyes, nose, or mouth.
And in its right hand... It held a long single-edged blade forged of translucent razor-sharp black ice.
VUUUM!
[Target Analyzed: Phantom Blade-Construct (Tier 4)]
"A swordsman..." Silas murmured softly.
The construct took one slow, deliberate step forward.

The weight distribution in its hips, the angle of its lead knee, the micro-tension in its forearms, and the low forty-five-degree tilt of its black ice blade were so utterly immaculate that Silas’s breath caught in his throat.
’Eh...? It’s far better than me...’
This was not a mindless beast swinging claws. In terms of pure, mechanical sword technique... the construct was better than Silas.
Silas knew his strengths.
He was a Lord. He commanded massive elemental firepower, a Mythic Gold Core, and adaptability too.
But the Entity before him was a pure swordsman.
FZZZT!
The construct vanished.
There was no sound of boots striking stone and no displaced air.
SHING!
A razor-thin line of black light cleaved diagonally through the space where Silas’s neck had been.

Using the pressure of the locked blades, it shifted its lead foot behind Silas’s heel, executing an instantaneous sweep while simultaneously driving its left elbow toward his temple.
’This thing fights like a professional too!’
Silas flared his Gold Core.
BOOM!
He didn’t play the technique game as he flooded the contact point with raw water mana.
"[Tidal Impact]!"
A concussive hydraulic shockwave exploded outward from the flat of his blade.
The point-blank explosion blew the construct three paces backward, forcing its feet to slide across the permafrost.

Yet the entity didn’t lose its balance for a fraction of a second. The moment its soles regained traction, it dropped into a low coiled stance, the black ice blade blurring into eight simultaneous thrusts that screamed through the dark like striking vipers.
TICK-TICK-CLANG-TICK-SHING-CLANG!
Silas was forced onto the defensive.
His golden longsword moved in desperate arcs, deflecting the thrusts by millimeters.
Every time his blade met the black ice, the construct altered the angle of attack mid-stroke, exploiting the microscopic gaps in Silas’s guard with chilling computer-like precision.
RIP!
A shallow cut opened along Silas’s right bicep, tearing the wool coat and slicing through the top layer of skin.
TICK!
Another thrust grazed his jawline, drawing a thin bead of scarlet blood that froze instantly in the bitter air.
Up on Silas’s shoulder, the obsidian bird had been clinging to his collar for dear life with its talons digging into his leather mantle.
It saw the construct’s blade cock back for a third thrust aimed directly at Silas’s throat.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK!"
’The hell does it want to do? Run?’ Silas really didn’t care at this point, this strike was exactly what he needed for an opening to slaughter this thing.
The bird didn’t flee.
Driven by some spark of loyalty or perhaps the realization that if the human died, it was going to be digested next... the obsidian familiar threw its wings wide!
It launched itself from Silas’s shoulder directly into the construct’s face.
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP!
Its dark crystalline wings battered against the featureless obsidian mask, and with a vicious metallic snap, its curved scythe-beak struck the construct’s right eye-ridge with a sharp clack.
The strike didn’t deal damage as the construct’s hide was harder than iron.
But it did something infinitely more valuable.
It disrupted the entity’s sightline for a tenth of a second and the lethal thrust aimed at Silas’s throat hitched, drifting three inches to the left.
’Not exactly what I planned but...’
"Good bird!" Silas roared, a tenth of a second was all a Gold Core Lord needed.
Silas didn’t try to out-fence the swordsman and he didn’t try to mimic its refined footwork.
’All of those are important but for a fight to the death?’
He abandoned finesse completely.
Silas dropped his center of gravity, stepped straight into the construct’s guard, and drove his left shoulder hard into its chest with the concussive force of a battering ram.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The collision shattered the construct’s lead clavicle.
As the entity staggered backward, Silas’s left hand shot out like an iron clamp, locking around the construct’s sword-wrist with a grip that cracked the chitin beneath his fingers.
"You’re a better swordsman than me," Silas grunted, his golden ringed blue eyes burning with savage fire. "Too bad this isn’t a tournament..."
VUUUM!
Golden lightning exploded from Silas’s palm, surging directly into the construct’s arm.
"Once more..." Silas breathed out. "Fulgur Annihilation!"
He really liked the name of this spell...
KRA-FLASH-BOOOOOOM!
Tens of thousands of volts of destructive lightning surged through the construct’s body as the entity arched backward.
Its featureless mask vibrated violently as the lightning cooked its internal mana circuits from the inside out.
Cracks of blinding golden light spiderwebbed across its obsidian hide, shattering its chitin plates into smoldering shards.
Before the paralyzed construct could collapse, Silas drew his golden longsword back with both hands.
He cycled the full rotational torque of his core, pulling moisture from the air and coating the mythril edge in five layers of pressurized heavy water!
"Tidal-Blade Arts: First Style... Severing Horizon!"
SHING-BOOOOOOOM!
The horizontal crescent wave cleaved through the construct’s waist at point-blank range.

The black ice blade shattered into dust, the construct was sliced cleanly in two, and the concussive heavy-water wave detonated outward, blasting the severed halves thirty yards across the floor to dissolve into inert puddles of gray slush.
Silas didn’t even watch it dissolve.
The instant the construct fell, he redirected his entire momentum toward the far wall.
The obsidian bird fluttered frantically, barely managing to latch back onto his left collar as Silas tore across the stone like a falling meteor.
The weeping eye was thirty paces away, floating low near the permafrost and its leathery lids were trembling violently.
"Fuuu..."
Silas knew its pattern now.
He knew it was going to slide. It was going to shift to the left, dart up the ice wall, or drop into the permafrost crevices to escape the kill-stroke so he prepared for the dodge.
He coiled his legs, priming a burst of Cyclone Slipstream to alter his trajectory mid-air the microsecond the organ made its evasive twitch.
’Don’t worry, you’re not escaping this time...’
He closed the distance.
...Twenty paces.
...Ten paces.
...Five paces.
Silas raised his golden blade high above his head with both hands locked around the hilt and his Mythic Gold Core screaming at maximum output!
’Dodge, damn you!’ Silas braced himself. ’Which way are you going?!’
The eye didn’t move.
It had room to slide as the wall to its right was completely open and the permafrost below was slick and frictionless.
It could have easily detached its leathery anchor and skittered up into the ceiling shadows just as it had done three times before.
Yet... it simply sat there.
The leathery gray skin relaxed and the thick blackened veins stopped pulsing.
And in that final second, the wide stone-gray pupil rolled slightly upward, meeting Silas’s gaze with an expression that carried no malice and no resistance.
It looked... tired.
It seemed to have simply given up.
Silas’s breath caught in his throat.
For a fraction of a heartbeat, genuine shock rippled through his mind as he was fully expecting his blade to hit empty ice again but he didn’t stop the swing.
SHING-CRACK!
The golden mythril blade cleaved straight into the center of the twenty-foot eyeball!
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The impact didn’t sound like cutting meat, instead it sounded like a massive, pressurized dam shattering under millions of tons of water.
SPLAT-SQUELCH-GUSH!
The giant organ violently ruptured and a geyser of thick oily pitch-black blood detonated outward in every direction.
The volume of visceral fluid hit Silas and the bird like a tidal wave.
The black gore washed over his hair, his face, his silver-threaded coat, and soaked through his trousers, completely drowning them in a foul, coppery deluge.
The obsidian bird was battered flat against Silas’s chest, its crystalline feathers thoroughly coated in thick sticky black slime until it looked like a drowned rat.
The entire chamber was painted in dripping smoking black gore.
THUD!
Silas landed on his feet, spitting a mouthful of bitter black fluid onto the permafrost, wiping his eyes with a drenched stained forearm.
"Disgusting..." Silas coughed, shaking his head. "Utterly repulsive."
Beside his ear, the bird let out a pathetic muffled cough. "Krrr... glug... caw..."
Then, the world began to tear apart.
CRACK! KRA-CRACK-RUMBLE!
With the death of the core Tier 5 entity, the power anchoring the cavern collapsed.

The ceiling vault hundreds of feet above began to fracture as massive house-sized fissures ripped through the solid basalt and ancient permafrost, and colossal slabs of rock began to detach, plummeting toward the floor in a catastrophic deafening cave-in.
BOOM! CRASH!
He looked at the eye.
’There’s nothing left of it...?’
"Time to go!" Silas shouted.
He didn’t look for an exit tunnel since there was no tunnel.
Silas bent his knees, his Gold Core flaring as he targeted a falling, carriage-sized slab of granite.
BOOM!
He leaped straight upward and he landed on the falling boulder, used its downward momentum to springboard higher, and vaulted onto a second falling stalactite.
KRA-BOOM!
He climbed the falling debris like a staircase, leaping from shattered rock to falling ice with wind mana roaring beneath his boots as he rocketed toward the fracturing ceiling vault.
High above, a jagged fissure exposed a sliver of pale gray light.
Silas reached the apex of his leap, pulled his golden longsword back with both hands, and unleashed a massive upward strike—
"Cyclone Slipstream!"
SHING-BOOOOOOM!
The emerald vacuum edge shattered the remaining six feet of surface permafrost into fine powder.
Silas broke through the crust, bursting into the open freezing air like an artillery shell, landing in a low sliding crouch on the pristine snowfields of the northern surface.
THUD!
Behind him, the ground violently collapsed inward, sinking into a massive gouge nearly a hundred yards wide as the subterranean cavern below imploded.
Silas stood up, brushing the dirt and drying black blood from his coat.
Cold mountain wind whipped his stained black hair across his forehead as he turned around, staring down into the enormous smoking crater in the earth with a bewildered dry squint.
’It was underground the entire time, eh?’ Silas thought, letting out a long frosty sigh.
The bitter northern wind whistled across the lip of the collapsed crater, whipping loose flakes of pulverized black shale and crystalline ice dust into the gray sky.
Silas stood on the edge of the yawning chasm with his boots planted firmly in the crust.
Beneath the dark leather soles, the earth groaned with the muffled aftershock settle of thousands of tons of collapsed basalt.
The fog had not simply transported him far away from the detachment; it had dragged him deep into the bedrock, depositing him directly at the threshold of that weeping monstrosity.
’Why specifically did it summon me there?’ Silas thought, raising a heavy leather-clad forearm to rub the nape of his neck.

The thick crust of black ichor coating his skin and hair was already hardening in the sub-zero air, snapping into brittle greasy scales under his fingers. ’Did it sense the furnace of the Gold Core and mistake it for a fuel source? Did it assume an isolated human was an easy meal? Or did the pull of this wretched basin naturally draw the anomaly toward the strongest foreign mana signature in the valley?’
He looked down at the state of his traveling coat.
The reinforced silver-thread embroidery along the lapels was completely ruined, drenched in tar-like coppery sludge that emitted a faint, alkaline vapor as it froze.
The hem of his trousers was stiff with the dead beast’s fluids.
He exhaled a long, cloudy breath that scattered across the wind, giving a dry, dismissive shrug.
’Doesn’t matter. It’s dead now.’
"SQUAWK! SQUAWK! KRRR-CLACK! CAW!"
On his shoulder, the obsidian bird launched into a violent convulsive fit of grooming.
It beat its crystalline wings against its flanks, sending sprays of sticky, half-frozen black slime clattering across the clean white snow like flecks of wet coal.
It hopped down Silas’s bicep, its razor-sharp talons clicking nervously against the polished metal plates of his vambrace.
The creature’s beady black eyes darted frantically toward the northwest.

It craned its neck, pointing its scythe-curved beak toward the jagged horizon, fluffing its matted plumage and squawking with an urgent desperate sort of excitement that made its entire hollow-boned frame vibrate.
It recognized this sector.
The biting draft here did not eddy or churn like the unnatural currents of the outer parts as it scoured down from the high glaciers in razor-sharp sheets.
The organic rotten-wood stench of petrified mountain pine had vanished too.
In its place was the dead bite of cold.
"You know where you’re going from here?" Silas asked, rolling his neck until the cervical vertebrae snapped with a series of sharp satisfying cracks.
The bird nodded with comical intensity, bobbing its crested head up and down so fast it nearly lost its footing on his arm.
It let out a rapid barrage of metallic clicks and rattling trills.
"Krrr-caw! Caw! Clack-clack!"

"Lead on, then," Silas muttered, adjusting the sword belt at his waist so the golden mythril scabbard sat comfortably against his hip. "And try to pick a path that doesn’t route through any more digestive tracts... My coat is out of clean patches, and I have no desire to skin another worm today."

chapters.title: Chapter 517: Foul Mouthed Deity [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: With a wet leathery snap of its wings, the bird launched into the freezing air.
Despite the coating of necrotic slime weighing down its primary feathers, the avian familiar cut through the sub-zero squall with startling grace.

It hugged the contours of the scree, staying low beneath the prevailing gale to avoid getting battered against the cliffs, weaving an erratic yet deliberate path between towering monoliths of black basalt that jutted from the permafrost like the shattered ribs of a forgotten leviathan.
WHOOSH!
Silas broke into a steady lope, falling in behind the bird’s dark silhouette.
With every stride, his heavy combat boots crushed the surface crust with a crunching sound with his feet finding instant traction on the uneven frost-heaved rock.
Within his chest, the Gold Core maintained a calm rotation, circulating rivers of radiant mana through his pathways and meridians.

The sub-zero wind lashed his face and whipped the gore-matted black bangs across his eyes, but the cold could not take root as the internal furnace of his core repelled the frost before it could numb his extremities.
"Huuu... I just want to get this done and over with..."
He kept his spiritual perception dialed wide, sweeping the jagged ridgelines flanking the path as the greasy suffocating atmospheric density of the weeping eye’s domain was gone.
’At least we won’t have to worry about mist when I station girls here...’
Out here, the mana was thin as there were no feral beasts stalking the perimeter.
The local fauna knew better than to approach this sector as they were entering the dead zone of the northern basin.
’Or what I assume to be a Dead zone...’

After nearly a quarter of an hour of navigating through a winding maze of frost-shattered canyons and plunging stone gullies, the obsidian bird banked sharply around the face of a mirror-smooth cliff of dark granite.
It flared its wings, hovering against a vicious updraft, and let out a piercing triumphant shriek.
"SQUAWWWWWK!"
Silas rounded the stone shoulder and came to an immediate halt with his boots grinding loose shale to a dead stop.
Directly ahead, dominating the center of an isolated, bowl-shaped depression, lay a colossal vertical puncture in the crust of the world.
It was not a jagged crevasse born of tectonic strain, nor was it the ragged collapsed rim of a volcanic sinkhole.
The opening was terrifyingly neat.

It formed a nearly flawless circle forty yards in diameter with its interior walls bored perfectly plumb through hundreds of feet of solid ancient bedrock, as if a spear of large proportions had been driven straight down through the continent’s spine and violently wrenched back out.
"Fuuu..."

The cold venting upward from the depths was so incomprehensibly severe that the moisture in the falling blizzard crystallized several yards before reaching the lip, disintegrating into microscopic diamond sparks that were hurled back into the atmosphere by the updrafts.
From the lightless throat of the shaft, a slow luminescence pulsed.
It was a deep ethereal azure like the color of an oceanic trench submerged beneath miles of pack ice.

The temperature radiating from the pit hovered at a point that defied basic thermodynamics, it felt like a dead immovable cold that felt as though it were actively working to freeze the flow of time, the vibration of molecules, and the very spark of consciousness itself.
’Weird...’
The obsidian bird hovered over the mouth of the yawning abyss.
It looked back at Silas over its wing, clicked its beak in an urgent unmistakable summons, folded its wings tightly against its flanks, and plummeted headfirst into the darkness.
Silas walked straight to the lip of the pit with the soles of his boots hung slightly over the sheer drop.
He leaned forward, squinting into the plunging shaft.
The ethereal blue light seemed to flicker thousands of feet below, swallowed by endless leagues of lightless granite.
"Looks deep enough," Silas remarked dryly to the empty wind.
He didn’t search the rock face for handholds and he didn’t bother uncoiling a tether, nor did he channel earth magic to construct a descending staircase along the perimeter.
He simply bent his knees, kicked off the permafrost, and stepped out into empty air.
The rush of the subterranean void was a lot.
WHOOSH!
Gravity seized Silas like an iron fist, accelerating his mass downward through the darkness with terrifying bone-rattling momentum.
The walls of the vertical flue blurred past in streaks of lightless slate, illuminated only by the rhythmic flashes of the blue glow far below.
The freezing air screamed in his ears, a deafening roar that ripped at his clothes and threatened to strip the breath clean from his lungs.
Several hundred feet ahead of him in the dark, the obsidian bird was gliding smoothly along the center of the thermal column.
Its dark crystalline wings were locked in an immaculate V-shape, effortlessly riding the freezing updrafts that rushed through its flight feathers.
Its little chest puffed with pride.

It had endured the horrors of the basin... It had slipped past the weeping eye... It had navigated the broken crags and brought the living breathing Lord of Blessed Land straight to the secret threshold.
’I’ve finally reached it...’ the bird thought, clicking its scythe-curved beak in self-satisfied vindication. ’I survived the fog! I brought the human! Mistress is right below, and soon—’
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A concussive detonation ripped through the shaft directly past the bird’s left wingtip.

The force of the falling human hit the tiny avian like a physical wall of iron, flipping it violently onto its back and sending it spinning beak-over-tail feathers through the freezing void like a dropped unraveled ball of twine.
"SQUAWWWWWWWK?!" the familiar shrieked in dizzying outrage, flailing its wings wildly in the vacuum pocket left in Silas’s wake.
Down below, the floor of the subterranean chamber rushed up to meet Silas at terminal velocity.
The ethereal blue luminescence expanded into a vast cathedral-sized cavern with the icy bedrock racing toward his boots at well over a hundred miles per hour.
Thirty feet above the stone floor, Silas’s eyes snapped wide.
He rotated his hips mid-air, snapping both palms downward toward the approaching floor.
"Hurricane Repulsion!"
BOOM!
A high-pressure atmospheric shockwave detonated from his gloves, colliding violently against the ancient permafrost and violently checking his terminal descent.

The sudden crushing deceleration dragged at his joints, but before the recoil could snap his ankles, Silas flared a secondary cushion of Cyclone Slipstream beneath his boots, scrubbing the remaining energy into a swirling ring of harmless pulverized rime.
THUD!
Silas touched down on the platform in a low three-point crouch.
One gloved hand grazed the glassy floor to steady his balance with the leather hissing softly against the slick surface.
He held the position for a fraction of a second, letting his center of gravity settle, before rising smoothly to his full height.
"Haah..."
He rolled his shoulders, the dry joints popping softly within the cavern’s dead silence, and cast his gaze across the expanse.
The scale of the chamber was staggering.
It was a vaulted dome large enough to house an entire fortress.
The ceiling was lost in high shadows, but the entire cavern was illuminated by towering monolithic pillars of translucent unmelting ice that spiraled upward like petrified frozen waterfalls.
The light they cast was unnatural like a cold oceanic cyan that seemed to drink in sound and movement.
And there, dead-center in the chamber, sat the monument.
A glacier, easily eighty feet wide and rising like a fortress wall of solid ice dominated the floor.
And suspended dead-center within that impenetrable block of primordial ice... was a woman.
She was entombed from her toes straight to the base of her throat with her body locked rigidly beneath feet of flawless crystal-clear stasis.
Only her pale head and the slender curve of her bare shoulders emerged from the flat vertical face of the glacier.
A thick matted mane of midnight-black hair, caked in centuries of untouched unmelting frost, cascaded over her face like a dark shroud, completely obscuring her features from view.
Only the sharp line of her jaw and a pair of parched severely cracked lips were visible through the tangled strands.
She looked dead like a forgotten tragic relic carved from marble and abandoned at the bottom of the world.
KRA-RUMBLE!
The moment Silas took a single step forward, the dry permafrost creaking beneath his boot and the frozen midnight-black hair shifted.
The woman slowly tilted her chin upward.
CRACK-CRACK-SNAP!
The centuries of thick white frost binding her dark eyelashes fractured with a brittle delicate sound that echoed off the distant ice pillars like snapping needles.
Beneath the matted bangs, her eyelids slowly peeled apart and her irises ignited.
It was not a soft glow.
It was a divine emerald-green blaze that lit up the entire chamber in a shocking wave of radiant jade light.
KRA-BOOOOOOOM!
The instantaneous release of her awakening aura sent a physical shockwave rolling through the bedrock.
The frozen platform groaned in agonizing submission, and spiderwebs of hairline fractures raced across the surrounding stalagmites.
The pressure within the vault spiked so violently that Silas’s silver-threaded coat snapped back against his thighs.
Yet... the glacier entombing her body did not yield.
Not a single fissure appeared across the ice binding her collarbones and not a drop of moisture melted from the surface.
The woman drew in a slow ragged breath.
The freezing air scraped through her dry, cracked throat with a harsh whistling rasp that sounded like iron dragged across stone.
She coughed violently, a wet rattling spasm that shook her shoulders within the icy collar, before she finally managed to force her chin down and focus her vision.
She blinked once.
...Twice.
Her divine emerald-green gaze locked squarely onto the mortal standing three paces before her.

She took in every detail with microscopic clarity like the broad shoulders, the relaxed unbothered posture, the hand resting with casual arrogance on the pommel of a golden longsword, the dark wool coat drenched in the foul unmistakable black blood of a very strong monster... and above all else, the roaring furnace of a Mythic Gold Core humming within his chest.
The woman’s divine green eyes dilated until the emerald light swallowed the whites entirely.
Her cracked trembling lips parted.
DRIP!

From beneath her long lashes, genuine tears of hysterical relief welled up, spilling over her pale cheeks and cutting steaming clean tracks through the centuries of dust and grime caked upon her face.
"Hu... Hu... Human...!" she stammered, her voice a cracked high-pitched croak that rattled off the cavern walls. "Ah... AH! A REAL FUCKING HUMAN LORD!"
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP-FLAP!
THUD!
From the ceiling flue above, the obsidian bird finally dropped out of the sky, tumbling violently onto the frictionless ice.
It skidded comically across the permafrost on its stomach with its tail feathers spinning, before colliding head-first into a jagged ice stalagmite with a pathetic hollow thump.
The bird shook its bruised head dizzily, blinked its dark eyes, and scrambled upright.
It ruffled its gore-stained feathers with immense, chest-puffing pride and waddled frantically over to the base of the glacier, letting out a series of self-congratulatory squawks.
"Krrr-caw! Caw! Clack!"
The frozen woman tilted her eyes downward toward the little familiar, her tears flowing freely as her voice cracked with overwhelming gratitude.

"You actually did it, you brilliant, beautiful, magnificent little feathered bastard!" she cried out, completely devoid of any divine composure, sniffling loudly as snot and tears ran down her frozen chin. "I take back every single insult! I take it all back! I won’t pluck your wings! I won’t roast you over a pit! I won’t feed your gizzard to the wolves! You actually brought one! A real Lord with a Gold Core!"
She whipped her head back toward Silas, her green eyes burning with a shameless longing.
The heat radiating off his body was undeniable.

"Lord! Sovereign! Noble master!" the Goddess of Beasts pleaded, her voice rising into a desperate wail that echoed throughout the frozen cathedral. "Please! Break this fucking ice! Shatter this miserable freezing rock and get me out of here!"
She strained against the frozen collar, leaning her chin forward as far as the unyielding ice allowed with her warm tears splashing against the slick permafrost and hissing into vapor.

"If you free me, I will submit to your rule completely!" she blurted out, abandoning every shred of divine dignity and ancient pride without a single second of hesitation. "I don’t care about titles! I will sign anything! I will join your territory! I will bend the knee, swear eternal fealty to Blessed Land, and become your Hero! Whatever enemy, whatever lord, whatever wretched kingdom offends your sight... point your finger, and I will tear their throats out and feed them to the soil!"
GURRRRRRRR-GL!
An undignified sound tore through the quiet cavern.
It originated deep within her frozen midsection... a ravenous earth-shaking rumble that reverberated off the ice pillars like rolling thunder.
The goddess froze.
A furious bright crimson blush burned through the pale frost on her cheeks, cutting straight through her divine aura.
She swallowed hard, licking her parched lips as she looked down at Silas with wide desperate eyes.

"Just... please..." she whimpered, her tone dropping into a pathetic breathless plea. "Please bring a warm blanket... a soft bed... and meat. Real, roasted, seasoned meat, not frozen fish and not cave lichen either! Meat with salt and fat! I will give you my entire existence, Lord! Just break the damn ice!"
Silas stood three paces from the base of the glacier.
He did not flare his Gold Core to channel a burst of shattering force into the frost.
He simply stood on the ground with his golden ringed blue eyes regarding the weeping foul-mouthed deity with an expression of amusement.
Slowly, he folded his arms across his blood-stained chest.
"That’s a very generous offer," Silas said. "And I might just take you up on it."
He took one deliberate step closer with the cold blue light of the chamber reflecting in his eyes as he held her desperate emerald gaze.
"But before I swing this blade... I’ll need you to answer some questions for me first."

sentences.text: With a wet leathery snap of its wings, the bird launched into the freezing air.
Despite the coating of necrotic slime weighing down its primary feathers, the avian familiar cut through the sub-zero squall with startling grace.

It hugged the contours of the scree, staying low beneath the prevailing gale to avoid getting battered against the cliffs, weaving an erratic yet deliberate path between towering monoliths of black basalt that jutted from the permafrost like the shattered ribs of a forgotten leviathan.
WHOOSH!
Silas broke into a steady lope, falling in behind the bird’s dark silhouette.
With every stride, his heavy combat boots crushed the surface crust with a crunching sound with his feet finding instant traction on the uneven frost-heaved rock.
Within his chest, the Gold Core maintained a calm rotation, circulating rivers of radiant mana through his pathways and meridians.

The sub-zero wind lashed his face and whipped the gore-matted black bangs across his eyes, but the cold could not take root as the internal furnace of his core repelled the frost before it could numb his extremities.
"Huuu...
I just want to get this done and over with..."

The local fauna knew better than to approach this sector as they were entering the dead zone of the northern basin.

"Looks deep enough," Silas remarked dryly to the empty wind.

He simply bent his knees, kicked off the permafrost, and stepped out into empty air.
