chapters.title: Chapter 518: Questions [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The cavern was so still that Silas could hear the microscopic snapping of frost forming along the edges of his dried gore-stained collar.
"Fuuu... Fuu..."

Every breath he drew felt like dragging powdered glass across his bronchial tubes, but beneath his ribs, the Mythic Gold Core spun as it was radiating an internal furnace-like warmth that completely warded off the chill.

He stood three paces from the base of the colossal glacier, his traveling coat heavy with the congealed blackened ichor of the weeping eye and his left hand resting casually against the gold wire-wrapped pommel of his sheathed mythril longsword.
The woman entombed within the ancient monolith blinked her jewel-bright emerald eyes.
Very slowly, with an agonizing stiffness that made the thick ancient rime coating her jaw crackle like snapping dry twigs underfoot, she tilted her head a fraction of an inch to the left.
Then, after a painful pause that seemed to test the brittle resilience of her neck muscles, she leaned it to the right.
"Questions...?" she rasped.
The sound was wretched like a dry scrape that resembled rusted iron dragging across jagged slate.
It echoed off the vaulted ceiling of translucent blue ice, making the obsidian bird perching on a nearby basalt spire ruffle its dark plumage nervously.

"You... you stand there looking like an abattoir chimney, mortal," she sputtered, her chapped purple-tinged lips trembling with pure indignation. "I am offering you my celestial authority. I am offering you my soul, my obedience, my eternal submission, and a seat beside a living deity on a silver platter... and you want to hold an administrative job interview while my kneecaps have been frozen into solid crystal for centuries?!"
"Questions keep my people alive, and they keep my things from burning down to ash," Silas replied.
His voice was level and completely unbothered by her divine posturing. He had the upper hand after all...
"I don’t invite ancient relics into my territory without knowing what kind of baggage is tethered to their skirts."

He reached into the interior breast pocket of his stiff blackened coat and his gloved fingers found the edge of the wax-treated parchment he had pried from the petrified knuckles of the dead expeditioner on the shelf above.

Carefully, so as not to shatter the brittle vellum in the sub-zero air, he unrolled the stiff cylinder, holding it outward between two fingers so the legible lines caught the oceanic cyan light radiating from the ice walls.

"Recognize the handwriting?" Silas asked, tapping a scorched corner of the parchment with his thumb. "Recovered this from a corpse clutching an iron chisel a few leagues north... He spent his final hours scribbling a very frantic, very terrified record while your world was being wiped off the map."
The woman’s emerald pupils contracted into razor-thin feline slits.
She leaned her chin forward against the icy collar as far as the ice allowed, her gaze tracking across the faded water-damaged iron-gall script.
"Let’s start with the first contradiction," Silas said, stepping half a pace closer.

The radiant sun-warm heat bleeding off his core washed across the base of the glacier, causing a thin shimmering film of water to bead along the lowest edge before instantly vaporizing into clean steam.

"What I was told and from the Bird, the Forever Ice was made as a seal... and from what I can gather, it’s an unbreakable prison meant to contain the rampaging Goddess of Beasts but Entry Forty-Six tells a completely different story. It describes an active war. It says the ice was actively fighting against you, and that the frost didn’t fall from the clouds... it erupted straight out of the deep crust like an inverted spear. Why was the ice fighting you if it was supposedly forged just to cage you?"
The woman let out a wet rattling scoff that sent tiny needles of frost flying from her lower lip.

"Because mortals are superstitious illiterate idiots who write epic histories based on whatever rubble is left standing after the storm clears," she muttered bitterly, rolling her eyes up toward the dark stone arch of the cavern roof. "A holy seal? A divine containment? Don’t make me spit! It wasn’t a calculated judgment handed down by some grand council of sages either... It was a filthy street brawl."
She paused, taking in a shallow whistling breath that rattled deep within her frozen lungs.

"Her name isn’t worth carving onto a privy wall, but she was a high-order Deity of Ice... a petty arrogant glacier-strumpet from the extreme northern polar caps. She drifted south, took one look at the geothermal leylines running through the Umbral Basin, and decided she wanted to turn my hunting grounds into her personal skating rink so we clashed over the boundary markers. Initially, she fought from the sky. She opened the heavens and brought down a blizzard so dense and heavy it choked the daylight out of the sky for forty days... But my beasts were born for jagged scree and rough weather so my mammoth-crushers and iron-furred panthers tore through her frost-golems like wet paper and she realized within three days that she couldn’t break my beasts from above."
A grim hatred settled into the pale lines of the goddess’s face, washing away her manic humor.

"So, she cheated. She realized my beasts drew their stamina directly from the living earth, from the volcanic veins pulsing deep beneath the bedrock so she disengaged from the airspace, condensed her entire divine authority into a single spear, and drove it directly into the planetary marrow beneath the basin floor."
The woman took in a deep breath.

"She didn’t drop cold from the clouds anymore... she transmuted the aquifers, the magma pockets, and the mineral roots of the entire valley into absolute zero. The permafrost exploded upward, frozen geysers thirty leagues wide detonated straight through the floor, turning the stone into liquid glass and freezing my pack from the claws up before they could even turn their heads. This cavern... this shelf... it’s not an ancient tomb designed by architects. It’s the fossilized impact crater of her final strike."
Silas nodded slowly, his mind slotting the pieces together.

The unnatural vertical shafts he had seen on the way down, the smooth, circular boreholes cutting through thousands of feet of solid granite without a single pick mark... they weren’t mining shafts at all.
They were the geological scars of pressurized geysers that had flash-frozen as they breached the surface.

"That leads directly into Entry Forty-Six," Silas said, his finger shifting down to a heavily scorched tear running across the middle of the paper. "The journal mentions an abattoir... It describes thousands of people dying in the span of a single breath. The Umbral Basin is a lightless frozen wasteland today with trees and some berries, populated only by feral anomalies and necrotic mist. Why were there armed mortals operating in these northern trenches centuries ago?"

"Because before this miserable ditch was frozen into a dead zone, it was a thriving basin!" the woman snapped with a small trace of nostalgic pride bleeding through her gravelly voice. "Mortals lived here by the thousands, you ignorant whelp! They built terraced stone townships along the south-facing cliffs, forged irrigation aqueducts that carried hot mineral water through the snow, and, above all else, they dug. The mineral wealth of the Umbral Basin was legendary across this place. Star-iron, mythril marrow, compressed atmospheric crystals... the deep veins here could fund three empires for ten generations."
Her voice dropped with the proud tone crumbling into a quiet hollow rasp.

"They were caught in the gears, human. Mortals are fragile things. They are made of salt water, warm meat, and brittle bone. When two divine entities unleash localized conceptual domains at point-blank range, mortal biology simply surrenders... If the shockwaves of our clashes didn’t liquefy their brains through the bedrock, her absolute zero reached into their chests and stopped their blood mid-pump. The glacier swallowed everything. The townships, the refining forges, the transport hoists... thousands of workers and guards were frozen into crystal statues before they could even drop their tools and a blooming civilization was snuffed out between a morning bell and an afternoon whistle."
She clenched her jaw so tightly that Silas could hear the enamel grind.

"And my beasts..." she whispered, her emerald eyes trembling with helpless rage. "Every single divine hound I had nurtured from a pup... My apex serpents... My sky-tearing dread-hawks... Every creature bound to my soul was butchered. If they weren’t crushed under falling mountain faces, their life-force was siphoned into her conceptual freeze to fuel the lock. Right now..."
She looked down at the pale bare flesh of her exposed shoulders, an expression of bitter suffocating humiliation washing over her features.
"...I have nothing left. Not a single pup... Not a single cub... My spiritual domain is an empty barren field and I am completely stripped."
She forced her chin up, looking Silas dead in the eyes with unabashed desperation.

"I will not lie to you, human Lord. You hold all the cards, and I am not too proud to admit what I am right now. In a straight brawl, I am useless to you... Centuries of conceptual stasis have sucked my divine reservoir down to the dregs as my meridians are brittle and my spiritual bones are cracked. Right now, a well-placed kick from an ordinary mortal foot soldier would probably knock my teeth out and give me a concussion. But...!"
Her irises flared with sudden feverish green fire.

"I am still the Goddess of Beasts! The authority over the fang, the claw, and the wild blood is carved into the very substrate of my divine core! You break this ice, you feed me, you give me shelter within your territory, and as I rebuild my strength, every drop of authority I reclaim belongs to you! I will tame the monstrosities of this basin for you! I will weave Beast contracts for your armies! I will forge mounts that can tear city gates off their hinges! And upon the shattered marrow of my ancient domain, I swear I will never raise a hand or a fang against you!"
Silas studied her face.
He didn’t see deceit at all, he saw her desperation instead.
"One more question," Silas said.
He turned the vellum, pointing his finger at the very last, jagged line of ink scrawled before the writer’s hand had succumbed to rigor mortis.
"The scout left a final warning. ’The seal was never meant to hold her... the seal was meant to contain the []... beware the deep mines.’ What is buried in the dark behind this wall?"
The goddess blinked.
She stared at the text, her brow furrowing in genuine uncomprehending bewilderment.
"Behind this wall...?" she echoed, tilting her head back against the ice shelf. "What in the nine hells is that dead fool rambling about?"

"You’re telling me you don’t know?" Silas pressed, his eyes narrowing into cold slits. "The expeditioner was terrified as he specifically warned whoever found his bones not to look for treasure, and that the ice was forged to keep something far worse from getting out."
The woman threw her head back and let out a dry barking laugh that dissolved into a violent coughing fit.

"Mortal paranoia!" she wheezed, spitting a fleck of rime onto the permafrost. "Total peasant nonsense! When people are dying in the dark, shivering in their own filth while the sky falls down, their little minds always invent some ancient lurking horror under the bedboards! It gives their deaths meaning! It makes them feel like they were part of some grand cosmic catastrophe instead of just collateral damage in a petty border squabble!"
She shook her head, her matted hair swaying against her pale neck.

"There was no slumbering primordial evil, human! There was no ancient world-eater tucked under the rocks! The Ice Deity wanted my territory, and I wanted to rip her throat out! The deep mines were just that... mines! The locals were digging deep into the crust to pull out high-grade ore, and when the Ice Deity inverted the mantle, she sealed the entire shaft system because that’s where the heat was rising from!"
Silas took a slow step forward, his gaze drifting past her exposed pale shoulders toward the dark monolithic wall of opaque black ice extending behind the glacier.
"Where does the main shaft sit, then?" he asked quietly.
The goddess went silent for a moment, her green eyes darting back and forth as she sorted through centuries of fragmented memories.
"Well..." she muttered, her tone suddenly losing its defensive edge.

"Right behind me, actually. The main extraction hoist of the Great Northern Borehole ran directly through the bedrock fault where she pinned me. The glacier filled the mouth of the tunnel like a cork driven into a wine jug."
’I see...’ Silas thought, his eyes hardening.
The pieces fell into place with chilling logic.
If the extraction tunnel lay directly behind her, then freezing her in this exact geographic coordinate served a dual purpose.
She was the anchor.
Her divine soul, locked in a stasis, acted as the weight holding the ice plug in place over the entrance to the deep mines.
Whether there was an ancient terror down there or simply millions of tons of unstable collapsed rock, Silas had zero intention of excavating it today.
’If there’s something sleeping in the deep crust, it can stay asleep. I’m pulling her out, but that shaft stays deadbolted.’
He exhaled a long breath, letting his posture relax as he looked back down at the shivering deity.

"Fuuu...
Fuu..."

It says the ice was actively fighting against you, and that the frost didn’t fall from the clouds... it erupted straight out of the deep crust like an inverted spear.
Why was the ice fighting you if it was supposedly forged just to cage you?"
The woman let out a wet rattling scoff that sent tiny needles of frost flying from her lower lip.

"Because mortals are superstitious illiterate idiots who write epic histories based on whatever rubble is left standing after the storm clears," she muttered bitterly, rolling her eyes up toward the dark stone arch of the cavern roof.
"A holy seal?
A divine containment?
Don’t make me spit!
It wasn’t a calculated judgment handed down by some grand council of sages either...
It was a filthy street brawl."
She paused, taking in a shallow whistling breath that rattled deep within her frozen lungs.
"Her name isn’t worth carving onto a privy wall, but she was a high-order Deity of Ice... a petty arrogant glacier-strumpet from the extreme northern polar caps.

She drifted south, took one look at the geothermal leylines running through the Umbral Basin, and decided she wanted to turn my hunting grounds into her personal skating rink so we clashed over the boundary markers.
Initially, she fought from the sky.
She opened the heavens and brought down a blizzard so dense and heavy it choked the daylight out of the sky for forty days...

But my beasts were born for jagged scree and rough weather so my mammoth-crushers and iron-furred panthers tore through her frost-golems like wet paper and she realized within three days that she couldn’t break my beasts from above."
A grim hatred settled into the pale lines of the goddess’s face, washing away her manic humor.
"So, she cheated.

She realized my beasts drew their stamina directly from the living earth, from the volcanic veins pulsing deep beneath the bedrock so she disengaged from the airspace, condensed her entire divine authority into a single spear, and drove it directly into the planetary marrow beneath the basin floor."
The woman took in a deep breath.
"She didn’t drop cold from the clouds anymore... she transmuted the aquifers, the magma pockets, and the mineral roots of the entire valley into absolute zero.

The permafrost exploded upward, frozen geysers thirty leagues wide detonated straight through the floor, turning the stone into liquid glass and freezing my pack from the claws up before they could even turn their heads.
This cavern... this shelf... it’s not an ancient tomb designed by architects.
It’s the fossilized impact crater of her final strike."
Silas nodded slowly, his mind slotting the pieces together.

The unnatural vertical shafts he had seen on the way down, the smooth, circular boreholes cutting through thousands of feet of solid granite without a single pick mark... they weren’t mining shafts at all.
They were the geological scars of pressurized geysers that had flash-frozen as they breached the surface.
"That leads directly into Entry Forty-Six," Silas said, his finger shifting down to a heavily scorched tear running across the middle of the paper.
"The journal mentions an abattoir...
It describes thousands of people dying in the span of a single breath.
The Umbral Basin is a lightless frozen wasteland today with trees and some berries, populated only by feral anomalies and necrotic mist.
Why were there armed mortals operating in these northern trenches centuries ago?"
"Because before this miserable ditch was frozen into a dead zone, it was a thriving basin!" the woman snapped with a small trace of nostalgic pride bleeding through her gravelly voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 519: Rikavariashaluna-El-Theris-Kalyndra [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, expanding his spiritual perception outward.

The Gold Core within his chest pulsed gently, sending an invisible high-frequency ripple of pure golden mana washing across the cavern floor, brushing against the perimeter walls, the ceiling stalactites, and everywhere around.
’Eluned and the girls should be coming here by now,’ He calculated.

"Eeeek! Ah! What is that?!" The Goddess suddenly squealed, her pale shoulders violently twitching within the ice collar as a vivid dark crimson blush exploded across her chapped cheeks. "Stop! Stop that! What is that golden thing you’re rubbing against my soul?! It tickles! It feels like hundreds of tiny warm brass needles brushing against the back of my neck and down my spine! Ah! It’s horribly ticklish!"
Silas opened his eyes, letting out a dry exasperated sigh as he pulled his mana back.
"You’re absurdly mana-sensitive for an entity that claims to be running on empty."

"I am an ancient celestial authority, you uncultured barbarian, not a brick wall!" she protested loudly, though she couldn’t stop a wide toothy grin from splitting her cracked lips. "So... does that mean the interrogation is concluded? Did I answer correctly? Am I hired, or am I going to freeze into a permanent coat rack?!"
Silas let his hands drop to his sides with the golden crossguard of his blade glinting in the pale light.

"You’re hired," Silas said. "Under my condition... You swear your soul, your divinity, and your physical existence to Blessed Land. You take the oath of a Hero and you answer directly to my command. There will be no rogue expeditions, no divine temper tantrums, and no insubordination."
"Do you have meat?" she asked immediately, her eyes wide and dead serious.
"I have an entire cold storage of wolf meat, smoked boar, hot bone broth and a lot more," Silas answered smoothly.

"DEAL! DONE! SIGNED IN BLOOD AND CARVED IN BONE!" the goddess screamed with hysterical glee, rattling the icicles hanging from the roof. "Hurry up and smash this miserable ice cube before my jaw shatters from shivering!"
"Hold your horses," Silas said, resting his palm on the pommel of his longsword. "If you’re going to become my Hero, I need a name. What do I write down?"
The goddess immediately pulled her chin up, puffing out her chest with as much grandeur as a woman frozen to her collarbone could muster.
Her emerald eyes flashed with a dramatic glow.
"Hear my true primordial name and tremble, mortal Lord! I am Rikavariashaluna-El-Theris-Kalyndra, High Warden of the Primeval Brood and Goddess of the Fanged Courts, Lady of—"
"Rika," Silas cut in flatly.
The goddess instantly choked on her own breath, her regal expression collapsing into a slack-jawed horrified stare. "R-Rika...?"
"Rika," Silas repeated, giving a single decisive nod. "It’s clean and I don’t have to spend five minutes reciting a poem every time I need you to summon a wolf. By the way, I’m Silas."
She stared at him, her mouth opening and closing like a landed trout.
Slowly, the indignant shock faded from her eyes, replaced by a strange warm softness.
A small genuine smile curled the corners of her cracked lips.
"Rika..." she murmured, testing the sound against her tongue. "Hmph. It’s short. Terribly mortal... but it has a nice ring to it. Very well, Lord Silas! Rika is ready! Break the shell!"
"Bird," Silas barked over his shoulder. "Clear the blast radius."
The obsidian familiar didn’t hesitate.

With a sharp terrified "Krrr-caw!" it launched from the basalt spire, beating its dark wings frantically to flutter behind a massive granite boulder thirty paces back, poking only its crested head and scythe-curved beak out from behind the stone.
Silas took a wide balanced stance before the glacier.
SHING!
He drew his mythril longsword.
The golden blade cleared the scabbard with a sharp ringing chime that vibrated through the dead air of the vault.
The polished metal caught the blue luminescence, but beneath the surface of the steel, a sun-bright radiance began to coil.
Rika watched the blade, her emerald irises darting nervously across the glowing steel.

’He has a Gold Core, that much is obvious from the heat,’ she thought, a knot of anxiety tightening in her throat. ’But this is ice forged by a high-order deity... It doesn’t melt under mere fire magic, and strikes just bounce off the stasis weave. How does a mortal longsword even begin to bite into—’
Silas didn’t strike blindly.
He lowered his chin, exhaling a thin stream of gray mist through his nostrils as he focused his intent, channeling a dense thread of refined mana directly into his optic nerves.
[Rip-Current Perception] was activated!
Instantly, the visual spectrum of the chamber dissolved.
The solid permafrost and the towering glacier lost their opaque density, transforming into a complex show of elemental currents and tectonic stress lines.

Silas saw the crystalline weave of the conceptual cold... billions of petrified mana threads anchored deep into the cavern floor, looping through the glacier, and converging directly into a swirling nexus locked around Rika’s collarbones.
’There,’ Silas spotted the structural flaw.
Right at the base of her left clavicle, three inches beneath the surface of the frost, lay an infinitesimal fracture.
It was a hairline stress fault born from Rika’s awakening aura when her divine eyes had first snapped open moments ago.
’Or maybe she has been doing it a lot but that part is weaker.’
The weave was slightly stretched with the threads pulling taut against the anchor.

’Eluned estimated that breaking through this thing through continuous flaming strikes would take at least thirty minutes of concentrated channeling,’ Silas thought, his Gold Core beginning to spin with violent escalating torque. ’Thirty minutes is an eternity is too long... I’m not waiting around for a slow thaw.’
VUUUUUUUUUM!
Silas opened the floodgates of his core.
Blinding golden flames erupted from his pores, wreathing his forearms and spiraling along the length of his longsword in a roaring pressurized vortex.
The sudden release of high-tier energy caused the permafrost beneath his boots to violently sublimate, throwing up a dense screen of hissing, superheated steam.
Rika gasped, the intense furnace-like heat washing over her frozen cheeks, stinging her frostbitten skin with sudden, glorious, and almost agonizing warmth.
Silas coiled his hips, shifting his weight onto the ball of his back foot.
BOOM!
Silas exploded forward.

He didn’t execute a wide sweeping slash, instead he channeled the entire kinetic weight of his charge, the rotational torque of his core, and the concentrated solar heat of his flames into a single, pinpoint thrust, driving the tip of his golden blade straight into the microscopic stress fracture,
CLANG-KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The collision sounded like a siege engine striking a mountain of solid iron.
A concussive shockwave of pulverized white rime detonated outward in a thirty-foot ring, blasting through the cavern and rattling the stalactites overhead like wind chimes.
For a terrifying heartbeat, nothing happened.

The golden blade remained wedged three inches into the face of the glacier as the incandescent flames hissed furiously against the unyielding ice, but the ice itself held firm, swallowing the heat without melting a single millimeter.
"D-Did it work?!" Rika shrieked, her voice pitching up in frantic panic. "Hit it again! Channel lightning! Hit it with a rock! Don’t tell me your sword bounced—"
TICK!
A sound no louder than a snapping hair echoed through the vault.
CRACK-CRACK-KRA-BOOM!
From the tip of Silas’s blade, thousands of radiant golden fractures violently spiderwebbed across the surface of the glacier.
The deep, ethereal cyan light within the ice died instantly, snuffed out by brilliant veins of golden fire that tore through the threads like acid eating through cotton.
"IT’S SPLITTING!" Rika screamed in hysterical delight.
Silas didn’t waste a second.
He wrenched the blade free, stepped into a tight half-spin, and brought the reinforced flat of his sword crashing horizontally against the fractured perimeter surrounding her shoulders.
KRA-SHATTER!
A colossal slab of ancient petrified ice broke away in a deafening cascade!
The conceptual collar pinning Rika’s throat snapped with a hollow crack.
Her body, completely released from centuries of immobility, pitched forward into the empty air, tumbling downward amidst a shower of heavy, tumbling ice boulders.
THUD!
Rika hit the permafrost in an uncoordinated heap, gasping and hacking as the cold air rushed into her uncompressed lungs.
Silas planted his boots, breathing heavily as he lowered his sword. He turned his eyes to the wall behind her.
The entire glacier had not shattered.
Despite pouring every ounce of force and core output into the strike, only the front face holding the goddess had broken free.
The massive, thirty-foot-thick foundation of black ice plugging the Great Northern Borehole remained largely intact, scarred with glowing cracks but holding firm against the void behind it.

’Damn,’ Silas thought, wiping a bead of sweat from his chin before it could freeze. ’Even with a Gold Core, conceptual magic left behind by an ancient deity is absurdly resilient... Cleaving through this entire formation would have taken hours.’
He looked down at the dark narrow fissure exposed at the base of the plug.
He wasn’t taking any chances with whatever was sleeping in the dark.
Silas thrust his left palm forward, channeling water mana.
"Ice Transformation!"
FZZZZZZT-SNAP!

The thousands of shattered ice chunks littering the floor liquefied instantly under his command, surging into the fissure like a torrent of molten glass before re-freezing into a smooth seamless twenty-foot-thick barricade of reinforced permafrost!
Silas let out a satisfied grunt. ’Good. The door stays locked.’
"I’M FREE! I’M ALIVE! I HAVE ANKLES! I HAVE KNEES!"
Before Silas could even turn his torso, a pale, shivering blur threw itself straight at his chest.
"Oof!"
Rika slammed into him with the uncoordinated momentum of a falling sack of grain, her freezing bare arms locking in an iron vice around his neck.

Silas’s boots lost their purchase on the slick, freshly formed permafrost, and the two of them tumbled to the ground, rolling across the stone in an undignified heap of flailing limbs and blood-crusted wool!

"THANK YOU! THANK YOU, YOU GLORIOUS SUN-FLAVORED HUMAN!" Rika wailed at the top of her lungs, burying her face straight into the crook of his neck, completely unbothered by the foul stench of the weeping eye’s black ichor. "I CAN BREATHE! I CAN SHIVER! I PROMISE I WILL NEVER COMPLAIN ABOUT BLIZZARDS AGAIN! PRAISE THE SOIL! PRAISE THE BEDROCK!"

"Hey! Get off me, you oversized stray!" Silas grunted, planting both hands against her shoulders and shoving her back with a scowl. "Hold still! You feel like a slab of frozen beef, and you’re getting snot on my tunic!"

"I don’t care! I love you! You are my savior, my master, my Lord! I’ll carve your face into a mountain!" she sobbed with tears flowing freely down her pale cheeks and freezing into tiny glittering pearls on his leather lapel.
"Hold still!"
Silas grabbed her chin with his left hand, forcefully tilting her head upright.
His golden ringed blue eyes locked onto her watering emerald irises, his fingertips flaring with a bright corona of Mythic Gold mana.
He slammed his index and middle fingers directly against the center of her forehead!
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A blinding aura of golden light erupted beneath his touch.
Dense rivers of gold mana surged from Silas’s core, pouring through her cranial meridians and diving deep into her vacant frozen spiritual reservoir.
The energy swept through her meridians like wildfire, burning away the lingering conceptual frost and anchoring her divine soul directly to Blessed Land.
[Hero Contract Has Been Established.]
[Name: Rikavariashaluna (Rika).]
[Tap To See Her Full Status Below]
Rika gasped, her entire body arching as the golden mana settled into her core, establishing an unbreakable warm link between her existence and the man kneeling above her.
"There," Silas exhaled, pulling his hand away as the golden crest faded beneath her pale skin. "You’re on the books so welcome to Blessed Land."
Rika touched her forehead with trembling fingers, her eyes wide with reverence.
Slowly, she leaned forward and pressed her forehead against his breastplate in a gesture of unreserved submission.
"My soul is yours, Lord Silas," she whispered, her voice surprisingly soft and solemn. "My fangs will strike only where you point. I swear it upon my very existence."
Silas let out a quiet chuckle, tapping her head with a gloved knuckle.
"Good. Now get your feet under you. You’re heavier than you look."
GURRRRRRRRRRRRRR-GL!
A sound like an erupting mud geyser tore through Rika’s midsection, vibrating violently against Silas’s ribs.
Rika froze.
A brilliant dark crimson blush burned through the pale frost on her cheeks, turning her entire face bright red.
She slowly lifted her head, looking up at him with watering shameless puppy-dog eyes.
"Lord Silas...?" she whimpered pathetically. "The... the contract mentioned roasted meat. You promised on your sovereign honor."
"I know, I know," Silas sighed, shaking his head with an amused grin.
He stood up, brushing the crushed ice from his knees, and offered her a hand.
Rika’s legs were like wet noodles as she wobbled violently, clinging to his arm for balance before she could even stand upright.
With a flick of his wrist, Silas opened his spatial inventory.
VUUUM!
A thick double-layered wool blanket materialized in the air. Silas caught it and wrapped it snugly around her shivering shoulders, bundling her up like a dark-haired mummy.
Next, he pulled out an insulated, fleece-lined leather mat, spreading it smoothly across the permafrost.

The Gold Core within his chest pulsed gently, sending an invisible high-frequency ripple of pure golden mana washing across the cavern floor, brushing against the perimeter walls, the ceiling stalactites, and everywhere around.
’Eluned and the girls should be coming here by now,’ He calculated.
"Eeeek!
Ah!
What is that?!" The Goddess suddenly squealed, her pale shoulders violently twitching within the ice collar as a vivid dark crimson blush exploded across her chapped cheeks.
"Stop!
Stop that!
What is that golden thing you’re rubbing against my soul?!
It tickles!
It feels like hundreds of tiny warm brass needles brushing against the back of my neck and down my spine!
Ah!
It’s horribly ticklish!"
Silas opened his eyes, letting out a dry exasperated sigh as he pulled his mana back.
"You’re absurdly mana-sensitive for an entity that claims to be running on empty."
"I am an ancient celestial authority, you uncultured barbarian, not a brick wall!" she protested loudly, though she couldn’t stop a wide toothy grin from splitting her cracked lips.
"So... does that mean the interrogation is concluded?
Did I answer correctly?
Am I hired, or am I going to freeze into a permanent coat rack?!"
Silas let his hands drop to his sides with the golden crossguard of his blade glinting in the pale light.
"You’re hired," Silas said.
"Under my condition...
You swear your soul, your divinity, and your physical existence to Blessed Land.
You take the oath of a Hero and you answer directly to my command.
There will be no rogue expeditions, no divine temper tantrums, and no insubordination."
"Do you have meat?" she asked immediately, her eyes wide and dead serious.
"I have an entire cold storage of wolf meat, smoked boar, hot bone broth and a lot more," Silas answered smoothly.
"DEAL!
DONE!
SIGNED IN BLOOD AND CARVED IN BONE!" the goddess screamed with hysterical glee, rattling the icicles hanging from the roof.
"Hurry up and smash this miserable ice cube before my jaw shatters from shivering!"
"Hold your horses," Silas said, resting his palm on the pommel of his longsword.
"If you’re going to become my Hero, I need a name.
What do I write down?"
The goddess immediately pulled her chin up, puffing out her chest with as much grandeur as a woman frozen to her collarbone could muster.
Her emerald eyes flashed with a dramatic glow.
"Hear my true primordial name and tremble, mortal Lord!
I am Rikavariashaluna-El-Theris-Kalyndra, High Warden of the Primeval Brood and Goddess of the Fanged Courts, Lady of—"
"Rika," Silas cut in flatly.
The goddess instantly choked on her own breath, her regal expression collapsing into a slack-jawed horrified stare.
"R-Rika...?"
"Rika," Silas repeated, giving a single decisive nod.
"It’s clean and I don’t have to spend five minutes reciting a poem every time I need you to summon a wolf.
By the way, I’m Silas."
She stared at him, her mouth opening and closing like a landed trout.
Slowly, the indignant shock faded from her eyes, replaced by a strange warm softness.
A small genuine smile curled the corners of her cracked lips.
"Rika..." she murmured, testing the sound against her tongue.
"Hmph.
It’s short.
Terribly mortal... but it has a nice ring to it.
Very well, Lord Silas!
Rika is ready!
Break the shell!"
"Bird," Silas barked over his shoulder.
"Clear the blast radius."
The obsidian familiar didn’t hesitate.

With a sharp terrified "Krrr-caw!" it launched from the basalt spire, beating its dark wings frantically to flutter behind a massive granite boulder thirty paces back, poking only its crested head and scythe-curved beak out from behind the stone.
Silas took a wide balanced stance before the glacier.
SHING!
He drew his mythril longsword.
The golden blade cleared the scabbard with a sharp ringing chime that vibrated through the dead air of the vault.
The polished metal caught the blue luminescence, but beneath the surface of the steel, a sun-bright radiance began to coil.
Rika watched the blade, her emerald irises darting nervously across the glowing steel.
’He has a Gold Core, that much is obvious from the heat,’ she thought, a knot of anxiety tightening in her throat. ’But this is ice forged by a high-order deity...
It doesn’t melt under mere fire magic, and strikes just bounce off the stasis weave.
How does a mortal longsword even begin to bite into—’
Silas didn’t strike blindly.
He lowered his chin, exhaling a thin stream of gray mist through his nostrils as he focused his intent, channeling a dense thread of refined mana directly into his optic nerves.
[Rip-Current Perception] was activated!
Instantly, the visual spectrum of the chamber dissolved.
The solid permafrost and the towering glacier lost their opaque density, transforming into a complex show of elemental currents and tectonic stress lines.

Silas saw the crystalline weave of the conceptual cold... billions of petrified mana threads anchored deep into the cavern floor, looping through the glacier, and converging directly into a swirling nexus locked around Rika’s collarbones.
’There,’ Silas spotted the structural flaw.
Right at the base of her left clavicle, three inches beneath the surface of the frost, lay an infinitesimal fracture.
It was a hairline stress fault born from Rika’s awakening aura when her divine eyes had first snapped open moments ago.
’Or maybe she has been doing it a lot but that part is weaker.’
The weave was slightly stretched with the threads pulling taut against the anchor.

’Eluned estimated that breaking through this thing through continuous flaming strikes would take at least thirty minutes of concentrated channeling,’ Silas thought, his Gold Core beginning to spin with violent escalating torque. ’Thirty minutes is an eternity is too long...
I’m not waiting around for a slow thaw.’
VUUUUUUUUUM!
Silas opened the floodgates of his core.
Blinding golden flames erupted from his pores, wreathing his forearms and spiraling along the length of his longsword in a roaring pressurized vortex.
The sudden release of high-tier energy caused the permafrost beneath his boots to violently sublimate, throwing up a dense screen of hissing, superheated steam.
Rika gasped, the intense furnace-like heat washing over her frozen cheeks, stinging her frostbitten skin with sudden, glorious, and almost agonizing warmth.
Silas coiled his hips, shifting his weight onto the ball of his back foot.
BOOM!
Silas exploded forward.

He didn’t execute a wide sweeping slash, instead he channeled the entire kinetic weight of his charge, the rotational torque of his core, and the concentrated solar heat of his flames into a single, pinpoint thrust, driving the tip of his golden blade straight into the microscopic stress fracture,
CLANG-KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The collision sounded like a siege engine striking a mountain of solid iron.
A concussive shockwave of pulverized white rime detonated outward in a thirty-foot ring, blasting through the cavern and rattling the stalactites overhead like wind chimes.
For a terrifying heartbeat, nothing happened.

The golden blade remained wedged three inches into the face of the glacier as the incandescent flames hissed furiously against the unyielding ice, but the ice itself held firm, swallowing the heat without melting a single millimeter.
"D-Did it work?!" Rika shrieked, her voice pitching up in frantic panic.
"Hit it again!
Channel lightning!
Hit it with a rock!
Don’t tell me your sword bounced—"
TICK!
A sound no louder than a snapping hair echoed through the vault.
CRACK-CRACK-KRA-BOOM!
From the tip of Silas’s blade, thousands of radiant golden fractures violently spiderwebbed across the surface of the glacier.
The deep, ethereal cyan light within the ice died instantly, snuffed out by brilliant veins of golden fire that tore through the threads like acid eating through cotton.
"IT’S SPLITTING!" Rika screamed in hysterical delight.
Silas didn’t waste a second.
He wrenched the blade free, stepped into a tight half-spin, and brought the reinforced flat of his sword crashing horizontally against the fractured perimeter surrounding her shoulders.
KRA-SHATTER!
A colossal slab of ancient petrified ice broke away in a deafening cascade!
The conceptual collar pinning Rika’s throat snapped with a hollow crack.
Her body, completely released from centuries of immobility, pitched forward into the empty air, tumbling downward amidst a shower of heavy, tumbling ice boulders.
THUD!
Rika hit the permafrost in an uncoordinated heap, gasping and hacking as the cold air rushed into her uncompressed lungs.
Silas planted his boots, breathing heavily as he lowered his sword.
He turned his eyes to the wall behind her.
The entire glacier had not shattered.
Despite pouring every ounce of force and core output into the strike, only the front face holding the goddess had broken free.
The massive, thirty-foot-thick foundation of black ice plugging the Great Northern Borehole remained largely intact, scarred with glowing cracks but holding firm against the void behind it.
’Damn,’ Silas thought, wiping a bead of sweat from his chin before it could freeze. ’Even with a Gold Core, conceptual magic left behind by an ancient deity is absurdly resilient...
Cleaving through this entire formation would have taken hours.’
He looked down at the dark narrow fissure exposed at the base of the plug.
He wasn’t taking any chances with whatever was sleeping in the dark.
Silas thrust his left palm forward, channeling water mana.
"Ice Transformation!"
FZZZZZZT-SNAP!

The thousands of shattered ice chunks littering the floor liquefied instantly under his command, surging into the fissure like a torrent of molten glass before re-freezing into a smooth seamless twenty-foot-thick barricade of reinforced permafrost!
Silas let out a satisfied grunt. ’Good.
The door stays locked.’
"I’M FREE!
I’M ALIVE!
I HAVE ANKLES!
I HAVE KNEES!"
Before Silas could even turn his torso, a pale, shivering blur threw itself straight at his chest.
"Oof!"
Rika slammed into him with the uncoordinated momentum of a falling sack of grain, her freezing bare arms locking in an iron vice around his neck.

Silas’s boots lost their purchase on the slick, freshly formed permafrost, and the two of them tumbled to the ground, rolling across the stone in an undignified heap of flailing limbs and blood-crusted wool!
"THANK YOU!

THANK YOU, YOU GLORIOUS SUN-FLAVORED HUMAN!" Rika wailed at the top of her lungs, burying her face straight into the crook of his neck, completely unbothered by the foul stench of the weeping eye’s black ichor.
"I CAN BREATHE!
I CAN SHIVER!
I PROMISE I WILL NEVER COMPLAIN ABOUT BLIZZARDS AGAIN!
PRAISE THE SOIL!
PRAISE THE BEDROCK!"
"Hey!
Get off me, you oversized stray!" Silas grunted, planting both hands against her shoulders and shoving her back with a scowl.
"Hold still!
You feel like a slab of frozen beef, and you’re getting snot on my tunic!"
"I don’t care!
I love you!
You are my savior, my master, my Lord!
I’ll carve your face into a mountain!" she sobbed with tears flowing freely down her pale cheeks and freezing into tiny glittering pearls on his leather lapel.
"Hold still!"
Silas grabbed her chin with his left hand, forcefully tilting her head upright.
His golden ringed blue eyes locked onto her watering emerald irises, his fingertips flaring with a bright corona of Mythic Gold mana.
He slammed his index and middle fingers directly against the center of her forehead!
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A blinding aura of golden light erupted beneath his touch.
Dense rivers of gold mana surged from Silas’s core, pouring through her cranial meridians and diving deep into her vacant frozen spiritual reservoir.
The energy swept through her meridians like wildfire, burning away the lingering conceptual frost and anchoring her divine soul directly to Blessed Land.
[Hero Contract Has Been Established.]
[Name: Rikavariashaluna (Rika).]
[Tap To See Her Full Status Below]
Rika gasped, her entire body arching as the golden mana settled into her core, establishing an unbreakable warm link between her existence and the man kneeling above her.
"There," Silas exhaled, pulling his hand away as the golden crest faded beneath her pale skin.
"You’re on the books so welcome to Blessed Land."
Rika touched her forehead with trembling fingers, her eyes wide with reverence.
Slowly, she leaned forward and pressed her forehead against his breastplate in a gesture of unreserved submission.
"My soul is yours, Lord Silas," she whispered, her voice surprisingly soft and solemn.
"My fangs will strike only where you point.
I swear it upon my very existence."
Silas let out a quiet chuckle, tapping her head with a gloved knuckle.
"Good.
Now get your feet under you.
You’re heavier than you look."
GURRRRRRRRRRRRRR-GL!
A sound like an erupting mud geyser tore through Rika’s midsection, vibrating violently against Silas’s ribs.
Rika froze.
A brilliant dark crimson blush burned through the pale frost on her cheeks, turning her entire face bright red.
She slowly lifted her head, looking up at him with watering shameless puppy-dog eyes.
"Lord Silas...?" she whimpered pathetically.
"The... the contract mentioned roasted meat.
You promised on your sovereign honor."
"I know, I know," Silas sighed, shaking his head with an amused grin.
He stood up, brushing the crushed ice from his knees, and offered her a hand.
Rika’s legs were like wet noodles as she wobbled violently, clinging to his arm for balance before she could even stand upright.
With a flick of his wrist, Silas opened his spatial inventory.
VUUUM!
A thick double-layered wool blanket materialized in the air.
Silas caught it and wrapped it snugly around her shivering shoulders, bundling her up like a dark-haired mummy.
Next, he pulled out an insulated, fleece-lined leather mat, spreading it smoothly across the permafrost.

chapters.title: Chapter 520: You Were Weak, So What? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Rika collapsed onto the mat with a grateful sigh, pulling the blanket tight around her throat.
Silas reached back into his inventory and brought out several more containers that Kaelia had carefully packed before the expedition marched north.
He pressed the release latches with a crisp clack.
The heavenly aroma of piping hot venison stew, roasted garlic bulbs, and heavily spiced braised mutton exploded into the freezing cavern air.
Rika’s emerald eyes nearly popped out of their sockets.
Her nostrils flared, drawing in the savory steam with an expression of pure ecstasy.
She threw the blanket back slightly, pressed both of her trembling frost-bitten hands together in front of her nose, and bowed her head toward Silas with reverent intensity.
"ITADAKIMASU!" she yelled at the top of her lungs.
Silas blinked, his eyebrows shooting up toward his hairline.
’...Itadakimasu? Did this ancient northern deity just bust out standard Japanese meal etiquette?’
Before he could even begin to dissect the bizarre linguistic anomaly, Rika abandoned every shred of divine dignity.
She lunged forward, grabbed the largest brass container with both hands, ignored the boiling steam and tipped the rim straight into her mouth.
Massive chunks of tender, slow-braised venison, rich bone marrow broth and spiced root vegetables disappeared down her throat in ravenous, terrifying gulps.
GLUG-GLUG-CHOMP-GULP!

"OH GODS! OH MOTHER OF EARTH! IT’S SO GOOD!" she screamed between mouthfuls, gravy and brown sauce splattering across her pale cheeks, chin, and fingers. "THE SALT! THE ANIMAL FAT! I CAN FEEL MY TONGUE AGAIN! LORD SILAS, I WILL DIE FOR YOU! I WILL SLAUGHTER ENTIRE PANTHEONS FOR THIS STEW! I LOVE YOU SO MUCH!"
Silas dropped cross-legged onto the mat beside her, resting his elbow on his knee as he watched her inhale the food with morbid amusement.
"Slow down, Rika. You’re going to choke to death ten minutes after I carved you out of a glacier."
"Can’t... stop... the void... demands tribute...!" she mumbled around a mouthful of mutton, already reaching for the second container.
Meanwhile, hundreds of feet above in the howling whiteout, the vanguard had arrived at the lip of the vertical drop.
The wind roared across the basalt crags, tearing at the heavy fur mantles of the girls.
The Blessed Wolves stood in a tight disciplined defensive ring around the horses, their golden eyes scanning the swirling snow for any lingering predators.
At the very edge of the abyss, Eluned stood motionless.

Her silver-emerald hair whipped violently in the gale and the tips were glowing with a soft pulsing green radiance as she closed her eyes, extending her spiritual roots through the deep tectonic strata of the mountain.
"He’s down there," Eluned announced, a brilliant breathtaking smile breaking across her ethereal face. "His core is burning strong and steady. I think he slayed the beast."
Behind her, Morwenna let out a long relieved breath, her hand easing off the grip of Tidebringer.

"Took the captain long enough," Morwenna chuckled, though her sharp gray eyes were burning with restless energy. "We slaughtered three Tier 5 abominations on the ridgeline just to clear a path through the mist... If he thought he was going to have all the action to himself in the basement, he’s dead wrong."

"Those beasts were sloppy," Tasmin said coolly, twirling one of her void-daggers with a quiet hum. ’Eluned’s roots pinned their flanks before Morwenna’s blade even cleared the scabbard so they barely qualified as warm-ups to people of their level.’

"Still, Tier 5 kills belong to the strongest," Kadi remarked, checking her staff. "We need to advance our personal strength since the Lord is moving at a pace that will leave us regular girls behind if we don’t bleed for our breakthroughs."
Aurelia and Aeliana nodded in quiet agreement, while the Princess clung nervously to the heavy fur-trimmed cloak of the towering warrior standing beside her.
Standing at the front of the precipice, towering over the other women like a walking mountain of muscle and mythril armor, was Thor.
The God of Thunder held the Princess securely in the crook of her left arm, looking down into the plunging azure shaft with a wide toothy grin.

"A glorious descent!" Thor bellowed, her booming voice easily drowning out the roaring blizzard. "No coward’s ladders! No creeping down ropes like frightened spiders! A true warrior plunges into the dark like a thunderbolt! Who goes first?!"
"I’m going," Morwenna said, already stepping up to the rim. "The captain is down there, and knowing him, he’s probably sitting in something repulsive..."
Without waiting for a countdown, the girls began their descent.
Morwenna leaped into the void first, her form vanishing into the azure mist.
Eluned followed in an effortless, gliding descent, her body dissolving into a swirl of luminescent green leaves that rode the thermal updrafts downward.
Tasmin, Kadi, Aurelia, and Aeliana dropped in rapid succession, utilizing wind arts, spatial blinks, and shadow steps to arrest their momentum along the smooth granite walls.
Thor let out a booming laugh that shook the snow from the cliffs, adjusting her grip on the shivering Princess.
"Clench your jaw, royal!" Thor roared cheerfully. "Do not bite your tongue on the landing!"
"WAIT—NO! LADY THOOOOOOR—!"
WHOOOOOOOOSH!
Thor stepped off the ledge with the crushing weight of a falling anvil, the boom of her falling divine mass echoing through the underground flue like a crack of thunder.
Down in the vault, Silas was in the middle of wiping a splash of gravy from his traveling coat when the ceiling vents began to whistle with violent displaced air.
THUD! THUD! SWOOSH!
Morwenna, Eluned, and Tasmin landed on the glassy permafrost in rapid succession with their weapons drawn and their senses flared to detect any lingering anomalies or hidden threats.

A split second later, a deafening thunderclap rattled the cavern walls as Thor touched down with bone-crushing momentum, fracturing the ice beneath her armored greaves and setting the dazed trembling Princess gently onto her feet.
"Perimeter clear!" Morwenna called out instinctively then, the girls froze.
Sitting comfortably on an insulated leather mat in the center of the ancient tomb was Silas Graves.
He was thoroughly drenched from his hair down to his boots in foul half-frozen black monster blood.
And curled within his lap, wrapped snugly in a thick wool blanket, was an extraordinarily gorgeous woman with wild cascading midnight-black hair, porcelain-pale skin, and vivid emerald-green eyes.
Her cheeks and lips were completely smeared with brown gravy and grease, and she was currently gnawing on the roasted bone of a monster leg while resting her cheek directly against Silas’s sternum.
The moment the newcomers landed, Rika’s emerald eyes snapped wide.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A terrifying divine pressure erupted from her petite frame!
The atmospheric pressure within the vault spiked so violently that the surrounding ice stalactites hummed with strain.

An ethereal towering phantom silhouette of a nine-horned apex beast manifested behind her shoulders, letting out a silent soul-crushing roar that caused the Princess to shriek and scramble behind Thor’s thighs!

"Halt, insolent mortals!" Rika bellowed with imperious divine thunder, her grease-covered chin held high with regal majesty. "Who dares intrude upon the private dining pavilion of the Goddess of the Fanged Bro—"
THWACK!
Silas casually reached down and delivered a sharp open-palmed chop to the crown of her head.

"Ow!" Rika yelped, the divine phantom instantly shattering into dust as she clamped both hands over her skull, looking up at Silas with watering betrayed eyes. "What was that for, Lord?! I was asserting our dominance! I was establishing the pecking order!"
"Tone down the cheap theatrics, you fraud," Silas said flatly, tossing a clean linen cloth directly onto her face. "Wipe your snout."
He looked up at his stunned vanguard, shaking his head with an exhausted dry sigh.

"Put the weapons away, girls," Silas told them. "She’s harmless... She can flare an impressive divine aura because her soul still holds the old celestial frequencies, but physically? She’s running on fumes. She’s so depleted right now that even Thora could probably tackle her into a snowbank and sit on her chest."
"Hey! That is deeply slanderous to a celestial authority!" Rika protested loudly, though she made zero attempt to climb out of his lap.

Instead, she burrowed deeper into his woolen coat, shamelessly pressing her freezing nose against his warm neck. "Haaah... so warm... Lord Silas, you are basically a walking furnace. Don’t push me away, my ribs are still half-frozen!"
She reached out with a sauce-stained hand, popping the latch on the third container and pulling out a fistful of braised venison.
Morwenna stood frozen, her left eyebrow twitching uncontrollably as she stared at the scene.
"Captain... did you go down an ancient monster trench and accidentally adopt an overgrown stray dog?"
"It’s like watching someone feed a miniature version of Thor," Tasmin muttered, slowly sliding her void-daggers back into their sheaths with a look of deadpan bewilderment.
At the mention of her name, Thor stepped forward from the shadow of the ice pillars.
The God of Thunder’s shoulders began to tremble. Her chest hitched once, twice, and then—
"BAHAHAHAHAHAHA! BWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
A deafening earth-shaking roar of pure laughter erupted from Thor’s throat.

She slapped her armored thigh with a sound like a cannon shot, tears of hilarious disbelief streaming from her blue eyes as she pointed a gauntleted finger straight at the woman curled in Silas’s lap.
The women stared at Thor in complete shock as Rika froze mid-chew. The piece of venison slipped from her fingers, dropping back into the brass container with a wet plop.
Her emerald eyes widened with pure horror and slowly, desperately, she tried to pull the wool blanket completely over her head, attempting to vanish into the fabric like an embarrassed turtle.
"Is that who I think it is?!" Thor bellowed between booming gasps of laughter. "By the high heavens, it is! Rikavariashaluna! So this is the miserable hole you crawled into after the northern wars!"
A muffled agonized groan rose from beneath the blanket: "Oh gods... why her? Why did it have to be the muscle-headed thunder ape...?"
Silas looked between the two, his brow arching high. "You two know each other?"
Thor wiped a tear of mirth from her eye, grinning from ear to ear with boisterous amusement.

"Know each other? We crossed hammers during the early divine campaigns, centuries before the continents fractured!" Thor roared, shaking her head. "I shattered three of her armored war-panthers with a single swing! Captain, you are looking at one of the weakest most pathetic deities that ever managed to scrape together an altar!"
Rika whipped the blanket off her head, her face blazing scarlet with furious indignation.
"I was an ecosystem guardian and a beast-tamer, you violent brute! My strength was in territory cultivation and pack synergy, not mindless brawling!"

"Even with your entire royal pack surrounding me, you couldn’t leave a single dent in my breastplate!" Thor laughed cheerfully, completely oblivious to how thoroughly devastating her words were. "To this day, none of the high courts have any idea how you attained a celestial seat! We all assumed the divine registry made an administrative error..."
Thor spoke without genuine malice as she was merely recounting the brutal reality of the ancient divine hierarchy but every word hit Rika like a physical hammer to the sternum.
The fallen goddess slumped against Silas’s chest, letting out a long, trembling sigh of complete crushing defeat.

’She’s right...’ Rika thought miserably, staring down at her sauce-stained knuckles. ’I was always the runt... The war gods stole my territories, the sky gods laughed at my beasts, and the moment a real ice deity showed up, I got shoved into a glacier for five hundred years like an unwanted turnip. I’m a joke...’
A heavy awkward silence descended over the leather mat then, Silas’s calm voice cut through the quiet.
"It doesn’t matter what you were before."
Rika blinked, slowly lifting her chin.
Silas stood up from the mat, gently setting her onto her own feet.
He looked down at her... looking past the sauce on her chin, past the tangled matted hair, and straight into her wounded emerald eyes.
He held out his right hand with his palm upward.

"I didn’t recruit you for what you did centuries ago," Silas said. "I recruited you for what you will become under my command. Blessed Land doesn’t look backward so swear your fangs to me once again, and I will give you the resources, the beasts, and the territory to become ten times stronger than you ever were as an isolated goddess."
Rika stared at the open, calloused hand extended before her.
The lingering shame, the humiliation, and centuries of bitter defeat melted away like morning frost before a rising sun.
Beneath her ribs, her dormant spiritual core gave a violent, rhythmic thump, fluttering with a sensation she hadn’t felt in an eternity.
...Ambition.
Her lips parted, and a radiant tearful smile broke across her face.
"Yes, Lord Silas," She whispered, her voice trembling with unbreakable reverence as she placed her small pale hand firmly into his grip.
"I’m with you to the end."
