"No coward’s ladders!
No creeping down ropes like frightened spiders!
A true warrior plunges into the dark like a thunderbolt!
Who goes first?!"
"I’m going," Morwenna said, already stepping up to the rim.
"The captain is down there, and knowing him, he’s probably sitting in something repulsive..."
Without waiting for a countdown, the girls began their descent.
Morwenna leaped into the void first, her form vanishing into the azure mist.
Eluned followed in an effortless, gliding descent, her body dissolving into a swirl of luminescent green leaves that rode the thermal updrafts downward.
Tasmin, Kadi, Aurelia, and Aeliana dropped in rapid succession, utilizing wind arts, spatial blinks, and shadow steps to arrest their momentum along the smooth granite walls.
Thor let out a booming laugh that shook the snow from the cliffs, adjusting her grip on the shivering Princess.
"Clench your jaw, royal!" Thor roared cheerfully.
"Do not bite your tongue on the landing!"
"WAIT—NO!
LADY THOOOOOOR—!"
WHOOOOOOOOSH!
Thor stepped off the ledge with the crushing weight of a falling anvil, the boom of her falling divine mass echoing through the underground flue like a crack of thunder.
Down in the vault, Silas was in the middle of wiping a splash of gravy from his traveling coat when the ceiling vents began to whistle with violent displaced air.
THUD!
THUD!
SWOOSH!
Morwenna, Eluned, and Tasmin landed on the glassy permafrost in rapid succession with their weapons drawn and their senses flared to detect any lingering anomalies or hidden threats.

A split second later, a deafening thunderclap rattled the cavern walls as Thor touched down with bone-crushing momentum, fracturing the ice beneath her armored greaves and setting the dazed trembling Princess gently onto her feet.
"Perimeter clear!" Morwenna called out instinctively then, the girls froze.
Sitting comfortably on an insulated leather mat in the center of the ancient tomb was Silas Graves.
He was thoroughly drenched from his hair down to his boots in foul half-frozen black monster blood.
And curled within his lap, wrapped snugly in a thick wool blanket, was an extraordinarily gorgeous woman with wild cascading midnight-black hair, porcelain-pale skin, and vivid emerald-green eyes.
Her cheeks and lips were completely smeared with brown gravy and grease, and she was currently gnawing on the roasted bone of a monster leg while resting her cheek directly against Silas’s sternum.
The moment the newcomers landed, Rika’s emerald eyes snapped wide.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A terrifying divine pressure erupted from her petite frame!
The atmospheric pressure within the vault spiked so violently that the surrounding ice stalactites hummed with strain.

An ethereal towering phantom silhouette of a nine-horned apex beast manifested behind her shoulders, letting out a silent soul-crushing roar that caused the Princess to shriek and scramble behind Thor’s thighs!
"Halt, insolent mortals!" Rika bellowed with imperious divine thunder, her grease-covered chin held high with regal majesty.
"Who dares intrude upon the private dining pavilion of the Goddess of the Fanged Bro—"
THWACK!
Silas casually reached down and delivered a sharp open-palmed chop to the crown of her head.
"Ow!" Rika yelped, the divine phantom instantly shattering into dust as she clamped both hands over her skull, looking up at Silas with watering betrayed eyes.
"What was that for, Lord?!
I was asserting our dominance!
I was establishing the pecking order!"
"Tone down the cheap theatrics, you fraud," Silas said flatly, tossing a clean linen cloth directly onto her face.
"Wipe your snout."
He looked up at his stunned vanguard, shaking his head with an exhausted dry sigh.
"Put the weapons away, girls," Silas told them.
"She’s harmless...
She can flare an impressive divine aura because her soul still holds the old celestial frequencies, but physically?
She’s running on fumes.
She’s so depleted right now that even Thora could probably tackle her into a snowbank and sit on her chest."
"Hey!
That is deeply slanderous to a celestial authority!" Rika protested loudly, though she made zero attempt to climb out of his lap.
Instead, she burrowed deeper into his woolen coat, shamelessly pressing her freezing nose against his warm neck.
"Haaah... so warm...
Lord Silas, you are basically a walking furnace.
Don’t push me away, my ribs are still half-frozen!"
She reached out with a sauce-stained hand, popping the latch on the third container and pulling out a fistful of braised venison.
Morwenna stood frozen, her left eyebrow twitching uncontrollably as she stared at the scene.
"Captain... did you go down an ancient monster trench and accidentally adopt an overgrown stray dog?"
"It’s like watching someone feed a miniature version of Thor," Tasmin muttered, slowly sliding her void-daggers back into their sheaths with a look of deadpan bewilderment.
At the mention of her name, Thor stepped forward from the shadow of the ice pillars.
The God of Thunder’s shoulders began to tremble.
Her chest hitched once, twice, and then—
"BAHAHAHAHAHAHA!
BWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
A deafening earth-shaking roar of pure laughter erupted from Thor’s throat.

She slapped her armored thigh with a sound like a cannon shot, tears of hilarious disbelief streaming from her blue eyes as she pointed a gauntleted finger straight at the woman curled in Silas’s lap.
The women stared at Thor in complete shock as Rika froze mid-chew.
The piece of venison slipped from her fingers, dropping back into the brass container with a wet plop.
Her emerald eyes widened with pure horror and slowly, desperately, she tried to pull the wool blanket completely over her head, attempting to vanish into the fabric like an embarrassed turtle.
"Is that who I think it is?!" Thor bellowed between booming gasps of laughter.
"By the high heavens, it is!
Rikavariashaluna!
So this is the miserable hole you crawled into after the northern wars!"
A muffled agonized groan rose from beneath the blanket: "Oh gods... why her?
Why did it have to be the muscle-headed thunder ape...?"
Silas looked between the two, his brow arching high.
"You two know each other?"
Thor wiped a tear of mirth from her eye, grinning from ear to ear with boisterous amusement.
"Know each other?
We crossed hammers during the early divine campaigns, centuries before the continents fractured!" Thor roared, shaking her head.
"I shattered three of her armored war-panthers with a single swing!
Captain, you are looking at one of the weakest most pathetic deities that ever managed to scrape together an altar!"
Rika whipped the blanket off her head, her face blazing scarlet with furious indignation.
"I was an ecosystem guardian and a beast-tamer, you violent brute!
My strength was in territory cultivation and pack synergy, not mindless brawling!"
"Even with your entire royal pack surrounding me, you couldn’t leave a single dent in my breastplate!" Thor laughed cheerfully, completely oblivious to how thoroughly devastating her words were.
"To this day, none of the high courts have any idea how you attained a celestial seat!
We all assumed the divine registry made an administrative error..."
Thor spoke without genuine malice as she was merely recounting the brutal reality of the ancient divine hierarchy but every word hit Rika like a physical hammer to the sternum.
The fallen goddess slumped against Silas’s chest, letting out a long, trembling sigh of complete crushing defeat.
’She’s right...’ Rika thought miserably, staring down at her sauce-stained knuckles. ’I was always the runt...
The war gods stole my territories, the sky gods laughed at my beasts, and the moment a real ice deity showed up, I got shoved into a glacier for five hundred years like an unwanted turnip.
I’m a joke...’
A heavy awkward silence descended over the leather mat then, Silas’s calm voice cut through the quiet.
"It doesn’t matter what you were before."
Rika blinked, slowly lifting her chin.
Silas stood up from the mat, gently setting her onto her own feet.
He looked down at her... looking past the sauce on her chin, past the tangled matted hair, and straight into her wounded emerald eyes.
He held out his right hand with his palm upward.
"I didn’t recruit you for what you did centuries ago," Silas said.
"I recruited you for what you will become under my command.

Blessed Land doesn’t look backward so swear your fangs to me once again, and I will give you the resources, the beasts, and the territory to become ten times stronger than you ever were as an isolated goddess."
Rika stared at the open, calloused hand extended before her.
The lingering shame, the humiliation, and centuries of bitter defeat melted away like morning frost before a rising sun.
Beneath her ribs, her dormant spiritual core gave a violent, rhythmic thump, fluttering with a sensation she hadn’t felt in an eternity.
...Ambition.
Her lips parted, and a radiant tearful smile broke across her face.
"Yes, Lord Silas," She whispered, her voice trembling with unbreakable reverence as she placed her small pale hand firmly into his grip.
"I’m with you to the end."

chapters.title: Chapter 521: Aki [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The clean-up was swift and seamless.

With Rika scampering about to help fold the mats... partially out of genuine loyalty, and partially out of terror that Thor might laugh at her again, the campsite was packed away in under five minutes.
Silas rolled his shoulders, his traveling coat stiff with congealed monster blood.
"Our work in the northern trench is done," Silas announced, looking around at his gathered women. "The fog monster is dead, Rika is secured, and my coat smells like a sewer. Let’s head home."
Before he could take a step toward the vertical shaft, a pair of slender leaf-scented arms wrapped tightly around his waist from behind.
Eluned buried her face between his shoulder blades, her soft emerald hair spilling over his collar.

"You are never jumping into a spatial breach alone again, Silas," Eluned murmured softly, her voice muffled against the fabric of his coat. "I felt you vanish when the fog took you and my heart nearly stopped."
Silas chuckled quietly, reaching back to pat her forearm with a gentle reassuring touch.
"I’m fine, Elu. Took a little detour, killed an overgrown eyeball, and picked up a stray dog."
"I am a Goddess of Beasts, not a stray dog!" Rika yelled from across the cavern, though she clamped her mouth shut the second Morwenna shot her a flat warning glare.
Aeliana stepped forward, her blond hair catching the ambient cyan light as an elegant knowing smile crossed her refined features.
"Lord Silas," the high-elf secretary said gracefully, "there is no need to subject the girls to a march through the northern blizzards."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "You have a shortcut?"

"Before we entered the deeper part of the basin, I anchored a primary spatial beacon at the main border," Aeliana explained, her eyes shimmering with intricate rotating geometric rings of spatial mana. "With the spatial distortion of the weeping eye destroyed, the atmosphere has completely stabilized so I can construct a spell capable of teleporting the entire party, including the Blessed Wolves directly back to our perimeter."
Silas smiled broadly.
"Aeli, Thank you... Do it."
Aeliana bowed with graceful poise, raising both hands toward the vaulted ceiling.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
Rings of brilliant mirror-like silver runes exploded outward from her fingertips, expanding into a massive rotating spatial array that engulfed the entire cavern in blinding light.
FLASH!
In the span of a single heartbeat, the cavern fell into deafening silence.
Silas, the girls, Thor, the Princess, and the newly sworn Goddess of Beasts vanished into the ether, leaving behind only the cold unmoving pillars of ice.
Minutes ticked by in the empty silent tomb.
Then, high above in the ceiling shaft, a tiny frantic scratching broke the quiet.
SCRITCH-SCRITCH-SCRITCH! PLOP!
A small pathetic creature tumbled out of the vertical flue, bouncing off a sloping stalagmite before crashing face-first into a snowdrift on the cavern floor.

It was an anomaly scavenged from the upper crags... a tiny horned mouse-beast barely the size of a man’s fist, its claws completely mangled and bleeding from its desperate attempt to brake its fall along the granite walls.
It scrambled upright, chittering in high-pitched panic with its beady black eyes darting around the massive lightless vault.
It was trapped.
The walls were made of ice and vertical basalt so its ruined claws had no hope of climbing back to the surface then, a low ominous sound rippled through the dead air.
CRACK! KRA-CRACK-SNAP-SHATTER!
Behind where Rika had been entombed, the ancient glacier suffered a catastrophic collapse.
Without the divine soul-anchor of the Goddess of Beasts to sustain the spell, the massive thirty-foot-thick plug of permafrost gave way.
Thousands of tons of ancient ice shattered into fine, powdery rime, completely unsealing the pitch-black, yawning maw of the Great Northern Borehole.
From the lightless depths of the ancient mine, something flickered.
It was a hypnotic purple luminescence.
The horned mouse tilted its twitching snout, drawn forward by an irresistible primal pull as it scampered across the pulverized ice, slipping into the dark tunnel.

It scurried past rows of petrified wooden support beams, ancient mining carts long turned to dust, and several strange human-shaped protrusions along the walls that resembled grotesque and agonizingly posed statues.
Deeper and deeper it crept, until the narrow tunnel opened into an enormous lightless abyss.
Standing in the center of the forgotten abyss was a monolithic statue carved of seamless void-black obsidian.
The tiny rodent approached the base of the titan, sniffing the stagnant dead air.
Suddenly, the obsidian surface of the monument rippled!
SPLAT!
A thick viscous globule of pulsing, purplish-black slime detached from the statue’s chest, shooting across the floor like a striking viper.
Before the mouse could squeak, the foul entity struck its snout, violently forcing its way through its nostrils, its eyes, and down its open gullet.
SQUEEEEEE—!
The chittering choked into a wet horrific gurgle.
The rodent’s tiny frame arched violently, its ribs snapping outward as its muscular tissue unnaturally expanded.
Its black eyes glazed over, igniting with an unnatural malevolent purple flame as the corrupted beast landed on all four paws, letting out a series of strange clicking sounds from its throat.
It turned its head toward the northern tunnel exit, catching the distant scent of the surface world.
With terrifying unnatural speed, the beast bolted into the dark, racing toward the world above.
[Several Days Later]
The morning sun crested the jagged obsidian ridge of the Umbral Basin, spilling pale amber light across the central courtyard of Blessed Land.
The air was clean, stripped of the oily bite of necrotic fog, smelling instead of damp pine and the sweet trace of woodsmoke drifting from the barracks.
Standing just beyond the shadow of the Keep’s vaulted portico, the Princess let out a soft sigh.
Her royal-blue hair caught the morning rays, shimmering like polished lapis lazuli as a gentle draft lifted the loose strands from her temples.
She was no longer wearing the understated silk court gown she had arrived in.

In its place was a traveling dress crafted by the territory’s master tailor... a garment of deep slate-gray wool lined with supple white buckskin, cinched at her slender waist with an embossed leather belt and edged in subtle leaf-green embroidery.
It moved with her body, neither binding her ribs nor trailing in the dust, giving her an effortless regal silhouette that looked like a Princess.
’I know my maids will hate it though.’
Gathered in a loose semicircle around the stone flagstones were the women she had become close with.
Tasmin stood with her arms folded across her leather-clad chest, her dark void-daggers resting quietly in their sheaths and her sharp eyes carrying a rare relaxed warmth.

Beside her, Brida leaned her weight on the haft of her cleaver poleaxe, chewing on a clean stalk, while Thora stood wiping grease from her calloused palms with a rag with her blacksmith’s apron smelling of smoke.

Eluned lounged gracefully near the central fountain that Silas had recently installed with her long emerald locks drifting on the breeze and the living vines wrapped around her wrists pulsing with green light.
Morwenna stood with Tidebringer slung across her broad shoulders, her boots coated in dried road grit, watching the royal scion with an amused smirk.

Even Talira had climbed out onto the high slate shingles of the Keep’s roof, basking in the direct heat of the morning sun like a crimson cat with her scaled wings half-spread as she lazily flicked her tail and gave a languid two-fingered wave toward the courtyard.
Thor stood broad and immovable near the center with her silver battle armor gleaming in the sun and Mjölnir strapped securely to her leather war-belt as her storm-blue eyes crinkled with good humor.

"You managed to survive seven days in the dark without getting eaten, trampled, or turned into an icicle," Morwenna called out, her gravelly voice breaking the morning quiet. "That’s better than half the deckhands I used to press into service on the salt coast... before I trained them of course"

"She didn’t just survive though, she carried her own bowl!" Thora grunted with approval, tossing her rag over a shoulder. "She didn’t complain about your bread, either... you should be grateful, that thing tastes like my shit."
"Fucking Dwar—"
Eluned stepped forward, offering a graceful gentle sweep of her hand.
"The forest spirits will miss your laughter at the spring, little one. The week passed far too swiftly and the basin was brighter with you among us."
’Look at her forming all these words like she’s not happy to get more alone time with him.’ Morwenna clicked her teeth, why did Elu insist on being so fake?
The Princess felt a sudden thick warmth swell behind her ribs.

For twenty-five years, parting words in her life had consisted of rigid court bows, calculating nods, and the cold rehearsed well-wishes of house retainers who cared only for her family’s annual stipend.
These women had seen her scream at ancient bone hands, watched her slip on carpets trying to throw kicks, and shared bowls of fatty stew around campfires under the dead earth.
She raised both hands, bowing her head with deep grace.
"Thank you. Every single one of you. I... I have never known seven days like these. I will not forget them."
"Don’t get all weepy on us now, Princess," Tasmin said, a slight grin touching the corner of her mouth. "You’ll make the Captain look soft."
Silas took a slow step forward, separating himself from the stone archway of the portico.
The Princess’s eyelashes fluttered as her gaze met his.
Bathed in the dawn light, the Lord of Blessed Land carried an imposing settled presence that made the air around him feel warm.
His dark hair had grown a fraction longer over the past week, the unruly black bangs brushing against his temples and grazing the collar of his clean charcoal-gray tunic.
Beneath his dark brows, his eyes were clear piercing blue, encircled by that unmistakable ring of gold that looked amazing.
He reached his right hand into the pocket of his coat, rubbing the back of his neck with his left in that familiar self-conscious manner.

"I’m usually pretty terrible at this sort of thing," Silas admitted. "Diplomatic gifts, courtly tokens... none of that was ever in my job description but Thora showed me how to set the wire, and Eluned helped me temper the facet so the mana wouldn’t bleed out."
He drew his hand from his coat, opening his broad calloused palm.
The Princess’s breath hitched in her throat.
Resting against his glove was a slender exquisite necklace.
The chain was forged of whisper-thin links of dark star-iron, cold and dark as midnight.
Suspended along the collar were five mana diamonds, their surfaces polished just enough to reveal the brilliant prismatic fires trapped within their cores... azure, amber, green, and deep violet.
They were the very stones they had recovered from the lower deposits of Mine KB22, carrying the mineral heartbeat of the deep earth.

"It’s not cut like royal jewelry," Silas said, stepping directly in front of her. "It’s a bit rough around the edges but the mana inside these diamonds has been stabilized by my core. If you ever find yourself in a room with a bad person, or someone tries to push a spiritual suppressive field onto you, the stones will flash and break the pressure wave."
He tilted his head slightly. "Mind if I put it on you?"

"I... I would be honored, Lord Silas," she murmured softly, her porcelain skin warming as she bowed her head and reached up to sweep her heavy, royal-blue hair over her left shoulder, baring the pale curve of her neck.
Silas stepped behind her.

His fingers were broad and rough and when the back of his knuckles grazed the sensitive skin at the base of her throat, an electric shiver raced down the Princess’s spine, making her shoulders lock for a fraction of a second.
CLICK!

The tiny star-iron clasp snapped securely into place as the cool weight of the diamonds settled against her collarbone, and immediately, a soothing pulse of warm mana rippled across her chest, perfectly synchronized with her heartbeat.
Silas stepped back around, looking down at her with a gentle satisfied nod.
"Looks good on you," he said quietly then, his blue-gold eyes met hers with a warm focus. "Stay safe out there, Aki."
The world seemed to drop its volume by half.
The syllables hung in the crisp mountain air like a bell struck in an empty temple.
The Princess stood motionless, her azure eyes wide, her lower lip parting in silent stunned wonder.
In the Supreme Royal Family, names were a divine privilege reserved exclusively for those who awakened a Lord Core.
To be an Unawakened scion was to be stripped of an identity, relegated to "The Asset," or "The Nameless One." depending on your gender.
To bestow a name upon oneself was punishable by exile and to have an outsider bestow an unauthorized title was considered high treason and a grave insult.
Yet as the word settled into her chest, there was no offense and there was no cold indignation.
There was only a violent fluttering swarm of warmth that exploded in her stomach, rising through her throat and staining her cheeks with an uncontrollable fiery pink blush.
He hadn’t given her a formal decree... he had given her an affectionate personal nickname.
’Aki.’
It was simple... but this name...
...It was hers.

His dark hair had grown a fraction longer over the past week, the unruly black bangs brushing against his temples and grazing the collar of his clean charcoal-gray tunic.
Beneath his dark brows, his eyes were clear piercing blue, encircled by that unmistakable ring of gold that looked amazing.
He reached his right hand into the pocket of his coat, rubbing the back of his neck with his left in that familiar self-conscious manner.
"I’m usually pretty terrible at this sort of thing," Silas admitted.
"Diplomatic gifts, courtly tokens... none of that was ever in my job description but Thora showed me how to set the wire, and Eluned helped me temper the facet so the mana wouldn’t bleed out."
He drew his hand from his coat, opening his broad calloused palm.
The Princess’s breath hitched in her throat.
Resting against his glove was a slender exquisite necklace.
The chain was forged of whisper-thin links of dark star-iron, cold and dark as midnight.
Suspended along the collar were five mana diamonds, their surfaces polished just enough to reveal the brilliant prismatic fires trapped within their cores... azure, amber, green, and deep violet.
They were the very stones they had recovered from the lower deposits of Mine KB22, carrying the mineral heartbeat of the deep earth.
"It’s not cut like royal jewelry," Silas said, stepping directly in front of her.
"It’s a bit rough around the edges but the mana inside these diamonds has been stabilized by my core.
If you ever find yourself in a room with a bad person, or someone tries to push a spiritual suppressive field onto you, the stones will flash and break the pressure wave."
He tilted his head slightly.
"Mind if I put it on you?"

I would be honored, Lord Silas," she murmured softly, her porcelain skin warming as she bowed her head and reached up to sweep her heavy, royal-blue hair over her left shoulder, baring the pale curve of her neck.
Silas stepped behind her.

His fingers were broad and rough and when the back of his knuckles grazed the sensitive skin at the base of her throat, an electric shiver raced down the Princess’s spine, making her shoulders lock for a fraction of a second.
CLICK!

The tiny star-iron clasp snapped securely into place as the cool weight of the diamonds settled against her collarbone, and immediately, a soothing pulse of warm mana rippled across her chest, perfectly synchronized with her heartbeat.
Silas stepped back around, looking down at her with a gentle satisfied nod.
"Looks good on you," he said quietly then, his blue-gold eyes met hers with a warm focus.
"Stay safe out there, Aki."
The world seemed to drop its volume by half.
The syllables hung in the crisp mountain air like a bell struck in an empty temple.
The Princess stood motionless, her azure eyes wide, her lower lip parting in silent stunned wonder.
In the Supreme Royal Family, names were a divine privilege reserved exclusively for those who awakened a Lord Core.
To be an Unawakened scion was to be stripped of an identity, relegated to "The Asset," or "The Nameless One." depending on your gender.
To bestow a name upon oneself was punishable by exile and to have an outsider bestow an unauthorized title was considered high treason and a grave insult.
Yet as the word settled into her chest, there was no offense and there was no cold indignation.
There was only a violent fluttering swarm of warmth that exploded in her stomach, rising through her throat and staining her cheeks with an uncontrollable fiery pink blush.
He hadn’t given her a formal decree... he had given her an affectionate personal nickname.
’Aki.’
It was simple... but this name...
...It was hers.

chapters.title: Chapter 522: Arrival At Rhyx City [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas reached out with his heavy palm resting firmly against her shoulder, giving her a reassuring pat that sent another bunch of butterflies tumbling through her midsection.

"And remember our contract," Silas added, an amused smirk tugging at his lips. "Use an anonymous offshore routing account when you transfer the money... If your accountants see an electronic wire sent directly to me, it’ll be quite a big issue."
Aki swallowed the lump in her throat, forcing her composure to knit back together, though she couldn’t wipe the bright, breathless smile from her face.
"I gave you my word, Lord Silas. Your account number is etched into my memory."

’And once those numbers enter the international clearing system,’ she thought with a flicker of clever royal pride, ’all I need to do is cross-reference the account’s primary registration routing through my private terminal... Your true name will appear right on my screen... unless you gave me a shell company but even a shell leaves a digital shadow.’
She took half a step forward, unable to restrain herself, and wrapped her slender arms firmly around his waist.
She pressed her cheek against his chest, inhaling the lingering heat radiating from his clothes.
Silas stood startled for half a second before his arms came around her back, returning the embrace with a gentle steady squeeze.
Aki pulled back slowly, her fingers lingering against his lapels before dropping away.
She couldn’t stop the small petulant pout that formed on her lips. "I don’t suppose... there is any possibility of an extension? Even three days?"
"You’ve already stayed seven," Silas chuckled. "Your household is probably tearing Rhyx City apart looking for their runaway princess."
"Can I come back, then?" she asked, her voice dropping into an earnest vulnerable plea. "Will the gates be open?"
"Anytime you need to breathe, Aki," Silas said softly. "You have an open invitation to Blessed Land."
"GWAHAHAHA! That’s enough sweet-talking! The morning temperature is rising, and the sky won’t wait for lovers’ goodbyes!"
Before Aki could say another word, a gauntlet slipped beneath her arms, and she was effortlessly scooped off the stone flagstones in a massive one-armed lift.
"Lady Thor!" Aki gasped, clutching her silk fan and her new necklace as her boots dangled two feet in the air. "A moment of dignity, please!"
"Dignity is for dead kings sitting on cold thrones!" Thor roared with booming cheer, resting the twenty-five-year-old royal securely against her broad silver breastplate.
The God of Thunder turned toward the assembled women, throwing her head back as her wild blonde locks danced in the gale.
"Farewell, people of the Keep! May your steel stay sharp, your mead stay cold, and your Lord keep his head on straight!"
"Safe travels, Thunderer!" Morwenna called out, raising Tidebringer in salute.
"Don’t drop the royal!" Thora barked with a wide grin.
Thor looked down toward the doorway of the Keep, where a pale face with wild midnight-black hair was peeking cautiously out from behind the heavy oak jamb.
Rika, wrapped in a wool blanket and clutching a half-eaten smoked sausage, shrank back into the shadows the second Thor’s storm-blue eyes locked onto her.

"And you, Rikavariashaluna!" Thor bellowed, her voice rattling the roof tiles. "Chew your meat properly! If I return and find out you choked on a chicken bone, I will carve your epitaph on a chamber pot!"
Rika’s muffled furious screech drifted from the dark interior.
"GO JUMP INTO A VOLCANO, YOU BLONDE GORILLA!"
Thor let out a booming belly laugh, then turned her gaze back to Silas Graves.
A sudden softer warmth settled over the deity’s rugged features.
She looked at the young Lord standing calmly on the stones.
He was young and his raw cultivation was still climbing the mortal tiers yet there was an immovable center to him.
A strange gravity that made beings like Eluned, Morwenna and even Rikavariashaluna willingly lay their heads beneath his banner without a single chain of coercion.
Thor flashed him a broad fearless grin, her blue eyes crackling with a tiny spark of golden static.
Silas met her gaze with a smirk tugging at his mouth, and gave her a slow wink.
A small crimson blush brushed across the high-altitude tan of Thor’s cheeks as she let out a loud delighted huff through her nose, shaking her head.
’By Odin’s beard... he really is a charming little bastard,’ Thor thought, her fingers twitching with the urge to reach down and ruffle his dark hair one last time. ’A very, very good boy.’
"We’re off!" Thor announced.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
With a singular concussive thrust of her muscular legs, the God of Thunder detonated into the sky.

The courtyard flags groaned beneath the explosive upward force, a hurricane of displaced air whipping the skirts and cloaks of the women below as Thor and the Princess shot straight into the cloudless blue sky like a golden artillery shell.
High above the valley floor, the wind shrieked as Thor swung Mjölnir in a wide arc above her head, the ancient uru metal humming with a deep cosmic vibration that tore through the atmospheric veil.
CRACK-SHATTER!
A jagged golden rift of concentrated Asgardian thunder tore open in the middle of the sky.
Thor dove straight through the fracture, the world of the Umbral Basin instantly dissolving into streaks of liquid light.
In less than a heartbeat, the violent gales ceased, replaced by the tranquil sun-drenched silence of the celestial crossroads.
They touched down gently upon the pristine white marble path of the eternal garden.
’Ah we’re no longer in the snowy area...?’ The Princess thought, that was far behind.
The colossal trees with silver bark and golden foliage swayed gently overhead, casting dappled shadows across the emerald lawns.
The air here was warm and fragrant, smelling of blooming starlight and undisturbed dew.
Thor set Aki onto her feet, allowing the Princess to smooth down her wool skirt and catch her breath.
"Well, little royal," Thor rumbled, rolling her broad shoulders until her silver pauldrons clanked together. "Did you enjoy your little holiday in the dirt? Was it worth seventeen counts of fraud?"
Aki didn’t hesitate.
Her azure eyes sparkled with an intensity that had never existed during her twenty-five years in the imperial capital.

"It was extraordinary," Aki breathed, her voice tumbling out in a rapid excited torrent as they walked along the marble lane. "Lady Thor, you have no idea... Eluned showed me how to identify mana herbs by the pattern of their root veins and Silas... Lord Silas took us into the deep trenches. We crossed blades with lots of monsters and he carved a literal goddess out of hundreds of years of solid ice and the food... they don’t serve tiny sterile portions on silver platters, hell they roast entire haunches of meat over open embers and pass it around with their bare hands!"
’Not to mention the alcohol...’
The Princess would sell a lot of things to get her hands on that mead again... It made her feel fuzzy in a good way.
Thor threw her head back, laughing boisterously at the girl’s uninhibited chatter.

"GWAHAHAHA! You sound like a tavern bard after three flagons of mead! See? I told you that boy knows how to run a hall! Don’t fret, little Princess. Once you settle your business, I’ll haul you back down there myself. I still owe that pirate woman a proper fight and the Dragon too."
They approached the center of the garden, where the tall dark-skinned guardian stood motionless, resting his weight against his obsidian-tipped spear.
The glowing white tribal marks across his bald scalp pulsed in steady pulse.
"Greetings, Daughter of Odin," the Gatekeeper intoned solemnly. "You return from the forgotten threshold."
"Greetings, spear-man!" Thor replied with an easy wave. "We’re taking the high transit back to the mortal plane. Open the upper atmospheric lane for the place where we came from!"
The guardian turned, the tip of his spear tracing an intricate circle in the air.
A towering arch of white marble flared to life, swirling with the cerulean light of the mortal realm’s upper stratosphere.
"Proceed," the guardian spoke.
Thor scooped Aki back into her arms with practiced ease, paying no heed to the Princess’s quiet squeak of protest and leaped straight through the swirling blue veil.
WHOOSH!
The serene gardens vanished.

Instantaneously, the crushing cold and thin vacuum of the upper stratosphere slammed into them but Thor maintained a shimmering frictionless sphere of golden thunder-mana around them, insulating the Princess from the sub-zero void.
Beneath them, the curvature of the mortal planet spread out in breathtaking splendor... an endless ocean of swirling white cloudbanks, broken far below by the glittering neon grid of Rhyx City.
Thor angled her descent, descending through the cloud cover with hypersonic acceleration.

The city grew from a circuit board of glowing lines into towering kilometer-high spires of chrome, glass, and steel as Thor banked hard around the eastern residential spires, decelerating with miraculous precision as she cleared the high-altitude smog layer.
With a soft muffled thump of displaced air, Thor touched down on the private polished marble terrace of the Princess’s penthouse suite.
She set Aki lightly onto the stone, crossing her arms over her silver breastplate with a broad satisfied smirk.
Aki stood on the terrace, the familiar smell of the city’s air scrubbers washing over her senses.
She turned, looking up at the towering Asgardian deity with a raised brow.
"Will you be staying for tea, Lady Thor? The household staff can prepare a roast."
Thor blinked, looking at the blue-haired royal as if she had grown a second head.

"Stay for tea in a glass cage?" Thor barked with a loud snort. "Are you thick in the skull, girl?! I’m flying straight back to Blessed Land! The Lord has a fresh cask of dwarven ale waiting in the cellar, and I have no intention of letting that pirate woman drink my share!"
Aki’s jaw dropped.
"Wait—right now?! You’re leaving immediately?!"
"Catch you later, little royal! GWAHAHAHA!"
KRA-BOOOOOOM!

A pillar of golden lightning erupted beneath Thor’s boots, blowing Aki’s hair and skirts wildly across the terrace as the God of Thunder rocketed back into the sky, vanishing into the upper storm clouds before the thunderclap had even faded.
Aki stood coughing in the ozone haze, stamping her boot in pure frustration.
"Unbelievable! You muscle-headed brute! You could have at least carried my luggage!"
"YOUR HIGHNESS!"
The heavy reinforced glass doors leading into the penthouse suite were thrown open with a frantic bang.
Three royal security maids, clad in pristine black-and-white formal uniforms, rushed out onto the terrace with their hands trembling and their faces pale as paper.
The lead maid, Mira, threw herself onto her knees before Aki with tears streaming down her cheeks.

"Praise the Ancestral Obelisk! You’re alive! You’re unharmed!" Mira wept, clutching the hem of Aki’s woolen traveling skirt. "When Lady Thor seized you from the balcony, the entire sector security grid went into a level-four lockdown! We thought... we thought the Asgardian had taken you as a celestial hostage!"
"Calm yourselves," Aki commanded, her tone instantly shifting back into the cool noble tone she had wielded for a decade.
She snapped her silk fan open, fluttering it with grace. "Lady Thor merely escorted me on a private excursion so there was no hostage situation and now, Stand up, Mira... Compose yourself."
Mira scrambled to her feet, wiping her eyes frantically, before her gaze drifted over the Princess’s attire.
"Your Highness... your dress," Mira stammered, horror dawning in her eyes. "What are you wearing? That fabric... it smells of wood ash and iron and your hair—"

"I was somewhere," Aki said smoothly, brushing past them into the climate-controlled warmth of the suite. "It is high-grade traveling wool. It kept me warm, which is more than I can say for the silk rags you usually pack."

"We must prepare a bath immediately!" the second maid cried, clasping her hands in sheer distress. "The Crown Prince’s motorcade has already entered this district... His Highness will be arriving at the penthouse in less than forty minutes to conduct an official inspection!"
Aki’s shoulders subtly stiffened as her grip on her silk fan tightened by a fraction of a millimeter.
"My brother is coming here?" she asked, her voice dropping into a cold flat tone.

"Yes, Highness!" Mira urged, gesturing toward the master quarters. "He received word of the security breach! If he arrives and finds you unwashed, smelling of common smoke and dressed like a mercenary, the reprimand will be catastrophic! Please, allow us to prepare the scented oils!"
"I have already bathed," Aki replied with an annoyed scowl, recalling the refreshing dip in the hot mineral spring in the Keep that morning. "I am perfectly clean."

Mira sniffled, leaning in slightly, and made a small distressed face. "Highness... with all due respect, you do not smell ’proper.’ You smell of... pine needles and wild mint. It is far too pungent for the parlor."
Aki felt an involuntary twitch in her eyebrow.
’Pungent?’
Eluned had spent two hours showing her how to harvest the silver-leaf ferns by the river, teaching her how to express the pure cold sap with a wooden mortar and pestle to craft natural soap cakes.
It was the exact same botanical compound that Silas used, which gave the Lord of Blessed Land that subtle captivating scent of fresh rain and mountain cedar.
To call it "improper" was an insult to the Goddess herself.
Before she could voice her defense, her maids seized her by the elbows, ushering her with respectful urgency down the private corridor toward the royal bathing pavilion.
"There is no time, Highness! The Prince’s schedule permits zero delays!"

chapters.title: Chapter 523: Standing Up For Myself [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki sighed, allowing herself to be herded into the expansive marble-clad bathhouse.
She knew when to pick her battles.

If she made a scene over soap, it would only raise suspicions regarding where she had spent the past week, and the last thing she needed was an audit sniffing around the coordinates of the Umbral Basin.
The bathing chamber was a sprawling temple of opulence.
Steam scented with imported vanilla, crushed lavender, and crushed pearls rose from a sunken pool carved from white calcite marble.
The three maids moved with practiced efficiency.
They reached for the buttons of her wool traveling dress, their fingers working the fastenings until the heavy garment slid from her shoulders.
"The fabric is shockingly durable," one of the maids whispered, running a thumb over the reinforced seams. "The stitching... it’s not imperial work, yet the tension on the thread is flawless."
"Set it aside carefully," Aki ordered, her azure eyes sharp. "If a single thread is frayed, I will dock your quarter’s stipend."
"Y-Yes, Highness!"
As Aki stepped out of the dress, her hands instinctively rose to the star-iron necklace resting against her collarbone.
Mira reached forward, a velvet-lined jewelry tray in hand with her fingers extending toward the star-iron clasp.
"Allow me to remove this rough piece, Highness. We must store it before the scented waters tarnish the—"
Aki’s hand clamped around Mira’s wrist like an iron band.
Her azure eyes snapped to the maid’s face, burning with a sudden freezing intensity that made the air in the steamy pavilion drop by five degrees.
"Touch this necklace," Aki said, her voice dropping to a dangerous icy whisper, "and you will spend the next three years scrubbing the sub-level filtration vents... Do you understand me?"
Mira swallowed hard, her knees buckling slightly under the sheer, unexpected pressure.
"I... I understand, Your Imperial Highness! Forgive my insolence!"
Aki released the maid’s wrist.
Her fingers gently traced the cold multifaceted surface of the raw mana diamonds resting on her chest.
The warm feeling from Silas’s core resonated through the star-iron links which was like a private untouchable anchor in the middle of this gilded cage.
She stepped down the shallow marble steps into the steaming pool, letting the hot lavender-infused water swallow her up to her collarbone.

The maids set to work with sponges, horsehair brushes, and scented soaps, scrubbing away the mountain dust from her limbs, washing and conditioning the silken waves of her blue hair until they fell in pristine liquid cascades down her back.

"Why is he coming?" Aki asked, closing her eyes as the maids combed through her damp locks. "My brother does not waste thirty minutes of travel time merely to check on the health of an Unawakened sister..."

"We do not know the full agenda, Highness," Mira replied softly, dabbing a plush towel against Aki’s shoulders. "Only that his aides sounded deeply agitated when they confirmed the security manifest. The Crown Prince was... displeased by the reports."
Aki’s lips thinned into a cold line.
’Displeased... He’s always displeased. The only thing that pleases him is seeing his name at the top of the war records.’
Once dried and perfumed, she was led to the adjoining dressing salon.
The maids worked with high speed, fitting her into a ceremonial imperial gown of layered sky-blue and silver silk.
The high rigid collar was reinforced with delicate bone stays, the long sleeves were embroidered with soaring golden phoenixes, and a pleated train trailed three paces behind her slippers.
It was a masterpiece of royal tailoring and it felt like wearing a lead sarcophagus.
"Haahh..."
They arranged her hair into an intricate braided crown woven with silver pins, leaving her long blue tresses to spill gracefully down her back.
Aki stared at her reflection in the full-length mahogany mirror.
The woman looking back was undeniably stunning, radiant with the flawless dignity of the First Princess of the World.
But her azure eyes were cold with her brow knitted in a weary scowl.
"Smile, Your Highness," Mira pleaded gently, offering a small nervous smile of her own. "You are terrifying when you scowl like that since you are the jewel of the court."
"I am a piece of painted glass," Aki murmured flatly, snapping her silk fan open with a soft dismissive clack.
A chime echoed through the penthouse intercom as a low robotic voice announced.
[Crown Royal Transport has docked at Private Pad Alpha! Crown Prince Alexander has cleared the perimeter security threshold!]
Aki drew in a slow deep breath, smoothing down the front of her silk gown, and turned toward the grand living parlor.
The double doors of the penthouse slid open with a heavy hiss.
Flanked by four heavily armored imperial bodyguards clad in black exosuits, the Crown Prince stepped across the threshold.
Alexander was tall... easily six feet two inches with the broad athletic shoulders of an active combatant.
He shared Aki’s striking, royal-blue hair, though his was cut short and slicked back with severe military precision.
At thirty years old, he carried the unmistakable suffocating aura of a high-tier Lord who had spent a decade commanding armies on the blood-soaked battlefields of the Sovereign Realm.
Aki swallowed hard as she watched him cross the plush carpet.
’Both Silas and my brother are the exact same height...’ the thought flashed involuntarily through her mind.
Yet the two men could not have felt more completely different.
Silas carried his power like a quiet slumbering mountain while Alexander carried his like an unsheathed blade held against someone’s throat.
It was loud and constantly demanding attention as well as submission, Aki gulped however Alexander did not greet her.

He unbuttoned his heavy black military greatcoat, tossed it casually onto the nearest armchair without breaking stride, and dropped his frame onto the central velvet sofa, spreading his boots wide on the carpet.
He leaned back, rubbing his temples with an expression of pure venomous irritation.
"That miserable, backwater slut," Alexander snarled, his voice a low grating rasp that made the room’s air feel heavy. "That filthy, half-blooded gutter rat."
Aki remained standing near the panoramic windows, resting her hands neatly over the ribs of her closed silk fan.
She didn’t blink as she had heard this exact rant three times this month already.
"I assume you are referring to our esteemed half-sister?" Aki asked, keeping her tone light.

"Who else?!" Alexander barked, his blue eyes flashing with violent fury. "Our father has completely lost his mind in his old age! The woman was a commoner from the lower side! A tavern girl he took to bed behind our late mother’s back before she even succumbed to her illness! And now... because the bastard happened to touch the Pillar and manifest a high-grade Purple Lord Core, Father is treating her like the second coming of the imperial lineage!"
He slammed his fist against the arm of the sofa with a muffled thud.

"A Purple Core! The same grade as mine! And now Father has plans to formally introduce her to the World Council. She’s going to be sitting on the primary strategy committee! A bastard with common blood in her veins, sitting at the table where the future of the World is decided, while she commands private detachments in the Sovereign Realm!"
He looked up at Aki, his eyes sweeping over her sky-blue silk gown with his lip curling in disgust.

"And you," he spat, gesturing aggressively toward her. "You stand there in silk, acting as if none of this affects you! If you had awakened a proper core at sixteen, we would have owned the family registry... We would have locked out every single illegitimate branch but no... you touched the stone and produced hollow nothingness! An Unawakened failure who can’t even circulate a single thread of mana to defend her own bloodline!"
Aki didn’t flinch.
She was used to the poison.
For years, she had been the family’s scapegoat.

Her father had cast her aside, her brother viewed her as an administrative embarrassment and when the half-sister had awakened her Purple Core, the imperial court had practically erased Aki’s name from the official succession ledgers.

’Even the bastard has a name,’ Aki thought, her fingers tightening around her fan. ’Every high noble, every soldier, every merchant in this city has a name. What do I have? The Nameless Scion... The Useless Princess...’
Then, a sudden memory brushed against her chest.
’Stay safe out there, Aki.’
The memory of Silas’s warm voice echoed through her thoughts.
She remembered the gentle, rough touch of his fingers against the nape of her neck as he fastened the star-iron chain.
’Aki.’
A soft uncontrollable flush rose to her cheeks.
She was not nameless anymore... In a fortified valley far beyond the reaches of this sterile metropolis, a Lord had looked her in the eyes and given her a title that belonged solely to her.
The corner of her lips twitched upward into a small secretive smile.
Alexander froze mid-breath.
His eyes narrowed into razor-thin slits as he caught the dreamy curve of her lips as the veins along his neck bulged with sudden explosive rage.
"What are you smiling about?!" Alexander roared, surging up from the sofa!
He crossed the distance between them in three heavy strides, his towering frame casting a massive intimidating shadow over her.

"Do you find the humiliation of our lineage amusing?!" he snarled, leaning his face down until he was barely an inch from her nose. "You stand there grinning like an idiot while our inheritance is dragged through the mud by common filth! You are an Unawakened parasite! If you weren’t so utterly useless, I wouldn’t have to share the family’s legacy with someone who carries gutter blood! Commoners are vermin! They are livestock bred to harvest ore and bleed in the lower trenches so people of our stature can rule! Every single one of them deserves to be put against a wall and crushed!"
The words hit the room like a hammer and Aki stood still.
In that moment, she didn’t see the Crown Prince of the World.

She saw Silas... he was a man who was a commoner and he had attended an academy on Scholarship as he told her not too long ago but this was the same person that bled for his people and who commanded devotion because he led from the front, not from an armchair.
Aki took a slow deliberate breath as she looked her terrifying brother straight in the eyes and perhaps, for the first time since she was born, she did not look down.
"You are wrong," Aki said and the silence that followed was suffocating.
Alexander’s face went completely blank with shock. "What did you just say?"

"I said, you are wrong, Alexander," Aki repeated. "Common blood does not make a person livestock and having a high-tier core does not make you a leader. Power without respect is just brute force... You sit here whining like a frightened child because a girl from the lower rim outworked you and earned Father’s attention. If your authority was truly absolute, you wouldn’t feel threatened by a commoner with a purple stone."
"You insolent little bitch!"
WHOOSH!
Alexander’s heavy right hand ripped through the air, raised high to strike her across the face but Aki didn’t close her eyes.
Her heart hammered wildly against her ribs, her breath caught in her throat, and pure terror spiked through her nervous system.
She had no mana so a single strike from a high-tier Lord’s palm would shatter her jawbone and throw her through the reinforced glass.
Yet she kept her chin raised.
Her azure eyes burned with a defiance that did not waver by a single fraction of a millimeter.
Alexander’s hand stopped three inches from her cheek as the wind from his swing whipped the blue bangs across her forehead, but the blow never landed.
The Crown Prince stood frozen with his eyes wide as he stared at his sister’s face.
In all his years, he had seen her bow, he had seen her weep, and he had seen her cower behind her silk fan.
He had never seen her look at him as if he were smaller than she was.
He looked down at his trembling, raised hand.
’What am I doing...?’ he thought, a sudden sick jolt of disgust hitting him. ’Striking an Unawakened in her own quarters...?’
He slowly pulled his hand back, clenching his fingers into a tight, white-knuckled fist.
His jaw clenched until the muscles twitched.
"You’ve grown bold, sister," Alexander hissed, his voice trembling with suppressed malice. "You spend a week locked away in your suite, and suddenly you think you understand how the world operates?"
He sneered, a cruel mocking smirk twisting his lips.
"Since you have developed such a profound appreciation for common grit and struggle... perhaps it is time you experienced it firsthand."
Aki frowned slightly. "What are you talking about?"
"Don a disguise," Alexander commanded, turning his back to her and marching toward the penthouse doors. "A simple hooded mantle and you are coming with me."
Aki tilted her head. "And if I refuse?"
Alexander paused at the threshold, glancing back over his shoulder with cold amusement.

"Then I will have the auditors freeze your household accounts within the hour. You want to speak about courage and power? Your punishment for insolence is simple... you are going to enter the ring, pick up a weapon, and face real living monsters in the pit."
Aki blinked once.
Twice.
Inside her chest, her heart did not sink.
Instead, a brilliant dazzling spark of pure adventurous excitement ignited behind her ribs.
’Real monsters...?’ she thought, her azure eyes shimmering with sudden, undisguised interest. ’Like... the ones in the basin?’
She quickly masked her expression, but Alexander caught the sudden brightness in her face.
He let out a derisive scoff.
"Sure. Keep that look on your face, sister. Let’s see how long it lasts when you’re smelling raw sulfur and rotting teeth."

chapters.title: Chapter 524: Fighting Monsters [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Ten minutes later, a heavy armored limousine was gliding silently through the elevated corridors of Rhyx City.
The interior of the vehicle was lined with dark synth-leather and soundproofed against the city’s neon roar.
Aki sat near the window, wrapped in an oversized charcoal-gray hooded traveling cloak that completely obscured her sky-blue silk gown.
She reached beneath the collar with her fingers lightly tapping the raw mana diamonds of Silas’s necklace, drawing immense silent reassurance from the steady feeling of his energy.
The limousine descended from the sunlit upper tiers, passing through the mid-level corporate plazas and plunging into the lower industrial districts where the light of the sun never reached.
The vehicle pulled into a reinforced subterranean parking bay beneath a sprawling brutalist concrete complex.
Above the heavy blast doors, a buzzing holographic sign flickered in harsh crimson light.
[RHYX SUB-TIER EXCAVATION & COMBAT SIMULATION FACILITY: ARENA 4]
It was the Monster Center.

In Rhyx City, the facility served a very specific purpose... It was an underground training ground where wealthy Unawakened noble scions and corporate heirs could experience combat against real low-tier beasts captured from the Sovereign Realm before they reached the age of sixteen to eighteen to attempt their Lord Core awakenings.
The monsters were strictly managed, categorized by tier, and kept behind reinforced kinetic barriers.
The limousine doors opened, and Alexander stepped out, followed by Aki and two plainclothes imperial guards.
They crossed the polished concrete lobby.
Despite their low-profile attire, the receptionist... a tired-looking man in his late thirties wearing a corporate uniform instantly froze the moment the Crown Prince stepped up to the counter.
The overwhelming pressure of Alexander’s aura was impossible to conceal.
"Y-Your Highness!" the clerk stammered, bowing so low his nose nearly touched the glass partition. "We... we were not informed of an inspection! The director is currently—"

"Quiet," Alexander cut in flatly, tossing an obsidian priority token onto the counter. "I don’t need the director... I need an isolated low-tier pit that is fully enclosed and has Class-C containment."
The clerk grabbed the token with trembling fingers, scanning it through his console.
"O-Of course! Arena Seven is completely vacant! Are you looking to run live combat drills for your elite guard, Prince Alexander?"

"Not for my guard," Alexander replied, his cold gaze shifting sideways toward the hooded figure standing beside him. "For my sister... She wishes to test her personal combat arts against wild monsters."
The clerk looked at Aki, his eyes darting to her slender frame beneath the charcoal cloak.
A look of horrified panic washed over his face.

"Your Highness... forgive my presumption, but... the First Princess is Unawakened," the clerk pleaded in a whisper. "Standard facility regulations strictly forbid non-awakened from entering live pits without a mercenary escort at least! Even a Tier-1 monster possesses enough raw physical strength to—"
VUUUM!

Alexander’s eyes flashed with a razor-thin glint of purple mana as the atmospheric pressure around the desk spiked, and the clerk choked, his voice dying in his throat as cold sweat drenched his collar.
"I am the Crown Prince," Alexander said softly. "Are you telling me that facility regulations supercede my authority?"
"N-No, Sire! Never! My apologies!" the clerk gasped, his hands flying across his keyboard. "Arena Seven is prepped! Access codes granted!"
Beside them, Aki didn’t look terrified at all. In fact, she puffed her chest out beneath her cloak, quietly pumping her small gloved fist with suppressed triumph.
’A real arena...’ she thought. ’Silas wouldn’t let me fight the leeches in the canyon and now I can actually try out what Morwenna and the other girls showed me!’
Everyone said it was tough to train with Brida and she agreed but even Brida had commended her skills too!
The clerk swallowed hard, catching her eager expression, and felt his sanity slipping. ’Is the royal family insane?! She looks like she’s going to a pastry shop!’
They were led down a long, sterile corridor lined with heavy blast doors to Arena Seven.
The chamber was massive... an eighty-foot circular pit lined with reinforced blood-stained concrete walls, roofed by an electrified barrier forty feet overhead.
Flanking the pit was an elevated observation deck separated by bulletproof, mana-resistant glass.
Alexander stepped up toward the observation stairs, pausing to look back at his hooded sister.

"Five beasts," Alexander decreed. "Tier 1 monsters. If you manage to survive all five without crying for the emergency extractors... I will grant you one personal favor. Anything within my authority."
Aki’s azure eyes flared with sharp focus. "A favor? In writing?"
Alexander let out a mocking laugh.
"Upon my honor as Crown Prince. But if you fail... you will submit to Father’s arranged marriage without another word of complaint. Agreed?"
"Agreed," Aki said instantly, without a shred of hesitation.
Alexander turned and ascended to the observation deck, taking a seat in the leather command chair behind the glass, crossing his legs as his guards flanked the console.
Down below, the clerk nervously guided Aki through the staging airlock into the equipment bay bordering the pit.
Racks of heavy standard-issue gear lined the steel walls... iron broadswords, steel round shields, heavy halberds, and crossbows designed for city guards.
"Your Highness... please, reconsider," the clerk whispered frantically. "Take a heavy tower shield! Or a mechanized repeating carbine! You don’t have mana to reinforce an edge!"
Aki ignored him completely.
Her eyes swept across the racks as she looked at the heavy iron swords and immediately shook her head.
’Too clumsy... Morwenna said heavy blades without mana reinforcement just throw your center of gravity into the mud.’
Her gaze settled upon a light recurve composite shortbow crafted from flexible dark ash, paired with a leather quiver holding twelve broadhead arrows with steel bodkin tips.
Beside it on the rack hung a slender, seven-inch hunting dagger with a cross-hatched leather grip.
’This is what I know,’ Aki thought, reaching out and lifting the bow.

During the quiet evenings in the Keep, when Silas was reviewing a lot of things, Tasmin as well as the other girls including Fenna had spent hours teaching her basic bow tension and draw alignment, while Morwenna had drilled her on grip transitions with a utility blade.
She strapped the quiver securely to her right hip, slung the hunting dagger at the small of her back beneath her cloak, and stepped up to the edge of the pit.
The clerk sighed, pulling the master lever with a trembling hand.
"Releasing Monster one... Tier 1 Goblin Scavenger."
CLANK-HISS!
Across the pit, a heavy steel gate rattled open.
From the dark drainage tunnel beneath the gate, a creature shambled out onto the blood-stained concrete.

It was a Goblin... a lean green-skinned feral anomaly roughly four feet tall, its scrawny torso covered in coarse gray bristles and its yellow bloodshot eyes darting around the arena with manic hunger.
In its clawed right hand, it dragged a jagged rusty iron cleaver, its drooling jaw lined with needle-like yellow teeth.
SCREEECH!
The beast spotted the hooded human maiden standing forty paces away.
It threw its head back, letting out a vile guttural shriek, and charged across the concrete floor, its splay-toed feet slapping against the stone with terrifying speed.
Up on the observation deck, Alexander leaned back in his leather chair, a cold satisfied smirk spreading across his lips.

’I just need to let it close the distance,’ the Crown Prince thought, his fingers tapping the armrest. ’The moment she smells the creature’s breath and sees the rusted iron swing toward her ribs, she will drop to her knees and beg for the barrier. A simple painful lesson to remind her where she belongs—’
Down in the pit, Aki didn’t blink.
Compared to a sixty-foot Tier 5 apex titan that shook the foundations of the northern mountains... this green little scavenger looked almost comical.
Her posture settled instantly.
Her shoulders dropped, her left foot sliding forward at a forty-five-degree angle, locking her center of gravity directly over her hips, just as Fenna had drilled into her.
She reached her right hand back, drawing a steel-tipped arrow from her quiver in a single fluid motion.
NOCK!
She drew the bowstring back to the corner of her jaw and the flexible ash limbs arched smoothly under the tension.
She didn’t possess mana to coat the arrowhead but her eyes were calm and as soon as the goblin reached twenty paces with its rusted cleaver raised high and its yellow teeth bared in a feral screech—
THWIP! WHOOOOOOSH!
The arrow released with a razor-thin whistle that cut clean through the concrete chamber.
THWACK-CRUNCH!
The steel bodkin tip struck the charging goblin dead-center between its bulging yellow eyes.
The force of the point-blank shot drove the arrow clean through the creature’s frontal bone, piercing the brain stem and exiting the back of its skull in a spray of dark fluid.
FLOP!
The goblin’s momentum died instantly.
The creature collapsed face-first onto the concrete like a dropped sack of wet flour, skidding two yards across the stone before coming to a dead twitching stop at the center of the pit.
Up on the observation deck, Alexander’s smirk vanished.
His blue eyes snapped wide, his jaw dropping open in paralyzed disbelief as his fingers dug straight into the leather padding of his chair.
Down in the blood-stained pit, Aki lowered the composite bow.
A thin strand of royal-blue hair slipped from beneath her charcoal hood.
She looked down at the dead monster, tilted her head with an amused effortless smirk, and whispered to herself.
"Light work."
The dead goblin lay on the scuffed concrete forty paces out, dark, viscous fluid pooling around its shattered skull.
The steel bodkin point had punched clean through bone and anchored into the floor with a muted tink.
Up in the observation booth, Alexander’s fingers were white-knuckled against the armrests, indenting the synthetic leather so deeply the seams strained.
"Next gate," Alexander barked into the console’s comm grille, his voice sounding tightl.
The facility technician scrambled, hands trembling over the toggle array.
"Y-Your Highness, protocol dictates an extraction cycle to clear the bio-sludge before—"
"I said open the gate."
"Opening Gate Two!" the technician squeaked, slamming a red toggle down.
KZZZZT... CLANK.
Across the blood-spattered arena floor, the heavy iron portcullis on the eastern perimeter rattled upward with hydraulic lines hissing out a thick plume of steam.
From the dark culvert emerged a Skitter-Hound... a Tier 1 monster that looked like a starved hyena stripped of skin, its lean musculature bound together by greasy gray sinew.
Instead of standard paws, its forelegs terminated in three-pronged calcified spurs that scraped the floor with a sickening sound.
TIK! TIK! TIK!
Its long narrow snout had split vertically into three hinged jaws lined with backward-curving teeth, drooling yellow bile that smoked against the floor.
It caught the scent of goblin marrow first as its neck hitched and then its milky lidless eyes locked onto Aki.
"Huuu..."
Aki didn’t backpedal.

Her breathing remained low, pulled deep into her abdomen and beneath her heavy traveling cloak, her posture stayed rooted with her feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly flexed to maintain her center of gravity over her hips.

’Don’t track the teeth,’ Tasmin’s voice echoed in her mind, clear as if she had placed a speaker in there. ’Predators feint with the jaw so watch the hips... The pelvis tells you where the weight goes before the muscle snaps.’
The Skitter-Hound lunged.

It didn’t charge in a straight line just as the Princess expected, it moved in a jagged erratic zig-zag with the calcified spurs on its forelegs gouging long white tracks into the concrete as it covered fifteen paces in the span of several heartbeats.
TIK-TIK-TIK... SCRAPE!
It feinted right with its torso twisting to throw off her line of sight, aiming to flank her blind spot and tear out her Achilles tendon but like she was taught, Aki didn’t try to track its head.

Her azure eyes stayed locked on the creature’s lower spine and the moment its hindquarters dipped to spring, she pivoted on her left heel, stepping forty-five degrees into its arc instead of retreating.
NOCK-DRAW!
The composite bow arched smoothly with the ash limbs groaning under the tension.
THWIP!
The arrow released at point-blank range.
The hound, airborne and committed to its pounce, saw the steel point rushing toward its chest and snapped its triple-hinged jaw shut mid-air, attempting to bite the shaft in two.
CRUNCH!
The broadhead arrow shattered through the left mandible, splintering the bone and tearing through the creature’s tongue as the force deflected the beast’s trajectory, throwing it off-balance mid-air.
It crashed heavily onto the floor beside Aki, rolling across the stone in a spray of yellow bile and shredded flesh.
THUD-SLIDE!
The beast shrieked as it scrambled to its feet, spurs scrabbling against the floor to whip around and clamp onto Aki’s thigh.
Aki didn’t reach for a second arrow.
’It’s too close for a draw,’ She thought. ’I should use the blade.’

Aki dropped the bow with her left hand, letting it clatter to the concrete as her right hand whipped around to the small of her back with her fingers locking around the cross-hatched leather grip of the seven-inch hunting dagger.
SHING.
She didn’t wait for the beast to regain its balance.
As the hound lunged upward, its remaining jaws wide, Aki lowered her center, drove her lead foot into the floor, and stepped straight inside the snap of its teeth.
Her left forearm, wrapped in the heavy wool of her cloak, drove hard into the creature’s throat, checking its forward momentum with a dull thump.
The beast’s hot acidic breath washed over her face with the bile spattering the collar of her tunic.
Before the hound’s spurs could rake her stomach, Aki reversed her grip on the dagger, bringing the steel down in a clean vertical ice-pick strike!
THWACK-CRUNCH!
The seven-inch blade punched straight through the base of the skull where the spine met the brainstem!

sentences.text: Ten minutes later, a heavy armored limousine was gliding silently through the elevated corridors of Rhyx City.
The interior of the vehicle was lined with dark synth-leather and soundproofed against the city’s neon roar.
Aki sat near the window, wrapped in an oversized charcoal-gray hooded traveling cloak that completely obscured her sky-blue silk gown.
She reached beneath the collar with her fingers lightly tapping the raw mana diamonds of Silas’s necklace, drawing immense silent reassurance from the steady feeling of his energy.
The limousine descended from the sunlit upper tiers, passing through the mid-level corporate plazas and plunging into the lower industrial districts where the light of the sun never reached.
The vehicle pulled into a reinforced subterranean parking bay beneath a sprawling brutalist concrete complex.
Above the heavy blast doors, a buzzing holographic sign flickered in harsh crimson light.
[RHYX SUB-TIER EXCAVATION & COMBAT SIMULATION FACILITY: ARENA 4]
It was the Monster Center.
In Rhyx City, the facility served a very specific purpose...

It was an underground training ground where wealthy Unawakened noble scions and corporate heirs could experience combat against real low-tier beasts captured from the Sovereign Realm before they reached the age of sixteen to eighteen to attempt their Lord Core awakenings.
The monsters were strictly managed, categorized by tier, and kept behind reinforced kinetic barriers.
The limousine doors opened, and Alexander stepped out, followed by Aki and two plainclothes imperial guards.
They crossed the polished concrete lobby.
Despite their low-profile attire, the receptionist... a tired-looking man in his late thirties wearing a corporate uniform instantly froze the moment the Crown Prince stepped up to the counter.
The overwhelming pressure of Alexander’s aura was impossible to conceal.
"Y-Your Highness!" the clerk stammered, bowing so low his nose nearly touched the glass partition.
"We... we were not informed of an inspection!
The director is currently—"
"Quiet," Alexander cut in flatly, tossing an obsidian priority token onto the counter.
"I don’t need the director...
I need an isolated low-tier pit that is fully enclosed and has Class-C containment."
The clerk grabbed the token with trembling fingers, scanning it through his console.
"O-Of course!

Are you looking to run live combat drills for your elite guard, Prince Alexander?"
"Not for my guard," Alexander replied, his cold gaze shifting sideways toward the hooded figure standing beside him.
"For my sister...
She wishes to test her personal combat arts against wild monsters."
The clerk looked at Aki, his eyes darting to her slender frame beneath the charcoal cloak.
A look of horrified panic washed over his face.

"Standard facility regulations strictly forbid non-awakened from entering live pits without a mercenary escort at least!
Even a Tier-1 monster possesses enough raw physical strength to—"
VUUUM!

Alexander’s eyes flashed with a razor-thin glint of purple mana as the atmospheric pressure around the desk spiked, and the clerk choked, his voice dying in his throat as cold sweat drenched his collar.
"I am the Crown Prince," Alexander said softly.
"Are you telling me that facility regulations supercede my authority?"
"N-No, Sire!
Never!
My apologies!" the clerk gasped, his hands flying across his keyboard.
"Arena Seven is prepped!
Access codes granted!"
Beside them, Aki didn’t look terrified at all.
In fact, she puffed her chest out beneath her cloak, quietly pumping her small gloved fist with suppressed triumph.
’A real arena...’ she thought. ’Silas wouldn’t let me fight the leeches in the canyon and now I can actually try out what Morwenna and the other girls showed me!’
Everyone said it was tough to train with Brida and she agreed but even Brida had commended her skills too!
The clerk swallowed hard, catching her eager expression, and felt his sanity slipping. ’Is the royal family insane?!
She looks like she’s going to a pastry shop!’
They were led down a long, sterile corridor lined with heavy blast doors to Arena Seven.
The chamber was massive... an eighty-foot circular pit lined with reinforced blood-stained concrete walls, roofed by an electrified barrier forty feet overhead.
Flanking the pit was an elevated observation deck separated by bulletproof, mana-resistant glass.
Alexander stepped up toward the observation stairs, pausing to look back at his hooded sister.
"Five beasts," Alexander decreed.
"Tier 1 monsters.
If you manage to survive all five without crying for the emergency extractors...
I will grant you one personal favor.
Anything within my authority."
Aki’s azure eyes flared with sharp focus.
"A favor?
In writing?"
Alexander let out a mocking laugh.
"Upon my honor as Crown Prince.
But if you fail... you will submit to Father’s arranged marriage without another word of complaint.
Agreed?"
"Agreed," Aki said instantly, without a shred of hesitation.
Alexander turned and ascended to the observation deck, taking a seat in the leather command chair behind the glass, crossing his legs as his guards flanked the console.
Down below, the clerk nervously guided Aki through the staging airlock into the equipment bay bordering the pit.
Racks of heavy standard-issue gear lined the steel walls... iron broadswords, steel round shields, heavy halberds, and crossbows designed for city guards.
"Your Highness... please, reconsider," the clerk whispered frantically.
"Take a heavy tower shield!
Or a mechanized repeating carbine!
You don’t have mana to reinforce an edge!"
