chapters.title: Chapter 525: Fighting Monsters [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Skitter-Hound’s entire body stiffened violently, its spurs digging six inches into the floor before the tension snapped like a cut wire.
It dropped limp, pinning her forearm against its chest.
"Haah... Haah..."
Aki wrenched the blade free with a wet schlick, planting a boot against the beast’s ribcage to shove the dead weight away.
She stood up, wiping the dark bile from her cheek with the back of her wrist with her breath steady and her azure eyes completely flat.
Up in the booth, the silence was deafening.
Alexander’s face had drained of color, replaced by a dark mottled crimson that crept up from beneath his high military collar as his breath came in shallow furious hitches.

An Unawakened noblewoman who had spent twenty-five years locked inside climate-controlled penthouses didn’t drop a bow, close the distance, and drive an ice-pick grip into an anomaly’s brainstem with that kind of motion?

’Of course I am well aware that we of the Royal Line are far more stronger than regular people.’ Alexander thought, they were much much stronger which was why she could pull all these movements. ’But isn’t this too much? What’s going on?’
"Sir..." the technician whispered, his voice shaking. "That’s two. Do I... do I initiate the rest interval?"
Alexander slowly rose from the command chair.
The air in the observation booth dropped ten degrees as his Purple Core resonated through his uniform.
He shoved the technician aside, his heavy leather glove slamming onto the console’s master override board.
"Three," Alexander growled. "Release the remaining three simultaneously."
The technician went pale.
"Highness, that violates every safety protocol in the facility! She’s an Unawakened! Three Tier 1s at once will create a cross-flock hunting formation! She won’t have room to reset her stance—"

"I said open the gates!" Alexander roared, his fist slamming through the plastic casing of the console and cracking the glass display. "If she wants to play the soldier, she can fight like one! OPEN THEM!"
BZZZZZT... CLANG-CLANK-CLANK!
The warning sirens in the arena shifted from yellow pulses to a continuous, blaring crimson wail.
HONK... HONK... HONK!
Across the pit, Gates Three, Four, and Five slammed open simultaneously.
Down on the floor, Aki’s ears twitched.
She didn’t look up at the observation glass and she didn’t shout a protest as the shrill sirens and the three distinct metallic slams told her everything she needed to know.
’Big Brotherrrr... He’s angry,’ she thought, a cold calm settling over her chest. ’He realized he lost the bet on the first two and now he wants to break me so he doesn’t have to honor his word.’
It wouldn’t be the first time that he had done so and she was sure that even if he begged, he would let the monsters rough her up a bit.
’...I’m used to it.’
It was like the time when he had let a monster chew on her hand and tear it off...
She reached down, scooping her composite bow from the floor with her left hand, and retreated four paces toward the center of the arena, creating an equal perimeter between all three gates.

From Gate Three slithered a Spined Stalker... a six-legged reptilian beast with overlapping slate-gray scales that absorbed the arena’s fluorescent glare and its low-slung body carrying a tail tipped with three venomous barbed quills.

From Gate Four charged an armored Boar-Beast which was a hulking mass of calcified muscle weighing nearly four hundred pounds, its skull fused into a solid battering plate of bone, snorting gray vapor as its hooves struck sparks against the concrete.
And from Gate Five leaped a second Skitter-Hound that was leaner and faster than the first, already circling wide to take her flank.
Three different monsters with three different speeds.
’A staggered rush,’ Aki calculated, her fingers reaching into the quiver.

She pulled two arrows at once, holding the second between her middle and ring fingers against the riser of the bow. ’The boar has the mass... if it hits me, my ribcage turns to dust and the lizard has the range with the tail. The hound will wait for me to commit to the boar before jumping my blind side.’
ROOOOOOAR!
The Boar-Beast broke first.
It lowered its bone-plated snout, its massive shoulders bunching, and charged in a straight line with the momentum of a runaway locomotive.
The floor shook beneath its hooves, throwing up chips of shattered concrete but Aki didn’t run.
She didn’t draw the string yet as she stood directly in its path, letting the distance close.
...Thirty paces.
...Twenty paces.
...Ten paces.
Behind her, the Spined Stalker whipped its tail forward, launching three venomous bone quills that sliced through the air with a razor-sharp hiss.
FZZZT-FZZZT-FZZZT!
’Now!’
Aki dropped her hips and threw herself into a low, forward slide.
She slid directly beneath the arc of the incoming quills with the bone darts whistling two inches above her forehead to slam into the charging Boar-Beast’s thick shoulder plate with a wet thud.
The boar didn’t even slow down, but the momentary distraction made its head tilt a fraction of an inch to the right as Aki’s slide halted right beside the boar’s left flank.
She rose to a knee, nocked the first arrow, and drew the bowstring until the nock touched her cheek.
THWIP! SPLAT!
She didn’t aim for the armored skull, instead she drove the bodkin point straight into the soft unarmored socket of the boar’s left eye.
SQUEEEEEEEE!
The beast let out a deafening, piercing shriek as the arrow penetrated four inches into its brain.

Its forward charge lost all cohesion as its legs locked, and the four-hundred-pound brute tumbled head-over-heels, flipping violently across the arena and crashing into the far perimeter wall with a boom.
KRA-CRUNCH!
Concrete dust rained from the wall as the boar twitched, it was stone-dead.
CRACK!
Before Aki could rise from her knee, the second Skitter-Hound struck.
It had closed the distance during her slide, leaping from the blind spot behind her left shoulder as its hinged jaws snapped wide, aimed straight for her exposed neck.
’Wha—-’
Aki twisted her torso, throwing her left arm up to shield her throat!
TEAR-CRUNCH!
The hound’s needle-like teeth sank deep into the meat of her left forearm, tearing through the heavy wool cloak and sinking into the muscle beneath.
A sharp bolt of agony tore through her arm as the shock made her vision flash white around the edges.
Aki gritted her teeth, refusing to scream as warm scarlet blood welled through the fabric of her sleeve, soaking her fingers.
The hound landed its front spurs on her chest, using its weight to bear her down to the floor, shaking its head violently to rip the flesh from her bone.
’Ah... Ah... I shouldn’t pull away.’ Aki thought, she would use this opportunity to leverage her advantage.
Aki didn’t pull her arm back.
Instead, she shoved her bleeding left arm deeper into the creature’s throat, choking its airway and denying it the leverage to tear.

With her right hand, she drew the second arrow she had held against the riser as she held the arrow like an ice-pick, thumb locked over the nock, and rammed the steel point upward through the soft tissue beneath the hound’s lower jaw.
PUNCH-SNAP!
The steel arrowhead tore through the tongue, through the roof of the mouth, and punched straight out between the hound’s ears.
The beast’s jaws went slack.
The teeth released her forearm, and the hound collapsed sideways as blood poured from its snout as it kicked twice and lay still.
Aki dragged herself to her feet, her left arm hanging limp with blood dripping from her fingertips and pattering against the stone.
Drip... Drip... Drip.
’I’m glad...’
If she didn’t get all that training, she would have been done in by now.
She was breathing in ragged gasps.
Her hair was matted with sweat with several blue locks plastered to her forehead and the pain in her arm was a white-hot iron spike, radiating all the way up into her collarbone.
She turned her head.
The Spined Stalker was eight paces away.
It had spread its six legs wide, clinging to the concrete floor like an oversized toad.
Its tail was cocked back over its head with the muscles coiling to loose another volley of quills. Its lidless yellow eyes tracked the blood running down her arm, sensing that the prey was broken.
Aki looked down at her left hand.
The fingers were twitching with blood slicking her palm so she couldn’t draw a bow. Her composite bow lay five paces away, its string severed by a stray claw during the hound’s tackle.
She reached behind her back with her functioning right hand.
Her fingers closed around the hunting dagger as she pulled it from its sheath, stepping over the dead hound.
’Why am I doing this?’ the thought flashed through her mind, clear and sudden amidst the adrenaline.

She could have stayed in the penthouse... She could have smiled at the tea ceremonies, bowed to her father, and allowed herself to be traded off to some high-ranking heir... She would have had silk dresses, private cruisers, and a life free of physical scars...
Then she felt the cold weight of the star-iron necklace resting against her sternum.
She remembered the way the morning wind felt at Blessed Land.
She remembered the wolves resting their massive snouts on her boots, treating her not as a useless piece of decorative glass, but as one of the pack.
She remembered Silas looking her dead in the eye and handing her a name that was entirely hers.
’Aki.’
’I am not a nameless asset,’ she thought, her grip tightening around the dagger’s hilt until her knuckles turned white. ’I... I... I’m me.’
HISSSSSSS!
The Spined Stalker whipped its tail forward and two quills screamed through the air.
Aki didn’t duck.

She tracked the angle of the tail’s snap, twisting her upper body just enough to let the first quill graze her right shoulder, slicing through the wool and drawing a shallow line of crimson across her deltoid while the second quill whistled past her cheek, clipping a lock of her blue hair.
Aki detonated forward.
Her silk slippers, scuffed and stained with blood, gripped the concrete with surprising traction as she crossed the eight paces in a desperate, sprinting lunge!
The Stalker opened its wide, needle-lined jaw, snapping its head forward to crush her knee but she leaped.
She cleared the snap of its jaws with her knees tucking tightly to her chest, and brought both boots down hard onto the creature’s scaly back.
KRA-CRACK!
The impact drove the lizard’s chest flat against the concrete, knocking the wind from its lungs with a wet gasp.
’Thankfully it’s Tier 1...’
She needed to put this much power and force into her attacks to wound one when the average Blessed Land soldier could just one-shot it.
Before the tail could swing around to impale her thighs, Aki dropped her full body weight down, driving her right knee into the back of its neck to pin its skull to the floor.
She reversed the hunting dagger in both hands, bringing the steel down with every ounce of physical strength, fury, and stubborn royal pride she possessed.
CHUNK!
The blade severed the spinal cord between the first and second vertebrae.
CHUNK!
She struck again, carving through the tough rubbery hide.
CHUNK!
The third strike shattered the skull base entirely with the blade burying itself to the hilt in the concrete beneath!
The Spined Stalker shuddered once, its six legs extending outward in a final spastic reflex, before going permanently limp.
The arena fell into suffocating silence as only the ragged, wheezing sound of Aki’s breath echoed off the high concrete walls.
She knelt there on the back of the dead beast with her hands drenched in dark reptilian blood and her left arm throbbing with vicious, burning agony.
Her charcoal cloak was shredded, her sky-blue traveling dress stained with bile, gore, and dirt.
Slowly, she lifted her head.
Her azure eyes cut through the glare of the arena lights, locking directly onto the observation window above.
She simply stared at her brother through the glass with a look in her eyes and up in the booth, Alexander stood frozen.
His breath was caught in his throat.
The purple mana coiling around his hands slowly sputtered out, dying into cold air as his guards stood rigid behind him, their eyes wide, completely unable to process what they had just witnessed.
An Unawakened... slaughtering five beasts with... zero magic?
Alexander’s jaw tightened.
Without a word, he turned on his heel and strode out of the observation booth, his heavy military boots striking the metal stairs with a hollow rhythm.
HISS... CLANK.
The staging airlock door hissed open, and Alexander stepped out onto the arena floor.

He walked past the mangled carcass of the goblin and he walked past the dead hound, his boots crunching on the shattered concrete where the boar had crashed as he soon stopped three paces from his sister.
Aki remained on her knee, looking up at him with her chest heaving and blood dripping steadily from her torn left forearm onto the lizard’s scales.
Alexander looked down at her.
His eyes were dark, stormy, and conflicted, torn between blistering wounded pride and an unsettling cold tremor of genuine disbelief.
He raised his right hand.
VUUUUUM!

A soft lilac-tinted healing aura ignited around his palm... it was a refined high-tier restorative mana from his Purple Core as he stepped forward, reaching down and grasping her mangled left forearm.
Aki stiffened with a sharp hiss escaping her teeth as the mana flooded the open puncture wounds.
The restorative energy swept through her damaged flesh like warm water.

The torn muscle fibers knit back together with a strange itching heat as the bleeding stopped, and the jagged skin smoothed over, leaving only faint pinkish silver marks where the hound’s teeth had pierced to the bone.
Within ten seconds, the throbbing agony subsided into a dull manageable ache.
Alexander released her arm, stepping back.
He wiped a drop of her blood from his leather glove as his brow furrowed deeply.
"Where..." Alexander began, his jaw clenching as he forced the words past his pride. "Where in the nine hells did you get that kind of experience?"
Aki didn’t answer.
She slowly stood up from the dead lizard, testing the weight on her left arm.
She rolled her shoulder, letting the shredded sleeve fall back into place, and smoothed down the front of her ruined tunic.

"I asked you a question, sister," Alexander pressed, his tone rising with irritated frustration. "You don’t learn stance control like that from books... You don’t take a beast’s bite to the forearm just to secure an angle for an eye strike unless someone drilled it into your skull with a wooden stave so who trained you? Was it one of the retired Lords? Did you hire a mercenary behind Father’s back?!"
Aki looked at him.
Her azure eyes were remarkably clear.
The lingering fear that had ruled her interactions with him for twenty-five years was completely gone and in its place was a suffocating indifference.
"That wasn’t part of the bet," Aki said softly.

sentences.text: The Skitter-Hound’s entire body stiffened violently, its spurs digging six inches into the floor before the tension snapped like a cut wire.
It dropped limp, pinning her forearm against its chest.
"Haah...
Haah..."

Up in the booth, the silence was deafening.
Alexander’s face had drained of color, replaced by a dark mottled crimson that crept up from beneath his high military collar as his breath came in shallow furious hitches.

An Unawakened noblewoman who had spent twenty-five years locked inside climate-controlled penthouses didn’t drop a bow, close the distance, and drive an ice-pick grip into an anomaly’s brainstem with that kind of motion?

"Sir..." the technician whispered, his voice shaking.

Alexander slowly rose from the command chair.
The air in the observation booth dropped ten degrees as his Purple Core resonated through his uniform.
He shoved the technician aside, his heavy leather glove slamming onto the console’s master override board.
"Three," Alexander growled.

The technician went pale.

She’s an Unawakened!
Three Tier 1s at once will create a cross-flock hunting formation!

CLANG-CLANK-CLANK!
The warning sirens in the arena shifted from yellow pulses to a continuous, blaring crimson wail.
HONK...
HONK...
HONK!
Across the pit, Gates Three, Four, and Five slammed open simultaneously.

’...I’m used to it.’
It was like the time when he had let a monster chew on her hand and tear it off...
She reached down, scooping her composite bow from the floor with her left hand, and retreated four paces toward the center of the arena, creating an equal perimeter between all three gates.

From Gate Three slithered a Spined Stalker... a six-legged reptilian beast with overlapping slate-gray scales that absorbed the arena’s fluorescent glare and its low-slung body carrying a tail tipped with three venomous barbed quills.

From Gate Four charged an armored Boar-Beast which was a hulking mass of calcified muscle weighing nearly four hundred pounds, its skull fused into a solid battering plate of bone, snorting gray vapor as its hooves struck sparks against the concrete.
And from Gate Five leaped a second Skitter-Hound that was leaner and faster than the first, already circling wide to take her flank.
Three different monsters with three different speeds.
’A staggered rush,’ Aki calculated, her fingers reaching into the quiver.

The hound will wait for me to commit to the boar before jumping my blind side.’
ROOOOOOAR!
The Boar-Beast broke first.
It lowered its bone-plated snout, its massive shoulders bunching, and charged in a straight line with the momentum of a runaway locomotive.
The floor shook beneath its hooves, throwing up chips of shattered concrete but Aki didn’t run.
She didn’t draw the string yet as she stood directly in its path, letting the distance close.

Behind her, the Spined Stalker whipped its tail forward, launching three venomous bone quills that sliced through the air with a razor-sharp hiss.
FZZZT-FZZZT-FZZZT!
’Now!’
Aki dropped her hips and threw herself into a low, forward slide.
She slid directly beneath the arc of the incoming quills with the bone darts whistling two inches above her forehead to slam into the charging Boar-Beast’s thick shoulder plate with a wet thud.
The boar didn’t even slow down, but the momentary distraction made its head tilt a fraction of an inch to the right as Aki’s slide halted right beside the boar’s left flank.
She rose to a knee, nocked the first arrow, and drew the bowstring until the nock touched her cheek.
THWIP!
SPLAT!
She didn’t aim for the armored skull, instead she drove the bodkin point straight into the soft unarmored socket of the boar’s left eye.
SQUEEEEEEEE!
The beast let out a deafening, piercing shriek as the arrow penetrated four inches into its brain.

Its forward charge lost all cohesion as its legs locked, and the four-hundred-pound brute tumbled head-over-heels, flipping violently across the arena and crashing into the far perimeter wall with a boom.
KRA-CRUNCH!
Concrete dust rained from the wall as the boar twitched, it was stone-dead.
CRACK!
Before Aki could rise from her knee, the second Skitter-Hound struck.
It had closed the distance during her slide, leaping from the blind spot behind her left shoulder as its hinged jaws snapped wide, aimed straight for her exposed neck.
’Wha—-’
Aki twisted her torso, throwing her left arm up to shield her throat!
TEAR-CRUNCH!
The hound’s needle-like teeth sank deep into the meat of her left forearm, tearing through the heavy wool cloak and sinking into the muscle beneath.
A sharp bolt of agony tore through her arm as the shock made her vision flash white around the edges.
Aki gritted her teeth, refusing to scream as warm scarlet blood welled through the fabric of her sleeve, soaking her fingers.
The hound landed its front spurs on her chest, using its weight to bear her down to the floor, shaking its head violently to rip the flesh from her bone.
Ah...
I shouldn’t pull away.’ Aki thought, she would use this opportunity to leverage her advantage.
Aki didn’t pull her arm back.
Instead, she shoved her bleeding left arm deeper into the creature’s throat, choking its airway and denying it the leverage to tear.

With her right hand, she drew the second arrow she had held against the riser as she held the arrow like an ice-pick, thumb locked over the nock, and rammed the steel point upward through the soft tissue beneath the hound’s lower jaw.
PUNCH-SNAP!
The steel arrowhead tore through the tongue, through the roof of the mouth, and punched straight out between the hound’s ears.
The beast’s jaws went slack.
The teeth released her forearm, and the hound collapsed sideways as blood poured from its snout as it kicked twice and lay still.
Aki dragged herself to her feet, her left arm hanging limp with blood dripping from her fingertips and pattering against the stone.
Drip...
Drip...
Drip.
’I’m glad...’
If she didn’t get all that training, she would have been done in by now.
She was breathing in ragged gasps.
Her hair was matted with sweat with several blue locks plastered to her forehead and the pain in her arm was a white-hot iron spike, radiating all the way up into her collarbone.
She turned her head.
The Spined Stalker was eight paces away.
It had spread its six legs wide, clinging to the concrete floor like an oversized toad.
Its tail was cocked back over its head with the muscles coiling to loose another volley of quills.
Its lidless yellow eyes tracked the blood running down her arm, sensing that the prey was broken.
Aki looked down at her left hand.
The fingers were twitching with blood slicking her palm so she couldn’t draw a bow.
Her composite bow lay five paces away, its string severed by a stray claw during the hound’s tackle.
She reached behind her back with her functioning right hand.
Her fingers closed around the hunting dagger as she pulled it from its sheath, stepping over the dead hound.
’Why am I doing this?’ the thought flashed through her mind, clear and sudden amidst the adrenaline.
She could have stayed in the penthouse...
She could have smiled at the tea ceremonies, bowed to her father, and allowed herself to be traded off to some high-ranking heir...
She would have had silk dresses, private cruisers, and a life free of physical scars...

chapters.title: Chapter 526: Silas Graves [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Alexander blinked, caught off guard. "What?"

"The bet," she repeated, her voice sounding steady. "Five beasts. I survived all five without asking for the barrier and you swore upon your honor as Crown Prince that you would grant me one personal favor... Anything within your authority."
Alexander’s expression hardened, his lip curling into a haughty dismissive sneer.

"Fine. A deal is a deal. What do you want? A private estate in the southern provinces? A larger budget allocation for your wardrobe? A personal escort detachment so you don’t embarrass the family again?"
Aki took half a step closer.
She looked him dead in the eyes, her voice ringing clear and loud across the empty blood-stained arena.
"My wish... is for you to fuck out of my life."
Alexander froze.
His blue eyes snapped wide, his breath catching in his throat as if he had been struck across the sternum with an iron hammer.

In all their twenty-five years, through every reprimand, every scolding, and every quiet evening in the imperial palace, he had never heard her raise her voice, let alone speak a single syllable of profanity.
"What did you just say to me...?" Alexander whispered, his voice trembling.

"You heard me," Aki said, her expression sounding deadpan with her chin held high. "I don’t want your money... I don’t want your guards... And I really, truly do not want to see your face for the foreseeable future. Leave my suite. Leave my staff alone and don’t ever darken my doorway again."
Without waiting for him to reply, without checking to see his reaction, and without offering the customary courtly bow, Aki turned on her heel.
She walked straight past the dead monsters toward the staging exit, her boots clicking against the concrete floor.
As she crossed the threshold into the equipment bay, she reached beneath her shredded cloak, pulling her private comm device from her pocket and dialing with a flick of her thumb.

"Mira," Aki spoke into the receiver, her tone becoming calm as the airlock doors began to close behind her. "Have the transport ready at the lower bay and have the bath refilled. I smell like lizard blood, and I need a fresh dress."
The doors slammed shut with a final clang, cutting off her footsteps and in the center of Arena Seven, Alexander remained standing motionless amidst the gore.
The two guards who had followed him down stood frozen near the wall, their eyes glued to the floor, terrified to even draw breath in the presence of the Crown Prince’s utter humiliation.
The arena lights buzzed, casting a harsh white glare over the dead beasts and the puddles of drying blood.
Alexander stared at the closed steel doors where his sister had vanished.
His chest felt strangely hollow.
A tight suffocating constriction clamped around his throat, thicker and heavier than any spiritual suppression field he had ever encountered on the battlefield.
’Fuck out of my life...’
The words echoed off the concrete walls of his mind, ringing with a finality that made his ribs ache.
Then, a sudden warm wetness tracked slowly down his left cheek.
DRIP!
A single solitary tear slipped from the corner of his eye, sliding down his pale jaw and falling into the open air.

It struck the concrete floor between his boots with a microscopic hiss and because of the boiling heat of his high-tier Purple Core, the droplet instantly flashed into a tiny wisp of white steam, vanishing into nothingness.
Alexander slowly raised his leather-gloved hand to his face with his fingers touching the damp trail beneath his eye.
He stared at the moisture on his leather glove as his breath hitched and his mind went completely blank.
The Crown Prince of the World swallowed hard, staring at the empty floor in the lightless basement.
’Why am I crying...?’
The damp chill of the parking concourse clung to the concrete like oil.
Aki stood on the raised curb three paces beyond the threshold of Arena Seven’s heavy security airlock.
The overhead sodium lamps hummed with a low drone, flickering every few seconds against the soot-stained exhaust flues.
"Haaaa... I want to go home..." Aki muttered. ’Or Blessed Land... I wouldn’t mind either way.’
She wanted to go to Blessed Land more though but Thor wasn’t going to be here for a while and there was no guarantee that Thor would agree to carry her a second time.
’Especially if she doesn’t want to...’
Aki could always bribe her with more food though.
Beneath the hem of her oversized charcoal traveling mantle, her hands hung relaxed at her sides.
Her left forearm knitted shut and purged of poison by Alexander’s lilac healing mana throbbed with a dull phantom heat, like an iron nail tapped lightly against marrow.
’Big Brother didn’t even heal me completely...’
She drew in a slow deep breath through her nose as the air down here tasted of diesel exhaust.
It was ugly yet, standing on the curb, watching the condensation bead along the yellow hazard lines of the concrete floor, an odd sensation bloomed behind her ribs.
’I told him to get out,’ she thought.
The realization sat in her chest like an unswallowed stone.

A small cold pang of guilt brushed against the base of her throat, cultivated across twenty-five years of being taught that an Unawakened scion’s entire purpose was to absorb the tempers of her superiors with downcast eyes and folded wrists.
Alexander was her elder brother, he held an active Purple Core and he commanded battalions across the Sovereign Realm.
In the grand architectural registry of the world, his blood was gold and hers was water.
...And she had looked him dead in his eyes and told him to fuck out of her life.
Her lips twitched as the pang of guilt flared, flickered, and was promptly smothered by an overwhelming surge of pure electric triumph.
’I did it.’
The heavy thud of combat boots broke her reverie.
Emerging from the security vestibule, Alexander strode into the harsh sodium light.
His matte-black greatcoat was buttoned to the chin, his posture rigid as a spear, but the easy suffocating arrogance that usually trailed his heels was absent.
He did not look at the armored retainers who fell into step behind him and he did not issue orders to the facility guards who stood bowed at ninety-degree angles along the wall.
He walked straight toward the idling limousine waiting in the VIP lane.
As he passed Aki, his pace hitched for a fraction of a second.
His blue eyes... the same shade as hers flicked toward her shoulder but he didn’t speak.
His jaw worked once with the teeth grinding behind pale lips, and his right hand curled into a fist so tight the reinforced leather of his glove creaked under the strain.
He tore his eyes away, ducked his head, and stepped into the rear compartment of the vehicle.
THUD!

The reinforced door slammed shut with a pressurized seal as the engine let out a low hum, and the limousine accelerated into the exit tunnel with its tires hissing against the slick pavement as its red taillights were swallowed by the gloom.
Aki watched the red glare fade, exhaling a thin cloud of mist into the chill.
SKRRRR!
A sleek silver-white luxury car glided smoothly around the eastern ramp, coming to a halt directly beside the curb where she stood.
The tinted rear passenger window slid down with a whisper of hydraulics, revealing the pale anxious face of her personal maid.
"Your Highness!" Mira gasped, her hands trembling as she unlocked the door. "Praise the heavens! Please, get in before the security drones flag the curb!"
Aki stepped down from the concrete ledge, ducked into the warm leather-scented cabin, and let the door pull itself shut with a muted click.
"Drive, Mira," Aki said softly, resting her head back against the plush synth-suede headrest. "Take the elevated bypass. I don’t want to sit in traffic at all."
"Right away, Highness!"
The car hummed to life, banking smoothly out of the underground complex and ascending the helix ramp toward the street level.
As they cleared the tunnel threshold and broke onto the high viaduct, the sky opened up.
Rain began to fall across Rhyx City... thick sheets of water that drummed relentlessly against the reinforced polycarbonate windshield.
Below the viaduct, the neon sprawl of the middle sectors smeared into blurry ribbons of electric cyan, harsh magenta, and rain-slicked asphalt.
Aki sat back, lifting her left hand to rest against the cool glass of the window.
She looked down at her fingers, curling them slowly into a fist.

’He thought I would cry,’ she mused, watching a rivulet of rainwater race across the exterior glass. ’He thought the smell of blood would make me vomit... Big Brother probably thought I’d curl into a ball on the floor and beg him to save me so he could hold the arranged marriage over my head like a leash.’
A soft, genuine laugh slipped from her throat.
It was quiet at first, barely a breath against the hum of the engine, but it grew into a bright clear chuckle that made Mira glance nervously into the rearview mirror.
"Highness?" Mira ventured cautiously, her knuckles white on the steering wheel. "Are... are you well? The Crown Prince looked... terrifying when he passed through the lower security checkpoint."
"I am better than well, Mira," Aki murmured, her azure eyes dancing with dark amusement. "I have never been more awake in my life."
She was beginning to act like Brida a bit but Aki didn’t hate it, she wanted to be half as confident as that woman.
The town car carved through the downpour, ascending the sweeping spirals of the upper tier where the rain-scrubbed glass towers of the high nobility pierced the lower clouds.
Within twenty minutes, the vehicle pulled into the private garage of her residential tower as the hydraulic security gates clanged shut behind them, sealing out the noise of the metropolis.
The elevator ride to the penthouse was silent.
The moment the private foyer doors parted, four senior security maids rushed forward with warm towels, silk wraps, and silver trays laden with restorative tonics.
"Highness! The bath has been drawn with crushed white lotus and eucalyptus!"
"We have prepared the evening tea—"
"Your gown is ruined, Highness, allow us to take the mantle—"
"Leave the towels," Aki commanded, stepping past them without breaking stride. "All of you, out of the bedchamber."
"B-But Highness—"
"Out," She repeated coldly.
The maids froze, exchanging wide-eyed terrified glances, before bowing deeply and retreating through the foyer double doors.
Left alone in the quiet expanse of her suite, Aki walked straight to the vanity room.

She stripped off the blood-spattered charcoal traveling cloak, unhooked the ruined, bile-stained wool tunic, and tossed them into the incinerator chute without a second thought then she kicked off her scuffed silk slippers, leaving them where they fell on the white marble floor.
"Finally... Some alone time..." Aki muttered, she never realized how much she would miss it.

She reached into her wardrobe, pulling out an oversized, soft charcoal-gray cotton shirt... a garment that reached past her mid-thighs, comfortable, loose, and completely lacking any sort of crests or stiff bone stays.
She pulled it over her head, shaking her long blue hair free so it tumbled in damp wild waves over her shoulders and then she caught her reflection in the full-length mirror.
Her collarbones were bare, save for the whisper-thin chain of dark star-iron resting against her skin.
The five uncut mana diamonds caught the recessed lighting, shimmering with azure, violet, and amber hues.
’I wonder can I draw mana from them...?’
Well she really didn’t know the first thing about Mana Gathering though.
She walked to the adjoining sitting room and tapped the intercom on the mahogany desk.
"Mira... Bring the terminal."
Five seconds later, the side door clicked open. Mira slipped in quietly, carrying a sleek slate-black encrypted financial tablet with her head respectfully bowed.
"Set it on the desk and take a seat," Aki instructed, walking over and leaning against the heavy wood.
Mira set the tablet down, perching nervously on the edge of the leather chair.
"Highness... if this is regarding the quarterly household audit—"

"It isn’t," Aki cut in, tapping the screen with her thumb to unlock the biometric password. "Log into the third offshore shell account... the one registered under the maritime trading dummy firm in the southern free ports."
Mira blinked, her brow furrowing in confusion. "The private trust? Highness, that ledger is only utilized for emergency capital reserves. The interest yield alone—"
"Open it," Aki said, her voice leaving no room for argument. "We are executing a transfer."
"A... a transfer?" Mira’s fingers flew across the interface, entering the twenty-four-digit encryption cipher.
The screen flashed emerald green, displaying a balance that stretched across nine digits. "How much are we allocating, Your Highness?"
"Twenty million Spirit Credits."
Mira’s hands froze over the screen.
Her jaw slowly dropped, her eyes bulging as she stared at the royal scion.
"T-Twenty million?! Highness! That is equivalent to the annual operating budget of a Level 30 Lord legion! Who could possibly require an offshore liquidity transfer of that scale?!"
"A debt," Aki replied smoothly, crossing her arms over her chest. "Room, board, and security fees."
’And worth every single cent,’ she added silently, remembering the roasted meat, the warm laughter around the fire, and the sight of Thor batting her playfully across the shoulders.
Mira swallowed hard, her chest heaving as she pulled up the transfer.
"I... understand. Please dictate the recipient’s institutional routing code and account registry."
Aki recited the twelve-digit alphanumeric string effortlessly.
She had repeated it in her head like a prayer every hour since stepping out of the Keep’s gates.
Mira typed the characters into the prompt.
The financial network of the central banking system processed the request with the progress bar sweeping across the interface.
BEEP!
A secondary window popped up on the high-resolution display, presenting the verified clearinghouse node and the registered legal identity attached to the recipient’s ledger.
"The routing is verified through the Valoria Bank," Mira said, squinting at the screen as she tilted the tablet slightly with her eyes widening as she read the owner’s name aloud.
"Registered recipient... Silas Graves."
The room fell quiet, save for the rain drumming against the balcony glass.
Aki stood still.
’Silas Graves.’
The name washed over her mind like cool spring water.

sentences.text: Alexander blinked, caught off guard.
"What?"
"The bet," she repeated, her voice sounding steady.
"Five beasts.
I survived all five without asking for the barrier and you swore upon your honor as Crown Prince that you would grant me one personal favor...
Anything within your authority."
Alexander’s expression hardened, his lip curling into a haughty dismissive sneer.
"Fine.
A deal is a deal.
What do you want?
A private estate in the southern provinces?
A larger budget allocation for your wardrobe?
A personal escort detachment so you don’t embarrass the family again?"
Aki took half a step closer.
She looked him dead in the eyes, her voice ringing clear and loud across the empty blood-stained arena.
"My wish... is for you to fuck out of my life."
Alexander froze.
His blue eyes snapped wide, his breath catching in his throat as if he had been struck across the sternum with an iron hammer.

In all their twenty-five years, through every reprimand, every scolding, and every quiet evening in the imperial palace, he had never heard her raise her voice, let alone speak a single syllable of profanity.
"What did you just say to me...?" Alexander whispered, his voice trembling.
"You heard me," Aki said, her expression sounding deadpan with her chin held high.
"I don’t want your money...
I don’t want your guards...
And I really, truly do not want to see your face for the foreseeable future.
Leave my suite.
Leave my staff alone and don’t ever darken my doorway again."
Without waiting for him to reply, without checking to see his reaction, and without offering the customary courtly bow, Aki turned on her heel.
She walked straight past the dead monsters toward the staging exit, her boots clicking against the concrete floor.
As she crossed the threshold into the equipment bay, she reached beneath her shredded cloak, pulling her private comm device from her pocket and dialing with a flick of her thumb.
"Mira," Aki spoke into the receiver, her tone becoming calm as the airlock doors began to close behind her.
"Have the transport ready at the lower bay and have the bath refilled.
I smell like lizard blood, and I need a fresh dress."
The doors slammed shut with a final clang, cutting off her footsteps and in the center of Arena Seven, Alexander remained standing motionless amidst the gore.
The two guards who had followed him down stood frozen near the wall, their eyes glued to the floor, terrified to even draw breath in the presence of the Crown Prince’s utter humiliation.
The arena lights buzzed, casting a harsh white glare over the dead beasts and the puddles of drying blood.
Alexander stared at the closed steel doors where his sister had vanished.
His chest felt strangely hollow.
A tight suffocating constriction clamped around his throat, thicker and heavier than any spiritual suppression field he had ever encountered on the battlefield.
’Fuck out of my life...’
The words echoed off the concrete walls of his mind, ringing with a finality that made his ribs ache.
Then, a sudden warm wetness tracked slowly down his left cheek.
DRIP!
A single solitary tear slipped from the corner of his eye, sliding down his pale jaw and falling into the open air.

It struck the concrete floor between his boots with a microscopic hiss and because of the boiling heat of his high-tier Purple Core, the droplet instantly flashed into a tiny wisp of white steam, vanishing into nothingness.
Alexander slowly raised his leather-gloved hand to his face with his fingers touching the damp trail beneath his eye.
He stared at the moisture on his leather glove as his breath hitched and his mind went completely blank.
The Crown Prince of the World swallowed hard, staring at the empty floor in the lightless basement.
’Why am I crying...?’
The damp chill of the parking concourse clung to the concrete like oil.
Aki stood on the raised curb three paces beyond the threshold of Arena Seven’s heavy security airlock.
The overhead sodium lamps hummed with a low drone, flickering every few seconds against the soot-stained exhaust flues.
"Haaaa...
I want to go home..." Aki muttered. ’Or Blessed Land...
I wouldn’t mind either way.’
She wanted to go to Blessed Land more though but Thor wasn’t going to be here for a while and there was no guarantee that Thor would agree to carry her a second time.
’Especially if she doesn’t want to...’
Aki could always bribe her with more food though.
Beneath the hem of her oversized charcoal traveling mantle, her hands hung relaxed at her sides.
Her left forearm knitted shut and purged of poison by Alexander’s lilac healing mana throbbed with a dull phantom heat, like an iron nail tapped lightly against marrow.
’Big Brother didn’t even heal me completely...’
She drew in a slow deep breath through her nose as the air down here tasted of diesel exhaust.
It was ugly yet, standing on the curb, watching the condensation bead along the yellow hazard lines of the concrete floor, an odd sensation bloomed behind her ribs.
’I told him to get out,’ she thought.
The realization sat in her chest like an unswallowed stone.

A small cold pang of guilt brushed against the base of her throat, cultivated across twenty-five years of being taught that an Unawakened scion’s entire purpose was to absorb the tempers of her superiors with downcast eyes and folded wrists.
Alexander was her elder brother, he held an active Purple Core and he commanded battalions across the Sovereign Realm.
In the grand architectural registry of the world, his blood was gold and hers was water.
...And she had looked him dead in his eyes and told him to fuck out of her life.
Her lips twitched as the pang of guilt flared, flickered, and was promptly smothered by an overwhelming surge of pure electric triumph.
’I did it.’
The heavy thud of combat boots broke her reverie.
Emerging from the security vestibule, Alexander strode into the harsh sodium light.
His matte-black greatcoat was buttoned to the chin, his posture rigid as a spear, but the easy suffocating arrogance that usually trailed his heels was absent.
He did not look at the armored retainers who fell into step behind him and he did not issue orders to the facility guards who stood bowed at ninety-degree angles along the wall.
He walked straight toward the idling limousine waiting in the VIP lane.
As he passed Aki, his pace hitched for a fraction of a second.
His blue eyes... the same shade as hers flicked toward her shoulder but he didn’t speak.
His jaw worked once with the teeth grinding behind pale lips, and his right hand curled into a fist so tight the reinforced leather of his glove creaked under the strain.
He tore his eyes away, ducked his head, and stepped into the rear compartment of the vehicle.
THUD!

The reinforced door slammed shut with a pressurized seal as the engine let out a low hum, and the limousine accelerated into the exit tunnel with its tires hissing against the slick pavement as its red taillights were swallowed by the gloom.
Aki watched the red glare fade, exhaling a thin cloud of mist into the chill.
SKRRRR!
A sleek silver-white luxury car glided smoothly around the eastern ramp, coming to a halt directly beside the curb where she stood.
The tinted rear passenger window slid down with a whisper of hydraulics, revealing the pale anxious face of her personal maid.
"Your Highness!" Mira gasped, her hands trembling as she unlocked the door.
"Praise the heavens!
Please, get in before the security drones flag the curb!"
Aki stepped down from the concrete ledge, ducked into the warm leather-scented cabin, and let the door pull itself shut with a muted click.
"Drive, Mira," Aki said softly, resting her head back against the plush synth-suede headrest.
"Take the elevated bypass.
I don’t want to sit in traffic at all."
"Right away, Highness!"
The car hummed to life, banking smoothly out of the underground complex and ascending the helix ramp toward the street level.
As they cleared the tunnel threshold and broke onto the high viaduct, the sky opened up.
Rain began to fall across Rhyx City... thick sheets of water that drummed relentlessly against the reinforced polycarbonate windshield.
Below the viaduct, the neon sprawl of the middle sectors smeared into blurry ribbons of electric cyan, harsh magenta, and rain-slicked asphalt.
Aki sat back, lifting her left hand to rest against the cool glass of the window.
She looked down at her fingers, curling them slowly into a fist.
’He thought I would cry,’ she mused, watching a rivulet of rainwater race across the exterior glass. ’He thought the smell of blood would make me vomit...
Big Brother probably thought I’d curl into a ball on the floor and beg him to save me so he could hold the arranged marriage over my head like a leash.’
A soft, genuine laugh slipped from her throat.
It was quiet at first, barely a breath against the hum of the engine, but it grew into a bright clear chuckle that made Mira glance nervously into the rearview mirror.
"Highness?" Mira ventured cautiously, her knuckles white on the steering wheel.
"Are... are you well?
The Crown Prince looked... terrifying when he passed through the lower security checkpoint."
"I am better than well, Mira," Aki murmured, her azure eyes dancing with dark amusement.
"I have never been more awake in my life."
She was beginning to act like Brida a bit but Aki didn’t hate it, she wanted to be half as confident as that woman.
The town car carved through the downpour, ascending the sweeping spirals of the upper tier where the rain-scrubbed glass towers of the high nobility pierced the lower clouds.
Within twenty minutes, the vehicle pulled into the private garage of her residential tower as the hydraulic security gates clanged shut behind them, sealing out the noise of the metropolis.
The elevator ride to the penthouse was silent.
The moment the private foyer doors parted, four senior security maids rushed forward with warm towels, silk wraps, and silver trays laden with restorative tonics.
"Highness!
The bath has been drawn with crushed white lotus and eucalyptus!"
"We have prepared the evening tea—"
"Your gown is ruined, Highness, allow us to take the mantle—"
"Leave the towels," Aki commanded, stepping past them without breaking stride.
"All of you, out of the bedchamber."
"B-But Highness—"
"Out," She repeated coldly.
The maids froze, exchanging wide-eyed terrified glances, before bowing deeply and retreating through the foyer double doors.
Left alone in the quiet expanse of her suite, Aki walked straight to the vanity room.

She stripped off the blood-spattered charcoal traveling cloak, unhooked the ruined, bile-stained wool tunic, and tossed them into the incinerator chute without a second thought then she kicked off her scuffed silk slippers, leaving them where they fell on the white marble floor.
"Finally...
Some alone time..." Aki muttered, she never realized how much she would miss it.

She reached into her wardrobe, pulling out an oversized, soft charcoal-gray cotton shirt... a garment that reached past her mid-thighs, comfortable, loose, and completely lacking any sort of crests or stiff bone stays.
She pulled it over her head, shaking her long blue hair free so it tumbled in damp wild waves over her shoulders and then she caught her reflection in the full-length mirror.
Her collarbones were bare, save for the whisper-thin chain of dark star-iron resting against her skin.
The five uncut mana diamonds caught the recessed lighting, shimmering with azure, violet, and amber hues.
’I wonder can I draw mana from them...?’
Well she really didn’t know the first thing about Mana Gathering though.

chapters.title: Chapter 527: At The World Council Summit [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: In Blessed Land, he was the Captain.
To Thor, he was the brat with the Gold Core and to the global streaming networks, he was a shadowy female phantom Lord named Vespera.
...But out here, under the unforgiving bureaucracy of the mortal plane, he was Silas Graves.
A sudden intense heat bloomed in Aki’s cheeks as she turned her face toward the dark windows with a soft helpless flush spreading all the way to the tips of her ears.
’Silas Graves, huh?’ she thought, her fingers subconsciously rising to trace the star-iron diamonds against her throat. ’Sounds... remarkably cute.’
"Highness?" Mira asked, looking up from the console.
The maid’s eyes widened slightly as she caught the unmistakable pink glow on the Princess’s porcelain face.

In eight years of service, she had seen suitors from everywhere... corporate heirs with personal war fleets, celebrated high-tier prodigies and so many more offer their names and titles to the First Princess and she had watched her mistress dismiss every single one of them with cold bored detachment.
They looked at her weirdly after that, why should she have a choice? She was an Unawakened after all...
Now, looking at a common name on a financial terminal, the First Princess of the World was blushing like a schoolgirl behind her sleeves.

"Execute the transfer, Mira," Aki said quickly, clearing her throat to reassemble her dignity. "And ensure the transaction log is scrubbed from the local cache... If my brother’s auditors attempt to trace the outbound flow, I want them chasing ghost servers or whatever."
"Right away, Highness," Mira replied, though a small knowing smile tugged at the corner of her mouth as her fingers confirmed the order.
’It seems my Princess has fallen in love...’
PING!
[Transaction Complete. 20,000,000 Spirit Credits Dispatched.]
Aki looked back out into the rain.
Somewhere across the world, in the city where he stayed or deep in the dark valleys of the Umbral Basin, Silas’s phone was chiming.
’We are even on the ledger, Lord Silas,’ she thought, her lips curving into a soft smile. ’Which means the next time I cross your gate... it won’t be on business.’
[A Few Days Later — Valoria City]
The morning light broke over the spires of Valoria City in a sharp blinding haze of pale amber and cold silver.
It was a noisy restless dawn.
The sky above the metropolis was crisscrossed with high-altitude security corridors, marked by the pulsing neon beacons of anti-air battery platforms.
Armored transport skiffs bearing the heraldry of planetary embassies cut through the smog, escorting dignitaries toward the central orbital lifts.
Today was not an ordinary date on the civic calendar.
Today was the convening of the World Council Summit... the single most publicized diplomatic assembly of the decade!
The sitting presidents and heads of all nine surviving global territories were converging upon the neutral perimeter to negotiate the shifting geopolitical boundaries of the post-calamity era.
In the upper residential wing of the Whitmore estate, the silence was a bit weird.
Penelope Whitmore yawned, a small sleepy sound that ruffled her dark purple bangs.
"Haahh..."
She pushed the heavy silk duvet off her legs, rubbing her eyes with the cuffs of an oversized pastel nightshirt.
She padded barefoot across the plush carpet to the floor-to-ceiling bay window overlooking the southern manicured gardens.
Below, private security detachments clad in the silver-and-amethyst armor of House Whitmore patrolled the perimeter walls with heavy mana-rifles with their hounds sniffing the iron railings.
Valoria was humming like a disturbed hive.
’Nine countries...’ Penelope mused, leaning her forehead against the cool glass.
Her history tutors had made her memorize the maps until her eyes bled.
Decades ago, before the first dimensional fractures ripped through the earth’s crust and the Sovereign Realm spilled its horrors onto mortal soil, the world had been different.

There were dozens of nations, sprawling continents with names that only existed in antique atlases now but when the sky tore open, entire landmasses had sunk beneath boiling seas or shattered into monster trenches.
If not for the Supreme Royal Family constructing the colossal Suppression Engines to stabilize the tectonic shifts, human civilization would have been snuffed out entirely.
Today, only Nine worldly powers remained.

’The United Hegemony of Shogya, the Sun-Crown of Khemet, the Albion Concordat, the Republic of Columbia, the Tsardom of Borealis, the Continental Directorate of Europa, the Federal Union of Amazonia, the Indus Sovereignty, and the Dominion of Australis.’
Penelope stretched her arms over her head with her purple pigtails flopping against her shoulder blades.
"Big Sister?" she called out, stepping through the doorway of her bedroom into the long, vaulted corridor.
Her bare feet made no sound against the polished parquet floor.
The morning was unusually quiet.
Usually, by this hour, the mansion was filled with the rhythmic clatter of training blades from the courtyard or the dry continuous murmur of Harper reviewing something or watching TV.
"Harper?"
Penelope descended the sweeping marble staircase into the grand entrance foyer and near the heavy, iron-reinforced double doors of the estate, a figure stood motionless.
Harper Whitmore stood in her travel clothes.
She wore a tailored charcoal overcoat cut close to her athletic frame, high combat boots laced with silver thread, and a dark leather travel bag resting beside her heel.

Her signature purple hair was tied back in a severe functional braid, and her wire-rimmed glasses rested high on the bridge of her nose as she had her gloved right hand pressed flat against the dark oak of the door but she wasn’t moving.
She was just standing there, staring at the grain of the wood.

"Big Sister!" Penelope smiled, jogging across the foyer flagstones with her pigtails bouncing. "Where are you going so early? The Summit feeds are starting in an hour! I told the kitchen staff to make the berry pastries you like—"
Harper didn’t turn around.
The silence that followed was suffocating, it was like the dead unnatural vacuum of a frozen lake.
Penelope skidded to a halt four paces back, her slippers catching on the rug as her smile slowly faltered.
"Harper...?"
Very slowly, Harper’s head tilted to the side.
Her shoulders were rigid, her posture locked in an unnatural alignment that looked alien to the graceful stance she usually held.
"I have a business meeting," Harper said and the voice made Penelope’s stomach lurch.
It was Harper’s voice... it carried the sweetness of House Whitmore’s head yet it was stripped of all inflection.
It was flat and monotone.
It sounded like words being read aloud by someone who had never heard human speech before, each syllable dropping like lead buckshot into the quiet foyer.

"A... a flight?" Penelope whispered, her brow furrowing in deep instinctual unease. "If you had a flight out of Valoria today, why didn’t you tell me last night? The entire city’s airspace is locked down for the Summit escorts! Nobody can get clearance unless—"
"It is urgent," Harper cut in as she gripped the brass handle of the front door, pulling it open.
A gust of cold morning wind whipped into the foyer, carrying the scent of rain.
It was really going to rain today.
Penelope took a step forward, her hand reaching out instinctively.
"Harper, wait! Who are you meeting? Where are you going?!"
Harper paused at the threshold.
She did not turn her torso, she merely rotated her neck over her shoulder, looking back at her younger sister.
"I am going to Khemet," Harper said.
Her voice dropped, carrying a chill that seemed to vibrate against the floorboards. "Do not speak of this further."
Penelope froze mid-stride with her breath seizing violently in her throat.
Behind the clear glass of Harper’s wire-rimmed spectacles, her eyes were wide. Her deep purple irises... the proud mark of the Whitmore lineage were not glowing with their usual electric violet mana.
Deep within the pupils, swimming beneath the surface like drowned serpents, was a hypnotic emerald-green light.
The temperature in the foyer seemed to plummet to absolute zero as the hair on Penelope’s arms stood on end and an overwhelming wave of pure terror paralyzing her limbs.
She couldn’t breathe and she couldn’t swallow. Every survival instinct hardwired into her mortal DNA screamed at her to drop to the floor and play dead.
Harper’s mouth curled into a twitch that resembled a smile then snapped back to stillness.
SLAM!
The heavy oak door slammed shut and the brass lock engaged with a deafening click that broke the trance.
Penelope dropped to her knees on the cold flagstones, clutching her ribs as air rushed violently back into her lungs.
She was trembling so hard her teeth clattered together with cold sweat drenching the collar of her nightshirt.
’That wasn’t her,’ Penelope thought, tears of pure terror welling in her eyes as she stared at the closed door. ’Her voice... her eyes... that wasn’t Big Sister.’
Penelope scrambled to her feet, stumbling across the foyer rug, her hands shaking violently as she bolted toward the grand staircase.
’She’s gone... She’s going to Khemet, and she isn’t in control.’
She reached her bedroom, throwing the door open and diving across the floor toward the nightstand where her phone lay.
Her fingers were slick with sweat, slipping twice across the glass screen before she managed to enter the password.
’Who can I go to...? Call the police...?’
Would they believe her or worse yet, would they be able to stop her? They would need protocols.
There was only one person she knew who didn’t care about noble protocols.
’Someone who can beat Sis too...’
Penelope dialed Lia’s number.
’Silas... Lia’s big brother... please pick up!’
[The World Council Summit — The Citadel of the Outer Threshold]
The Summit was not held within the borders of any of the nine nations.

It took place on the Citadel of the Outer Threshold... a massive artificial island-fortress constructed fifty leagues off the western continental shelf, anchored directly over the primary convergence nexus of the planetary Suppression Engines.
The sky above the island was a sterile featureless grey, scrubbed clean of clouds by high-tier atmospheric stabilizers.
Four concentric rings of automated naval battle-platforms patrolled the black oceanic swells below, while squadrons of military skiffs carved precise patrol grids through the restricted airspace.

No commercial vessels were permitted within a hundred miles as only craft bearing the verified diplomatic transponders of the World Council or the heads of state were granted descent vectors through the kinetic barrier domes.
At the center of the island rose the Grand Assembly Spire... a brutalist monolith of white titanium and black granite that soared three hundred yards into the heavens.

A sleek black-and-gold imperial limousine bearing the twin-headed eagle crest of the Supreme Royal Family glided across the elevated causeway, coming to a halt before the monumental marble staircase leading to the grand entrance.
The rear door opened, and Aki stepped out.
She wore a ceremonial gown of deep midnight-blue velvet, trimmed along the hem and collar with understated silver thread.
The high rigid collar framed her neck with imperial dignity, while the star-iron necklace rested securely beneath the fabric, invisible to the scanning arrays of the perimeter guards.
Her royal-blue hair was styled in an immaculate low chignon secured by twin silver pins, and her silk fan was tucked neatly into the sash at her waist.
Flanking her side was Mira, carrying an official diplomatic portfolio with her posture straight and her eyes forward.
Aki looked up at the colossal titanium pillars of the entrance.
’The highest point of authority on the planet,’ she thought, feeling the low-frequency hum of the massive Suppression Engines vibrating through the soles of her shoes.
The World Council operated in the shadow of the Supreme Royal Family.

While the King and Prince held sovereignty through their stewardship of the Engines, the Council itself managed the daily administration, trade routes, and military resource allocations of the nine surviving territories.

Its membership was an exclusive terrifying circle... mostly composed of ancient Lords who had lived over a century, their lifespans stretched by high-tier cores, supplemented by the matriarchs and magistrates of the highest noble clans, such as House Bloom.
Aki ascended the marble steps, her boots clicking in a steady rhythm.
"Halt."

Four World Council Enforcers... towering men encased from neck to toe in ivory-white kinetic power-armor, carrying heavy disruption polearms stepped forward, their visors glowing with pale amber scanning beams.
The leading enforcer scanned the biometric cipher on Aki’s wrist.
BEEP!
[Clearance Verified: First Princess of the World.]
The enforcers retracted their polearms, stepping aside with crisp precision.

"Welcome, Your Highness," the guard intoned through his vocal synthesizer. "The main assembly chamber remains restricted until the arrival of the Sovereign Heads... You are directed to the Grand Rotunda Lounge on Tier Three!"
"Understood," Aki replied and she swept past them into the grand foyer.
The interior of the Citadel was an overwhelming monument to concentrated wealth and power.
Vaulted ceilings thirty paces overhead were inlaid with massive mosaics of compressed mana-crystals, casting a brilliant warm luminescence across acres of polished white marble.
Statues of the ancestral Lords who forged the early border pacts lined the wide corridors, their stone eyes staring down at the arriving delegates.
Aki took the private anti-gravity lift to the third tier, emerging into the Grand Rotunda Lounge.
The room was vast, an open-concept room lined with velvet couches, floating crystal bars, and panoramic floor-to-ceiling viewports overlooking the stormy black ocean below.
The lounge was already populated.
