[A Few Days Later — Valoria City]
The morning light broke over the spires of Valoria City in a sharp blinding haze of pale amber and cold silver.
It was a noisy restless dawn.
The sky above the metropolis was crisscrossed with high-altitude security corridors, marked by the pulsing neon beacons of anti-air battery platforms.
Armored transport skiffs bearing the heraldry of planetary embassies cut through the smog, escorting dignitaries toward the central orbital lifts.
Today was not an ordinary date on the civic calendar.
Today was the convening of the World Council Summit... the single most publicized diplomatic assembly of the decade!
The sitting presidents and heads of all nine surviving global territories were converging upon the neutral perimeter to negotiate the shifting geopolitical boundaries of the post-calamity era.
In the upper residential wing of the Whitmore estate, the silence was a bit weird.
Penelope Whitmore yawned, a small sleepy sound that ruffled her dark purple bangs.
"Haahh..."
She pushed the heavy silk duvet off her legs, rubbing her eyes with the cuffs of an oversized pastel nightshirt.
She padded barefoot across the plush carpet to the floor-to-ceiling bay window overlooking the southern manicured gardens.
Below, private security detachments clad in the silver-and-amethyst armor of House Whitmore patrolled the perimeter walls with heavy mana-rifles with their hounds sniffing the iron railings.
Valoria was humming like a disturbed hive.
’Nine countries...’ Penelope mused, leaning her forehead against the cool glass.
Her history tutors had made her memorize the maps until her eyes bled.
Decades ago, before the first dimensional fractures ripped through the earth’s crust and the Sovereign Realm spilled its horrors onto mortal soil, the world had been different.

There were dozens of nations, sprawling continents with names that only existed in antique atlases now but when the sky tore open, entire landmasses had sunk beneath boiling seas or shattered into monster trenches.
If not for the Supreme Royal Family constructing the colossal Suppression Engines to stabilize the tectonic shifts, human civilization would have been snuffed out entirely.
Today, only Nine worldly powers remained.

’The United Hegemony of Shogya, the Sun-Crown of Khemet, the Albion Concordat, the Republic of Columbia, the Tsardom of Borealis, the Continental Directorate of Europa, the Federal Union of Amazonia, the Indus Sovereignty, and the Dominion of Australis.’
Penelope stretched her arms over her head with her purple pigtails flopping against her shoulder blades.
"Big Sister?" she called out, stepping through the doorway of her bedroom into the long, vaulted corridor.
Her bare feet made no sound against the polished parquet floor.
The morning was unusually quiet.
Usually, by this hour, the mansion was filled with the rhythmic clatter of training blades from the courtyard or the dry continuous murmur of Harper reviewing something or watching TV.
"Harper?"
Penelope descended the sweeping marble staircase into the grand entrance foyer and near the heavy, iron-reinforced double doors of the estate, a figure stood motionless.
Harper Whitmore stood in her travel clothes.
She wore a tailored charcoal overcoat cut close to her athletic frame, high combat boots laced with silver thread, and a dark leather travel bag resting beside her heel.

Her signature purple hair was tied back in a severe functional braid, and her wire-rimmed glasses rested high on the bridge of her nose as she had her gloved right hand pressed flat against the dark oak of the door but she wasn’t moving.
She was just standing there, staring at the grain of the wood.
"Big Sister!" Penelope smiled, jogging across the foyer flagstones with her pigtails bouncing.
"Where are you going so early?
The Summit feeds are starting in an hour!
I told the kitchen staff to make the berry pastries you like—"
Harper didn’t turn around.
The silence that followed was suffocating, it was like the dead unnatural vacuum of a frozen lake.
Penelope skidded to a halt four paces back, her slippers catching on the rug as her smile slowly faltered.
"Harper...?"
Very slowly, Harper’s head tilted to the side.
Her shoulders were rigid, her posture locked in an unnatural alignment that looked alien to the graceful stance she usually held.
"I have a business meeting," Harper said and the voice made Penelope’s stomach lurch.
It was Harper’s voice... it carried the sweetness of House Whitmore’s head yet it was stripped of all inflection.
It was flat and monotone.
It sounded like words being read aloud by someone who had never heard human speech before, each syllable dropping like lead buckshot into the quiet foyer.
"A... a flight?" Penelope whispered, her brow furrowing in deep instinctual unease.
"If you had a flight out of Valoria today, why didn’t you tell me last night?
The entire city’s airspace is locked down for the Summit escorts!
Nobody can get clearance unless—"
"It is urgent," Harper cut in as she gripped the brass handle of the front door, pulling it open.
A gust of cold morning wind whipped into the foyer, carrying the scent of rain.
It was really going to rain today.
Penelope took a step forward, her hand reaching out instinctively.
"Harper, wait!
Who are you meeting?
Where are you going?!"
Harper paused at the threshold.
She did not turn her torso, she merely rotated her neck over her shoulder, looking back at her younger sister.
"I am going to Khemet," Harper said.
Her voice dropped, carrying a chill that seemed to vibrate against the floorboards.
"Do not speak of this further."
Penelope froze mid-stride with her breath seizing violently in her throat.
Behind the clear glass of Harper’s wire-rimmed spectacles, her eyes were wide.
Her deep purple irises... the proud mark of the Whitmore lineage were not glowing with their usual electric violet mana.
Deep within the pupils, swimming beneath the surface like drowned serpents, was a hypnotic emerald-green light.
The temperature in the foyer seemed to plummet to absolute zero as the hair on Penelope’s arms stood on end and an overwhelming wave of pure terror paralyzing her limbs.
She couldn’t breathe and she couldn’t swallow.
Every survival instinct hardwired into her mortal DNA screamed at her to drop to the floor and play dead.
Harper’s mouth curled into a twitch that resembled a smile then snapped back to stillness.
SLAM!
The heavy oak door slammed shut and the brass lock engaged with a deafening click that broke the trance.
Penelope dropped to her knees on the cold flagstones, clutching her ribs as air rushed violently back into her lungs.
She was trembling so hard her teeth clattered together with cold sweat drenching the collar of her nightshirt.
’That wasn’t her,’ Penelope thought, tears of pure terror welling in her eyes as she stared at the closed door. ’Her voice... her eyes... that wasn’t Big Sister.’
Penelope scrambled to her feet, stumbling across the foyer rug, her hands shaking violently as she bolted toward the grand staircase.
’She’s gone...
She’s going to Khemet, and she isn’t in control.’
She reached her bedroom, throwing the door open and diving across the floor toward the nightstand where her phone lay.
Her fingers were slick with sweat, slipping twice across the glass screen before she managed to enter the password.
’Who can I go to...?
Call the police...?’
Would they believe her or worse yet, would they be able to stop her?
They would need protocols.
There was only one person she knew who didn’t care about noble protocols.
’Someone who can beat Sis too...’
Penelope dialed Lia’s number.
’Silas...
Lia’s big brother... please pick up!’
[The World Council Summit — The Citadel of the Outer Threshold]
The Summit was not held within the borders of any of the nine nations.

It took place on the Citadel of the Outer Threshold... a massive artificial island-fortress constructed fifty leagues off the western continental shelf, anchored directly over the primary convergence nexus of the planetary Suppression Engines.
The sky above the island was a sterile featureless grey, scrubbed clean of clouds by high-tier atmospheric stabilizers.
Four concentric rings of automated naval battle-platforms patrolled the black oceanic swells below, while squadrons of military skiffs carved precise patrol grids through the restricted airspace.

No commercial vessels were permitted within a hundred miles as only craft bearing the verified diplomatic transponders of the World Council or the heads of state were granted descent vectors through the kinetic barrier domes.
At the center of the island rose the Grand Assembly Spire... a brutalist monolith of white titanium and black granite that soared three hundred yards into the heavens.

A sleek black-and-gold imperial limousine bearing the twin-headed eagle crest of the Supreme Royal Family glided across the elevated causeway, coming to a halt before the monumental marble staircase leading to the grand entrance.
The rear door opened, and Aki stepped out.
She wore a ceremonial gown of deep midnight-blue velvet, trimmed along the hem and collar with understated silver thread.
The high rigid collar framed her neck with imperial dignity, while the star-iron necklace rested securely beneath the fabric, invisible to the scanning arrays of the perimeter guards.
Her royal-blue hair was styled in an immaculate low chignon secured by twin silver pins, and her silk fan was tucked neatly into the sash at her waist.
Flanking her side was Mira, carrying an official diplomatic portfolio with her posture straight and her eyes forward.
Aki looked up at the colossal titanium pillars of the entrance.
’The highest point of authority on the planet,’ she thought, feeling the low-frequency hum of the massive Suppression Engines vibrating through the soles of her shoes.
The World Council operated in the shadow of the Supreme Royal Family.

While the King and Prince held sovereignty through their stewardship of the Engines, the Council itself managed the daily administration, trade routes, and military resource allocations of the nine surviving territories.

Its membership was an exclusive terrifying circle... mostly composed of ancient Lords who had lived over a century, their lifespans stretched by high-tier cores, supplemented by the matriarchs and magistrates of the highest noble clans, such as House Bloom.
Aki ascended the marble steps, her boots clicking in a steady rhythm.
"Halt."

Four World Council Enforcers... towering men encased from neck to toe in ivory-white kinetic power-armor, carrying heavy disruption polearms stepped forward, their visors glowing with pale amber scanning beams.
The leading enforcer scanned the biometric cipher on Aki’s wrist.
BEEP!
[Clearance Verified: First Princess of the World.]
The enforcers retracted their polearms, stepping aside with crisp precision.
"Welcome, Your Highness," the guard intoned through his vocal synthesizer.
"The main assembly chamber remains restricted until the arrival of the Sovereign Heads...
You are directed to the Grand Rotunda Lounge on Tier Three!"
"Understood," Aki replied and she swept past them into the grand foyer.
The interior of the Citadel was an overwhelming monument to concentrated wealth and power.
Vaulted ceilings thirty paces overhead were inlaid with massive mosaics of compressed mana-crystals, casting a brilliant warm luminescence across acres of polished white marble.
Statues of the ancestral Lords who forged the early border pacts lined the wide corridors, their stone eyes staring down at the arriving delegates.
Aki took the private anti-gravity lift to the third tier, emerging into the Grand Rotunda Lounge.
The room was vast, an open-concept room lined with velvet couches, floating crystal bars, and panoramic floor-to-ceiling viewports overlooking the stormy black ocean below.
The lounge was already populated.

chapters.title: Chapter 528: At The World Council Summit [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Scattered throughout the hall were the scions, heirs, and high-ranking retainers of the global elite.
Young men and women clad in military dress uniforms, silk robes from the Shogunate Isles, and heavy jewel-encrusted tunics from the Indus Sovereignty mingled in quiet murmuring clusters.
High-tier mana signatures hummed through the air... mostly Blue Cores, with the occasional flare of a high-ranking core whose presence commanded immediate space.
Aki walked toward the central refreshment terrace with her movements calm and graceful.
She didn’t look at the whispering groups...
’It’s useless to think about it.’
She knew what they were saying, it was impossible not to ever since she had heard the murmurs at every state banquet since she turned sixteen.
’The useless one.’
’Look at her... not a drop of mana in her veins.’
’Why does the King even bring her? The Crown Prince commands fleets, and she’s just decorative glass.’
Aki approached the polished obsidian bar, resting one gloved hand on the counter. "Chilled mineral water, please."
"Allow me, Your Highness."
A smooth oily voice cut in from her right and Aki turned her head slightly.

Standing beside her was a young man in his early twenties, possessing sharp noble features, slicked-back chestnut hair, and an expensive tailored three-piece suit cut from void-silk that shimmered with blue defensive enchantments.
A heavy gold signet ring bearing the soaring falcon crest of the Republic of Columbia rested on his pinky finger.
He lifted two crystal flutes of pale golden champagne from the bar, offering one toward her with a dazzling smile.

"Julian Vanderbilt," he introduced himself, his eyes lingering with unhidden assessment over the curves of her velvet gown. "Son of President Vanderbilt of the Republic of Columbia... It is a rare honor to find the celebrated First Princess standing unaccompanied in such an austere hall."
Aki did not reach for the glass.
Her azure eyes met his with flat unblinking calm. "I requested water, Mr. Vanderbilt and I am quite content with my own company."
Julian didn’t lower the glass.
His smile remained fixed, though the corners of his eyes tightened with the slight irritating arrogance common to corporate scions who were never told ’no.’

"A simple drink between allies, Princess," Julian murmured, taking a half-step closer, his shoulder subtly crowding her space against the bar counter. "Surely the royal family allows for polite conversation with the delegation that funds forty percent of the northern perimeter’s defensive ammunition?"
"I have no interest in your conversation, Mr. Vanderbilt," Aki said, her voice dropping a bit sounding cold. "Step back."
Julian let out a quiet scoffing chuckle through his nose. He set the champagne glasses down onto the marble counter with a sharp clack, turning his full torso to face her.
The warmth in his expression died, replaced by that familiar condescending sneer she had seen on her brother’s face a thousand times.

"You have quite the temper for an Unawakened woman, Princess," Julian said, his voice dropping into a low murmur that barely carried beyond the counter. "You carry yourself as if that title still holds weight but let’s be realistic about what you are in this room... You don’t have a Lord Core... You can’t circulate a single volt of mana. If the engines on this island failed right now, the environmental pressure would snap your delicate spine like a dry twig."
He leaned in with his breath smelling of mint and expensive brandy.

"A woman of your... status... has only one true value to the high courts and we all know it, even you... your ancestral bloodline. A convenient vessel to produce an heir for someone who actually wields power so you should be using this summit to secure a patron who can protect your budget when your father finally decides to discard—"
"Hey. You."
A sharp feminine voice cut through the air behind them.
It wasn’t loud, but it carried a strange crackling heat that made the hair on the back of Julian’s neck instantly stand on end.
Julian frowned, turning his head over his shoulder with an irritated scowl.
"Who the hell is—"
SWOOSH!
A blur of fiery flowing crimson hair cut through the lounge’s warm light like a streak of burning phosphorus.

Before Julian Vanderbilt could even register the motion, before the defensive enchantments on his void-silk suit could cycle their barriers, a slender leather-clad foot materialized in the center of his vision.
CRACK-THWACK!

The kick was executed with terrifying violence in a rising straight-line snap that drove the steel-reinforced toe of a combat boot directly and without a microsecond of hesitation straight into the fork of Julian Vanderbilt’s groin.
KRA-SNAP!
The sound that echoed through the Grand Rotunda was sickening... it was a wet muffled crunch of compressed flesh and fracturing pelvic cartilage.
Julian’s eyes instantly bulged until the whites were completely bloodshot.
The breath was violently expelled from his lungs in a sharp, wheezing shriek that sounded like a stepped-on bagpipe.
"GYAAAAAAAH—!"
The force of the kick lifted the son of the Columbian President four inches off the polished marble floor.

He collapsed sideways, violently slamming his forehead against the edge of the obsidian bar with a hollow thump, before spilling onto the white floor tiles in a twitching fetal heap, clutching his crotch with both hands as his mouth opened and a string of bloody saliva pooled on the marble.
The surrounding delegates went dead silent as laughter died mid-throat, crystal flutes froze half-raised and the low murmur of political negotiations collapsed into stunned horror.
Standing over the crumpled body of the corporate heir was a young woman who looked like an active wildfire given human shape.
Her hair was a brilliant cascading mane of liquid crimson that fell in jagged radiant waves past her shoulder blades.
Her porcelain skin contrasted sharply with eyes of pure burning ruby red that flashed with visible atmospheric heat.

She was dressed in a sleek high-collared combat tunic of deep ash-gray, cinched with weapon belts holding twin curved hunting daggers with her posture exuding the effortless feeling of an apex hunter.
Seraphina Bloom pulled her boot back, letting the leather heel tap lightly against the stone with a crisp clack.
She looked down at the writhing man with an expression of pure disgust.

"Men like you are a blight on the species," Seraphina spat, her voice ringing clear through the dead silence of the lounge. "Every time you open your greasy mouths, you make the rest of the world look like an abattoir."
She let out a long irritated sigh, rolling her ruby eyes toward the high ceiling mosaics.

"Ugh. It’s because of pathetic entitled insects like this that my mother treats every male in our household like a piece of upholstery... You strut around with your father’s title, flapping your gums about ’bloodlines’ and ’useful vessels,’ and you can’t even take a basic physical strike without crying on the floor."
Seraphina raised her right boot, casually planting the sole directly onto the back of Julian’s head, grinding his cheek into the marble floor with steady merciless pressure.
CRUNCH!
"N-Ngh... stop... my father... is the Pres—" Julian choked out, his fingers clawing uselessly at her leather greave.

"I don’t give a damn if your father is the Emperor of the Sun," Seraphina said coldly, pressing her heel down harder until his nose cartilage audibly clicked. "You’re soft and you’re brittle... My prospective consort, or rather my Fiancee, wouldn’t behave like this."
Why couldn’t everyone be like Silas? Well except her Dad...
She paused, a reflective hum escaping her throat as she tapped her boot rhythmically against the side of Julian’s skull.
TAP! TAP!
"Hell," Seraphina muttered, almost to herself, "Silas wouldn’t even flinch from a direct kick to the groin... You take one tap to the jewels and you’re lying in your own spit, This is disgusting."
Aki stood by the bar with her azure eyes wide and her silk fan frozen in her hands.
’Silas...?’
Her heart gave a violent sudden leap behind her ribs.
Before Seraphina could drive her heel through Julian’s jaw, a broad iron-plated gauntlet reached out from the crowd, gently catching the crimson-haired girl by the shoulder of her tunic.
"Alright, Sera, that’s enough," a relaxed, easygoing voice chuckled from behind her. "You’re going to crack the floor tiles, and the Council charges double for architectural repairs..."
Seraphina clicked her tongue, though she relented, pulling her boot off the groaning man’s head and crossing her arms over her chest with an annoyed pout.
"He deserved worse, Val. He was breathing too loud."
Stepping out from behind the crimson-haired prodigy was a tall strikingly handsome young man with unruly sun-bleached blonde hair and sharp hazel eyes.
He was clad in a full suit of brilliant gold mythril plate armor... the signature war-gear of House Sterling.

The armor was polished to an immaculate mirror sheen, though several microscopic dents and hairline scorch marks along the left pauldron betrayed that the metal had seen real brutal dungeon crawls rather than ceremonial parades.
He wore no helmet, instead a heavy iron-and-gold gauntlet was resting casually on his hip as he looked down at the whimpering Columbian heir with an amused shake of his head.
Valerius Sterling crouched down on one knee beside the twitching man, offering an open gauntleted hand with an easy boyish smile.
"Rough landing, buddy," Valerius said, his tone remarkably friendly and conversational. "Here, let me give you a hand up before the security enforcers come over to file an incident report..."
Julian Vanderbilt, his face covered in sweat and bloody saliva, looked up at the golden-armored heir of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate with desperate tear-filled relief.
"T-Thank you, Sterling..." Julian wheezed, his trembling fingers reaching out to grasp the gold gauntlet. "That crazy bitch... she broke my—"
The moment Julian’s fingers closed around the metal palm, Valerius’s smile didn’t fade.
Instead, Valerius pivoted his hips, loaded his weight onto his back knee, and drove his heavy iron-plated combat boot straight up between Julian’s thighs with the concussive force of a battering ram.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOM!
"HUUUUUURRRRRRRRGH?!"
A sound that didn’t belong to any known human language tore from Julian’s throat.
His entire body arched like a drawn bow, his feet flying up into the air as the second kick struck the exact same pulverized nerve cluster.
His eyes rolled back into his skull, showing only the whites, and he collapsed limp onto the floor, blissfully unconscious with a thin line of white foam bubbling from his lips.
THUD!
Valerius rose smoothly to his full height, dusting off the knee of his gold mythril greave with a satisfied nod.
He looked around at the petrified frozen crowd of high-born delegates, clearing his throat in a pleasant tone.

"A brief educational PSA for the honored guests of the Republic," Valerius announced cheerfully, resting both hands on his hips. "When addressing a lady... specifically, the First Princess of the World, one generally bows, offers a polite greeting, and steps three paces back so you aren’t breathing your cheap cologne into her face. That’s basic etiquette, gentlemen. Take notes..."
He turned back toward Seraphina, letting out a long sigh as he adjusted his pauldron.

"Though, you’re right, Sera," Valerius remarked, sighing a bit. "Silas definitely wouldn’t be doing any of this... He would probably avoid the trouble or something though, he’s not the kind of person that’ll be a hero."
Aki stood entirely frozen against the obsidian counter.
Once was an anomaly or perhaps a coincidence of common names.
Twice... spoken by the favored prodigy of House Bloom and the direct heir of the Sterling Conglomerate, both referencing personal combat habits and temperaments meant...
’They know him,’ the realization slammed into Aki’s mind like a physical blow. ’They know Silas Graves!’
Aki took a slow deliberate step away from the bar.
Her azure eyes locked onto the tall, blonde noble standing in the golden armor as she lowered her silk fan, her composure slipping for the barest fraction of a second as her voice tumbled out.
"You know... Silas?"
Valerius Sterling paused.
He turned his head, his hazel eyes blinking once, twice, in mild surprise as he took in the royal maiden standing before him.

He looked at her royal-blue hair, the delicate imperial features, and then... for a brief bizarre second, his gaze flicked down toward the collar of her velvet gown and caught the faintest glimpse of the star-iron chain resting beneath the silk.
A proud grin stretched across Valerius’s handsome face as he puffed his chest out in his gleaming gold armor, resting an iron thumb against his breastplate.
"Know him?" Valerius chuckled boisterously, winking at the stunned Princess. "Your Highness... Silas Graves is my... best... friend."

Before Seraphina could drive her heel through Julian’s jaw, a broad iron-plated gauntlet reached out from the crowd, gently catching the crimson-haired girl by the shoulder of her tunic.
"Alright, Sera, that’s enough," a relaxed, easygoing voice chuckled from behind her.
"You’re going to crack the floor tiles, and the Council charges double for architectural repairs..."
Seraphina clicked her tongue, though she relented, pulling her boot off the groaning man’s head and crossing her arms over her chest with an annoyed pout.
"He deserved worse, Val.
He was breathing too loud."
Stepping out from behind the crimson-haired prodigy was a tall strikingly handsome young man with unruly sun-bleached blonde hair and sharp hazel eyes.
He was clad in a full suit of brilliant gold mythril plate armor... the signature war-gear of House Sterling.

The armor was polished to an immaculate mirror sheen, though several microscopic dents and hairline scorch marks along the left pauldron betrayed that the metal had seen real brutal dungeon crawls rather than ceremonial parades.
He wore no helmet, instead a heavy iron-and-gold gauntlet was resting casually on his hip as he looked down at the whimpering Columbian heir with an amused shake of his head.
Valerius Sterling crouched down on one knee beside the twitching man, offering an open gauntleted hand with an easy boyish smile.
"Rough landing, buddy," Valerius said, his tone remarkably friendly and conversational.
"Here, let me give you a hand up before the security enforcers come over to file an incident report..."
Julian Vanderbilt, his face covered in sweat and bloody saliva, looked up at the golden-armored heir of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate with desperate tear-filled relief.
"T-Thank you, Sterling..." Julian wheezed, his trembling fingers reaching out to grasp the gold gauntlet.
"That crazy bitch... she broke my—"
The moment Julian’s fingers closed around the metal palm, Valerius’s smile didn’t fade.
Instead, Valerius pivoted his hips, loaded his weight onto his back knee, and drove his heavy iron-plated combat boot straight up between Julian’s thighs with the concussive force of a battering ram.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOM!
"HUUUUUURRRRRRRRGH?!"
A sound that didn’t belong to any known human language tore from Julian’s throat.
His entire body arched like a drawn bow, his feet flying up into the air as the second kick struck the exact same pulverized nerve cluster.
His eyes rolled back into his skull, showing only the whites, and he collapsed limp onto the floor, blissfully unconscious with a thin line of white foam bubbling from his lips.
THUD!
Valerius rose smoothly to his full height, dusting off the knee of his gold mythril greave with a satisfied nod.
He looked around at the petrified frozen crowd of high-born delegates, clearing his throat in a pleasant tone.
"A brief educational PSA for the honored guests of the Republic," Valerius announced cheerfully, resting both hands on his hips.

"When addressing a lady... specifically, the First Princess of the World, one generally bows, offers a polite greeting, and steps three paces back so you aren’t breathing your cheap cologne into her face.
That’s basic etiquette, gentlemen.
Take notes..."
He turned back toward Seraphina, letting out a long sigh as he adjusted his pauldron.
"Though, you’re right, Sera," Valerius remarked, sighing a bit.
"Silas definitely wouldn’t be doing any of this...
He would probably avoid the trouble or something though, he’s not the kind of person that’ll be a hero."
Aki stood entirely frozen against the obsidian counter.
Once was an anomaly or perhaps a coincidence of common names.
Twice... spoken by the favored prodigy of House Bloom and the direct heir of the Sterling Conglomerate, both referencing personal combat habits and temperaments meant...
’They know him,’ the realization slammed into Aki’s mind like a physical blow. ’They know Silas Graves!’
Aki took a slow deliberate step away from the bar.
Her azure eyes locked onto the tall, blonde noble standing in the golden armor as she lowered her silk fan, her composure slipping for the barest fraction of a second as her voice tumbled out.
"You know...
Silas?"
Valerius Sterling paused.
He turned his head, his hazel eyes blinking once, twice, in mild surprise as he took in the royal maiden standing before him.

He looked at her royal-blue hair, the delicate imperial features, and then... for a brief bizarre second, his gaze flicked down toward the collar of her velvet gown and caught the faintest glimpse of the star-iron chain resting beneath the silk.
A proud grin stretched across Valerius’s handsome face as he puffed his chest out in his gleaming gold armor, resting an iron thumb against his breastplate.
"Know him?" Valerius chuckled boisterously, winking at the stunned Princess.
"Your Highness...
Silas Graves is my... best... friend."

chapters.title: Chapter 529: At The World Council Summit [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The gilded marble of the Grand Rotunda felt small.
Aki’s throat constricted with a dry swallow catching behind her tongue.
She stood pinned beneath the glare of the vaulted crystal chandeliers with her silk fan gripped so tightly against her ribs that the polished jade ribs groaned.
’So Silas has a friend in the human world?’
The thought ricocheted through her skull.
’Ah... I really didn’t expect it...’
Hearing his name tossed around in the perfumed air of an imperial summit lounge by the heir of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate felt like watching a mountain being forced into a jewelry box.
It was weird.
Valerius Sterling leaned forward in his mirror-sheened gold armor, hazel eyes crinkling with genuine boyish curiosity.
The broad grin never left his lips as he tapped an iron gauntlet against his hip.
"Wait a second, Princess," Valerius asked, tilting his head. "Do you actually know Silas? Is that why you’re asking about him?"
Aki parted her lips to deny it.
The denial was already on the tip of her tongue since she had to protect his anonymity.
The entire world thought Blessed Land was commanded by a warlord named Vespera, and Silas had explicitly warned her about spreading his identity.
’I keep my promise—’
Then, the floorboards beneath her slippers hummed.
FWOOSH!
Aki’s chest locked.
The blood in her veins seemed to run backwards feeling icy and thin, while a bead of cold sweat broke along the nape of her neck and tracked down her spine.
The air in the Grand Rotunda which was climate controlled and perfumed with synthetic jasmine spiked thirty degrees in the span of a single heartbeat.
She was an Unawakened so she could not perceive the spiritual frequencies of a Lord Core, nor could she see the invisible circuits of mana circulating through human meridians.
But when a presence was so overwhelmingly dense that it physically altered the laws of physics around it, even ordinary mortal flesh screamed in terror.
The oxygen grew thin, scorching her nostrils with every shallow breath as the moisture on her lips evaporated, and the fine velvet of her midnight-blue gown grew uncomfortably hot against her skin.
Beside Valerius, Seraphina Bloom had not moved an inch yet the red-haired prodigy seemed to expand, her silhouette warping the air like a heat shimmer rising from an asphalt highway at noon.
Her ruby eyes were narrowed into razor-thin slits, glowing with a molten fury that burned through the room’s ambient light.

Her small manicured teeth were clenched so hard the jaw muscles rippled beneath her porcelain skin, and her right hand hung open near the curved grip of her hunting dagger, her fingers twitching with microscopic murderous intent.
The marble beneath Seraphina’s combat boots began to dry-bake with faint spiderweb fissures crackling outward from her heels.
"Do you know Silas?" Seraphina repeated.
The words were not loud, but they carried the crushing pressurized hiss of a furnace door swinging wide open.
Valerius’s smile instantly evaporated.
He let out a long sigh, rolling his eyes toward the vaulted ceiling as he took half a step back, raising his iron gauntlets in placating surrender.
"Oh, sweet Mother of Iron, here we go again," Valerius muttered under his breath, shaking his blonde head. "Sera, please. Don’t melt the carpet. We can’t afford it..."
Seraphina ignored him as if he was not there.
Her burning red gaze remained pinned to Aki’s face, searching every twitch of her eyelashes and every hitch of her throat.
’So she doesn’t care whether I’m the Princess of the World?’

Aki’s royal training... years of surviving inquisitorial scrutiny and smiling through venomous court banquets kicked into gear as she swallowed the suffocating dry heat in her mouth, snapped her silk fan open with a sharp sound, and offered a faintly embarrassed courtly laugh behind the painted silk.

"Good heavens, no," Aki said smoothly, letting a touch of noble bewilderment soften her azure eyes. "I was referring to Sir Silas of the Northern Border Lancers... For a moment, I feared the rumors of his dishonorable discharge had reached the social registries but I assure you, Lady Bloom, I have never had the pleasure of crossing paths with this... ’Silas Graves’ you speak of."
The silence in the lounge held for two excruciating seconds then Seraphina blinked.
WHOOSH!
The scorching pressurized heat vanished and the temperature plummeted back to its crisp base so fast that the condensed moisture in the air hissed against the bar counter.

The molten ruby glow in Seraphina’s eyes faded, softening into a clear vibrant crimson, and the terrifying predator who had just pulverized a man’s pelvis transformed back into an elegant albeit slightly tense high-born maiden.
Seraphina drew in a slow breath through her nose, adjusting the high leather collar of her ash-gray tunic.
She looked genuinely sheepish with a small rosy tint touching the apples of her pale cheeks.
"Oh," Seraphina murmured, her shoulders dropping an inch. "I... see. Well. That is quite alright, then."
She cleared her throat, crossing her arms defensively beneath her chest, though her tone remained slightly prickly as she looked away.

"I apologize for the display, Your Highness. I... got ahead of myself. It’s just that... if that idiot was skulking around behind my back, entertaining imperial royalty in private suites without informing me first, I would have had to travel across two sectors just to break his ribs... I don’t appreciate people touching what belongs to House Bloom."
Aki lowered her fan an inch, her curiosity overriding her caution.
"What belongs to House Bloom? If I may ask... what precisely is your relationship with this Silas Graves?"
Seraphina lifted her chin with her red hair catching the chandelier light like liquid copper as a proud shameless smirk curled her lips.
"He is my prospective consort," Seraphina announced without a shred of hesitation. "And my soon-to-be fiancé... The formal paperwork is just yet to be signed."
THUMP!
Aki’s heart gave an involuntary violent lurch against her ribs as blood rushed to her ears and a sudden bizarre ringing drowned out the soft classical music drifting from the lounge speakers.
’Consort...? Fiancé?!’
The words felt like a direct physical slap.
’Silas Graves... getting married to a high-born noble from House Bloom?!’
Aki’s mind spun into frantic irrational turmoil.
Silas, tied to this sharp-tongued, red-haired hellion who kicked corporate heirs in the groin for breathing too loud?
Silas, submitting to the suffocating diplomatic etiquette of the Bloom clan?!
Yet, even as the panic flared, Aki’s sharp diplomatic instincts took over.
She kept her face a flawless mask of courtly poise, tilting her head with a gracious radiant smile.

"Is that so?" Aki said, her voice smooth as warmed honey. "Then allow me to offer my early congratulations, Lady Bloom... From the manner in which you and Lord Sterling speak of him, this Silas Graves sounds like a man of extraordinary character and formidable steel."
Seraphina beamed, the arrogant pride puffing out her chest once more.
"He is. An utter brute in combat, hopelessly stubborn, and completely lacking in basic courtly refinement... but he has fine steel in his marrow. Thank you, Princess and your blessing is noted."
Aki smiled back, though beneath the silk of her fan, her jaw clenched tight.

’Prospective consort,’ Aki analyzed ruthlessly, dissecting the exact syllables Seraphina had chosen. ’"Prospective." "Soon-to-be." "Yet to be signed" Which means Silas hasn’t signed a single damn piece of paper!’
A quiet triumphant breath slipped through Aki’s lips.
Seraphina’s mother, Etilga Bloom, was notorious across the continental networks for running her household like a private penal colony.
If Silas was the man Aki knew... there was not a chance in the nine hells he would ever let House Bloom collar him as a pet consort.

’If anyone in the human world has a claim to his side,’ Aki thought, her fingers subconsciously rising to brush against the star-iron chain beneath her collar. ’it isn’t a girl who threatens to break his ribs. It’s me... He gave me a name... so it’s only right if I stay with him.’
The memory sent a warm defiant pulse fluttering through her belly, washing away the sting of Seraphina’s declaration.
"Security! Clear the corridor! Make way!"
Heavy hurried boots thudded against the marble as four World Council enforcers in ivory-white armor hurried toward the bar, their disruption batons humming with low-voltage suppression fields.

They skidded to a halt, taking in the scene which was the son of the Columbian President lying face-down in a pool of his own spit, bloody tooth fragments scattered across the floor, while the First Princess of the World, the daughter of Magistrate Bloom, and the heir of House Sterling stood chatting by the counter like old friends at a garden party.
The leading guard leader turned pale beneath his visor with his hands hovering nervously near his utility belt.
"Your Highness!" the guard leader stammered, bowing frantically toward Aki. "W-We detected a mana discharge! What occurred here? Was there a terrorist breach?! Did someone assault you?!"
Aki closed her fan with a soft decisive snap, turning her azure gaze upon the enforcers with the chilling untouchable majesty of the Supreme Royal Family.

"Assault?" Aki asked, raising a delicate brow in mild regal disdain. "Nothing of the sort, Officer. Mr. Vanderbilt simply suffered an unfortunate episode... He approached me to offer a greeting, became terribly light-headed from the altitude stabilizers, and took a rather severe tumble against the counter. Lord Sterling and Lady Bloom were kind enough to catch him before he injured his skull further."
Valerius nodded sagely, resting his gauntleted hand over his heart with an expression of pure saintly innocence.
"A tragic accident, truly. The man’s balance is utterly atrocious. You really should look into recalibrating the gravitational sub-plates on this tier, Captain."

The guard leader stared from Valerius’s pristine gold armor down to Julian Vanderbilt’s crushed groin, where the distinct indentation of an iron combat boot was still clearly visible in the torn fabric of his trousers.
The guard swallowed hard.
To question the word of the First Princess was treason and to accuse the direct daughter of Magistrate Bloom was career suicide.
Then to file a battery report against House Sterling meant their legal teams would drown his precinct in litigation until his grandchildren retired.
"I... I understand, Your Highness!" the guard barked, sweat beading on his upper lip. "Medical unit! Transport Mr. Vanderbilt to the trauma wing immediately! Quietly! Through the service hoist!"

Two guards hoisted the limp, groaning form of the corporate heir onto a grav-stretcher, rushing him out of the lounge as a cleaning servitor rolled forward, spraying neutralizing foam over the blood and polishing the marble back to a blinding sheen.
Aki turned back to the bartender, who was still trembling behind the glassware.
"My chilled mineral water, please and prepare two of your finest vintage reserves for my companions."
"R-Right away, Highness!"
Aki exhaled softly, feeling the tension bleed out of the room as she tapped the star-iron necklace beneath her velvet dress.
Over the past three days, during her private hours in the penthouse, she had discovered an extraordinary property within the raw mana diamonds Silas had tempered.
The stones did not merely shield her against external pressure waves.
If she focused her intent and pressed her thumb against the central diamond, she could consciously draw out the purified mana stored within the crystalline structure!

By channeling the heat directly through her forearms and legs, she could artificially reinforce her physical muscle fibers, accelerating her movement speed and striking power by nearly three hundred percent.
The drawback was brutal though... because she possessed no natural mana circuits, her mortal capillaries and muscles took the full brunt of the friction.

Using it for more than four seconds left her limbs bruised and aching for hours but in that split second when Julian had crowded her space, before Seraphina had intervened, Aki’s fingers had been resting on the diamond, ready to drive an accelerated palm strike through the man’s windpipe.
She smiled a bit.
’I had it covered. But having a fire-breathing prodigy kick him was certainly more entertaining.’
She picked up her tall crystal glass of iced water, gesturing gracefully toward the expansive lounge.
"Lord Sterling, Lady Bloom... would you care to join me at the terrace table? Standing by the bar seems terribly prone to... environmental hazards."

chapters.title: Chapter 530: At The World Council Summit [IV / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "I would be honored, Princess," Valerius grinned, eagerly scooping up a crystal tumbler of aged amber liquor. "Anywhere that puts me further away from my father’s corporate retainers is a paradise."
Seraphina accepted a flute of dark red sparkling wine, offering a polite nod. "Lead the way, Your Highness."
The three of them moved across the Grand Rotunda, the surrounding crowd of young nobles and military aides hastily parting like the sea before them.
They took their seats at a secluded semicircular lounge near the panoramic viewports.
Below the thick quartz glass, the black stormy ocean of the outer threshold churned violently with white-capped waves crashing against the reinforced titanium pilings of the Citadel’s foundation.

Out across the dark water, a massive armored diplomatic cruiser bearing the soaring eagle insignia of the Republic of Columbia was slowly docking at the primary lower slipway, its searchlights cutting through the sea spray.
Aki took a slow sip of her mineral water, letting the cold liquid settle her nerves as she glanced at the chronological display floating above the terrace entrance.
"The heads of state are running remarkably late," Aki remarked, setting her glass onto the coaster. "The opening bell was scheduled for nine hundred hours... It is nearly a quarter past."
Seraphina swirled the red wine in her glass, her sharp ruby eyes watching the Columbian cruiser’s mooring lines secure.
"Are they stalling on purpose? A collective diplomatic posturing tactic? My father always says that if you make the World Council wait ten minutes, you control the first half of the agenda."
Aki offered a soft knowing shake of her head.

"Not this time, Lady Bloom. The logistics of this summit are a nightmare. Because of the spatial distortion caused by the Sovereign Realm, cross-continental transport between the Nine Major Powers requires navigating through heavily fortified corridor gates. If there is a minor storm in the Shogunate ocean trenches, or an atmospheric mana-shear above the Amazonian basin, an entire delegation’s fleet can be delayed by hours... They will arrive shortly though, the security grid wouldn’t remain on high alert otherwise."
Aki tilted her head, her clear azure eyes studying the two young nobles sitting across from her.
"Tell me... is this the first time either of you has attended a full convening of the World Council Summit?"
Valerius took a generous gulp of his liquor, grimacing slightly at the burn before resting his armored elbow on the back of the sofa.

"First time for both of us," Valerius admitted, running a hand through his messy blonde locks. "Usually, my old man keeps me locked away in the corporate vaults or dumps me into Secret Realms to dig up ancient relics... He says high-society summits are ’wasted on my unrefined temperament.’ The only reason I’m here today is because the Sterling Conglomerate is co-signing the security infrastructure budget for the new northern perimeter, and he wanted to show off his heir in full mythril plate like a prized stallion."
Seraphina sighed, resting her chin in her palm as she stared down at the dark water.

"My mother dragged me along for similar reasons. House Bloom is presenting a formal motion to annex three coastal mining sectors in the southern gulf and she wanted her favored daughter standing behind her chair so the other delegates remember that our family commands enough raw firepower to incinerate their ports if they vote against us."
Aki smiled, though a melancholic shadow crossed her features as she looked down at the delicate bubbles rising in her glass.

"Then allow me to offer you both a piece of seasoned advice," Aki said softly, her voice carrying the tired wisdom of someone who had spent years observing the wolves of the high court. "Do not let the grandeur of this chamber fool you... The World Council Summit is not a venue for treaties or peace. It is a slaughterhouse cloaked in velvet."
Valerius raised a brow, while Seraphina’s eyes sharpened.

"Your houses are external invited clans," Aki explained, her tone measured and deliberate. "You sit in the middle tier... wealthy, powerful, but ultimately viewed as tools by the ancient Council heads and the Presidents. If a dispute erupts between the Republic of Columbia and the United Hegemony today, they will not clash directly as they will target the assets of the independent houses to test each other’s leverage. Keep your hands off your weapons. Do not respond to verbal provocations and whatever you do... do not look directly into the eyes of the King when he takes the dais."
Seraphina frowned, her pride bristling slightly.
"And what of insects like that man? Am I supposed to let men like that talk down to imperial scions without breaking their teeth?"
Aki let out a self-deprecating chuckle.

"I am grateful for your intervention, Lady Bloom. Truly. But..." Aki looked away, her gaze drifting out across the stormy sea. "...I have endured remarks like his for nearly a decade. In the eyes of the high court, an Unawakened Princess is merely an ornamental vessel, an asset to be traded away when the political ledger demands it so you get used to the poison after a while. You learn to smile, let the words wash over you, and remember that their opinions carry only as much weight as you grant them."
Valerius’s jaw tightened.
The easygoing boyish humor drained from his face, replaced by a quiet coldness.
’She sounds exactly like my mother...’
Well before she cheated on his father and abandoned them.
Beside him, Seraphina’s fingers drummed restlessly against her glass, her ruby eyes smoldering with renewed irritation.
"That’s garbage, Princess," Valerius said bluntly, his voice surprisingly firm. "You’re the First Princess of the World so you shouldn’t have to ’get used’ to being talked to like common scrap."

"It is simply the reality of our hierarchy, Lord Sterling," Aki replied softly, offering them a bittersweet gentle smile. "Should Mr. Vanderbilt’s father attempt to raise a formal grievance regarding his son’s... unfortunate fall... I will use my authority to ensure neither House Sterling nor House Bloom faces diplomatic censure."
She rose from the sofa, smoothing down the heavy velvet of her midnight-blue gown.
She left her half-finished glass on the marble table, looking down at them with an expression that was remarkably calm, yet carrying a heartbreaking trace of royal resignation.
"That is... assuming my authority persists until the closing bell."
Before Valerius could question her, the sharp metallic blare of a ceremonial horn echoed through the Grand Rotunda.
HONNNNNG... HONNNNNG!
The heavy titanium blast doors leading toward the central spire hissed open.
A squad of twelve World Council enforcers marched out, planting their halberds against the floor with a synchronized deafening sound.
CLANG!

"ATTENTION ALL DELEGATES AND HONORED GUESTS!" the herald’s voice boomed through the acoustics. "THE GOVERNING BODIES HAVE DOCKED! THE GREAT ASSEMBLY CHAMBER IS NOW OPEN FOR CONVENING! PROCEED TO YOUR DESIGNATED STATIONS!"
Aki offered Valerius and Seraphina a graceful flawless courtly bow.
"It seems our time is up. I wish you both fortune in the chamber so watch your backs."
"You too, Princess," Valerius said softly, rising to return the bow with solemn uncharacteristic formality.
Aki turned and walked toward the primary access corridor, her chin held high and her spine straight as an arrow.
The Great Assembly Chamber was an amphitheater of terrifying proportions.

Constructed entirely of seamless void-black obsidian and polished white titanium, the circular hall rose five tiers high, vaulted by an immense domed skylight of reinforced quartz that revealed the stormy gray heavens above.
At the center of the chamber sat the Grand Table... a ring-shaped slab of solid celestial marble, etched with glowing runic arrays that dampened magical output to prevent sudden magical skirmishes.
Surrounding the Grand Table were several massive high-backed thrones carved of dark star-iron, each bearing the illuminated seal of a power.

Behind the high table, ascending the sloping walls of the amphitheater, were rows of tiered stadium seating reserved for the scions, corporate advisors, and high military retainers of the attending nations.
Aki stepped through the private imperial archway, guided by two silent enforcers.
The chamber was already alive with suffocating high-tier pressure as sitting at the far northern arc of the high table were the World Council Heads.
They were terrifying legendary entities as there were seven of them in total...
Ancient Lords or perhaps their descendants who had survived the first part of the Apocalypse that plagued centuries ago with their physical aging halted by high-tier cultivation.

Five of them chose to maintain absolute anonymity, cloaked in heavy hooded robes of midnight-silk woven with anti-divination wards and their faces obscured by smooth featureless masks of polished white porcelain.
Their spiritual presences were vast and immovable, like glaciers resting beneath a frozen sea.
Only the Magistrates sat unmasked.
Among them was Magistrate Bloom... Seraphina’s father.
He was a severe middle-aged man with sharp features, his hair streaked with iron-gray and wearing formal dark robes embroidered with the burning crimson crest of House Bloom.
He sat with his hands folded over the pommel of an ancestral saber, his cold gaze sweeping across the arriving delegates like a hawk scanning a field of mice.
Aki’s gaze drifted past him, landing upon the seat reserved for the Supreme Royal Family.
Sitting there, rigid and immaculate in his formal black military dress uniform, was Crown Prince Alexander.
His medals gleamed in the harsh hall lights, but his face was an unreadable mask of cold stone.
As Aki walked past the lower tier toward her designated guest station near the main royal dais, Alexander’s eyes flickered toward her.
For a fraction of a second, their gazes met but Aki did not flinch.

Alexander’s throat hitched. His jaw clenched tight with a muscle twitching beneath his cheek as he violently averted his gaze, staring fixedly down at the blank holographic console before him, refusing to acknowledge her existence.
Aki took her seat, a quiet razor-sharp smile touched the corner of her lips.
’Still terrified of his own tears,’ she thought coolly. She never thought she would ever enjoy seeing her Brother so miserable...
The peripheral doors opened, and the secondary delegations began to file in.
The scions and heirs ascended to the mezzanine tiers.
Valerius Sterling and Seraphina Bloom took their positions directly behind the Bloom Magistrate’s station with Valerius’s golden armor catching the light like a miniature sun.
Aki observed the arriving children of the global elite. Among them, several radiated staggering power.
Walking among the Indus delegation was a young man who stood out with striking majesty.

He was tall, lithe, and broad-shouldered, completely shirtless despite the chill of the titanium hall, his dark rich brown skin etched from neck to wrists in intricate glowing crimson runic war-tattoos that pulsed with the rhythmic heat of an active volcano.
Atop his head, thick immaculate folds of saffron and gold silk were wrapped in a traditional warrior’s turban, held in place by a single, blood-red ruby brooch.
He walked barefoot, his golden-amber eyes sweeping across the amphitheater with lazy amusement while carrying a curved scimitar sheathed in beaten brass.

Beside the Shogunate delegation walked twin swordsmen clad in layered white silk haori, their twin katanas humming with synchronized wind mana, while the youth of Borealis were draped in the silver-furred pelts of Tier 4 frost-bears, their faces scarred from northern trial rites.
Then, the great bronze herald trumpets sounded three deafening blasts.
BRAAAAM! BRAAAAM! BRAAAAM!
"HERALDING THE ARRIVAL OF THE GOVERNING BODIES OF THE NINE MAJOR POWERS!"
The massive southern gates ground open, and the heads of state entered in full ceremonial procession, each accompanied by their chief ministers and honor guards.
The room held its breath as the rulers of humanity stepped onto the obsidian floor, each stepping forward to declare their presence before the Council.
First came the United Hegemony of Shogya, represented jointly by its dual monarchs.
King Zhao Xian of the Shogunate Isles strode forward, an elderly man with a long white beard, draped in imperial yellow silk embroidered with five-clawed dragons with his posture straight as a spear.

Beside him walked King Minamoto no Masashi of the Yamato Sector, his jet-black hair tied in a traditional high topknot, clad in lacquered black-and-gold samurai armor that rattled with the resonance of a hundred battlefield victories.
"The United Hegemony stands present," King Zhao intoned, his voice carrying the deep weight of the eastern dynasties.
Next came the Sun-Crown of Khemet.
Striding across the marble was Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur, a tall striking man with bronze skin, sharp aquiline features, and eyes of pure liquid gold.

He wore an immaculate modern white military suit accented by a heavy gold pectoral collar inlaid with lapis lazuli and carnelian, an ornate headdress of beaten gold framing his severe sun-darkened brow.
"Khemet honors the covenant," Menes declared, his voice echoing off the high dome.

From the west marched the Albion Concordat, led by Prime Minister Sir Arthur Pendelton, an austere silver-haired statesman in an impeccably tailored navy three-piece suit, leaning lightly on a cane topped with a polished star-iron orb, his cold blue eyes missing nothing.
"Albion is seated," Pendelton stated crisply.

Behind him walked the Republic of Columbia, represented by President Julian Vanderbilt Senior... a broad-chested ruthless corporate titan with iron-gray hair, wearing a charcoal pinstripe suit and his fingers adorned with heavy signet rings.
His face was thunderous and his jaw locked in fury... there was no doubt having just received word that his son was currently having his pelvis reconstructed in the trauma ward.
"Columbia acknowledges the assembly," Vanderbilt growled, taking his seat with aggressive finality.
From the frozen north came the Tsardom of Borealis, headed by Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov.

He was a colossal bear-like man standing nearly seven feet tall, his massive chest covered in medals and an enormous mantle of white dire-wolf fur draped over his broad shoulders while his heavy beard was frosted with residual ice-mana.
"Borealis answers the summons," Volkov rumbled, the floor vibrating beneath his heavy iron boots.

Next strode the Continental Directorate of Europa, led by Chancellor Henri de Montmirail, a sharp-featured bespectacled diplomat in minimalist gray robes, flanked by high-ranking guild arbiters carrying stacks of holographic treaty ledgers.
"Europa is in attendance," Montmirail nodded politely.
Then came the Federal Union of Amazonia.
A collective murmur rippled through the upper tiers as their leader crossed the floor.

She was High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva... the first female head of state in Amazonian history, a legendary Lord who had unified the fractured jungle territories through merciless military conquest.
She was a woman in her late forties with olive-tanned skin, sharp, feline dark eyes, and raven-black hair pulled into a high ponytail.
A jagged combat scar ran from her left ear down into the collar of her dark olive dress uniform, which was adorned with the polished fangs of primeval river leviathans.
She walked with the coiled grace of a black jaguar, radiating an aura of iron-fisted authority that made even the Tsardom guards tense their grips.
"Amazonia claims its seat," Da Silva announced, her husky, commanding voice cutting clean through the chamber’s whispers.

From the sacred river valleys came the Indus Sovereignty, led by Chief Minister Rajesh Varma, an imposing white-bearded patriarch in pristine ivory sherwani silk, a vibrant emerald brooch gleaming upon his chest, accompanied by four temple battle-mages whose eyes glowed with raw psionic mana.
"Indus preserves the peace," Varma spoke with serene poise.

Finally, the Dominion of Australis was heralded by Governor-General Malcolm Sterling-Cross, a weather-beaten frontier commander with a scarred jaw, wearing a dark khaki service dress adorned with the crimson insignia of the Southern Trench Fleet.
"Australis is present," Malcolm barked with blunt military efficiency.
The heads of state took their respective thrones around the Grand Table, their aides stepping back to form defensive perimeters then, the side doors opened once more.

chapters.title: Chapter 531: At The World Council Summit [V / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Stepping onto the floor with smooth noble grace were the two invited corporate titans with the first being Lohan Sterling, Patriarch of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate, clad in immaculate silver robes that shimmered with micro-enchantments, his cold calculating eyes immediately scanning the room and Etilga Bloom, the terrifying Matriarch of House Bloom, a breathtakingly beautiful woman in high-collared crimson silk whose mere presence caused the surrounding air to smell of scorched earth.
They approached the high table, offering deep polished bows toward the hooded World Council Heads.

"House Sterling extends its gratitude to the World Council for this gracious invitation," Lohan spoke smoothly, his voice carrying the oily confidence of a man who owned the debt of half the nations present.
"House Bloom honors the gathering of the realm," Etilga added, her tone cool and sounding unapologetic.
How could she...? When she knew the truth about some of those people under the hood...
They were directed to two wide high-backed chairs positioned at the secondary tier of the Grand Table, bridging the gap between the governing heads and the Council.
The hall began to settle yet, as Aki scanned the Grand Table, her breath caught in her throat.
There were three seats that remained entirely vacant.
At the very pinnacle of the table, elevated two steps above all others, was the Grand Imperial Throne... the seat of the King of the World.
And resting directly opposite the throne, positioned on the outer perimeter facing the gathered rulers of humanity, were two newly added chairs of dark walnut, upholstered in rich violet velvet.
Above them, hovering in crystalline light, were two holographic nameplates that made every diplomat in the room stare in quiet unsettled awe.
[LORD VESPERA — BLESSED LAND]
[LORD SKY — ALLIED LORD]
The two Lords who had the most successful broadcast that shattered every streaming record in human history and their seats were completely empty.
A suffocating tense silence gripped the Grand Assembly Chamber as delegates exchanged nervous wide-eyed glances.
’They haven’t arrived...?’ Aki thought, her heart hammering against her ribs. ’Silas and Evelyn... they’re late?!’
To arrive late to an imperial state assembly was an insult punishable by imprisonment but to arrive late to a World Council Summit...?
In the presence of the nine global heads of state, the ancient Council heads, and the Supreme Royal Family was an act of suicidal madness.
It was a declaration of disrespect!
Before the murmurs could erupt into open outrage, the air in the chamber died.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The temperature did not rise or fall and the lighting did not flicker but instead, the crushing concept of gravity seemed to multiply by ten thousand.

The massive quartz skylight overhead groaned beneath a sudden invisible atmospheric spike as the runic arrays along the Grand Table flared violently in blinding emerald panic, struggling to neutralize the incomprehensible ocean of power that flooded the room like a collapsing star.
In the stadium seating, several low-tier corporate aides and unawakened attendants collapsed forward against their desks with blood pouring from their noses as their lungs seized.
Even the high-tier Lords... men who commanded armies clutched the arms of their chairs with their faces turning pale as paper and their meridians groaning under the suffocating weight.
The private imperial doors swung open and walking through the threshold alone, was the King of the World.
He was a man who looked barely in his late forties with his physical aging halted at the pinnacle of human vitality.
He possessed shoulder-length, brilliant royal-blue hair that cascaded over his shoulders like liquid sapphire, framing a face of cold breathtaking majesty.

His beauty was on another level... He was not dressed in ceremonial armor or heavy gold mantles like one would think, the man wore a bespoke double-breasted suit of midnight-navy wool instead, unbuttoned at the collar and tailored to perfection over a broad imposing frame.
Beneath his dark brows, his eyes were deep oceanic blue.
"Haaa.... I can breathe..."
"Long Life The King..."
"The Pressure... It’s Gone?"
He was the Sovereign of Humanity and the master of the ancient machines that kept the planet from sliding into the abyss.

He strode across the obsidian floor with his steps making no sound against the stone, The King of the World did not look at the bowed heads of the nine presidents and he did not acknowledge the standing salutes of the World Council Enforcers either.
He ascended the two marble steps, turning his imposing frame to face the assembly, and sat upon the Grand Imperial Throne.

The suffocating pressure stabilized properly, settling over the chamber like an iron blanket that permitted speech, but demanded submission as the King rested his elbows on the star-iron armrests with his fingers loosely laced together over his lap.
"Be seated," the King commanded.
His voice was not loud yet it resonated directly inside the skull of every single living being in the room, carrying the deep vibration of tectonic plates shifting beneath the ocean.
The nine presidents, the Council Heads, and the noble patriarchs took their seats with hurried trembling care.

The King let his cold gaze sweep across the vast chamber, lingering for a fraction of a second on Alexander, passing smoothly over Aki without a flicker of emotion, before settling directly upon the two vacant violet-velvet chairs at the foot of the table.
His dark brows narrowed by an infinitesimal fraction of a millimeter.
"It appears," the King spoke. "that our newly anointed ’Hero of Humanity’ has chosen to exercise her prerogative of punctuality."
A collective terrified gulp rippled through the throats of all of the delegates as nobody breathed and nobody dared to offer an excuse either.
The brazen disrespect of leaving the King of the World waiting was an offense that usually ended in entire cities being stripped of their charter!
The King held the silence for three agonizing heartbeats then, his expression smoothed back into that unreadable calm.

"No matter," the King declared, unlacing his fingers. "We do not stall the fate of nine nations for rogue Lords. Before we open the floor to the territorial petitions regarding the northern rift... there is an imperial matter of succession that requires the formal witness of this Council."
He turned his piercing blue eyes toward the gathered delegates, his lips curving into an enigmatic smile that carried zero warmth.
"As the rumors circulating the global communications networks have so eagerly speculated... the Supreme Royal Family does not allow extraordinary talent to languish in obscurity."
The King raised his right hand.
CLAP! CLAP!
Two crisp echoing claps reverberated off the obsidian walls.
At the far eastern flank of the chamber, the massive gold-embossed double doors of the Imperial Inner Sanctum ground open with a deep hiss and a soft collective gasp tore through the mezzanine tiers.
Emerging from the shadow of the archway, stepping into the harsh white luminescence of the assembly floor, was a young woman.
She looked barely twenty-two years old, walking with an exquisite hypnotic grace that commanded every pair of eyes in the hall.
Her hair was a cascading radiant mane of vivid royal-blue... the unmistakable pure-blooded hue of the imperial lineage, identical to the hair of Crown Prince Alexander and Princess Aki.
Yet, as she stepped into the light and raised her porcelain face, the breath died in Aki’s throat.
Her eyes were not the oceanic blue of the royal line, they were pure radiant gold.

A blinding luminous amber-gold that pulsed with the unmistakable frequency of an active Purple Lord Core, she had a spiritual signature so dense and potent it set the air around her skirts shimmering with visible violet heat.

The woman herself was dressed in an immaculate imperial court gown of layered white and amethyst silk, cinched at her slender waist with an embroidered sash bearing the twin-headed imperial phoenix as she walked to the center of the obsidian floor, coming to a halt directly before the Grand Imperial Throne.
With slow breathtaking perfection, she swept her amethyst skirts to the side, sinking into a flawless unhurried courtly curtsy before the King and the gathered rulers of the earth.
She lifted her chin, her golden eyes flashing with a bit of authority as her melodic voice rang through the absolute silence of the Great Assembly Chamber.
"I greet the Sovereign King, the honored Council, and the Heads of the Nine Nations... I am Princess Kiera. The Second Princess of the World."
The air inside the Great Assembly Chamber quieted down in an instant.
Down in the center of the obsidian floor, Kiera held her curtsy for three unbroken seconds before rising back to her full height.
Her chin remained lifted at an exact level angle, which showed that she was not acting insolent but she didn’t cow in front of their might either.
Silence held the room by the throat.

Up in the mezzanine, packed across four ascending tiers behind reinforced brass rails, several hundred aides, diplomats, and junior guild analysts were staring down with their mouths half-open but nobody spoke.
The leaks on Y had been circulating for three solid weeks.
Most people in high-tier administrative circles had treated the entire thread as clickbait nonsense.

The platform was a toxic unmoderated swamp of manufactured court scandals, fabricated guild bounties, and fake territorial squabbles cooked up by commodity speculators to tilt the quarterly futures markets.
Anyone with half a brain knew how dangerous the site could be when it drifted too far into real bloodlines.

Five months ago, an anonymous ring of digital agitators out of the southern river basin had tried to run an illicit generative-rendering campaign targeting High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva... flooding regional feeds with high-resolution nude composite images of the Amazonian leader.
The operation hadn’t lasted twelve hours.

Da Silva hadn’t bothered with formal diplomatic inquiries, civil injunctions, or communications tribunals as she had requisitioned a river gunboat, ignored four regional flight corridors, and personally flattened the offshore server installation with seismic charges, executing every programmer involved behind the burning concrete pilings before the local fire boats even cleared their slips.

The global tech cartels had spent the following week aggressively stripping generative visual models out of civilian operating systems, terrified of having Amazonian void-gunners breach their penthouse boardrooms next.
Because of that bloodbath, almost nobody believed anonymous forum threads anymore.
Yet here she stood.
Right in the dead center of the most heavily fortified room on Earth, breathing the sterile air of the inner perimeter as she was living proof that the rumors on the board had been dead accurate.
And she wasn’t some frail hidden bastard tucked away in a country villa to rot... the pressure radiating from her chest was vibrant and fully awakened.
Down in the lower semi-circle, several diplomats from the Albion and Europa delegations glanced across the Grand Table toward Aki.
The looks were thick with pity as Aki saw them out of the corner of her eye.
She didn’t turn her head, but her ribs tightened until it hurt to breathe.
It was ugly.
Everyone in the chamber knew the basic arithmetic of the royal family... The First Princess was Unawakened.
She had lived twenty-five years with inert, empty veins, unable to ignite a single spark of mana, an ornamental bloodline asset with zero military value.
Now, without warning, an Awakened spare had stepped out of the fog, carrying pure imperial blood and a vibrant spiritual signature.
Aki was going to be replaced and sidelined too.

She was perhaps going to be stripped of whatever ceremonial budget she still drew from the royal household, relegated to some forgotten coastal manor, or married off to someone the moment her father needed to grease a treaty wheel.
Even with that execution hanging over her head, she was still technically the secondborn so she held higher legal power than ninety percent of the people sitting in the hall.
But the looks remained and Aki’s jaw tightened with her back teeth meeting behind closed lips.
The King broke the quiet.

He remained rested against the dark star-iron backrest of the Grand Imperial Throne with his bespoke double-breasted navy wool coat hanging open and his oceanic blue eyes looking flat though they showed a little bit of emotion.
"Kiera Zel Castellian," the King spoke.
The middle syllable dropped like an anvil onto stone.
...Zel.
A collective sharp hiss of air swept through the stadium tiers and Aki’s knuckles clicked beneath the heavy velvet of her midnight-blue gown.
Zel was the royal blood-seal.
It was the ancestral middle name granted solely to legitimate heirs of the Royal line who possessed combat awakening.

Alexander had it... Alexander Zel Castellian. It was stamped into the wax of every military deployment he authorized, announced by the heralds at the gates of every citadel, and etched onto the silver scabbard at his hip.
Aki didn’t have one.
When her sixteenth winter had passed without a core igniting behind her ribs, the imperial scribes had quietly omitted the syllable from her civic papers as she was simply The First Princess.
She was someone with no name.
From the edge of her peripheral vision, Aki saw two more junior aides from the Columbia delegation nudge each other, glancing her way with that sickening sympathetic tilt of their heads.
Aki let out a slow silent stream of air through her nose, keeping her eyes fixed on the horizontal seam of the titanium wall across the pit.

’Aki is cooler than Kiera anyway,’ she thought, the words firing through her mind with childish venom. ’It’s a garbage name... You can walk down any commercial boulevard in any city, shout the name Kiera, and half a dozen shop girls selling knockoff perfumes will turn around. How many girls in this world have the name Aki? Just one... and it’s me.’
