chapters.title: Chapter 532: At The World Council Summit [VI / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki knew it was cope.
She knew it was a pathetic embarrassing delusion, a thin paper-mache shield she was holding up to stop her chest from caving in on itself but she clung to it with everything she had.
Right now, in front of more than five hundred people, she couldn’t allow a single muscle in her cheek to twitch.
She was jealous... furious, bitter, and burning with a toxic envy that tasted like iron shavings under her tongue but she kept her face in a frozen expression.
If she lost her temper now, if she let even a sliver of that resentment show on her face, she would tumble deeper into her father’s bad side than she already was.
And sliding down into the King’s bad side was a quick way to stop existing.
The King continued with his deep voice carrying through the acoustics without a microphone, rattling the glass in the mezzanine lamps.
"When the Queen departed this world shortly after the First Princess drew her first breath..."

He let the sentence hang for two heavy suffocating seconds and there was a deliberate pause over the timeline... it was a quiet inflection that laid the late Queen’s death squarely on Aki’s shoulders.
Aki’s pulse thumped once, sounding hard and flat against her ears but she didn’t flinch.
She had heard that exact phrasing in the corridors since she was seven years old.
The Queen bled out because the child took her life and gave no mana in return.
The words were similar to an ancient blade, it had grown dull from overuse, but it still left a familiar cold ache behind her ribs.

"The grief was severe," the King said smoothly, his gaze drifting lazily toward the eastern arc of the Grand Table. "In my search for solace, I traveled east, deep into the sovereign territories of the United Hegemony. It was there, among the coastal valleys and ancient shrine peaks, that I met the most beautiful woman I have ever laid eyes upon... A daughter who carried the combined martial heritage of both the Yamatoan warrior clans and the ancient dynasties of the Shogunate Isles."
He lowered his chin slightly, letting the room absorb the weight of the confession.
"She was Kiera’s mother and it brings me sorrow to state that she succumbed to an incurable lung rot three years past but her lineage remains intact."
The King gestured toward the two eastern monarchs seated side-by-side at the Grand Table.

"The United Hegemony sheltered my daughter when the world was volatile," the King said. "The Crown does not leave debts unsettled so in the coming territorial allocations, the Hegemony’s trade corridors will receive a total exemption from imperial transit tariffs for the next twenty years, along with three Tier-5 deep-sea mining anchors transferred directly to their coastal fleet."
King Zhao Xian of the Shogunate Isles and King Minamoto no Masashi of the Yamato Sector exchanged a rapid imperceptible glance.
Then, both men rose smoothly from their star-iron chairs, bowing deeply from the waist.
"The United Hegemony bows before the grace of the Crown," King Zhao intoned, his long white beard brushing the collar of his imperial yellow robes. "We shall guard the eastern waters with our lives."
Beside him, Minamoto bowed with one hand resting flat against the black lacquer of his samurai cuirass with the plates clattering softly in the quiet.
Across the circle, the other seven rulers looked on with thinly veiled jealousy.
A twenty-year tariff exemption and three Tier-5 deep-sea anchors were absurd economic concessions!
It was the kind of leverage that could tilt regional maritime trade balances for half a century.

In their heads, both eastern monarchs were undoubtedly offering silent reverent prayers to the dead woman whose brief encounter with the King had just handed their nations an insurmountable geopolitical advantage.

Added benefits could mean a lot of things down the road... It could mean that once both of them had the requisite age and experience, their delegates might even be elevated to permanent seats on the World Council.
More benefits also meant that in every single negotiation that followed today, the Hegemony would hold the upper hand.
The King dismissed their bows with a lazy wave of his left hand, turning his sapphire eyes back down to the girl on the floor.
"Come forward, Kiera," he commanded gently. "It appears the staff failed to prepare an official seat for you at the Grand Table."
Kiera didn’t show a shred of anger as she took two light steps forward, sinking into another graceful low curtsy with her voice ringing clear and melodious through the hall.

"There is no need to trouble the servants, Father," she said softly, keeping her chin dipped with humility. "The affairs of the world far exceed the importance of a single chair... If it pleases the Crown, I am more than content to remain standing at your flank, or even sit upon the stone floor. I grew up in the mountain barracks of Yamato so I am well accustomed to cold stone."
Aki’s jaw tightened behind her collar.

’Look at that,’ Aki thought, her stomach turning with disgust. ’Look at the way she words it. "Accustomed to cold stone." She’s playing the humble, mistreated, self-sacrificing daughter for every scrap of sympathy she can wring out of him... It’s an act! It’s completely calculated to pull at him!’
Aki glanced toward Alexander.
Her elder brother was sitting three chairs down with his face drained of color.
His hands were clenched so hard against his knees that the fabric of his black dress trousers was tearing along the outer seams.

Alexander had spent so many years trying every possible angle to earn their father’s approval... he had bled in the northern trenches, executed prisoners without blinking, and paraded his Purple Core before every visiting dignitary but the King had never given him anything more than a cold dismissive nod.

’It’s not going to work on him,’ Aki reassured herself, watching her father’s stone-faced profile. ’Father doesn’t have a soft bone in his entire body. When Alexander took a magic spear through his shoulder at nineteen and knelt on the marble waiting for praise, Father just told him his footwork was pathetic and docked his legion’s budget. He’s going to tell her to shut her mouth and stand by the wall—’
"Nonsense."
The King’s voice was remarkably soft.
His expression... that eternal immovable mask of granite actually melted as a warm genuine smile touched his lips as he tapped his right thigh with his heavy signet ring.
"Come here," the King said. "Sit."
The entire Great Assembly Chamber seemed to drop ten degrees in an instant.

Alexander’s head jerked up with his sapphire eyes wide and bloodshot, staring at his father with an expression of pure uncomprehending horror while Aki felt the breath punch straight out of her lungs.
’Sit... on his lap?!’
Kiera hesitated, her golden eyes wide with delicate modesty.
"Father... before the governing heads... that would be improper—"
"I am the Sovereign," the King replied smoothly, his tone leaving no room for argument. "What I permit is proper... Come."
Kiera gathered her amethyst skirts, murmuring a quiet submissive "Yes, Father" and ascended the marble steps of the dais.
She sat down upon his knee, smoothing her dress over his navy wool trousers, resting her hands neatly over her lap.
The King rested his broad heavy palm flat on the marble surface of the table with his posture completely relaxed and his arm lightly framing her back.
It was an open declaration that not only was Kiera recognized... She was the favorite as well!
Alexander looked like he was about to choke on his own tongue.
For decades, he and Aki had shared the same cold silence from their progenitor... an absence of affection that had defined every waking hour of their upbringing.
Now, this girl had walked into the room, spoken three humble sentences in an eastern accent, and was sitting on the King’s lap like a treasured pet while people watched.
The people of the other nations kept their heads down, sensing that this was strictly an internal royal bloodline affair and the tension was suffocating.

The other seven heads of state wanted to throw hateful glares at her, furious that the United Hegemony was reaping astronomical benefits simply because of a royal bastard, but everyone in the room knew that showing open hostility here was pure suicide.
Everyone, except for one.
Standing near the perimeter wall, stationed directly behind High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva’s chair, was a young female junior officer from the Amazonian honor guard.
She was broad-shouldered, barely twenty with her dark olive uniform crisp and her jaw set with the fierce independent pride typical of the Amazonian military.
She looked at Kiera sitting on the King’s lap as she looked at the Hegemony monarchs practically glowing with favor and her lips peeled back in a sudden venomous sneer.
...The woman simply glared at Kiera with pure undisguised contempt and that glare lasted less than a single microsecond.
The King didn’t even turn his neck.
His sapphire irises merely flared with a blinding pulse of void-light.
FZZT!
There was no incantation and there was no mana projection either... Nobody could feel a rush of wind or a sound of an impact.
The Amazonian woman simply stopped existing.
One millisecond, she was a living breathing human being composed of bone, blood, and military wool.
The next millisecond, the physical space she occupied was empty with not a single trace of ash fell to the floor and not a scrap of her uniform remained.
The air collapsed inward to fill the sudden microscopic vacuum with a pathetic pop, barely rustling the hair of the officer standing next to her.
A collective terrified gasp caught in the throats of the people.
Destruction.
The terrifying authority of the King of the World as he didn’t need to fight and he didn’t need to chant for it.
If your core power was vastly inferior to his, he could simply command the molecular bonds of your physical matter to unspool and vanish into the ether.
The King tapped his finger on the marble.
TAP!
"Whose subordinate was that?" the King asked, his voice smooth and conversational, as if he were inquiring about a smudge on the glass.
High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva didn’t hesitate for a tenth of a second as she rose immediately, snapped her fist to her chest in a crisp military salute, and lowered her head three inches.

"An undisciplined frontier recruit from the jungle perimeter, Your Imperial Majesty," Da Silva stated, lacking any fear. "She lacked the psychological fortification required for this assembly... Her failure reflects upon my command so I offer my formal apology to the Crown."
The King stared down at her for three agonizing seconds.
Then, his eyes narrowed slightly, and he gave a curt dismissive wave.
"Discipline your ranks, High Marshal. The air in this chamber is expensive and I have no patience for insects who cannot manage their eyes."
"Understood, Majesty," Da Silva replied, taking her seat with iron composure, though the other guards behind her were visibly shaking with their knuckles white against their sidearms.
The King shifted his weight, resting his chin on his palm.
Princess Kiera remained perfectly serene upon his lap, her golden eyes watching the table with quiet detachment.

"Given that our esteemed guests from Blessed Land have yet to grace us with their presence," the King said, his gaze drifting lazily toward the two empty violet-velvet chairs, "we shall delay the formal petitions regarding the northern rift borders. It would be... unseemly... to divide the northern soil without Lord Vespera present to state her terms."
A quiet tense murmur ran through the hall once again.
Lord Vespera. Why was she so late? Did she have a death wish? Disrespecting the summons by walking in late was an insult of the highest order.
Aki’s chest felt tight.
Beneath the dark blue velvet of her lap, her fingers traced the edge of her star-iron chain under her collar.
’Where are you, Silas?’ she thought, the question clawing at her throat.
Did he have any idea what this room was? Her father had just turned a human being into empty air without lifting a single finger.
If Silas tried his usual blunt, unbothered attitude here, the King wouldn’t debate him... he’d crush him into dust before the first sentence left his mouth.
The King lowered his arm, resting both forearms across the celestial marble and the amber light overhead glinted off his sapphire eyes as he addressed the room.

"In the meantime," the King said. "we shall redirect the assembly toward our infrastructural foundations. Before we discuss foreign borders, we must confirm the stability of the terrestrial perimeter."
Then the man tapped his ring finger against the celestial marble of the Grand Table.
TAP!
The sharp singular sound traveled clean across the five tiers, vibrating through the baffles of the vaulted obsidian ceiling and the silence that followed was heavy and brittle.
Nobody was looking at the vacant spot behind High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva anymore.
Aki kept her hands locked in her lap beneath the velvet folds of her midnight-blue gown and she didn’t let her shoulders slump.
Her gaze remained pinned to the horizontal seam of the titanium wainscoting across the floor, but inside her skull, her pulse was hammering a violent rhythm against her eardrums.
’That aside, Father used Destruction,’ she thought, the word tasting like lead shavings on her tongue. ’That woman... she just died without even realizing what happened.’

sentences.text: Aki knew it was cope.
She knew it was a pathetic embarrassing delusion, a thin paper-mache shield she was holding up to stop her chest from caving in on itself but she clung to it with everything she had.
Right now, in front of more than five hundred people, she couldn’t allow a single muscle in her cheek to twitch.
She was jealous... furious, bitter, and burning with a toxic envy that tasted like iron shavings under her tongue but she kept her face in a frozen expression.
If she lost her temper now, if she let even a sliver of that resentment show on her face, she would tumble deeper into her father’s bad side than she already was.
And sliding down into the King’s bad side was a quick way to stop existing.
The King continued with his deep voice carrying through the acoustics without a microphone, rattling the glass in the mezzanine lamps.
"When the Queen departed this world shortly after the First Princess drew her first breath..."

He let the sentence hang for two heavy suffocating seconds and there was a deliberate pause over the timeline... it was a quiet inflection that laid the late Queen’s death squarely on Aki’s shoulders.
Aki’s pulse thumped once, sounding hard and flat against her ears but she didn’t flinch.
She had heard that exact phrasing in the corridors since she was seven years old.
The Queen bled out because the child took her life and gave no mana in return.
The words were similar to an ancient blade, it had grown dull from overuse, but it still left a familiar cold ache behind her ribs.
"The grief was severe," the King said smoothly, his gaze drifting lazily toward the eastern arc of the Grand Table.
"In my search for solace, I traveled east, deep into the sovereign territories of the United Hegemony.
It was there, among the coastal valleys and ancient shrine peaks, that I met the most beautiful woman I have ever laid eyes upon...
A daughter who carried the combined martial heritage of both the Yamatoan warrior clans and the ancient dynasties of the Shogunate Isles."
He lowered his chin slightly, letting the room absorb the weight of the confession.
"She was Kiera’s mother and it brings me sorrow to state that she succumbed to an incurable lung rot three years past but her lineage remains intact."
The King gestured toward the two eastern monarchs seated side-by-side at the Grand Table.
"The United Hegemony sheltered my daughter when the world was volatile," the King said.

"The Crown does not leave debts unsettled so in the coming territorial allocations, the Hegemony’s trade corridors will receive a total exemption from imperial transit tariffs for the next twenty years, along with three Tier-5 deep-sea mining anchors transferred directly to their coastal fleet."
King Zhao Xian of the Shogunate Isles and King Minamoto no Masashi of the Yamato Sector exchanged a rapid imperceptible glance.
Then, both men rose smoothly from their star-iron chairs, bowing deeply from the waist.
"The United Hegemony bows before the grace of the Crown," King Zhao intoned, his long white beard brushing the collar of his imperial yellow robes.
"We shall guard the eastern waters with our lives."
Beside him, Minamoto bowed with one hand resting flat against the black lacquer of his samurai cuirass with the plates clattering softly in the quiet.
Across the circle, the other seven rulers looked on with thinly veiled jealousy.
A twenty-year tariff exemption and three Tier-5 deep-sea anchors were absurd economic concessions!
It was the kind of leverage that could tilt regional maritime trade balances for half a century.

In their heads, both eastern monarchs were undoubtedly offering silent reverent prayers to the dead woman whose brief encounter with the King had just handed their nations an insurmountable geopolitical advantage.
Added benefits could mean a lot of things down the road...
It could mean that once both of them had the requisite age and experience, their delegates might even be elevated to permanent seats on the World Council.
More benefits also meant that in every single negotiation that followed today, the Hegemony would hold the upper hand.
The King dismissed their bows with a lazy wave of his left hand, turning his sapphire eyes back down to the girl on the floor.
"Come forward, Kiera," he commanded gently.
"It appears the staff failed to prepare an official seat for you at the Grand Table."
Kiera didn’t show a shred of anger as she took two light steps forward, sinking into another graceful low curtsy with her voice ringing clear and melodious through the hall.
"There is no need to trouble the servants, Father," she said softly, keeping her chin dipped with humility.
"The affairs of the world far exceed the importance of a single chair...
If it pleases the Crown, I am more than content to remain standing at your flank, or even sit upon the stone floor.
I grew up in the mountain barracks of Yamato so I am well accustomed to cold stone."
Aki’s jaw tightened behind her collar.
’Look at that,’ Aki thought, her stomach turning with disgust. ’Look at the way she words it.
"Accustomed to cold stone." She’s playing the humble, mistreated, self-sacrificing daughter for every scrap of sympathy she can wring out of him...
It’s an act!
It’s completely calculated to pull at him!’
Aki glanced toward Alexander.
Her elder brother was sitting three chairs down with his face drained of color.
His hands were clenched so hard against his knees that the fabric of his black dress trousers was tearing along the outer seams.

Alexander had spent so many years trying every possible angle to earn their father’s approval... he had bled in the northern trenches, executed prisoners without blinking, and paraded his Purple Core before every visiting dignitary but the King had never given him anything more than a cold dismissive nod.
’It’s not going to work on him,’ Aki reassured herself, watching her father’s stone-faced profile. ’Father doesn’t have a soft bone in his entire body.
When Alexander took a magic spear through his shoulder at nineteen and knelt on the marble waiting for praise, Father just told him his footwork was pathetic and docked his legion’s budget.
He’s going to tell her to shut her mouth and stand by the wall—’
"Nonsense."
The King’s voice was remarkably soft.
His expression... that eternal immovable mask of granite actually melted as a warm genuine smile touched his lips as he tapped his right thigh with his heavy signet ring.
"Come here," the King said.
"Sit."
The entire Great Assembly Chamber seemed to drop ten degrees in an instant.

Alexander’s head jerked up with his sapphire eyes wide and bloodshot, staring at his father with an expression of pure uncomprehending horror while Aki felt the breath punch straight out of her lungs.
’Sit... on his lap?!’
Kiera hesitated, her golden eyes wide with delicate modesty.
"Father... before the governing heads... that would be improper—"
"I am the Sovereign," the King replied smoothly, his tone leaving no room for argument.
"What I permit is proper...
Come."
Kiera gathered her amethyst skirts, murmuring a quiet submissive "Yes, Father" and ascended the marble steps of the dais.
She sat down upon his knee, smoothing her dress over his navy wool trousers, resting her hands neatly over her lap.
The King rested his broad heavy palm flat on the marble surface of the table with his posture completely relaxed and his arm lightly framing her back.
It was an open declaration that not only was Kiera recognized...
She was the favorite as well!
Alexander looked like he was about to choke on his own tongue.
For decades, he and Aki had shared the same cold silence from their progenitor... an absence of affection that had defined every waking hour of their upbringing.
Now, this girl had walked into the room, spoken three humble sentences in an eastern accent, and was sitting on the King’s lap like a treasured pet while people watched.
The people of the other nations kept their heads down, sensing that this was strictly an internal royal bloodline affair and the tension was suffocating.

The other seven heads of state wanted to throw hateful glares at her, furious that the United Hegemony was reaping astronomical benefits simply because of a royal bastard, but everyone in the room knew that showing open hostility here was pure suicide.
Everyone, except for one.
Standing near the perimeter wall, stationed directly behind High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva’s chair, was a young female junior officer from the Amazonian honor guard.
She was broad-shouldered, barely twenty with her dark olive uniform crisp and her jaw set with the fierce independent pride typical of the Amazonian military.
She looked at Kiera sitting on the King’s lap as she looked at the Hegemony monarchs practically glowing with favor and her lips peeled back in a sudden venomous sneer.
...The woman simply glared at Kiera with pure undisguised contempt and that glare lasted less than a single microsecond.
The King didn’t even turn his neck.
His sapphire irises merely flared with a blinding pulse of void-light.
FZZT!
There was no incantation and there was no mana projection either...
Nobody could feel a rush of wind or a sound of an impact.
The Amazonian woman simply stopped existing.
One millisecond, she was a living breathing human being composed of bone, blood, and military wool.
The next millisecond, the physical space she occupied was empty with not a single trace of ash fell to the floor and not a scrap of her uniform remained.
The air collapsed inward to fill the sudden microscopic vacuum with a pathetic pop, barely rustling the hair of the officer standing next to her.
A collective terrified gasp caught in the throats of the people.
Destruction.
The terrifying authority of the King of the World as he didn’t need to fight and he didn’t need to chant for it.
If your core power was vastly inferior to his, he could simply command the molecular bonds of your physical matter to unspool and vanish into the ether.
The King tapped his finger on the marble.
TAP!

High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva didn’t hesitate for a tenth of a second as she rose immediately, snapped her fist to her chest in a crisp military salute, and lowered her head three inches.

chapters.title: Chapter 533: Mark IV Sovereign Suppression Arrays [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The King leaned forward with his heavy star-iron signet ring dragging a hollow line across the polished white marble.

"Specifically," the King said, his voice dropping into that deep tone that resonated directly within the ribcages of every delegate in the room, "the operational status of the regional Suppression Engines..."

The shift in the room was instantaneous as the courtly paranoia and petty bloodline jealousies evaporated, replaced by the cold survival-driven tension of nine nations facing the reality of their own crumbling borders.
Every leader at the Grand Table understood the architecture of the civilized world.

The primary Suppression Engine... the titanic ancestral anchor that stabilized the dimensional fabric of the entire globe existed in a classified sector whose coordinates were known to nobody alive except the King himself.
But beneath the bedrock of each of the Nine Major Powers lay an immense regional sub-engine, buried leagues beneath the continental crust.

Those nine colossal machines ran continuously, humming day and night, pumping harmonic stabilization frequencies through the planet to keep the Sovereign Realm’s chaotic spatial tides from breaching the crust and drowning humanity in horrors.
Without those nine sub-engines running at full operational capacity, the planar gates would collapse inward, tearing the countries apart from the mantle up.
Yet, keeping them running was an economic and military nightmare.

Over the past four decades, merchant syndicates, ruling oligarchs, and state-backed guilds had grown dependent on anti-suppression dampeners... obscenely expensive technological counter-arrays capable of temporarily neutralizing an engine’s harmonic field over a tight sector.

The mechanism was simple which was by temporarily cutting off the suppression waves over a specific valley or ocean trench, influential factions capable of buying the hardware could artificially pry open controlled gates directly into the Sovereign Realm.
Through those artificial gates flowed the lifeblood of the global economy... high-tier beast cores, refined ether, mineral ores, and alchemical marrow.

It was an endless multibillion-credit engine of greed and the friction from thousands of unsanctioned mining gates cycling open and closed every fiscal quarter was slowly grinding the ancient planetary machinery into scrap.
Prime Minister Sir Arthur Pendelton of the Albion Concordat leaned forward first.
The silver-haired statesman rested both hands on his cane with the polished star-iron orb on its pommel clicking against the table’s beveled edge.
His pale hawk-like face was lined with deep exhaustion and his tailored navy three-piece suit remained uncreased despite the humidity that had spiked after the kinetic display.

"Your Imperial Majesty," Pendelton began, his voice carrying the clipped precision of the western administrative houses. "Albion must place a formal urgent grievance upon the docket... Over the past four quarters, the seismic monitoring arrays stationed along our Channel trench have recorded an eight-point-four percent harmonic drift in the regional sub-engine’s core frequency so the dampening field is no longer uniform and it fluctuates during peak lunar tides."
Beside him, Chancellor Henri de Montmirail of Europa adjusted his wire-rimmed spectacles, tapping his terminal to project a rotating volumetric wireframe of his own stats into the air between them.

"Europa’s geodetic networks corroborate the Albion data, Majesty," Montmirail stated. "The Alpine faultline sub-engine is exhibiting identical symptoms... The harmonic resonance is slipping by nearly nine cycles per minute during heavy gate cycles. These sub-engines were constructed by the ancestral architects centuries ago and they were engineered to endure, yes... built with the assumption that their internal power would last forever but they were never designed to withstand the violent spatial backwash caused by hundreds of private industrial syndicates activating synthetic anti-suppression dampeners every single day."
Montmirail looked up through his lenses with his gaze sweeping across the other rulers.
"The structural cooling channels within the sub-engines are calcifying and hey require an immediate maintenance overhaul."
The chamber erupted into an immediate tense rustle of shuffling parchment, muttered arguments, and shifting boots.
Several delegates from the secondary tiers exchanged skeptical defensive looks.
Questioning the integrity of the ancestral machines was always dangerous... it bordered on suggesting that the royal bloodline’s foundational craftsmanship was flawed.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior of Columbia scowled, his broad heavy shoulders bunching against his charcoal pinstripe suit.
He slammed both palms onto the table with the signet rings on his thick fingers clicking sharply against the stone.

"An immediate maintenance overhaul?!" Vanderbilt barked, his iron-gray hair catching the harsh downlight. "Do you have any concept of the industrial fallout, Henri? You speak like an academic who has never had to balance a national power grid! If you take a regional sub-engine offline for maintenance... even with secondary stabilization grids, you have to sever every commercial rift gate within six hundred leagues! Half the manufacturing foundries in Columbia depend entirely on raw core imports from the western basins! Indirectly, you would trigger an immediate catastrophic energy depression across three continents!"
"And what happens if an engine suffers an uncontained harmonic rupture, Julian?!" Pendelton countered sharply, his voice cutting through Vanderbilt’s bluster like a razor.
The silver-haired Prime Minister leaned over his cane with his eyes blazing.

"They need to be checked for the safety of the world! Do you think your quarterly manufacturing quotas will matter if the Alpine sub-engine fractures?! Even if a single country experiences an uncontrolled outbreak, the loss of human lives would be simply too catastrophic to count! A breach of that magnitude would bleed across the shared continental faultlines, triggering chain-reaction failures in the neighboring grids! We would be burying entire metropolitan sectors under concrete and artillery within seventy-two hours..."
The argument hung in the air...
Pendelton was right, and every leader at the table knew it.
The economic disruption of an engine shutdown was terrifying, but the alternative was planetary extinction.

The King didn’t interject as he sat back with his arm still resting loosely behind Kiera’s back, listening to the two statesmen bicker with the detached unhurried patience of a ruler who already held the ledger.
He raised his right forefinger by half an inch.
TAP!
The stone rang and the room fell instantly silent.

"The Prime Minister makes a valid point," the King said. "The ancestral machines were built for a different world. My forebears did not anticipate an era where private mining cartels would run hundreds of anti-suppression dampeners concurrently to maximize quarterly ether yields... The wear on the harmonic crystals are real."
A visible wave of relief washed over Pendelton and Montmirail with their shoulders dropping slightly.

"Therefore," the King continued, sweeping his sapphire gaze across the nine rulers, "the Crown will intervene. I shall assemble an imperial delegation of Royal Engineers... technicians trained exclusively in the ancestral architectural styles and harmonic frequencies and dispatch them across the Nine Major Powers to perform harmonic recalibrations on every regional sub-engine."
He paused, his eyes narrowing to cold slits.
"However... recalibration is merely a stopgap, a temporary patch on an aging foundation if you will. To permanently resolve the structural degradation of the world, the Crown has not remained idle."
The King reached forward, tapping a series of complex runes directly onto the celestial marble surface of the Grand Table.
HUMMMMMM!

The center of the ring lit up with a brilliant flash of cyan light as the wireframe of the old continental engines dissolved, replaced by a massive intricately detailed three-dimensional holographic schematic that expanded until it filled the center of the pit.
It was a titanic multi-tiered monolith of void-iron and star-iron conduits, wrapped in concentric interlocking rings of compressed mana-crystals that pulsed with an oceanic blue glow.
It was vast and terrifyingly complex... an inverted fortress designed to be driven directly into the molten mantle of the earth.
A collective gasp swept through the mezzanine galleries as the technical advisors and guild scribes leaned forward, scrambling to record this.

"For the past decade, working under my personal design directives and utilizing the proprietary archives of the Throne, the Royal Engineers have been fabricating the next generation of planetary dampeners," the King announced. "The Mark IV Sovereign Suppression Arrays."
The leaders of the Nine Nations stared at the blue schematic in stunned silence.

"These units," the King explained, his hand tracing the outer rotation of the crystalline containment rings, "utilize an active harmonic compression spell... Rather than passively dampening spatial turbulence through raw suppression, the Mark IV actively absorbs the dimensional friction bleeding from the Sovereign Realm, refining it into ultra-dense stable ether currents that can be channeled directly into continental defense grids or stored in national reserves. They are vast and their structural footprint is four times the scale of the ancestral models but they will soon be ready... perhaps within a year or two."
He withdrew his hand, resting it flat on the table once more.

"However... because of their scale and the unprecedented pressure of their compression chambers, the Mark IV cannot be calibrated in a controlled laboratory environment. It requires live real-world deployment over an active country."
The King’s sapphire eyes swept slowly across the nine rulers, lingering on each of their faces.
"The Crown requires a nation to volunteer its soil for the initial prototype testing phase."
The Great Assembly Chamber went dead quiet.
Volunteer your own land?
Every president, king, and governor in the room immediately began running the brutal calculations.

If the Mark IV functioned as the King promised, whichever nation hosted the prototype would instantly become the most fortified energy-abundant superpower on the globe, completely immune to the spatial decay threatening the rest of the world.

But if the prototype suffered a containment collapse during its initial core ignition cycle... the resulting spatial implosion would tear through the tectonic crust, vaporizing an entire province into the void.
Before Grand Tsar Volkov of Borealis could weigh the risks, and before King Zhao of Shogya could consult his diviners, a voice rang out with sharp finality.
"The Federal Union of Amazonia volunteers."
Every eye in the amphitheater snapped toward High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva.
The Amazonian leader sat tall with her posture rigid as an iron pike and her feline dark eyes locked straight onto the King without a single flicker of hesitation.
The jagged scar running down her neck caught the blue light of the holographic engine.

"The Amazonian river basin contains the densest and most volatile rift clusters on the globe," Da Silva stated, her commanding voice cutting clean through the chamber’s silence. "Our soil is already saturated with mana from the Sovereign Realm so if your Mark IV array can hold the line beneath the canopy of our southern trenches, it can hold anywhere on Earth... Amazonia will provide the testing ground, the raw labor, and the military perimeter defense so we would be happy to assist the Crown."
Aki watched the Amazonian president from her low-tier seat with her eyes narrowing slightly.

’Smart woman,’ Aki analyzed ruthlessly, feeling the cold logic behind the move. ’She just watched Father erase one of her honor guards without lifting a finger and her delegation was on the verge of diplomatic isolation. She knew her standing with the Crown took a direct hit... Volunteering for the prototype is a much better way to get back on the good side of the King. She wipes away the stain of her dead soldier, eliminates the King’s displeasure, and positions Amazonia at the front of the line for imperial engineering priority. A ruthless gamble indeed.’
The King’s mouth curved into a slow approving smile.
The residual coldness in his sapphire eyes receded, replaced by the satisfaction of a ruler whose bait had been taken instantly.

"Decisive as always, High Marshal," the King nodded, his tone carrying genuine warmth. "The Crown accepts the volunteer petition of the Federal Union of Amazonia... We shall continue the operational discussions regarding the deployment protocols and testing schedules at a later time."
Da Silva placed her right fist over her heart, dipping her chin three inches.
"Amazonia thanks the Sovereign."
With the foundational matters settled and the prototype allocated, the King shifted his posture slightly.
Princess Kiera remained poised upon his lap, adjusting her skirts with quiet grace, her golden eyes watching the room with that same serene untouchable poise.
The King turned his attention toward the secondary tier of the Grand Table, where the two outside noble titans sat in their tailored finery.
"Now," the King said. "Let us address our two newest additions to the table. Patriarch Sterling and Matriarch Bloom... Your reputations precede you."
Lohan Sterling stood immediately.
He didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second.

The Patriarch of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate stepped forward, his silver robes shimmering under the white overhead lamps like polished mercury, his long fingers adjusting the cuffs of his embroidered sleeves as he offered a flawless bow from the waist.
Like Kiera, it was neither too low to appear subservient and nor too stiff to seem insolent.
’Tch... so this bastard has a bit of sense after all.’ Etilga thought.
"House Sterling is profoundly honored by the gracious invitation of the World Council and the Throne," Lohan said.
He didn’t waste time with flowery imperial poetry or theatrical humility as he handled his business with cold executive perfection.
Nobody wanted to listen to the other ramble on and on... All that paid off was action at the end of the day!
With a flick of his signet ring, he transmitted an encrypted financial ledger into the center of the ring, projecting a sleek silver holographic interface into the air before the heads of state.

"We come before this assembly with a comprehensive business prospect," Lohan continued, his sharp eyes sweeping across the gathered rulers. "Currently, the logistical pipeline supporting the northern perimeter defense is bleeding twenty-eight percent of its operating capital on transport tariffs, incompatible ammunition gauges, and fragmented supply chains split across six different private contractors... Why?.. Because the northern frontier relies on outdated, disparate manufacturing standards that fail under sustained sub-zero mana combat."
He tapped a sequence of keys on his terminal, highlighting the northern rail networks in bright amber.

"The Sterling Financial Conglomerate," Lohan proposed, his voice smooth as warmed oil, "is prepared to fully underwrite the construction of ten automated heavy-munitions foundries directly along the northern railway corridor. We will standardize all artillery, mana-core casings, and void-iron penetrators to the military standard, cutting replenishment times by sixty percent."
He paused, letting the numbers sink into the minds of the military ministers before delivering his terms.

"In exchange, House Sterling requests an exclusive fifteen-year procurement concession for all raw titanium and unrefined void-iron deposits extracted from the newly stabilized northern trench sectors."
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior’s face darkened instantly.
The Columbian corporate titan leaned forward, opening his mouth to vehemently contest the concession on behalf of his own domestic defense contractors—
THUD!
Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov of Borealis slammed his massive bear-like fist onto the celestial marble!

These sub-engines were constructed by the ancestral architects centuries ago and they were engineered to endure, yes... built with the assumption that their internal power would last forever but they were never designed to withstand the violent spatial backwash caused by hundreds of private industrial syndicates activating synthetic anti-suppression dampeners every single day."
Montmirail looked up through his lenses with his gaze sweeping across the other rulers.
"The structural cooling channels within the sub-engines are calcifying and hey require an immediate maintenance overhaul."
The chamber erupted into an immediate tense rustle of shuffling parchment, muttered arguments, and shifting boots.
Several delegates from the secondary tiers exchanged skeptical defensive looks.
Questioning the integrity of the ancestral machines was always dangerous... it bordered on suggesting that the royal bloodline’s foundational craftsmanship was flawed.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior of Columbia scowled, his broad heavy shoulders bunching against his charcoal pinstripe suit.
He slammed both palms onto the table with the signet rings on his thick fingers clicking sharply against the stone.
"An immediate maintenance overhaul?!" Vanderbilt barked, his iron-gray hair catching the harsh downlight.
"Do you have any concept of the industrial fallout, Henri?
You speak like an academic who has never had to balance a national power grid!
If you take a regional sub-engine offline for maintenance... even with secondary stabilization grids, you have to sever every commercial rift gate within six hundred leagues!
Half the manufacturing foundries in Columbia depend entirely on raw core imports from the western basins!
Indirectly, you would trigger an immediate catastrophic energy depression across three continents!"
"And what happens if an engine suffers an uncontained harmonic rupture, Julian?!" Pendelton countered sharply, his voice cutting through Vanderbilt’s bluster like a razor.
The silver-haired Prime Minister leaned over his cane with his eyes blazing.
"They need to be checked for the safety of the world!
Do you think your quarterly manufacturing quotas will matter if the Alpine sub-engine fractures?!
Even if a single country experiences an uncontrolled outbreak, the loss of human lives would be simply too catastrophic to count!
A breach of that magnitude would bleed across the shared continental faultlines, triggering chain-reaction failures in the neighboring grids!
We would be burying entire metropolitan sectors under concrete and artillery within seventy-two hours..."
The argument hung in the air...
Pendelton was right, and every leader at the table knew it.
The economic disruption of an engine shutdown was terrifying, but the alternative was planetary extinction.

The King didn’t interject as he sat back with his arm still resting loosely behind Kiera’s back, listening to the two statesmen bicker with the detached unhurried patience of a ruler who already held the ledger.
He raised his right forefinger by half an inch.
TAP!
The stone rang and the room fell instantly silent.
"The Prime Minister makes a valid point," the King said.
"The ancestral machines were built for a different world.
My forebears did not anticipate an era where private mining cartels would run hundreds of anti-suppression dampeners concurrently to maximize quarterly ether yields...
The wear on the harmonic crystals are real."
A visible wave of relief washed over Pendelton and Montmirail with their shoulders dropping slightly.
"Therefore," the King continued, sweeping his sapphire gaze across the nine rulers, "the Crown will intervene.

I shall assemble an imperial delegation of Royal Engineers... technicians trained exclusively in the ancestral architectural styles and harmonic frequencies and dispatch them across the Nine Major Powers to perform harmonic recalibrations on every regional sub-engine."
He paused, his eyes narrowing to cold slits.
"However... recalibration is merely a stopgap, a temporary patch on an aging foundation if you will.
To permanently resolve the structural degradation of the world, the Crown has not remained idle."
The King reached forward, tapping a series of complex runes directly onto the celestial marble surface of the Grand Table.
HUMMMMMM!

The center of the ring lit up with a brilliant flash of cyan light as the wireframe of the old continental engines dissolved, replaced by a massive intricately detailed three-dimensional holographic schematic that expanded until it filled the center of the pit.
It was a titanic multi-tiered monolith of void-iron and star-iron conduits, wrapped in concentric interlocking rings of compressed mana-crystals that pulsed with an oceanic blue glow.
It was vast and terrifyingly complex... an inverted fortress designed to be driven directly into the molten mantle of the earth.
A collective gasp swept through the mezzanine galleries as the technical advisors and guild scribes leaned forward, scrambling to record this.

"For the past decade, working under my personal design directives and utilizing the proprietary archives of the Throne, the Royal Engineers have been fabricating the next generation of planetary dampeners," the King announced.
"The Mark IV Sovereign Suppression Arrays."
The leaders of the Nine Nations stared at the blue schematic in stunned silence.
"These units," the King explained, his hand tracing the outer rotation of the crystalline containment rings, "utilize an active harmonic compression spell...

Rather than passively dampening spatial turbulence through raw suppression, the Mark IV actively absorbs the dimensional friction bleeding from the Sovereign Realm, refining it into ultra-dense stable ether currents that can be channeled directly into continental defense grids or stored in national reserves.
They are vast and their structural footprint is four times the scale of the ancestral models but they will soon be ready... perhaps within a year or two."
He withdrew his hand, resting it flat on the table once more.
"However... because of their scale and the unprecedented pressure of their compression chambers, the Mark IV cannot be calibrated in a controlled laboratory environment.
It requires live real-world deployment over an active country."
The King’s sapphire eyes swept slowly across the nine rulers, lingering on each of their faces.
"The Crown requires a nation to volunteer its soil for the initial prototype testing phase."
The Great Assembly Chamber went dead quiet.
Volunteer your own land?
Every president, king, and governor in the room immediately began running the brutal calculations.

If the Mark IV functioned as the King promised, whichever nation hosted the prototype would instantly become the most fortified energy-abundant superpower on the globe, completely immune to the spatial decay threatening the rest of the world.

But if the prototype suffered a containment collapse during its initial core ignition cycle... the resulting spatial implosion would tear through the tectonic crust, vaporizing an entire province into the void.
Before Grand Tsar Volkov of Borealis could weigh the risks, and before King Zhao of Shogya could consult his diviners, a voice rang out with sharp finality.
"The Federal Union of Amazonia volunteers."
Every eye in the amphitheater snapped toward High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva.
The Amazonian leader sat tall with her posture rigid as an iron pike and her feline dark eyes locked straight onto the King without a single flicker of hesitation.
The jagged scar running down her neck caught the blue light of the holographic engine.
"The Amazonian river basin contains the densest and most volatile rift clusters on the globe," Da Silva stated, her commanding voice cutting clean through the chamber’s silence.
"Our soil is already saturated with mana from the Sovereign Realm so if your Mark IV array can hold the line beneath the canopy of our southern trenches, it can hold anywhere on Earth...
Amazonia will provide the testing ground, the raw labor, and the military perimeter defense so we would be happy to assist the Crown."
Aki watched the Amazonian president from her low-tier seat with her eyes narrowing slightly.

’Smart woman,’ Aki analyzed ruthlessly, feeling the cold logic behind the move. ’She just watched Father erase one of her honor guards without lifting a finger and her delegation was on the verge of diplomatic isolation.
She knew her standing with the Crown took a direct hit...
Volunteering for the prototype is a much better way to get back on the good side of the King.
She wipes away the stain of her dead soldier, eliminates the King’s displeasure, and positions Amazonia at the front of the line for imperial engineering priority.
A ruthless gamble indeed.’
The King’s mouth curved into a slow approving smile.
The residual coldness in his sapphire eyes receded, replaced by the satisfaction of a ruler whose bait had been taken instantly.
"Decisive as always, High Marshal," the King nodded, his tone carrying genuine warmth.
"The Crown accepts the volunteer petition of the Federal Union of Amazonia...
We shall continue the operational discussions regarding the deployment protocols and testing schedules at a later time."
Da Silva placed her right fist over her heart, dipping her chin three inches.
"Amazonia thanks the Sovereign."
With the foundational matters settled and the prototype allocated, the King shifted his posture slightly.
Princess Kiera remained poised upon his lap, adjusting her skirts with quiet grace, her golden eyes watching the room with that same serene untouchable poise.
The King turned his attention toward the secondary tier of the Grand Table, where the two outside noble titans sat in their tailored finery.
"Now," the King said.
"Let us address our two newest additions to the table.
Patriarch Sterling and Matriarch Bloom...
Your reputations precede you."
Lohan Sterling stood immediately.
He didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second.

The Patriarch of the Sterling Financial Conglomerate stepped forward, his silver robes shimmering under the white overhead lamps like polished mercury, his long fingers adjusting the cuffs of his embroidered sleeves as he offered a flawless bow from the waist.
Like Kiera, it was neither too low to appear subservient and nor too stiff to seem insolent.
’Tch... so this bastard has a bit of sense after all.’ Etilga thought.
"House Sterling is profoundly honored by the gracious invitation of the World Council and the Throne," Lohan said.
He didn’t waste time with flowery imperial poetry or theatrical humility as he handled his business with cold executive perfection.
Nobody wanted to listen to the other ramble on and on...
All that paid off was action at the end of the day!
With a flick of his signet ring, he transmitted an encrypted financial ledger into the center of the ring, projecting a sleek silver holographic interface into the air before the heads of state.
"We come before this assembly with a comprehensive business prospect," Lohan continued, his sharp eyes sweeping across the gathered rulers.

"Currently, the logistical pipeline supporting the northern perimeter defense is bleeding twenty-eight percent of its operating capital on transport tariffs, incompatible ammunition gauges, and fragmented supply chains split across six different private contractors...
Why?..
Because the northern frontier relies on outdated, disparate manufacturing standards that fail under sustained sub-zero mana combat."
He tapped a sequence of keys on his terminal, highlighting the northern rail networks in bright amber.

"The Sterling Financial Conglomerate," Lohan proposed, his voice smooth as warmed oil, "is prepared to fully underwrite the construction of ten automated heavy-munitions foundries directly along the northern railway corridor.
We will standardize all artillery, mana-core casings, and void-iron penetrators to the military standard, cutting replenishment times by sixty percent."
He paused, letting the numbers sink into the minds of the military ministers before delivering his terms.

"In exchange, House Sterling requests an exclusive fifteen-year procurement concession for all raw titanium and unrefined void-iron deposits extracted from the newly stabilized northern trench sectors."
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior’s face darkened instantly.
The Columbian corporate titan leaned forward, opening his mouth to vehemently contest the concession on behalf of his own domestic defense contractors—
THUD!
Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov of Borealis slammed his massive bear-like fist onto the celestial marble!

chapters.title: Chapter 534: It’s All Business On This Table [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The impact rattled the glassware across four desks as the northern ruler stood up, his white dire-wolf fur mantle shifting over his massive shoulders and his gray beard bristling with residual frost-mana.

"Borealis accepts the Sterling proposal!" Volkov boomed, his heavy voice echoing like artillery fire through the chamber. "My men in the frost-trenches are sick to death of receiving Columbian artillery shells that jam in our cannon breeches because some bureaucrat in a pinstripe suit shaved an eighth of an inch off the brass casing to maximize corporate margins! Sterling foundries make good reliable steel! Their ordnance doesn’t crack when the frost-giants charge the perimeter so Borealis allies with House Sterling on this motion!"
Lohan Sterling dipped his head toward the Tsar with a razor-sharp victorious smile playing across his thin lips.
’That’s more money for me~’
"The Sterling Conglomerate will ensure the brave warriors of Borealis have the finest ordnance on the planet, Grand Tsar," Lohan said smoothly.
With the northern superpower throwing its immense military weight behind the deal, Vanderbilt’s objections died in his throat.
The World Council Magistrates nodded in quiet unison with their stylus seals stamping approval into the digital ledger.

Lohan had executed his negotiation with ruthless efficiency, locking down an exclusive raw-material monopoly across the entire northern frontier and securing a military alliance with the Tsardom in under five minutes.
The King’s gaze shifted to the woman seated beside Lohan.
"And Matriarch Bloom?" the King asked, raising an eyebrow. "I understand your house has placed a formal petition on the docket?"
Etilga Bloom did not stand.
She remained seated in her high-backed star-iron chair with her spine rigid as a drawn bow, radiating an aura of blistering confidence that made several surrounding delegates lean back.
Her crimson robes were cut close to her athletic frame, embroidered with burning phoenix threads and her vibrant red hair cascaded over her shoulders like liquid embers.
She carried herself with an imperious temperament... a woman who looked at the rulers of the world as if they were squabbling tenants on her estate.
It was suicidal behavior but if there was anybody capable of pulling it off, it was her.

"House Bloom does not build factories, Your Majesty," Etilga said, her voice smooth but also carrying a dangerous, crackling warmth that made the nearby Council guards sweat beneath their armor. "We hold territory. Specifically... the three coastal mining sectors located in the southern gulf corridor."
A sharp rustle of papers swept through the southern delegations.

"Those three sectors," Etilga continued coldly, her ruby eyes glittering with lethal intent, "have suffered eleven separate pirate breaches and three coastal rift incursions over the past six months alone... The regional prefectures are weak. Their private militias are cowards who retreat behind concrete seawalls the moment a leviathan breaks the surface. House Bloom formally requests the full annexation of those three sectors under our direct martial administration."

"Outrageous!" Prime Minister Sir Arthur Pendelton barked, leaning forward with his cane rattling against the stone. "Those three sectors border the Albion Concordat’s primary southern trade route... You are asking this Council to let a private noble house station an active Lord army directly upon our maritime flank! That is an unacceptable escalation!"
Etilga Bloom slowly turned her head toward the silver-haired statesman as she simply smiled... a slow crescent of a smile that promised complete merciless incineration.
The woman truly did not give a fuck.

"Sir Arthur," Etilga murmured, the air around her chair visibly warping with heat as her crimson mana flared. "If your navy was capable of keeping mutated sea-krakens from chewing through your own cargo freighters, my family wouldn’t have to step in and secure the waters for you... My private Lord army does not retreat nor do we negotiate with pirates. We burn them until the sea boils to steam, and the shipping lanes remain open."
Sitting up in the mezzanine, Seraphina Bloom leaned over the brass railing with her arms crossed, watching her mother with fierce glowing pride.
Beside her, Valerius Sterling shuddered, taking another nervous sip from his smuggled silver flask while muttering about how terrifying the Bloom bloodline was.
Down at the Grand Table, Magistrate Bloom... Etilga’s husband sat silently among the Magistrates.
He didn’t speak but his mere presence as a sitting Magistrate of the highest judicial authority on Earth hung over the table like an immovable iron shield.
The delegates looked at Etilga with genuine awe.

It was partly because her husband’s position gave her immense institutional immunity, but mostly because they respected her confidence and the undeniable benefits of allying with the overwhelming military might of House Bloom.
Governor-General Malcolm Sterling-Cross of Australis leaned forward, rubbing his weather-beaten, scarred jaw with a rough thumb.

"Australis supports the annexation," Malcolm barked with blunt military pragmatism. "My southern convoys lost two supply skiffs to those gulf raiders last month... If Lady Bloom wants to turn those pirate coves into glass and keep the straits open, she has my vote. Better a fiery noble than dead sailors. Australis allies with House Bloom!"
Etilga bowed her head with cool flawless dignity toward the Australis commander.
"A wise decision, Governor-General. Your fleets will enjoy unhindered protected passage through Bloom waters."
With Australis throwing its full support behind her, and with her husband’s silent authority sealing the legal framework, Etilga received exactly what she wanted.
...Both noble titans had executed their business flawlessly.
Aki watched it all from her seat with a tired, hollow quietness behind her ribs.

’Steel, territory, money,’ she thought, feeling the small star-iron necklace resting warm against her collarbone beneath her velvet gown. ’It never changes... The entire world gathered in one room, and all they care about is who gets to bleed the earth dry.’
The King waited until the holographic ledgers dissolved from the center of the ring, leaving the celestial marble clear once more then he unlaced his fingers, shifting his posture slightly.
Princess Kiera remained poised upon his lap, her golden eyes watching the room with placid grace.
His sapphire eyes hardened, sweeping over the assembly with cold command as the air in the Great Assembly Chamber tightened once more.
He leaned forward, his heavy hands resting on the celestial marble.
"And to move on to the next part of the meeting..." the King spoke, his voice echoing off the obsidian walls.
"Forgive the interruption, Your Imperial Majesty."
Every eye at the Grand Table snapped toward the western quadrant.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior of the Republic of Columbia leaned forward, his massive square-jawed profile illuminated by the stark downlight of the central chandelier.
He was a broad man, built like a shipyard crane, his iron-gray hair combed back with aggressiveness, wearing a charcoal pinstripe suit cut from void-fiber wool that absorbed the light.
On his left pinky, a platinum signet ring encrusted with a raw yellow ether diamond clicked sharply against the marble slab as he steepled his thick fingers.
The King’s sapphire eyes drifted slowly toward the Columbian leader but he didn’t snap.
His eyelids merely dropped by a fraction of an inch... a silent signal that usually made regional governors break out in cold sweat.
"President Vanderbilt," the King murmured. "The Crown was about to open the floor to the territorial dockets... It is rare for Columbia to step out of protocol before the agenda is called."
"Protocol is designed to serve the stability of the realm, Sire," Vanderbilt replied smoothly but he didn’t flinch.
As the supreme executive of the most industrialized capitalist republic on the planet, he operated on the conviction that money, manufacturing, and firepower were the only real gods in human history.

"And stability requires fiscal transparency... Before this assembly turns its gaze toward the unclaimed soil of the northern rifts, the Republic of Columbia must formally address the matter of the Continental Defense Subsidies."
A faint uneasy murmur fluttered through the mezzanine tiers.
Aki’s eyes narrowed.
’The subsidies,’ she thought with her pulse steadying into a cold beat. ’He’s playing his leverage early.’
Vanderbilt reached out with a thick, manicured finger, tapping a series of executive keys on his slate.
BZZZZT!

A massive, golden-hued holographic projection expanded into the air above the Grand Table, displaying a dizzying multi-layered financial waterfall of trade ledgers, raw material shipments, and ammunition distribution routes spanning three continents.

"For the past seven fiscal years," Vanderbilt said, his voice ringing with the authority of a boardroom predator, "the defense of the northern perimeter line... the barrier holding the ice-abominations of the upper trench from flooding the civilized areas has been treated by this Council as a shared burden but the ledger tells a very different story."
He flicked his wrist, zooming in on the ammunition pipelines feeding the frontier forts.

"Currently, the Republic of Columbia underwrites forty-two percent of all heavy ordnance deployed along the permafrost defense trench," Vanderbilt stated, looking directly around the circle, daring any of the other eight rulers to contradict him. "We manufacture ninety percent of the high-velocity tungsten penetrators... We supply sixty percent of the kinetic shield capacitors and over the last three quarters, my government has absorbed nearly four hundred billion Spirit credits in unpaid tariff differentials just to keep the rail-freighters rolling through the winter storms."
He turned his square jaw back toward the King with his expression hardening into cold defiance.

"Now, we sit here today and watch House Sterling receive an exclusive state-backed monopoly over northern foundry construction," Vanderbilt continued, casting a sharp venomous glance at Lohan Sterling, who sat serenely three chairs away, smoothing the silver embroidery of his sleeve. "We watch the United Hegemony receive a twenty-year blanket exemption from imperial maritime duties... Yet Columbia is expected to continue footing the bill for the perimeter’s ammunition reserves without a single adjustment to our raw ether import quotas. That is not an alliance, Majesty."
He took a deep breath.
"...That is an extraction."
The room held its breath.

To speak so bluntly about money in front of the Throne especially after the King had just demonstrated his absolute power of Destruction moments earlier... required either arrogance or immense structural leverage.
Vanderbilt had the leverage.

If Columbia decided to halt its rail-freighters for even two weeks, the northern defense perimeter would run out of high-caliber artillery shells, and Tsar Volkov’s soldiers would be forced to fight Tier-4 frost-giants with bayonets and bare fists.
The King listened without interrupting as he tapped his index finger against his knee... the knee that Kiera wasn’t sitting on.
TAP!
"A compelling presentation, Julian," the King said softly. "You speak as if Columbia manufactures those shells out of civic charity."
The King’s lips curled into a thin smile that made the hairs on the back of Aki’s neck prickle.

"Let us correct the ledger," the King continued, his deep voice slicing clean through the corporate rhetoric. "Columbia manufactures forty-two percent of the northern perimeter’s ordnance because the Throne grants your republic an exclusive zero-tax import corridor for raw abyssal bauxite directly through the central leylines... You sell those tungsten shells back to the northern garrisons at a thirty-four percent markup over baseline fabrication costs. Your domestic syndicates netted over one point two trillion credits in gross dividend payouts last year alone from that ’unpaid tariff differential.’"
Vanderbilt’s jaw twitched, but he held his ground.
"The risks of processing abyssal ore are astronomical, Sire—"

"The Crown does not barter with its arsenals," the King interrupted, his voice dropping into a tone that made the glass flutes on the sideboards ring like tuning forks. "However... I acknowledge the logistical strain upon your western rail networks. Therefore, the Crown will settle the subsidy dispute here and now."
The King gestured casually with his left hand, and a royal cipher stamped itself directly over Vanderbilt’s golden projection, turning the text a deep royal blue.

"The Republic of Columbia’s import quota for refined ether silt will be increased by fifteen percent for the next three fiscal cycles," the King decreed. "In exchange, Columbia will immediately relinquish its proprietary patent locks on the Mark II heavy artillery breeches, transferring the manufacturing schematics directly to House Sterling’s new automated foundries in the northern rail-head... The supply line will be unified. Your profit margins will remain protected, and the perimeter will remain armed. The matter is now closed."
Vanderbilt stared at the blue royal seal hovering in the air.
His eyes flickered with rapid calculation.

A fifteen percent increase in refined ether silt was worth billions on the commercial energy exchange... more than enough to offset the loss of the artillery patent locks, especially since his domestic factories were already pivoting toward high-tier energy weaponry.
The Columbian President slowly lowered his hands, dipping his head in a stiff respectful nod.
"Columbia accepts the terms of the Crown," Vanderbilt said with his voice tightening. "The rail-freighters will continue to run without delay."
"Good," the King murmured with his eyes half-lidded. "Then let us move—"
"There is, however... one additional matter, Majesty."
The King stopped. His eyebrows drew together by a millimeter as the temperature around the dais instantly dropped.
"Julian," the King said, his tone entirely devoid of warmth. "You are testing the limits of my afternoon."
Vanderbilt did not back down.
His broad face flushed a dark mottled crimson with the corporate statesman giving way to an enraged humiliated patriarch.
He turned his heavy head with his eyes burning with undisguised venom as his gaze locked onto the lower guest arc... straight onto Aki.

"It is not a matter of state finance, Sire," Vanderbilt rumbled, his voice shaking with tightly suppressed fury. "It is a matter of basic conduct and roya discipline. Less than an hour ago, in the Grand Rotunda outside these very doors, my only son... Julian Vanderbilt Junior, the recognized heir to the Columbian Executive Board was brutally assaulted."
