"For the past seven fiscal years," Vanderbilt said, his voice ringing with the authority of a boardroom predator, "the defense of the northern perimeter line... the barrier holding the ice-abominations of the upper trench from flooding the civilized areas has been treated by this Council as a shared burden but the ledger tells a very different story."
He flicked his wrist, zooming in on the ammunition pipelines feeding the frontier forts.

"Currently, the Republic of Columbia underwrites forty-two percent of all heavy ordnance deployed along the permafrost defense trench," Vanderbilt stated, looking directly around the circle, daring any of the other eight rulers to contradict him.
"We manufacture ninety percent of the high-velocity tungsten penetrators...

We supply sixty percent of the kinetic shield capacitors and over the last three quarters, my government has absorbed nearly four hundred billion Spirit credits in unpaid tariff differentials just to keep the rail-freighters rolling through the winter storms."
He turned his square jaw back toward the King with his expression hardening into cold defiance.

"Now, we sit here today and watch House Sterling receive an exclusive state-backed monopoly over northern foundry construction," Vanderbilt continued, casting a sharp venomous glance at Lohan Sterling, who sat serenely three chairs away, smoothing the silver embroidery of his sleeve.
"We watch the United Hegemony receive a twenty-year blanket exemption from imperial maritime duties...
Yet Columbia is expected to continue footing the bill for the perimeter’s ammunition reserves without a single adjustment to our raw ether import quotas.
That is not an alliance, Majesty."
He took a deep breath.
"...That is an extraction."
The room held its breath.

To speak so bluntly about money in front of the Throne especially after the King had just demonstrated his absolute power of Destruction moments earlier... required either arrogance or immense structural leverage.
Vanderbilt had the leverage.

If Columbia decided to halt its rail-freighters for even two weeks, the northern defense perimeter would run out of high-caliber artillery shells, and Tsar Volkov’s soldiers would be forced to fight Tier-4 frost-giants with bayonets and bare fists.
The King listened without interrupting as he tapped his index finger against his knee... the knee that Kiera wasn’t sitting on.
TAP!
"A compelling presentation, Julian," the King said softly.
"You speak as if Columbia manufactures those shells out of civic charity."
The King’s lips curled into a thin smile that made the hairs on the back of Aki’s neck prickle.
"Let us correct the ledger," the King continued, his deep voice slicing clean through the corporate rhetoric.

"Columbia manufactures forty-two percent of the northern perimeter’s ordnance because the Throne grants your republic an exclusive zero-tax import corridor for raw abyssal bauxite directly through the central leylines...
You sell those tungsten shells back to the northern garrisons at a thirty-four percent markup over baseline fabrication costs.
Your domestic syndicates netted over one point two trillion credits in gross dividend payouts last year alone from that ’unpaid tariff differential.’"
Vanderbilt’s jaw twitched, but he held his ground.
"The risks of processing abyssal ore are astronomical, Sire—"
"The Crown does not barter with its arsenals," the King interrupted, his voice dropping into a tone that made the glass flutes on the sideboards ring like tuning forks.
"However...
I acknowledge the logistical strain upon your western rail networks.
Therefore, the Crown will settle the subsidy dispute here and now."
The King gestured casually with his left hand, and a royal cipher stamped itself directly over Vanderbilt’s golden projection, turning the text a deep royal blue.
"The Republic of Columbia’s import quota for refined ether silt will be increased by fifteen percent for the next three fiscal cycles," the King decreed.

"In exchange, Columbia will immediately relinquish its proprietary patent locks on the Mark II heavy artillery breeches, transferring the manufacturing schematics directly to House Sterling’s new automated foundries in the northern rail-head...
The supply line will be unified.
Your profit margins will remain protected, and the perimeter will remain armed.
The matter is now closed."
Vanderbilt stared at the blue royal seal hovering in the air.
His eyes flickered with rapid calculation.

A fifteen percent increase in refined ether silt was worth billions on the commercial energy exchange... more than enough to offset the loss of the artillery patent locks, especially since his domestic factories were already pivoting toward high-tier energy weaponry.
The Columbian President slowly lowered his hands, dipping his head in a stiff respectful nod.
"Columbia accepts the terms of the Crown," Vanderbilt said with his voice tightening.
"The rail-freighters will continue to run without delay."
"Good," the King murmured with his eyes half-lidded.
"Then let us move—"
"There is, however... one additional matter, Majesty."
The King stopped.
His eyebrows drew together by a millimeter as the temperature around the dais instantly dropped.
"Julian," the King said, his tone entirely devoid of warmth.
"You are testing the limits of my afternoon."
Vanderbilt did not back down.
His broad face flushed a dark mottled crimson with the corporate statesman giving way to an enraged humiliated patriarch.
He turned his heavy head with his eyes burning with undisguised venom as his gaze locked onto the lower guest arc... straight onto Aki.
"It is not a matter of state finance, Sire," Vanderbilt rumbled, his voice shaking with tightly suppressed fury.
"It is a matter of basic conduct and roya discipline.
Less than an hour ago, in the Grand Rotunda outside these very doors, my only son...
Julian Vanderbilt Junior, the recognized heir to the Columbian Executive Board was brutally assaulted."

chapters.title: Chapter 535: The Exhibition of Succession [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: A collective sharp intake of breath hissed through the hall.
Up in the mezzanine, Valerius Sterling choked on his breath as his armored elbow slipped off the railing with a loud clank.
Beside him, Seraphina Bloom didn’t move, but her crimson eyes flared with sudden mocking amusement.
Down at the Grand Table, Lohan Sterling’s head turned sharply.

The Patriarch of House Sterling didn’t look at Vanderbilt as his cold eyes flicked straight up toward the mezzanine, locking onto his blonde armored son with an expression that could have frozen boiling oil.
Valerius immediately looked down at his boots, pretending to inspect a scratch on his mythril greaves.
On the other side, Matriarch Etilga Bloom did the exact opposite.
The fiery red-haired woman leaned back in her star-iron chair, crossing her legs beneath her crimson silk robes with her chest puffing out with blatant unapologetic pride.

Her lips curved into a wicked grin as she caught her daughter Seraphina’s eye up in the gallery, offering a tiny approving nod that practically screamed a lot of words but Seraphina knew what she meant.
’Good girl.’
Vanderbilt’s voice rose, vibrating with outrage.

"My boy was surrounded, provoked, and physically brutalized! His pelvic girdle was shattered by a blunt impact, and his internal organs suffered severe concussive hemorrhaging. He is currently lying in an emergency regeneration tank in the medical ward, breathing through a synthetic lung, while the scions responsible sit comfortably in your galleries!"
Vanderbilt slammed his fist onto the marble again.
BANG!

"Valerius Sterling threw the strike and so did Seraphina Bloom as not only did she do that but she also drew a weapon and threatened an official diplomatic envoy but the instigator... the woman who authorized the violence, who stood by and commanded the attack under the guise of royal authority was your own daughter!"
Vanderbilt thrust a thick trembling finger directly at Aki.
"The First Princess!"
The entire amphitheater turned as more than five hundred pairs of eyes pivoted like synchronized searchlights, pinning Aki to her low-tier seat.
Aki’s stomach plummeted into a cold bottomless abyss.
She kept her spine straight as an arrow with her hands folded over her velvet lap, but inside her chest, her heart was hammering with sickening violence.

She had known Vanderbilt wouldn’t let it go, it was obvious the boy’s father would demand blood but hearing the supreme leader of a global superpower openly denounce her before the entire World Council, demanding her head as if she were a common delinquent, felt like having a bucket of freezing ditch-water dumped over her bare skin.

’Here it comes,’ Aki thought with the terror rising in her throat like bile. ’This is what I was afraid of... My authority is completely hollow. I have no core, I have no army and now the wolves know it.’
She looked at her father.

She looked at the King, desperately searching that carved-marble profile for even the faintest flicker of parental defense... a single word, a sharp rebuke, an imperial declaration that no foreign president had the right to drag his firstborn daughter through the dirt.
The King didn’t even look down at her.

He sat there with his heavy sapphire eyes resting on Vanderbilt with cold impenetrable detachment and beside him, Princess Kiera tilted her head as her amber-gold eyes flicked toward Aki with an expression that was impossible to read...
It was neither cruel nor sympathetic, but utterly distant, like a traveler watching a stray dog limp across an alleyway.
"Julian," the King spoke, his voice dangerously flat. "You bring schoolyard brawls into the Great Assembly Chamber."

"My son’s spine was fractured, Majesty!" Vanderbilt bellowed, his face dark with blood. "This was not a schoolyard brawl! It was an unprovoked attack on a sovereign delegation! I demand formal compensation! I demand that the Sterling and Bloom houses face diplomatic censure, and I demand that the First Princess be stripped of her diplomatic immunity and placed under formal house arrest until an official inquiry is concluded!"
The silence in the room was absolute.
Aki felt the blood drain from her face.
’House arrest... Stripped of her immunity...?’
If she was locked in a tower, she would never see the light of day again.
She would be completely erased from the court, buried alive while Kiera took every scrap of her life.
’I know you don’t like me but still...’
She waited for the King to strike Vanderbilt down.
’This is a disrespect to your royal name right...?’
She waited for the void-light to flare in his eyes, to turn the Columbian President into dust for daring to demand the arrest of a royal princess.
’Don’t you love your royal reputation...?’
It didn’t happen.
The King merely drummed his fingers against the celestial marble.
TAP! TAP! TAP!
"Hold that thought, Julian," the King said.
The words were so casual and so completely dismissive that Vanderbilt actually blinked in confusion.
"Sire...?"

"I said, hold that thought," the King repeated, his voice dropping into a quiet icy tone that brooked no further argument. "We shall address the conduct of the youth and make do on your grievances in due time but the World Council does not halt the machinery of global security to debate broken pelvic bones so sit down."
Vanderbilt’s mouth pressed into a thin white line.
His chest heaved and his fingers clenching into fists, but the crushing weight of the King’s aura was already pressing down upon his shoulders like a mountain of lead.
Slowly, the Columbian President sank back into his high star-iron chair, his eyes shooting a final murderous glare toward Aki.
Aki sat frozen, her breath coming in shallow silent sips.

’He didn’t defend me,’ the realization echoed through her skull. ’He didn’t deny it... He didn’t tell Vanderbilt to watch his tongue... He just told him to "hold that thought." Is he going to use me as a bargaining chip? When the meeting is over, he’ll throw me to the Columbians to balance the ledger?’
Every shred of safety she had ever clung to as a princess had just dissolved into thin air.
From this moment on, every noble house, every foreign envoy, every opportunistic vulture in the capital knew that the First Princess was unprotected.
...She was fair game.
The King swept his gaze across the Grand Table, deliberately erasing the incident from the docket.
"Now," the King said, his voice rising, filling the vaulted dome with authority. "Let us address the foundational purpose of this emergency summit... The matter of the Northern Rift."
The atmosphere in the room snapped instantly back to razor-sharp tension.
Every head of state sat up straight.

The scribes in the mezzanine gripped their styluses, and the holographic arrays above the center of the ring shifted, projecting a massive sweeping topographic map of the fractured northern continental border.

"As this assembly is well aware," the King explained with his hand tracing the jagged red fracture line cutting across the map, "six weeks ago, a massive shift of the planet stabilized an expanse of over forty thousand square kilometers within the Sovereign Realm’s transitional corridor... It sits directly between the borders of the Republic of Columbia and the Tsardom of Borealis."
He zoomed the display in, revealing dense pulsing clusters of deep purple and crystalline silver beneath the digital frost.

"The initial orbital scans have confirmed what our diviners predicted," the King continued. "The sector contains the largest unrefined deposit of void-iron, spirit-core silt, and primal ether crystals discovered in the last forty years... A resource reserve capable of supplying the defensive armaments of the civilized world for the next half-century."
The eyes of every ruler around the circle burned with naked ravenous hunger.

"Under normal royal charters," the King said, "contested transition corridors are partitioned based on geographic proximity... However, both Columbia and Borealis claim exclusive historic drilling rights to the subterranean leylines feeding that rift and neither nation has shown a willingness to compromise."
"Because there is nothing to compromise!" Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov roared, standing up so violently that his star-iron chair screeched against the obsidian floor.
SCREEECH!
The massive bear of a man pointed a thick calloused finger at the holographic map.

"The northern trench has been watered with the blood of Borealis soldiers for five generations!" Volkov bellowed with his voice shaking the mezzanine glass. "Our ice-fortresses hold the perimeter! Our men freeze in the mud while Columbian mining conglomerates sit in air-conditioned suites eight hundred leagues away, trading paper shares... That void-iron sits on our tectonic shelf so it belongs to the Tsardom by right of blood and iron!"

"Your tectonic shelf was drawn on outdated maps eighty years ago, Nikolai!" Vanderbilt shouted back, jumping to his feet as his prior grievances were instantly forgotten in the face of trillions of credits in raw minerals. "The entire underground drainage of that rift flows directly into the Columbian western aquifer! If you drill those void-iron veins with your primitive heavy-bore rigs, you will fracture the mana leylines and poison our domestic water reserves! Columbia has already invested six hundred billion credits in non-invasive acoustic extraction platforms so the corridor belongs under Columbian administrative jurisdiction!"

"Non-invasive?!" King Zhao of the United Hegemony cut in, his ancient dragon-embroidered sleeves fluttering as he stood. "You call setting up three hundred mechanized dredging platforms non-invasive, Julian?! If Columbia takes that rift, the western trade winds will carry the ether runoff straight into the Shogunate ocean trenches! It will disrupt our maritime harvesters... The Hegemony demands a thirty percent partition of all extracted ether silt to offset ecological damage!"

"And what of Europa?!" Chancellor Henri de Montmirail argued, his wire-rimmed glasses slipping down his nose as he slammed his treaty ledger onto the marble. "The Alpine trade agreements explicitly state that any newly discovered transit corridors must be subject to open-market guild bidding! You cannot simply carve up the Sovereign Realm like a slaughtered hog between two border nations!"

"Silence, you ink-stained bureaucrat!" Volkov roared back with frost-mana crackling across his massive knuckles. "If Europa wants void-iron, pick up an axe and come dig it out of the permafrost yourselves!"
The Great Assembly Chamber collapsed into chaos.
The rulers of humanity were screaming at each other across the Grand Table with envoys shouting over the railings.

The Indus mages were chanting defensive mantras as their psionic auras flared, the Albion Prime Minister was banging his star-iron cane against the floor like a madman, and Vanderbilt looked like he was about to physically leap across the celestial marble to strangle the Tsar of Borealis.
The King watched the brawl unfold with cold simmering disgust as he opened his mouth to speak.
"Gentlemen—"
His voice was instantly swallowed as the deafening roar of nine sovereign delegations screaming over mineral rights and trade routes drowned out the Throne entirely.
The King’s hand clenched into a fist against the armrest.
CREAK!

The star-iron armrest groaned, the ancient metal warping under the terrifying force of his grip as a dark suffocating shadow began to bleed into the King’s sapphire irises with the void-light of Destruction flickering at the edges of his pupils—
"QUIET."
The word didn’t come from the King.
It came from the far northern arc of the table, from the shadowed bench where the seven World Council Heads sat.
VOOOOOOOM!
A terrifying suffocating eruption of pure boiling crimson mana blasted outward from the central hooded figure.
The crimson aura wasn’t hot like fire... it was viscous and heavy as liquid iron, expanding in a concussive wave that washed over every inch of the amphitheater.
WHAM!
The overwhelming spiritual gravity slammed into the nine rulers like a falling ceiling.
Tsar Volkov was physically shoved back into his chair with the breath punched out of his massive chest.
Vanderbilt’s knees buckled, forcing him down into his seat as his paper ledgers scattered across the floor.
Up in the mezzanine, dozens of junior aides dropped to their knees, clutching their throats, gasping for air as the crimson light bathed the obsidian walls in a terrifying bloody haze.
It was a crushing mountain of pure power... a spiritual presence so absurdly vast and so violently refined that it simply froze the blood in everyone’s veins.
Aki gripped the arms of her chair with her vision swimming as the crimson mana pressed against her chest like an iron plate.
Even without a Lord core, she could feel the terrifying weight of it.
At the Council bench, the hooded figure sat perfectly still.
She wore heavy midnight-silk robes woven with anti-divination wards, her face completely obscured by a smooth featureless mask of polished white porcelain.
Only her hands were visible and they were pale with elegant fingers resting lightly over the edge of the stone.
"You bicker like stray dogs over a scrap of meat," the Council Member spoke.
Her voice was unmistakably female as it echoed through the crimson haze chillingly.

"Need I remind you that not only do you sit before the Throne but you sit within the inner sanctum of the World Council... If you cannot conduct the business of humanity with dignity, I will strip the voices from your throats and settle the borders myself."
The silence in the room was terrified as even Tsar Volkov didn’t dare utter a syllable.
He sat back with his chest heaving and his eyes wide as he stared at the porcelain mask.
The female Council Member slowly withdrew her aura.
FSHHHH!
The crimson mana contracted, swirling back into the folds of her midnight robes like mist receding into a cave, leaving the room cold and dead quiet once more.
She settled back into her high-backed seat, folding her hands into her sleeves as if nothing had happened.
The King released his grip on the warped armrest.
He didn’t look back at the Council bench, nor did he mention her name as he merely offered a quiet respectful dip of his head toward her station.
"Thank you," the King murmured softly.
He turned his gaze back toward the nine trembling heads of state.

"Arguing will not get you anywhere," the King said, his voice sounding calm for someone that almost wanted to kill all of them moments ago. "A war between Columbia and Borealis over a mining corridor would crack the regional leylines and invite the very extinction we seek to prevent. The Crown will not permit it..."
The leaders exchanged nervous bewildered glances.
’What does he have in mind...?’ Aki thought, her eyes darting between her father and the silent Council Heads.
She remembered the guest protocols sent out three weeks ago.

Her father hadn’t just summoned the heads of state and their financial ministers... The decree had explicitly mandated that every delegation bring their top advisors, their young relatives, and their recognized heirs.
Even High Marshal-President Da Silva, who had no children of her own, had brought her twenty-two-year-old younger sister along with the Amazonian retinue.
Was this why? Had the King planned this from the very beginning?
The King’s mouth curved into a slow, deliberate smile.
"If the elders cannot agree on how to divide the earth," the King announced, his voice filling the hall with grand authority, "then the youth shall decide it for them."
A collective rustle ran through the mezzanine.

"Here, within the fortified grounds of the Citadel," the King continued, "the Crown shall host the Exhibition of Succession... A martial showcase taking place directly within a stabilized sector of the Sovereign Realm’s transitional zone and the preparations have already been completed by the Royal Engineers."

It was a crushing mountain of pure power... a spiritual presence so absurdly vast and so violently refined that it simply froze the blood in everyone’s veins.
Aki gripped the arms of her chair with her vision swimming as the crimson mana pressed against her chest like an iron plate.
Even without a Lord core, she could feel the terrifying weight of it.
At the Council bench, the hooded figure sat perfectly still.
She wore heavy midnight-silk robes woven with anti-divination wards, her face completely obscured by a smooth featureless mask of polished white porcelain.
Only her hands were visible and they were pale with elegant fingers resting lightly over the edge of the stone.
"You bicker like stray dogs over a scrap of meat," the Council Member spoke.
Her voice was unmistakably female as it echoed through the crimson haze chillingly.
"Need I remind you that not only do you sit before the Throne but you sit within the inner sanctum of the World Council...
If you cannot conduct the business of humanity with dignity, I will strip the voices from your throats and settle the borders myself."
The silence in the room was terrified as even Tsar Volkov didn’t dare utter a syllable.
He sat back with his chest heaving and his eyes wide as he stared at the porcelain mask.
The female Council Member slowly withdrew her aura.
FSHHHH!
The crimson mana contracted, swirling back into the folds of her midnight robes like mist receding into a cave, leaving the room cold and dead quiet once more.
She settled back into her high-backed seat, folding her hands into her sleeves as if nothing had happened.
The King released his grip on the warped armrest.
He didn’t look back at the Council bench, nor did he mention her name as he merely offered a quiet respectful dip of his head toward her station.
"Thank you," the King murmured softly.
He turned his gaze back toward the nine trembling heads of state.
"Arguing will not get you anywhere," the King said, his voice sounding calm for someone that almost wanted to kill all of them moments ago.
"A war between Columbia and Borealis over a mining corridor would crack the regional leylines and invite the very extinction we seek to prevent.
The Crown will not permit it..."
The leaders exchanged nervous bewildered glances.
’What does he have in mind...?’ Aki thought, her eyes darting between her father and the silent Council Heads.
She remembered the guest protocols sent out three weeks ago.
Her father hadn’t just summoned the heads of state and their financial ministers...
The decree had explicitly mandated that every delegation bring their top advisors, their young relatives, and their recognized heirs.
Even High Marshal-President Da Silva, who had no children of her own, had brought her twenty-two-year-old younger sister along with the Amazonian retinue.
Was this why?
Had the King planned this from the very beginning?
The King’s mouth curved into a slow, deliberate smile.
"If the elders cannot agree on how to divide the earth," the King announced, his voice filling the hall with grand authority, "then the youth shall decide it for them."
A collective rustle ran through the mezzanine.
"Here, within the fortified grounds of the Citadel," the King continued, "the Crown shall host the Exhibition of Succession...
A martial showcase taking place directly within a stabilized sector of the Sovereign Realm’s transitional zone and the preparations have already been completed by the Royal Engineers."

chapters.title: Chapter 536: Lord Vespera’s Presence [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: He swept his gaze over the tiered seating where the young heirs and scions sat.

"The rules are simple. Each of the Nine Major Powers may enter two representatives. They must be blood relatives, recognized heirs, or sworn vassals of your respective houses, aged twenty-five or below. The nation whose champion stands victorious at the end of the exhibition shall receive the exclusive unhindered primary drilling rights to the contested northern rift for the next five years."
The room went completely still as the rulers absorbed the decree... What the King wanted was a tournament.
A blood-showcase of the next generation to settle a multi-trillion-credit territorial dispute.

"Furthermore," the King added, his tone taking on an unusually conversational edge, "this exhibition will not be conducted behind closed doors. It shall be broadcast live across the global networks. The Crown intends to get in on this... ’streaming’ phenomenon... that seems to dominate the civilian communications sphere these days."
The delegates blinked in utter bewilderment.
A stream? The Supreme King of the World hosting a live internet broadcast of a high-stakes Lord tournament?
Before anyone could process the absurdity of it, Princess Kiera shifted upon his lap.
Her face lit up with a brilliant smile, her golden eyes sparkling with genuine girlish excitement as she looked up at the King’s severe profile.

"Father... really? A stream?" Kiera asked, her voice sounding melodic and carrying cleanly across the quiet pit. "Streams are like... one of my favorite things to watch! The duels, the live chat feeds, the ranking ladders... it’s so exciting!"
The King looked down at her and right there, in front of the entire governing body of the human race, the terrifying tyrant of the world smiled.
He raised his heavy hand and affectionately patted Kiera on the head, his fingers smoothing her sapphire hair with tender care.
"Then you shall have your stream, my dear," the King murmured warmly.
Aki felt a sharp burning knot tighten in her throat.

’Look at that,’ Aki thought with her nails digging into her palms until she felt the skin break beneath her velvet gown. ’He doesn’t care about media engagement... He doesn’t give a damn about global streaming culture either. He’s doing the entire thing just to indulge his favored daughter.’
Essentially... the whole world is dancing to her tune.
The King looked back up, the warmth vanishing instantly from his face as he addressed the noble houses.

"In the interest of true competition," the King declared, "the invitation is not limited strictly to the Nine Powers... Both House Sterling and House Bloom are granted entry into the bracket. Should a scion of either noble house emerge victorious, the northern drilling rights shall be transferred to their respective family enterprises."
Lohan Sterling’s eyes flared with intense corporate hunger, while Etilga Bloom’s grin widened, her ruby eyes blazing with excitement.
Up in the mezzanine, Seraphina reached down, resting her palm against the hilts of her twin hunting daggers, while Valerius let out another long resigned groan.
Then, the King’s sapphire gaze slowly turned but he didn’t look at Alexander.
His eyes drifted down to the lowest tier of the royal guest arc, locking directly onto Aki.
Aki flinched.
It was a microscopic movement, barely an eighth of an inch, but her entire body went ice-cold.
The King was staring straight at her with his eyes steady and lacking any sort of pity.
’No...’ Aki’s mind screamed, her pulse spiking into pure panic. ’What is he doing? Why is he looking at me?!’
She was Unawakened and she had no core but she was twenty-five years old.
...The exact upper age limit of the tournament.

’Is he going to put me in this... tournament?’ the horrifying thought exploded behind her eyes like an artillery shell. ’He’s going to put me in the sand against Awakened monsters to settle Vanderbilt’s grievance... He’s going to let them slaughter me on a live global broadcast just to clear my name off the ledger—’
The King drew a breath with his lips parting to speak.
"THE MEETING IS IN SESSION! YOU ARE NOT ALLOW—"
A muffled panicked shout echoed from beyond the massive reinforced double doors at the primary diplomatic entrance.
BAM!
The sound of a heavy combat boot striking titanium rang through the vestibule.
Before the twelve World Council Enforcers stationed at the threshold could even raise their halberds, the colossal five-ton star-iron blast doors were casually shoved open.
CREEEEEEAK... SLAM!
The heavy doors hit the reinforced stone stops with a deafening shuddering crash that sent a shockwave vibrating through the floorboards.
The entire Great Assembly Chamber snapped its attention toward the shattered entrance.
Fifty high-tier rifles came up in unison with the targeting lasers painting the smoke-filled doorway with a web of red beams; however a figure stepped through the threshold.
"Gods above..." a smooth feminine voice complained, echoing lazily through the room. "You people really need to oil those hinges. That was embarrassing."
The smoke cleared and standing at the top of the grand marble staircase was a woman.
She was lithe and breathtakingly striking, possessing a pale, flawless complexion framed by shoulder-length jet-black hair that fell in casual, slightly messy waves around her sharp jawline.
Resting on the bridge of her straight nose was a pair of thin wire-rimmed reading glasses that gave her an infuriatingly calm air.
She wore a bespoke double-breasted suit of charcoal-black wool, tailored to perfection, with crisp white cuffs and a loosened black silk tie resting against her collar.
Her right arm was casually extended, holding a half-eaten paper bag of roasted nuts while her left sleeve was completely empty.

The dark wool fabric of the left arm was neatly pinned against her ribcage, the empty cuff drifting lightly in the air currents blowing from the ventilation flues and making her silhouette look amazing.
Beneath the clear lenses of her glasses, her eyes were glowing.
WHOOSH!

They were a deep terrifying violet that pulsed with a spiritual power that made the air within five paces of her leather dress shoes visibly warping, bending the white hall light into jagged purple prisms.
She simply raised her single right hand, offering a lazy two-fingered wave to the five hundred frozen petrified people staring at her in dead silence.

"Afternoon, everyone," Kara said, she was completely unbothered by the fact that she had just breached the most secure room on the planet. "Sorry about the door. You can call me Lord Vespera... or Kara White from Valoria City. Whichever one rolls off the tongue easier..."
Aki’s jaw dropped. The breath died entirely in her throat, her blue eyes wide as dinner plates.
’Silas..?!’
Up in the mezzanine, Seraphina Bloom’s ruby eyes dilated into tiny pinpricks of pure shock with her grip freezing solid over her daggers.
Beside her, Valerius Sterling’s jaw hung low.
At the Grand Table, the King slowly rose from his throne.
His sapphire eyes locked onto the black-haired woman on the stairs with his immense suffocating presence rising like a tidal wave.
"Lord Vespera," the King spoke, his voice carrying the weight of an angry god. "You enter the World Council unannounced... You breach the outer perimeter and you arrive alone."
The King’s gaze flickered past her shoulder, looking into the empty dust-choked corridor behind her.
"Where is Lord Sky?"
Kara stopped at the top of the stairs, popping a roasted nut into her mouth and chewing slowly.
She pushed her glasses up her nose with her right thumb, letting out a small tired sigh.

"Yeah, about that," Kara said, her voice sounding flat and deadpan. "Lord Sky won’t be joining us today... He came down with an extraordinarily tough sickness about several hours ago. He’s terribly bedridden with high fever and chills."
Kara let out a sigh.
"Oh what a tragedy~"
’Well, she did say that she needed to go on a date somewhere... They definitely don’t need to know that,’ Silas thought dryly.
Kara stepped down the marble stairs with her single right hand tucking into her trouser pocket as her leather dress shoes tapped rhythmically against the stone.
Click! Click! Click!

She casually strolled past the frozen guards, completely ignoring the King’s rising aura, her violet eyes scanning the seating arrangements until they landed on the western arc... specifically, on Chancellor Henri de Montmirail of Europa.

"Oh, hey, Chancellor," Kara said, offering a friendly familiar wave with her right hand toward the bespectacled diplomat. "Good to see you. Valoria City’s infrastructure has been holding up pretty well lately. Thanks for funding the new transit line out in Sector Two, by the way. Made getting to the high-speed rail much easier!"
Chancellor Montmirail blinked, his face flushing a bright furious crimson as the sudden blistering spotlight of the entire world swung directly onto him.
"Ah... Y-Yes, of course, Lord Vespera!" Montmirail stammered, frantically adjusting his glasses. "Europa always prioritizes civic infrastructure for its... distinguished citizens!"
Instantly, seven heads of state turned, shooting burning glares straight at the Europa delegation.
The United Hegemony had just received massive trade concessions because of an imperial bastard, but this?
Having the most terrifying viral Awakened on the planet... humanity’s supposed sole Gold Core born, raised, and casually paying taxes within Europa’s borders?
That was a checkmate of astronomical proportions!
If Blessed Land formally aligned with Europa, the global balance of power would shatter overnight.
Kara walked over to the foot of the Grand Table, stopping directly in front of the high chair draped in violet velvet marked [LORD VESPERA].
She pulled her right hand from her pocket, grabbed the back of the star-iron chair, and pulled it out, sinking into the plush velvet cushions with a long sigh.
"Haah~ Good to be here..."
She leaned back, crossed her long legs, and let out a tiny delicate yawn, covering her mouth with her right knuckles.

"Lord Vespera," Magistrate Bloom boomed from the Council bench, his voice laced with cold fury. "An imperial summons is scheduled to the minute! You are nearly an hour past the opening bell! What conceivable justification do you have for delaying the governing bodies of humanity?!"
Kara tilted her head, looking up at the Magistrate through her wire-rimmed lenses with an expression of mild deadpan annoyance.
"I overslept," Kara said bluntly.
Aki felt a drop of cold sweat roll down the back of her neck.
’She... she overslept?!’

"And honestly?" Kara continued, gesturing casually with her right hand toward the high ceiling. "I didn’t even have a proper suit for this circus... I spent forty minutes running through three different boutiques in the commercial district just trying to find a double-breasted cut that didn’t look completely ridiculous with only one sleeve. Plus, you people didn’t even book me a private transport. Do you have any idea how many administrative security checkpoints I had to sit through while I rented a plane? How did you expect me to get here on time?"
The entire chamber stared at her in stunned disbelief and Aki stared at the black-haired woman with her heart doing somersaults behind her ribs.

’Silas is being blatantly disrespectful,’ Aki realized, a mixture of terror and hysterical amusement bubbling in her chest. ’In front of the King... In front of the World Council... She’s treating the most terrifying summit in human history like an annoying trip to the post office.’
But as Aki looked around the room, she saw the truth dawn on the faces of the other rulers.
Nobody was moving to strike her down.

Even the King, whose Destruction had atomized an Amazonian guard for a mere sideways glance twenty minutes ago, was simply standing there with his sapphire eyes narrowed, absorbing her words without raising a finger.
Because everyone in the room knew what she was worth.
...A Gold Core.
The apex of being a Lord. If she was truly what the world believed her to be, then normal laws, diplomatic protocols, and royal etiquette simply did not apply to her.
There was nothing they could legally or militarily do to touch her without risking a catastrophe of the highest order.
And she clearly knew it.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior let out a deep frustrated sigh.
’Why can’t these damned anomalies ever be obedient corporate assets who dance to the will of the markets?’ he thought, his jaw tightening as he stared across the floor.
Yet, as the quiet dragged on, a subtle cold skepticism began to bleed into the eyes of several rulers.
Tsar Volkov frowned with his heavy brow furrowing while King Zhao tilted his head, his eyes squinting through his white eyebrows.
Where was the pressure?
When the King spoke, the air turned to lead.
When the Council Member intervened, the room drowned in crimson gravity but Kara White was just sitting there in a tailored suit, eating roasted nuts out of a paper bag.

Sure, they could sense that she had mana... the purple glow in her eyes and the distortion around her shoulders proved she wasn’t an ordinary human but where was the suffocating spiritual signature of a Lord with a Gold Core?
Why couldn’t they feel the crushing weight of a core that supposedly surpassed the Purple rank?
Was she a fraud?
Had Blessed Land staged the entire Unmovable Wall broadcast using high-yield explosives and synthetic broadcast filters to fabricate a legend?
The King took a slow step forward, resting his hands heavily against the celestial marble of the table.

"Lord Vespera," the King spoke, his voice dropping into a dangerous rumble that vibrated through the floorboards. "You claim a seat at this table but diplomatic leverage in this chamber is not granted by reputation or public broadcasts... It is determined by the power of the core beating within your chest."
The King’s eyes locked onto her violet lenses intensely.
"Show this assembly what you are."
Kara looked at the King but she didn’t flinch, hell she didn’t look offended.
Her lips slowly curved into an amused smile.
"Right now?" Kara asked softly. "Before lunch?"
She let out another quiet resigned sigh, resting her single right elbow on the table.
"Fine but someone bring me a glass of wine first. Flying through those air corridors was remarkably dry."

A terrified junior attendant from the service station scrambled forward, his hands trembling so violently that the dark red sparkling wine sloshed against the rim of the crystal flute as he set it down before her.
Kara reached out with her right hand, taking the stem of the glass between two slender fingers.
She swirled the dark red liquid once... Twice then, she took a slow, leisurely sip.
CLINK!
She set the empty crystal flute down onto the marble coaster, running the tip of her tongue lightly across her lower lip to catch a stray drop of crimson wine.
Then, she exhaled.
"Sure..."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The world seemed to fracture inside the room as a detonation of pure suffocating golden erupted from her chest like a collapsing star.
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!

The reinforced quartz domed skylight fifty feet above shrieked with spiderweb fractures blooming across the glass and the hexagonal barriers surrounding the area instantly shattered, collapsing into rain of glittering blue sparks.
The more I write about the King Of The World, the more this guy pisses me off.... Haah...

She set the empty crystal flute down onto the marble coaster, running the tip of her tongue lightly across her lower lip to catch a stray drop of crimson wine.
Then, she exhaled.
"Sure..."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The world seemed to fracture inside the room as a detonation of pure suffocating golden erupted from her chest like a collapsing star.
CRACK!
CRACK!
CRACK!

The reinforced quartz domed skylight fifty feet above shrieked with spiderweb fractures blooming across the glass and the hexagonal barriers surrounding the area instantly shattered, collapsing into rain of glittering blue sparks.
The more I write about the King Of The World, the more this guy pisses me off....
Haah...

chapters.title: Chapter 537: We Need Her [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The golden light was so absurdly thick that the air physically turned into liquid pressure, slamming down upon every living soul in the Great Assembly Chamber like an oceanic trench collapsing inward.
"AGGGGGH!"
Up in the mezzanine, dozens of junior diplomats, guild scribes, and corporate analysts were instantly knocked unconscious with their eyes rolling back as they slumped over the brass railings.

Down at the Grand Table, Tsar Volkov’s massive bear-like frame was physically pinned to the back of his chair with the breath violently expelled from his lungs as his teeth rattled in his skull while Vanderbilt grabbed the edge of the table with both hands with his knuckles turning purple as the terrifying gravity forced his forehead toward the marble.
Even the hooded World Council Heads were forced back, their midnight robes whipping violently in the gravitational tempest.
Aki couldn’t breathe.
Her vision went black with her ribs groaning under a weight that felt like an entire continent resting on her collarbone and then, as suddenly as it had arrived...
SNAP!
The pressure vanished.

The golden light collapsed back into her chest in the span of a single heartbeat, leaving behind only the hysterical shrill of dying barrier alarms and the frantic gasping of five hundred terrified trembling people clutching their chests.
Kara White sat calmly in her violet-velvet chair.
She pushed her wire-rimmed glasses back up the bridge of her nose with a single unbothered finger, looking around the devastated gasping chamber with an amused smirk.
"So," Kara murmured, her smooth voice echoing through the deafening silence. "Is that enough?"
The King remained standing at the dais with his fingers digging deep into the celestial marble and his sapphire eyes wide, dilated with genuine shock.
Because everyone who had survived that single suffocating pulse knew the impossible truth.
Kara White... Lord Vespera... was not a fraud.
She was truly a Gold Core.

And from the dense multi-layered harmonic resonance of that golden eruption, she had already broken through the threshold... she was already standing firmly within the Second Phase of Core Refinement!
WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
The light in the air didn’t vanish though the pressure had dissipated.
It folded inward toward the center of the black-haired woman’s chest in a sharp implosive vacuum that made the deep obsidian flagstones beneath the amphitheater vibrate like struck anvils.
For four or five seconds after the last brilliant filament was swallowed back into the fabric of her tailored suit, nobody in the Great Assembly Chamber drew air.

In the mezzanine galleries, three junior administrative secretaries hung limp over the polished brass balustrades with their eyes rolled white into their skulls and their dropped styluses clattering rhythmically down the tiered stone risers before coming to rest in the gutters.
The King remained seated.

His broad star-iron-ringed fingers dug into the beveled lip of the celestial marble table, pressing with enough unconscious force to produce spiderweb hairline fractures across the polished white slab.
His deep eyes... usually looking cold and immovable remained wide, locked with intensity onto the woman seated in the violet-velvet chair.
Within the classified iron-bound archives of the Throne, the history of human awakening was recorded with obsessive chronological precision from the very first dawn following the Cataclysm.
Across those centuries of blood, ruined civilizations, and tectonic upheaval, humanity’s historical books had recorded precisely two Gold Cores.
The first was Odin.
He was a legendary figure who had walked the earth during the chaotic second generation, rising shortly after the founding World Council Heads had carved out their quarantine zones.
His awakening had not been an orderly progression through the standard spectrum of cores... It had been a violent phenomenon that the chroniclers of the old era could only describe as pure fantasy.

When he stood within the Pantheon, dozens of conflicting elemental affinities had ignited within his spiritual pathways simultaneously harmonizing into a singular gold core that instantly established him as the undisputed apex of mortal survival.
Yet the moment he descended into the Sovereign Realm, he vanished from human records.
He never ascended back into the mortal world or perhaps he had, once, to inspect the bloodied aftermath after the Novice Trials, but he had never shown his face before the governing bodies again.
Time flowed differently in the Sovereign Realm... down in those weird planes, where the spatial geometry bent back on itself, decades ran like water.
What had been several centuries for humanity had likely been thousands of years for Odin.

Down there, far beyond the reach of human communication relays and imperial diviners, he had ascended completely, taking the mantle of the God of Asgard... existing on the tier of a true deity, or perhaps standing even higher, towering above the primal horrors that ruled the outer dark.
The only reminder humanity had of that lineage was Thor.
Odin’s firstborn daughter and even she was an erratic unpredictable entity.
She claimed the title of Protector of Midgard, but the King of the World could count on one hand the number of times she had actually stepped forward to prevent a continental disaster.

Most of her time on the mortal plane was spent wandering the coastal trade cities, drinking herself into a stupor, and stuffing her stomach with mountain-high plates of roasted meats, sweet breads, and imported pastries.

She was a deity in her own right with her physical power alone capable of leveling city blocks with a flick of her wrist, but she treated the affairs of the World Council like ants squabbling over spilled sugar.

The King had never quite known whether her complete indifference was a deliberate insult from Odin for the ancient sins the royal house had committed during the early era, but he despised her all the same.
The second Gold Core was the First King.

The ancient patriarch of House Castellian and the founding progenitor whose brilliance had elevated their bloodline to the Throne and birthed the very Suppression Engines that kept the continents from sliding into the abyss.
Unlike Odin, the first Castellian had not been a warrior.
He was a scholar and an inventor who spent his days locked away in vaults surrounded by half-assembled clockwork, ether batteries, and runic blueprints.

In his personal journals, which were passed down through the royal line under unbroken blood-seals, the First King had described his Gold Core not as an engine of war, but as a curse of perception... A curse Of Knowledge.

He wrote that the core poured so much raw cosmic architecture into his brain that the simple act of thinking was agonizing like a constant burning migraine that felt as though his skull were being split open with an iron wedge.
Through that terrible unceasing clarity, he had designed the primary Suppression Engine and the nine regional sub-engines.
Yet he had perished shortly after humanity’s first great Citadel was assaulted during the early days of the Apocalypse.
A Tier-7 Black Dragon... an ancient calamity that modern rankers only read about in sealed bestiaries had breached the outer wards and leveled the capital.
The First King, having spent his entire life expanding his mind rather than reinforcing his physical combat shell, was wiped out in the initial blast wave.
His death, however, had not ended his legacy.
His research survived, preserved by his children.

It was the Second King who had taken those incomprehensible schematics and actually forged the Suppression Engines, anchoring them deep into the tectonic crust and saving the human species over the centuries that followed and with each dying breath of a monarch, the fundamental spark of that ancestral lineage was transferred into the next heir through the royal blood-rite.
When the authority had passed to the current King, he had inherited two distinct gifts... Destruction, and one other power that he had never once revealed to the World Council.
For decades, those gifts had bred silent, festering questions in his heart.

If the First King had possessed Destruction within that golden spark, why hadn’t he used it to atomize the Black Dragon? Why hadn’t his own father used it to secure dominance over the other eight nations?
And above all... what made a Gold Core so terrifyingly different?
The King’s fingers twitched against the celestial marble.
When Kara’s presence had detonated across the chamber a moment ago, his hand had trembled.
It was an imperceptible shake, completely hidden from the assembly, but he had felt it deep in his marrow.
She was strong.

She was not yet on his level since he had cultivated for a long time, bathing his soul pathways in the distilled ether of the deepest royal vaults but she was approaching the threshold with terrifying speed.

’Why are Gold Cores so inherently unfair?’ the King thought, his jaw setting so hard the tendon stood out like wire against his neck. ’The rest of humanity bleeds for decades to refine a single facet of a Purple Core, and this stray from the west reaches the Second Phase before she even learns how to dress for court...’

Down at the table, Kara leaned back into the plush violet velvet of her chair, letting out a long relaxed breath through her nose as she tapped the rim of her empty crystal glass with her single right forefinger.
CLINK!

"Hey," she said, her voice cutting through the ringing silence as she glanced toward the terrified serving staff huddled near the northern wall. "Are you going to pour another round, or do I have to ask the King to pass his pitcher? What does a girl have to do for some more good wine around here..."
The chamber slowly began to pull itself together as the dead silence gave way to the muted sounds of ragged breathing, boots shifting on the stone floor, and papers rustling on desks.
The rulers around the Grand Table forced their expressions into neutral dignified masks, though the sheen of cold sweat glistening along their temples betrayed them.
Every single person sitting at that marble slab was running the exact same calculation... Blessed Land must be bought.
A Gold Core was an existential deterrent.

If any one of the Nine Major Powers managed to tie Kara White to their standard... through marriage, trade treaties, land grants, or joint military charters... The global balance of power would irrevocably tilt in their favor!
The fact that she held citizenship in Europa meant nothing.
Independent rankers of her caliber didn’t give a damn about municipal borders, and Chancellor Montmirail’s flushed terrified face proved that Europa held zero administrative control over her.
She was a free agent holding the ultimate weapon.

’We need her,’ thought King Zhao of Shogya with his white beard trembling as his fingers traced the gold silk of his dragon robe. ’A Gold Core aligned with our deep-sea mining anchors would make the Hegemony untouchable...’

’Whatever she wants,’ Da Silva concluded internally, her dark feline eyes measuring Kara’s shoulders with a look. ’We offer her an honorary marshalcy in the Amazonian Vanguard and if she wants land, we carve out three provinces or how many she wants.’
Then, a dry grating sound broke the reverie.
TCH!
It was a scoff.
A sharp disrespectful click of the tongue that echoed across the quiet marble like a dropped wrench.
Every head at the table turned.
President Julian Vanderbilt Senior sat hunched forward with his charcoal suit soaked through with sweat at the armpits and his chest still heaving from the spiritual suffocation he had just endured.
Despite the terror that had forced him toward the table moments before, his broad square-jawed face had curdled into an expression of bitter disdain.

The humiliation of being pressed into the stone like a bug was eating away at his composure, and the sight of this girl treating the supreme summit of humanity like a cheap terrace cafe pushed his corporate arrogance past the breaking point.
He glared openly across the marble slab, his voice cutting through the hall with harsh abrasive venom.

"A Gold Core?" Vanderbilt sneered, the words tumbling out of his mouth in a loud bark that made the surrounding diplomats recoil in horror. "The world is expected to tremble before a miraculous anomaly, and what arrives? A crippled delinquent that sounds like she came from the Slums! We are told Gold Cores exist on an untouchable divine plane above mortal limitations... that a Second Phase refinement makes you the equal of a Lord in their third or fourth refinement stage! Yet look at you! You sit there with an empty sleeve pinned to your ribs! If you are so grand, so untouchable, why the hell are you missing an arm? You couldn’t even heal your own dam—"
CRUNCH!
Vanderbilt’s voice slammed to a dead halt.
The entire table paused and their eyes darting toward the violet chair in stunned disbelief.
Kara hadn’t flinched.
She hadn’t summoned a blade or blasted him into paste as she merely had her single right hand buried in the small brown paper bag she had smuggled past the security gates.

She had pulled out a large roasted hickory nut, tossed it casually into the air, caught it cleanly in her mouth right in the middle of his tirade, and bitten down with an audible sharp crack that echoed off the stone.
CRUNCH! CRUNCH!
She chewed slowly, unbothered by the guards still aiming their rifles at her perimeter, completely unfazed by the fact that the leader of a global superpower had just shouted insults at her face.
Her mouth was full with her cheek bulging slightly as she swallowed, taking a measured luxurious sip of the remaining wine from the glass before her.
She lowered the glass with a soft clatter.
Looking through her clear wire-rimmed lenses, she fixed her glowing violet eyes directly on Vanderbilt’s trembling red-faced profile.
"Are you... done?" she asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 538: Crazy Woman [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Her voice was flat like she was mildly inconvenienced, it was the way a person might ask a noisy ceiling fan to stop squeaking.

Vanderbilt managed to drag a wheezing gasp of air into his burning lungs as he coughed violently, wiping a bead of cold sweat from his upper lip with his pride desperately struggling to reassert itself before the assembly.

"I asked a legitimate question, Lord Vespera," Vanderbilt rasped. "If your core is the celestial miracle you claim it to be... why can’t you heal your lost arm? A true sovereign does not sit before the World Council missing half their limbs."
Kara let out a small quiet sigh of relief, leaning back against the violet velvet.

"Ah, that’s good," she murmured, brushing a stray fleck of salt from her tailored lapel. "I thought you were going to ask me why I was eating or something... I didn’t even have breakfast this morning, so I really didn’t want to listen to a fifteen-minute PowerPoint telling me how I shouldn’t eat."
Vanderbilt’s face turned an ugly mottled purple. "You mock this assembly—"
"Who said I couldn’t heal it?" Kara interrupted.
The room went dead silent.
Kara reached up with her single right hand, unpinning the charcoal wool of her left sleeve and with a slow, deliberate motion, she pulled the dark fabric back, exposing her left shoulder.
The arm was severed cleanly three inches below the joint with the stump smooth and completely healed over with old unblemished scar tissue.
Then, she exhaled.
SHNNNNN!
A soft shimmer of pure gold light ignited directly beneath the surface of her skin.
The light wasn’t chaotic as before but it was humming with a frequency that made the hairs on Aki’s arms stand on end.

Before the eyes of more than five hundred people, bone shot forth from the stump like growing coral... Muscle fibers, crimson and dense as steel cables, wove themselves into existence across the newly formed humerus in less than a second.

Arteries pulsed, skin knitted across the tissue like pale silk, and within the span of three heartbeats, a completely flawless left arm extended from her shoulder, terminating in five slender fully formed fingers.
A collective terrified gasp tore through the mezzanine.
"Impossible..." Chancellor Montmirail breathed with his glasses slipping down his nose. "Instantaneous cellular recreation... without an alchemical catalyst..."
Kara held up her newly formed left hand as she flexed the fingers once and then twice.
The knuckles popped with clean healthy clicks.
’If she can do that so easily,’ Vanderbilt thought, his mind reeling with dread, ’then why the hell did she—’
SHING... SHKKK!
A flash of violet mana severed the air!
Before anyone could even register the movement of her right hand, a razor-thin blade of mana flashed across her own shoulder and the left arm detached instantly.
THWACK!
The freshly severed limb landed heavily on the celestial marble table directly in front of Vanderbilt, bouncing once before sliding to a halt beside his digital terminal.
SPLAT!
A shower of hot bright crimson blood sprayed across the white stone with several heavy droplets splashing straight onto Vanderbilt’s silk tie and the lapel of his charcoal jacket.
"AGH!"

Vanderbilt physically leaped backward in his chair with his boots scrambling frantically against the floor and his face drained of every drop of color as he stared at the bloody twitching arm sitting on the table before him with horror.
FZZZZZZT!
At the shoulder, Kara’s wound didn’t even bleed.
The moment the flesh parted, a golden filament of light sealed the stump shut, returning it instantly to that same smooth pale scar tissue she had walked in with.
Then, she pointed her single right forefinger at the severed arm on the table.
WHOOOOOOSH!
A terrifying silent eruption of crimson fire engulfed the flesh.
The flame burned with heat that melted the marble.

It simply consumed the biological matter at an atomic level, turning bone, muscle, and blood into a shower of glittering disintegrating red sparks that vanished into the air like burning embers, leaving the white stone completely bare and unblemished.
Even the blood that had splashed on Vanderbilt was attended to as well.
Kara pulled her sleeve down, pinning the empty charcoal cuff neatly back against her ribs with one hand and a safety pin she took from her pocket.

"Like I said," Kara explained smoothly, leaning back and resting her single elbow on the armrest, "I’ve already built a pretty solid public reputation using just the one arm... Changing my branding now would just confuse the livestream audiences."
She looked directly at Vanderbilt, her violet eyes glinting behind her glasses with amused chilling contempt.
"Besides... I really haven’t run into a challenge in this world that was worth using two hands for anyway so why bother?"
She tapped the glass again.
CLINK!
"More wine, please. Still dry."
One of the masked World Council Magistrates at the northern bench leaned forward, his voice muffled behind his heavy linen cowl.

"Lord Vespera! You sit within the Grand Assembly of humanity! This is not a tavern for you to consume alcohol while mutilating yourself for theatrical amusement! Why are you demanding wine at an emergency summit?!"
Kara tilted her head back toward the Council bench, looking at the Magistrate through her lenses with a deadpan expression.

"Well," Kara said reasonably, "do you have a menu? If you’re serving tea, coffee, or maybe some sparkling cider, I’m completely open to alternatives but right now, you people have only put out stale water and fermented grapes... Bring me a menu, and I’ll order something else. Who the hell doesn’t serve food at events?"
The Magistrate’s mouth clamped shut beneath his cowl.
He sat back, his robes rustling with tightly suppressed rage, completely incapable of formulating a response to someone who treated the highest judicial bench on Earth like a cheap roadside diner.
A terrified attendant scrambled forward with an open bottle of aged vintage, frantically filling Kara’s crystal flute before scurrying backward like a frightened crab.
Across the amphitheater, a single horrifying realization settled over every living soul in the room...
This woman wasn’t just powerful... She was completely out of her mind!
She had severed her own limb and burned it to ash in front of the heads of state simply because she didn’t want to change her internet brand.
She operated with a level of carefree casualness that made the King’s cold tyranny look orderly by comparison.
You couldn’t threaten her and you couldn’t bribe her with polite etiquette.
She did whatever the hell she wanted because she possessed the violent capacity to back it up.
Kara took a slow appreciative sip of the wine, smacking her lips lightly before turning her attention back toward the dais.

"Anyway," Kara said, swirling the glass. "What about my negotiations? The diplomatic summons explicitly relayed the fact that Blessed Land had a seat at this table to settle ourselves so I’m here and ready to talk business."
The King did not flinch.
He looked down at her from the high throne with his eyes cold.

"Your business is noted, Lord Vespera," the King said flatly. "However... because you chose to arrive nearly an hour past the bell, the scheduled docket has shifted. The formal discussions regarding the sovereignty of Blessed Land and your terms are hereby postponed until the conclusion of the Exhibition of Succession."
Kara blinked behind her glasses as she paused with the glass halfway to her mouth.
"Exhibition of... what?"

"A martial tournament," the King stated, his tone carrying the grand immovable weight of a decree. "To resolve the contested drilling rights of the northern transitional corridor. A bracket held directly within a stabilized sector of the Sovereign Realm, featuring the youth of the Nine Powers..."
Kara blinked once more.
She lowered the glass, an expression of boredom washing over her features.
"A tournament," she muttered under her breath, rolling her eyes toward the ceiling. "Great... Another gladiatorial pit. How original."
The King’s lips twitched slightly.

"The Crown does not restrict the arena strictly to the sovereign houses," the King added, leaning forward as his gaze locked onto Kara with a sharp edge. "Although you hold citizenship within the administrative districts of Europa, Lord Vespera, your status grants you total autonomy. Should you wish to expedite your diplomatic standing, you are formally permitted to enter the Exhibition... You may align yourself with any nation, noble house, or faction currently seated at this table, lending your blade to their cause."
Kara let out a flat dry snort, looking at the King as if he had just asked her to fetch his slippers.

"Oh, please," Kara said, waving her single hand dismissively. "You just want to put a Gold Core on the billboard so you can juice your live viewer numbers for the stream... You’re using me for free exposure."
CREAK!
The King’s fingers dug into the armrest, the metal groaning audibly under his grip and his jaw tightened with a microscopic vein throbbing at his temple.
’This insolent, arrogant...’ he thought, swallowing down the sudden urge to blast the entire western quadrant of the table into atoms.
She was infuriating!
She treated the Throne like an annoying corporate promoter trying to book a guest appearance on a local broadcast.
The King cleared his throat, deliberately drawing his presence back and refusing to let her drag him into a public spat.
He turned his head away from Kara.
Slowly, his sapphire gaze drifted down toward the lowest tier of the royal guest arc and straight onto the First Princess.
Aki’s pulse hitched, the rhythm stumbling in her throat like a dying engine.
Her father’s unblinking gaze bore straight through her velvet collar and across the vast, circular expanse of the Grand Assembly pit, the hush returned with a sickening quickness.
The whisper of Kara White’s severed arm dissolving into crimson sparks had faded into the background, yet the air remained fiercely ionized, tasting like copper wire laid across a raw tongue.
The First Princess stayed locked in her low-tier seat.

Under the heavy navy folds of her skirts, her thighs were clamped tight together with her slippers pressed completely flat against the black flagstones to kill the involuntary tremor crawling up her calves.

She did not blink and she did not dare to let her shoulders slump, nor did she glance up toward the mezzanine where hundreds of corporate eyes were watching her like vultures circling a dying animal in the brush.
The King shifted his posture on the high throne.
His star-iron signet ring dragged a slow dull screech across the celestial marble of the Grand Table with a sound like a blade scraping over bone.

"Now," the King spoke, his voice dropping into a tone that vibrated straight through the floorboards and settled into the marrow of everyone present. "Regarding the earlier grievance raised by President Vanderbilt..."
Aki’s fingers curled into tight white-knuckled knots within the folds of her lap.
’No...’ she thought, the breath backing up into her throat turning hot and sour. ’Not this. Please, Father, not this...’
Beside the Throne, Princess Kiera tilted her head slightly from her perch upon the King’s right knee.
Her amber-gold irises flickered with passive porcelain tranquility, watching Aki with the mild detachment of a noble studying a beetle struggling against a sticky floorboard.
Crown Prince Alexander remained frozen three chairs down with his knuckles gray-white against his slate and his bloodshot eyes fixed entirely on the blank glass.
He wouldn’t lift his chin.
For thirty years, he had shared the same cold silence from their progenitor, but now that the executioner’s axe was hovering over his sister’s neck, Alexander looked anywhere else.
The King did not rise as he leaned his broad forearms upon the marble, peering down at his nameless firstborn daughter with chilling neutrality.
"You, too, may participate in this contest," the King decreed.
The air in the mezzanine galleries snapped like dry twigs.
Alexander’s jaw clicked open in unmasked disbelief.
Up in the higher tiers, dozens of junior aides and guild scribes leaned forward against the brass safety bars, muttering frantic questions behind their cuffs.

"Like House Sterling and House Bloom," the King continued, completely unbothered by the collective ripple of shock coursing through the five tiers, "the First Princess shall enter as her own independent faction within the bracket..."
"Majesty!"
The sharp bark came from the western arc.
Prime Minister Sir Arthur Pendelton rose half an inch from his star-iron seat, planting the brass ferrule of his cane into the stone with an audible thud.

"The First Princess is Unawakened!" Pendelton protested, his silver eyebrows drawn in furious incredulous disbelief. "Her core pathways are entirely inert! To send an unawakened civilian into an active transitional sector of the Sovereign Realm is not an exhibition... it is state-sanctioned slaughter! The atmospheric power of the Sovereign Realm will rupture her internal organs before she even clears the gate and the international media will brand this court as butchers!"
The King did not turn his head toward the Albion prime minister.
He didn’t offer a rebuttal, to everyone he didn’t even acknowledge that Pendelton had spoken.

He simply let the warning hang in the freezing air like dead weight, making it unmistakably clear to every ruler in the amphitheater that whether the girl was crushed by spatial gravity or dismembered by a beast was an outcome of zero consequence to the Crown.

"The rules of the Exhibition remain absolute," the King stated, his sapphire eyes pinned exclusively on Aki. "Every recognized faction must field two representatives... You must secure a second combatant to fight under your banner. What you offer them as compensation is entirely your own affair and the Crown will furnish no stipends, no enchanted armaments, and no household retainers to bolster your cause."
He paused, letting the silence hang like an executioner’s noose around her neck.

"Or... on the other hand," the King added. "you may rise from your seat right now. You may walk to the center of the Grand Assembly floor, bow your head, and formally apologize to President Vanderbilt Senior for the injuries sustained by his son. If you do so, perhaps the two of you can find common ground regarding a... suitable punishment."

FZZZZZZT!
At the shoulder, Kara’s wound didn’t even bleed.

Then, she pointed her single right forefinger at the severed arm on the table.
WHOOOOOOSH!
A terrifying silent eruption of crimson fire engulfed the flesh.
The flame burned with heat that melted the marble.

Even the blood that had splashed on Vanderbilt was attended to as well.
Kara pulled her sleeve down, pinning the empty charcoal cuff neatly back against her ribs with one hand and a safety pin she took from her pocket.
"Like I said," Kara explained smoothly, leaning back and resting her single elbow on the armrest, "I’ve already built a pretty solid public reputation using just the one arm...

She looked directly at Vanderbilt, her violet eyes glinting behind her glasses with amused chilling contempt.
"Besides...

She tapped the glass again.
CLINK!
"More wine, please.
Still dry."

Why are you demanding wine at an emergency summit?!"

The Magistrate’s mouth clamped shut beneath his cowl.
He sat back, his robes rustling with tightly suppressed rage, completely incapable of formulating a response to someone who treated the highest judicial bench on Earth like a cheap roadside diner.
A terrified attendant scrambled forward with an open bottle of aged vintage, frantically filling Kara’s crystal flute before scurrying backward like a frightened crab.
Across the amphitheater, a single horrifying realization settled over every living soul in the room...
This woman wasn’t just powerful...
