chapters.title: Chapter 539: Don’t You Have A Human Heart? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Down across the semi-circle, President Julian Vanderbilt Senior slowly expanded his chest.
The terror and humiliation that had soaked his collar moments before vanished completely, swallowed whole by the dark hungry ambition of a conqueror who had just smelled blood in the water.

The lingering burning spots from Kara White removing her blood on his silk lapel were forgotten as he adjusted his platinum cufflinks, his heavy square jaw jutting forward in satisfaction as he leaned over the table.
’A suitable punishment...’ Vanderbilt thought, his mind racing through legal precedents, marital treaties, and financial leverage like an automated printing press.

’She is useless as a martial asset,’ he calculated ruthlessly, his small, dark eyes drilling into Aki’s pale profile. ’She has no core and she has no mana. She couldn’t kill an unranked pest if her life depended on it but she carries the pure untainted blood of the first King! If the King permits it... I will demand her hand in marriage for Julian! Once she is bound by contract to the Vanderbilt registry, any child she bears will combine royal blood with Columbian industrial infrastructure... That heir will hold a legitimate unquestionable bloodline claim to the Throne! If I cannot wear the crown in my lifetime... my grandson will take it!’
The snare was ironclad.
Aki’s breath came in thin ragged sips and her chest felt as though it were being compressed between two sheets of cold iron.
Her shoulders caved in slightly beneath the heavy midnight velvet of her gown.
Did she have a choice?
There was no choice.
The entire summit was an engine built to grind her to dust as her father had stripped away the final shred of her royal immunity with a few casual words.

If she refused to apologize, she would be hurled into an active Sovereign Realm rift zone against Awakened prodigies... monsters like the bare-chested Indus warrior with the burning crimson tattoos, the lightning-fast blade masters of Yamato, or the armored brutes of Borealis.
Even if the runic non-lethal dampening wards kept her heart beating, she would still be brutally battered into the dirt on a global livestream feed.
It would provide the exact public legal justification her father needed to erase her from the royal records once and for all, casting her out into the streets as an embarrassment to the lineage.
The secret wager with Alexander didn’t matter and her quiet pride in the name Silas had given her didn’t matter.

The only road forward... the only way to survive the afternoon and keep drawing breath was to lower herself to the flagstones, press her forehead against the freezing stone at Vanderbilt’s leather shoes, and beg for mercy like a disgraced scullery maid.
Her eyes stung, blurring with the hot bitter sting of unshed tears as Aki desperately wanted to turn her head toward the violet-velvet chair.
She wanted to look at Kara... she wanted to look through the black-haired, one-armed disguise and catch the familiar irreverent glint in Silas’s eyes.
...The only person who had ever looked at her without seeing a royal defect.
’No,’ she told herself, biting her lower lip until the metallic taste of blood flooded her mouth. ’Don’t look at him... Don’t let him see you like this...’
She couldn’t bear to let him witness her complete pathetic surrender.
Even draped in a woman’s silhouette, he was Silas.
He had stood against the horrors of the Sovereign Realm without flinching... she refused to make him watch her crawl on her belly before the men who had spent her entire life stepping on her neck.
Yet the silence was dragging.
The King sat unmoving and Vanderbilt’s thin, cruel smile widened by the second with his eyes practically undressing her political future.
Aki’s jaw loosened.
Slowly... agonizingly... her head began to tilt downward.
Her chin dipped toward her collarbone and her spine curved with her velvet skirts rustling softly against the cushioned bench as her upper body began the humiliating descent toward the floor.
And then...
She stopped dead.
It was not out of any sudden defiance but rather because her body physically seized, frozen in place by an invisible suffocating wall.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A soundless vibration ripped through the marrow of every living thing in the hall.
It was not the explosive blinding detonation of golden light that had shattered the skylights minutes earlier.
...It was infinitely worse.
The air itself turned rancid as it was with the unmistakable metallic stench of fresh murder, ruptured organs, and rotting bone marrow.
It felt as though an invisible stagnant swamp of pure concentrated death had suddenly breached the foundation stones and flooded the chamber to the ceiling.
DRIP! DRIP!
Up in the third tier of the Borealis delegation, a junior military attache clamped both hands between his thighs with his face turning the color of curdled milk.
A dark warm stain spread rapidly across the gray wool of his trousers.
His nervous system had completely surrendered to primal panic, voiding his bladder before his conscious mind could even process the threat.
Down across the Grand Table, the World Council Magistrates recoiled in their high chairs.
SHING!
Magistrate Bloom’s right hand flew to the hilt of his ancestral saber with his knuckles turning chalk-white as a violent sheath of crimson mana erupted around his forearms in pure desperate reflex.

Beside him, the female Council Member who had previously suppressed the entire room with her gravity field sat rigid as an iron bar with her featureless white porcelain mask trembling as her manicured fingernails dug deep into the celestial marble.
The aura leaking from the violet chair was no longer golden or divine.
It manifested as thin hair-like needles of blood-tinged golden lightning that whipped across the table’s surface, etching microscopic grooves into the ancient stone with persistent hisses.
’How many...?’
The horrifying question screamed through the minds of every hardened veterans, rulers and Lords in the room.

’How many thousands of monsters... how many mountains of corpses... how many screaming humans or monsters had this woman butchered with her bare hands to forge a bloodlust this terrifyingly powerful?!’
This was not the presence of a hero at all if she could be called one, she felt like an executioner yet, amidst that suffocating swamp of hostility...
Aki felt nothing.
...Not a single microscopic ounce of the pressure touched her skin.

The air surrounding her small low-tier chair remained completely sweet and cool as if an invisible flawless sphere of tranquility had settled over her shoulders, insulating her completely from the nightmare drowning the rest of the amphitheater.
Aki’s chin snapped upward and Kara was still seated in the violet-velvet chair.
She had not risen as she sat with her legs crossed at the ankle with her tailored charcoal suit uncreased and her left sleeve pinned flat to her ribs.
But her wire-rimmed reading glasses were gone, held loosely between the knuckles of her single right hand, dangling against her knee.

Her jet-black hair was gently lifting, floating in the micro-gravity generated by her soul pathways and beneath those dark bangs, her glowing violet irises had contracted into two terrifying vertical needles of rage locking straight onto the King of the World.
Aki’s breath caught.
Her heart slammed against her ribs with an impact so violently tender that her vision blurred entirely with hot tears spilling over her lashes and running down her pale cheeks into her collar.
’Si- Silas... didn’t let me bow,’ Aki thought, her soul shuddering within her chest. ’Silas... is sitting there, threatening the King for me.’
The silence in the Great Assembly Chamber was suffocating.
Nobody dared to shift a boot as even the King remained frozen against his throne, his sapphire eyes pinned to the seated black-haired woman whose murderous intent was aimed directly at his forehead.
Kara tilted her head with her right arm resting casually across the star-iron armrest of her chair.
When she spoke, she didn’t shout.
"King of the World..."
Kara’s violet eyes flared with the golden needles whipping across the marble toward the dais.
"Don’t you... have a human heart?"
The King stared down from the star-iron dais with his sapphire irises completely motionless.
Across the vast span of the Great Assembly Chamber, not a single breath stirred.

The King’s jaw was locked and he looked at Kara as though she were speaking a dead tongue... as if the word heart were an archaic untranslatable glyph carved into a tomb rather than an organ in his chest.
"A heart?" the King murmured. "You disrupt the governance of mankind to preach morality, Lord Vespera?"
Kara let out a soft dry breath through her nose.
SHHHHH!
The blood-tinged golden lightning did not explode outward anymore as she withdrew it instead.
In the span of a single heartbeat, the suffocating miasma of murderous intent receded, folding neatly back into her chest like a blade slipping into an oiled scabbard.

The rancid stench of torn marrow vanished and the oppressive atmospheric gravity lifted, leaving the hundreds of petrified dignitaries in the mezzanine gasping for air, clutching their collars as if they had just been hauled up from the bottom of an ocean trench.
Kara leaned back into the plush violet velvet of her chair, resting her single right elbow on the armrest.
She reached up with her right hand, casually unfolding the wire-rimmed glasses she had been holding by the temple, and slid them back over her ears, pushing the bridge up her nose with her thumb.
"Yeah," She said, dismissive of the five hundred people recovering from near-fatal cardiac arrest. "Maybe I overexaggerated... A little theatrical, honestly. My bad."

Down along the guest arc, Aki remained frozen as the cold, suffocating terror of having to bow before Vanderbilt was gone, replaced by a surreal ringing disbelief as she stared at the black-haired woman sitting alone at the table.
Kara tilted her head with her violet eyes glinting behind the clean lenses.

"Let’s be real for a second, Majesty," Kara continued. "What kind of backwards, dysfunctional parenting manual are you working out of up there? Because from where I’m sitting, your entire domestic philosophy is a joke..."
The silence in the hall turned brittle.
Alexander’s head jerked up from his desk with his bloodshot eyes widening in horror.
Beside the King, Princess Kiera didn’t move though her golden gaze was fixed unblinkingly on Kara and the pleasant curve of her lips slowly freezing over.

"Watch your tongue, girl," the King warned, the sound vibrating through the marble table. "You sit before the Throne and the discipline and lineage of House Castellian are not matters for an upstart Lord to dissect."

"Lineage?" Kara scoffed, letting out a short mocking laugh that echoed cleanly off the vaulted dome. "You call this discipline? You have a daughter... your own flesh and blood, born of your royal house and your solution to her not awakening an internal battery is to treat her like a broken chair in the corridor. Abandoning a child just because she didn’t inherit the family fireworks is just a pathetic cowardly excuse."
The King’s eyelids lowered by a fraction of an inch with his sapphire gaze turning to frozen iron.

"A princess is not an ornament, Lord Vespera," the King replied. "The royal bloodline exists solely to anchor the civilization of this planet against the dark... A noble of House Castellian who cannot manifest a core cannot bear the weight of a Royal title. She is a civilian who drains the prestige of the Crown and beyond that... her very birth brought about the death of my Queen. She took the life of the only woman worthy to sit at my side then returned nothing to the realm in return. Why should the Throne waste its sentiment on an empty vessel?"
He laid it out before the governing bodies of the world without a single trace of hesitation.
In his mind, it was an unassailable equation... A daughter who had cost him his Queen and produced no mana was a net negative on the species’ balance sheet.
Kara didn’t blink, she didn’t even look outraged... The woman just looked pityingly unimpressed.

"Her birth killed your Queen?" Kara asked, resting her chin on her right palm with her violet eyes boring straight through him. "And you blame a newborn infant for uterine hemorrhaging and shock? That’s what we’re going with? You’re the Monarch of humanity, wielding ancient authority, and you hold a grievance against a baby because your medical mages couldn’t stabilize your wife’s vitals? What a childish thing to do..."
A sharp audible intake of breath hissed through the mezzanine.

Up in the Bloom family box, Matriarch Etilga Bloom covered her mouth, her ruby eyes blazing with scandalous delight, while Lohan Sterling’s hands tightened around his legs, staring at Kara as if she were walking across a minefield in silk slippers.
The King’s fist clenched against the armrest with the metal groaning audibly.
"She failed the fundamental requirement of her blood—"
"Do you actually feel things for your own children?" Kara interrupted.
The question wasn’t shouted.
It was asked quietly, with the casual devastating directness of a physician noting an incurable infection.
The King stopped.
His lips remained parted with the next cold decree dying in his throat.
For the first time since the summit had convened, the monarch looked completely derailed.
His sapphire eyes flickered, his gaze shifting across the semicircular table, suddenly finding more than five hundred pairs of eyes staring back at him in dead waiting silence.
"Feel... what?" the King muttered, the words leaving his mouth with an awkward disjointed stiffness.
Kara chuckled.

"Look at you," Kara said, shaking her head. "You actually had to process that. ’Feel what?’ That’s incredible... A father who doesn’t even comprehend the concept of parental affection. It’s honestly worse than I thought."

"You speak from complete ignorance!" the King snapped back, his voice rising, the composure cracking just enough to show the defensive brittle pride beneath the crown. "I have preserved this empire! I have tempered my house into the sharpest blade humanity possesses! Alexander commands the northern legions! Kiera wields an core that will safeguard our eastern sea borders for a generation! I have provided them with resources, legions, and the greatest martial inheritance on the globe!"
"You didn’t raise children," Kara said. "You bred tools and you aren’t even good at managing them."
She leaned forward, pointing her single right forefinger across the celestial marble.
"You used your son as an example right...? Now let’s take a look at your son," Kara said.

sentences.text: Down across the semi-circle, President Julian Vanderbilt Senior slowly expanded his chest.
The terror and humiliation that had soaked his collar moments before vanished completely, swallowed whole by the dark hungry ambition of a conqueror who had just smelled blood in the water.

The lingering burning spots from Kara White removing her blood on his silk lapel were forgotten as he adjusted his platinum cufflinks, his heavy square jaw jutting forward in satisfaction as he leaned over the table.
’A suitable punishment...’ Vanderbilt thought, his mind racing through legal precedents, marital treaties, and financial leverage like an automated printing press.
’She is useless as a martial asset,’ he calculated ruthlessly, his small, dark eyes drilling into Aki’s pale profile. ’She has no core and she has no mana.
She couldn’t kill an unranked pest if her life depended on it but she carries the pure untainted blood of the first King!
If the King permits it...
I will demand her hand in marriage for Julian!
Once she is bound by contract to the Vanderbilt registry, any child she bears will combine royal blood with Columbian industrial infrastructure...
That heir will hold a legitimate unquestionable bloodline claim to the Throne!
If I cannot wear the crown in my lifetime... my grandson will take it!’
The snare was ironclad.
Aki’s breath came in thin ragged sips and her chest felt as though it were being compressed between two sheets of cold iron.
Her shoulders caved in slightly beneath the heavy midnight velvet of her gown.
Did she have a choice?
There was no choice.
The entire summit was an engine built to grind her to dust as her father had stripped away the final shred of her royal immunity with a few casual words.

If she refused to apologize, she would be hurled into an active Sovereign Realm rift zone against Awakened prodigies... monsters like the bare-chested Indus warrior with the burning crimson tattoos, the lightning-fast blade masters of Yamato, or the armored brutes of Borealis.
Even if the runic non-lethal dampening wards kept her heart beating, she would still be brutally battered into the dirt on a global livestream feed.
It would provide the exact public legal justification her father needed to erase her from the royal records once and for all, casting her out into the streets as an embarrassment to the lineage.
The secret wager with Alexander didn’t matter and her quiet pride in the name Silas had given her didn’t matter.

The only road forward... the only way to survive the afternoon and keep drawing breath was to lower herself to the flagstones, press her forehead against the freezing stone at Vanderbilt’s leather shoes, and beg for mercy like a disgraced scullery maid.
Her eyes stung, blurring with the hot bitter sting of unshed tears as Aki desperately wanted to turn her head toward the violet-velvet chair.
She wanted to look at Kara... she wanted to look through the black-haired, one-armed disguise and catch the familiar irreverent glint in Silas’s eyes.
...The only person who had ever looked at her without seeing a royal defect.
’No,’ she told herself, biting her lower lip until the metallic taste of blood flooded her mouth. ’Don’t look at him...
Don’t let him see you like this...’
She couldn’t bear to let him witness her complete pathetic surrender.
Even draped in a woman’s silhouette, he was Silas.
He had stood against the horrors of the Sovereign Realm without flinching... she refused to make him watch her crawl on her belly before the men who had spent her entire life stepping on her neck.
Yet the silence was dragging.
The King sat unmoving and Vanderbilt’s thin, cruel smile widened by the second with his eyes practically undressing her political future.
Aki’s jaw loosened.
Slowly... agonizingly... her head began to tilt downward.
Her chin dipped toward her collarbone and her spine curved with her velvet skirts rustling softly against the cushioned bench as her upper body began the humiliating descent toward the floor.
And then...
She stopped dead.
It was not out of any sudden defiance but rather because her body physically seized, frozen in place by an invisible suffocating wall.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A soundless vibration ripped through the marrow of every living thing in the hall.
It was not the explosive blinding detonation of golden light that had shattered the skylights minutes earlier.
...It was infinitely worse.
The air itself turned rancid as it was with the unmistakable metallic stench of fresh murder, ruptured organs, and rotting bone marrow.
It felt as though an invisible stagnant swamp of pure concentrated death had suddenly breached the foundation stones and flooded the chamber to the ceiling.
DRIP!
DRIP!
Up in the third tier of the Borealis delegation, a junior military attache clamped both hands between his thighs with his face turning the color of curdled milk.
A dark warm stain spread rapidly across the gray wool of his trousers.
His nervous system had completely surrendered to primal panic, voiding his bladder before his conscious mind could even process the threat.
Down across the Grand Table, the World Council Magistrates recoiled in their high chairs.
SHING!
Magistrate Bloom’s right hand flew to the hilt of his ancestral saber with his knuckles turning chalk-white as a violent sheath of crimson mana erupted around his forearms in pure desperate reflex.

Beside him, the female Council Member who had previously suppressed the entire room with her gravity field sat rigid as an iron bar with her featureless white porcelain mask trembling as her manicured fingernails dug deep into the celestial marble.
The aura leaking from the violet chair was no longer golden or divine.
It manifested as thin hair-like needles of blood-tinged golden lightning that whipped across the table’s surface, etching microscopic grooves into the ancient stone with persistent hisses.
’How many...?’
The horrifying question screamed through the minds of every hardened veterans, rulers and Lords in the room.

’How many thousands of monsters... how many mountains of corpses... how many screaming humans or monsters had this woman butchered with her bare hands to forge a bloodlust this terrifyingly powerful?!’
This was not the presence of a hero at all if she could be called one, she felt like an executioner yet, amidst that suffocating swamp of hostility...
Aki felt nothing.
...Not a single microscopic ounce of the pressure touched her skin.

The air surrounding her small low-tier chair remained completely sweet and cool as if an invisible flawless sphere of tranquility had settled over her shoulders, insulating her completely from the nightmare drowning the rest of the amphitheater.
Aki’s chin snapped upward and Kara was still seated in the violet-velvet chair.
She had not risen as she sat with her legs crossed at the ankle with her tailored charcoal suit uncreased and her left sleeve pinned flat to her ribs.
But her wire-rimmed reading glasses were gone, held loosely between the knuckles of her single right hand, dangling against her knee.

Her jet-black hair was gently lifting, floating in the micro-gravity generated by her soul pathways and beneath those dark bangs, her glowing violet irises had contracted into two terrifying vertical needles of rage locking straight onto the King of the World.
Aki’s breath caught.
Her heart slammed against her ribs with an impact so violently tender that her vision blurred entirely with hot tears spilling over her lashes and running down her pale cheeks into her collar.
’Si- Silas... didn’t let me bow,’ Aki thought, her soul shuddering within her chest. ’Silas... is sitting there, threatening the King for me.’
The silence in the Great Assembly Chamber was suffocating.
Nobody dared to shift a boot as even the King remained frozen against his throne, his sapphire eyes pinned to the seated black-haired woman whose murderous intent was aimed directly at his forehead.
Kara tilted her head with her right arm resting casually across the star-iron armrest of her chair.
When she spoke, she didn’t shout.
"King of the World..."
Kara’s violet eyes flared with the golden needles whipping across the marble toward the dais.
"Don’t you... have a human heart?"
The King stared down from the star-iron dais with his sapphire irises completely motionless.
Across the vast span of the Great Assembly Chamber, not a single breath stirred.

The King’s jaw was locked and he looked at Kara as though she were speaking a dead tongue... as if the word heart were an archaic untranslatable glyph carved into a tomb rather than an organ in his chest.
"A heart?" the King murmured.
"You disrupt the governance of mankind to preach morality, Lord Vespera?"
Kara let out a soft dry breath through her nose.
SHHHHH!
The blood-tinged golden lightning did not explode outward anymore as she withdrew it instead.
In the span of a single heartbeat, the suffocating miasma of murderous intent receded, folding neatly back into her chest like a blade slipping into an oiled scabbard.

The rancid stench of torn marrow vanished and the oppressive atmospheric gravity lifted, leaving the hundreds of petrified dignitaries in the mezzanine gasping for air, clutching their collars as if they had just been hauled up from the bottom of an ocean trench.
Kara leaned back into the plush violet velvet of her chair, resting her single right elbow on the armrest.
She reached up with her right hand, casually unfolding the wire-rimmed glasses she had been holding by the temple, and slid them back over her ears, pushing the bridge up her nose with her thumb.
"Yeah," She said, dismissive of the five hundred people recovering from near-fatal cardiac arrest.
"Maybe I overexaggerated...
A little theatrical, honestly.
My bad."

Kara tilted her head with her violet eyes glinting behind the clean lenses.
"Let’s be real for a second, Majesty," Kara continued.
"What kind of backwards, dysfunctional parenting manual are you working out of up there?
Because from where I’m sitting, your entire domestic philosophy is a joke..."
The silence in the hall turned brittle.

chapters.title: Chapter 540: Siding With Aki [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Every eye in the amphitheater swiveled to Crown Prince Alexander.
The young man sat rigid as a corpse, his face dead white with his hands trembling against his terminal and his lower jaw clamped so tightly that a line of saliva ran down his chin.
He looked like an animal that had spent years being beaten with an iron rod every time it failed to jump high enough.

"He awakened," Kara continued, stripping away the entire illusion of the royal family. "He bled for you for so long... He broke his bones carrying your standard, executing your enemies, doing everything you told him an Awakened prince was supposed to do and what did it get him? The second a little girl born of some side affair in the eastern provinces manifests a Purple Core, you drag her out, set her on your knee like a prized porcelain doll, and completely erase thirty years of your son’s loyalty in front of the entire world... He’s sitting right there, Majesty. He looks like he’s about to have an aneurysm, and you haven’t looked him in the eye once today."
Alexander’s head lowered slightly, his shoulders beginning to shake with silent violently suppressed tremors.
Kara adjusted her glasses with a crisp flick of her finger, her gaze sweeping back up to the high dais, locking onto the King with contempt.

"I was born an orphan," Kara stated. "I grew up in Valoria City. I never met my mother, never knew my father, never had a single soul to look out for me but I’ll tell you this: if I had been cursed with a father like you, I would have thrown myself off the nearest observation spire years ago... People like you have no right to call themselves parents. You’re just a parasite wearing an imperial coat, using your own blood to feed your ego."
The Great Assembly Chamber fell into an abyss of horrified silence as nobody breathed and nobody rustled paper.
The First Princess sat in her low chair, her hands trembling in her lap, her vision blurring entirely as hot silent tears carved clean paths through the dust on her cheeks.
Nobody had ever said it.

In the entire history of House Castellian, through the cold isolation, beatings, and neglect, not a single human being had ever dared to stand before the King of the World and tell him the ugly truth...
That he was a monster to his own blood.
On the dais, the King did not speak as the stillness around him warped.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUU!
The deep dark void-light bled into his irises, replacing the sapphire brilliance with a swirling bottomless blackness that began to pull the ambient light out of the air.
The temperature around the throne plummeted to absolute zero with the moisture in the air crystallizing into dark frost along the star-iron backrest.
It was the unmistakable prelude to Destruction... the same unconditional erasure that had wiped the Amazonian officer out of existence twenty minutes ago but Kara didn’t flinch.
She sat back in her violet-velvet chair, crossed her legs, and watched the void-light consume his pupils with her lips slowly curling into a wide smirk.
"What?" Kara provoked softly, her violet eyes glinting through her lenses with mocking disdain. "You want to kill me now? For telling the truth in front of your peers?"
She tapped the armrest with her single right hand with her smile widening into a terrifying fearless grin.
"Go ahead and try it, King... Bring out that ancestral Destruction passed down from the First King."
Kara tilted her head, her voice dropping to a confident whisper.
"It won’t work on me."
The King paused, his sapphire eyes flickering downward toward the edge of the celestial marble table.

The dark void-light that had begun pooling at the rims of his irises did not violently detonate as everyone expected... it wavered, thinning out into fine, stagnant smoke before dissolving back into his spiritual pathways.
His broad chest rose and fell once, catching slightly at the throat.
Across the entire circular expanse of the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence had ceased to be mere courtly decorum.
More than five hundred people sat frozen in place, their gazes darting frantically between the high star-iron throne and the one-armed woman lounging in the violet-velvet chair.
’Destruction was passed down from the First King?’
The whispered question echoed through the minds of every dignitary in the hall, utterly alien and terrifying.

To the World Council, the King’s authority was an undisputed constant of the post-Apocalypse era... a catastrophic martial power native to his person that had atomized Lords, collapsed rogue bastions, and held the continental borders rigid for generations.
None of the nine major powers had ever been told of its true genesis as not even the oldest records preserved in Europa’s central archives spoke of ancestral marrow-transference.
Yet the King himself was trembling.

It was an imperceptible microscopic shudder running along the thick tendon of his right wrist, completely masked from the gallery above, but his knuckles were drained of all color where his signet pressed against the white stone.
’How does she know?’
The question tore through his thoughts with concussive force.
It was a blood-sealed imperial secret.
The lineage of House Castellian had kept the truth chained in the dark crypts beneath the Citadel ever since the First King had perished in the ashes of humanity’s original capital.
The world was meant to believe the reigning monarch was simply born to be the best.

The transference of the ancestral embers, the agonizing ritual of absorbing a predecessor’s dying core, the two distinct arts bound to the crown... no living being outside the immediate throne had ever spoken those syllables aloud.
’Is she plagued by it?’
The King stared at Kara with his breath caught cold in his ribs.
...The Knowledge.
The horrific double-edged curse that had broken their founding ancestor’s mind.

The First King had written of it with trembling ink-spattered hands in the private royal grimoires... A Gold Core did not merely accumulate power, it forcibly opened the mind to the raw mechanics of the universe, dumping infinite architecture, ancestral memories, and cosmic truths into the cerebral cortex until the skull felt as though it were being split apart by rusted iron wedges.
The First King had died screaming not just from the Black Dragon’s claws, but from the agony of knowing too much...
’Does she see through the veil?’ The thought tightened like a noose around the King’s throat. ’Does she know of the second power? Does she know what I hide beneath my heart?’
The King was too silent to know how to proceed.
For the first time since he had taken the crown, he was genuinely shaken.
He glanced down at the violet chair, his pupils contracting as he took in her posture.
Kara was smiling.
It wasn’t a fierce battle-hungry grin, nor was it the haughty smirk of an arrogant Lord.
It was an amused casual expression that showed she had seen every single gear turning inside his head, read the panic written across his marrow, and found the entire spectacle wonderfully pathetic.
There were a hundred desperate questions rotating through the King’s mind... questions about Asgard, about the First King’s journals, about the threshold demanding to be torn from her throat.
Yet before the King could force his tongue to move or compose a shred of dignity, Kara let out a soft dismissive breath through her nose.
"You know what? Never mind," Kara said, rolling her shoulders back against the violet velvet.
Her voice was completely normal, carrying a relaxation that sounded entirely out of place in a hall built for royal decrees.

"Maybe I overstepped a little bit. It’s my bad, honestly. I get a little cranky when my blood sugar drops, and having people yell before I’ve had breakfast makes me talk too much. Forget I said anything."
The casual retreat fell upon the table like a lead weight.
She offered the apology with an airy flick of her single right wrist, not caring in the slightest that she had just rattled the mental foundations of the most powerful ruler on Earth.
The diplomats around the table blinked with their mouths dry as they were unable to keep up with the whiplash of her temperament.

"However," Kara continued, resting her right elbow on the armrest and leaning her cheek against her knuckles with her wire-rimmed glasses catching the harsh glare of the chandelier, "let’s talk about the Blessed Land negotiations a bit because to be completely frank with everyone sitting at this table... I’m already feeling pretty damn disrespected."
The air in the chamber tautened instantly.

"We haven’t even formally opened the dockets," Kara said, her violet eyes sliding across the semi-circle of rulers, lingering for half a heartbeat on Julian Vanderbilt Senior’s sweat-soaked collar, "and already I’ve had people barking at me and people staring at my empty sleeve like I’m a carnival freak. I came here in good faith to discuss the territory but I don’t really like the behavior of some of the people in these seats and if this is how the World Council treats independent sovereigns... maybe I shouldn’t bother negotiating at all."
She tapped her fingers against her jaw, letting out a small lazy yawn.
"I could always just pack my bags and disappear straight down into the Sovereign Realm for the next hundred years."
SHK!
Every ruler at the Grand Table stiffened simultaneously.
The words hit them like an electric shock straight through the chest.
’Disappear into the Sovereign Realm.’
It was the ultimate nightmare scenario for the World Council... a phrase that sent cold dread running down the spine of every military strategist and corporate oligarch on the planet.
A Gold Core was dangerous enough sitting inside Europa’s borders but if she pulled an Odin?

If she abandoned the mortal plane entirely, descended through the rifts, and vanished into the endless expanses of the Sovereign Realm where no mortal radar, no orbital satellite, and no army could ever track her?
Humanity’s only Gold Core would become an unreachable untouchable phantom.
And if she ever decided to emerge from a rift fifty years later, she could tear down a civilization over breakfast and vanish before the sirens even went off.

’Wait,’ thought Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov, his thick frost-bitten fingers tightening against his knees as his strategic mind kicked into gear. ’The Umbral Basin is an isolated sector right? The transition portals there are unstable. If she wants to maintain Blessed Land with how big it’s going to become, she has to rely on the World Council’s supply chains. She has to buy our—’
"Don’t bother doing the math, Tsar," Kara said, cutting through his thoughts as if he had spoken them through a megaphone.
Volkov flinched, his massive frame jerking back against his chair.
Kara smiled, her violet eyes glowing faintly behind her clear lenses and locking straight onto the King’s pale face.

"I don’t need your supply lines," she said, her voice dropping into a light melodic drawl that carried to the highest rafters. "Because after all... the All-Father of Asgard, Odin, already sent word. He called for me to come down and meet him in Asgard."
THUD!
It felt as though the entire room had dropped ten feet into the earth.
The King stiffened so violently that the star-iron backrest of the throne groaned under the sudden spike of his aura!
The air inside the dome grew blistering with the moisture on the walls instantly evaporating into thin hissing steam.
’Odin called for her?!’
The revelation was a hammer blow that shattered every remaining shred of leverage the World Council held.
Odin.
The First Gold Core who had abandoned humanity centuries ago to sit above the deities in the deepest most unfathomable layers of the Sovereign Realm.
And now, the first new Gold Core born in human history was casually sitting here, drinking their wine, telling them that Odin himself had already extended an invitation to his court.
The entire dynamic of the room inverted in an instant.

Kara White wasn’t an upstart lord looking to buy trade permits or beg for recognition... She already had the greatest sponsor in existence waiting for her in the deep trenches so she was simply stopping by the World Council out of mild curiosity, checking to see if humanity had anything worth trading before she turned her back on them forever.
They had zero leverage.

While the nine rulers and the seven hooded magistrates were still choking on the geopolitical weight of that reality, Kara pushed her star-iron chair back with a soft, effortless scrape against the stone.
She stood up.
Her tailored double-breasted suit fell into place with the empty left sleeve pinned flat to her ribs, swaying slightly in the hot drafts rolling off the dais.

"So, yeah," Kara said, stretching her neck until the joints popped with clean, muffled clicks. "Since you people want to waste time with this little Tournament of Succession to fight over dirt, and since the Princess over there needs a second combatant so she doesn’t have to apologize to Julian’s little syndicate..."
She stepped out from behind the Grand Table with her single right hand tucking into her trouser pocket.
"I’ll just go with Aki myself."
The announcement fell upon the assembly like a falling bell.
"Lord Vespera!" President Julian Vanderbilt Senior choked out, his heavy square face turning pale as ashes. "You cannot possibly—"
"I’m entering the bracket as her representative," Kara continued, ignoring his presence.
She turned her head, looking up toward the elevated boxes where the noble houses were seated.

Bring out that ancestral Destruction passed down from the First King."
Kara tilted her head, her voice dropping to a confident whisper.
"It won’t work on me."
The King paused, his sapphire eyes flickering downward toward the edge of the celestial marble table.

The dark void-light that had begun pooling at the rims of his irises did not violently detonate as everyone expected... it wavered, thinning out into fine, stagnant smoke before dissolving back into his spiritual pathways.
His broad chest rose and fell once, catching slightly at the throat.
Across the entire circular expanse of the Grand Assembly Chamber, the silence had ceased to be mere courtly decorum.
More than five hundred people sat frozen in place, their gazes darting frantically between the high star-iron throne and the one-armed woman lounging in the violet-velvet chair.
’Destruction was passed down from the First King?’
The whispered question echoed through the minds of every dignitary in the hall, utterly alien and terrifying.

To the World Council, the King’s authority was an undisputed constant of the post-Apocalypse era... a catastrophic martial power native to his person that had atomized Lords, collapsed rogue bastions, and held the continental borders rigid for generations.
None of the nine major powers had ever been told of its true genesis as not even the oldest records preserved in Europa’s central archives spoke of ancestral marrow-transference.
Yet the King himself was trembling.

It was an imperceptible microscopic shudder running along the thick tendon of his right wrist, completely masked from the gallery above, but his knuckles were drained of all color where his signet pressed against the white stone.
’How does she know?’
The question tore through his thoughts with concussive force.
It was a blood-sealed imperial secret.
The lineage of House Castellian had kept the truth chained in the dark crypts beneath the Citadel ever since the First King had perished in the ashes of humanity’s original capital.
The world was meant to believe the reigning monarch was simply born to be the best.

The transference of the ancestral embers, the agonizing ritual of absorbing a predecessor’s dying core, the two distinct arts bound to the crown... no living being outside the immediate throne had ever spoken those syllables aloud.
’Is she plagued by it?’
The King stared at Kara with his breath caught cold in his ribs.
...The Knowledge.
The horrific double-edged curse that had broken their founding ancestor’s mind.
The First King had written of it with trembling ink-spattered hands in the private royal grimoires...

A Gold Core did not merely accumulate power, it forcibly opened the mind to the raw mechanics of the universe, dumping infinite architecture, ancestral memories, and cosmic truths into the cerebral cortex until the skull felt as though it were being split apart by rusted iron wedges.
The First King had died screaming not just from the Black Dragon’s claws, but from the agony of knowing too much...
’Does she see through the veil?’ The thought tightened like a noose around the King’s throat. ’Does she know of the second power?
Does she know what I hide beneath my heart?’
The King was too silent to know how to proceed.
For the first time since he had taken the crown, he was genuinely shaken.
He glanced down at the violet chair, his pupils contracting as he took in her posture.
Kara was smiling.
It wasn’t a fierce battle-hungry grin, nor was it the haughty smirk of an arrogant Lord.
It was an amused casual expression that showed she had seen every single gear turning inside his head, read the panic written across his marrow, and found the entire spectacle wonderfully pathetic.
There were a hundred desperate questions rotating through the King’s mind... questions about Asgard, about the First King’s journals, about the threshold demanding to be torn from her throat.
Yet before the King could force his tongue to move or compose a shred of dignity, Kara let out a soft dismissive breath through her nose.
"You know what?
Never mind," Kara said, rolling her shoulders back against the violet velvet.
Her voice was completely normal, carrying a relaxation that sounded entirely out of place in a hall built for royal decrees.
"Maybe I overstepped a little bit.
It’s my bad, honestly.
I get a little cranky when my blood sugar drops, and having people yell before I’ve had breakfast makes me talk too much.
Forget I said anything."
The casual retreat fell upon the table like a lead weight.
She offered the apology with an airy flick of her single right wrist, not caring in the slightest that she had just rattled the mental foundations of the most powerful ruler on Earth.
The diplomats around the table blinked with their mouths dry as they were unable to keep up with the whiplash of her temperament.

"However," Kara continued, resting her right elbow on the armrest and leaning her cheek against her knuckles with her wire-rimmed glasses catching the harsh glare of the chandelier, "let’s talk about the Blessed Land negotiations a bit because to be completely frank with everyone sitting at this table...
I’m already feeling pretty damn disrespected."
The air in the chamber tautened instantly.

"We haven’t even formally opened the dockets," Kara said, her violet eyes sliding across the semi-circle of rulers, lingering for half a heartbeat on Julian Vanderbilt Senior’s sweat-soaked collar, "and already I’ve had people barking at me and people staring at my empty sleeve like I’m a carnival freak.

I came here in good faith to discuss the territory but I don’t really like the behavior of some of the people in these seats and if this is how the World Council treats independent sovereigns... maybe I shouldn’t bother negotiating at all."
She tapped her fingers against her jaw, letting out a small lazy yawn.
"I could always just pack my bags and disappear straight down into the Sovereign Realm for the next hundred years."
SHK!
Every ruler at the Grand Table stiffened simultaneously.
The words hit them like an electric shock straight through the chest.
’Disappear into the Sovereign Realm.’
It was the ultimate nightmare scenario for the World Council... a phrase that sent cold dread running down the spine of every military strategist and corporate oligarch on the planet.
A Gold Core was dangerous enough sitting inside Europa’s borders but if she pulled an Odin?

If she abandoned the mortal plane entirely, descended through the rifts, and vanished into the endless expanses of the Sovereign Realm where no mortal radar, no orbital satellite, and no army could ever track her?
Humanity’s only Gold Core would become an unreachable untouchable phantom.
And if she ever decided to emerge from a rift fifty years later, she could tear down a civilization over breakfast and vanish before the sirens even went off.
’Wait,’ thought Grand Tsar Nikolai Volkov, his thick frost-bitten fingers tightening against his knees as his strategic mind kicked into gear. ’The Umbral Basin is an isolated sector right?
The transition portals there are unstable.
If she wants to maintain Blessed Land with how big it’s going to become, she has to rely on the World Council’s supply chains.
She has to buy our—’
"Don’t bother doing the math, Tsar," Kara said, cutting through his thoughts as if he had spoken them through a megaphone.
Volkov flinched, his massive frame jerking back against his chair.
Kara smiled, her violet eyes glowing faintly behind her clear lenses and locking straight onto the King’s pale face.
"I don’t need your supply lines," she said, her voice dropping into a light melodic drawl that carried to the highest rafters.
"Because after all... the All-Father of Asgard, Odin, already sent word.
He called for me to come down and meet him in Asgard."
THUD!
It felt as though the entire room had dropped ten feet into the earth.
The King stiffened so violently that the star-iron backrest of the throne groaned under the sudden spike of his aura!
The air inside the dome grew blistering with the moisture on the walls instantly evaporating into thin hissing steam.
’Odin called for her?!’
The revelation was a hammer blow that shattered every remaining shred of leverage the World Council held.
Odin.
The First Gold Core who had abandoned humanity centuries ago to sit above the deities in the deepest most unfathomable layers of the Sovereign Realm.
And now, the first new Gold Core born in human history was casually sitting here, drinking their wine, telling them that Odin himself had already extended an invitation to his court.
The entire dynamic of the room inverted in an instant.
Kara White wasn’t an upstart lord looking to buy trade permits or beg for recognition...

She already had the greatest sponsor in existence waiting for her in the deep trenches so she was simply stopping by the World Council out of mild curiosity, checking to see if humanity had anything worth trading before she turned her back on them forever.
They had zero leverage.

While the nine rulers and the seven hooded magistrates were still choking on the geopolitical weight of that reality, Kara pushed her star-iron chair back with a soft, effortless scrape against the stone.
She stood up.
Her tailored double-breasted suit fell into place with the empty left sleeve pinned flat to her ribs, swaying slightly in the hot drafts rolling off the dais.
"So, yeah," Kara said, stretching her neck until the joints popped with clean, muffled clicks.

"Since you people want to waste time with this little Tournament of Succession to fight over dirt, and since the Princess over there needs a second combatant so she doesn’t have to apologize to Julian’s little syndicate..."
She stepped out from behind the Grand Table with her single right hand tucking into her trouser pocket.
"I’ll just go with Aki myself."
The announcement fell upon the assembly like a falling bell.
"Lord Vespera!" President Julian Vanderbilt Senior choked out, his heavy square face turning pale as ashes.
"You cannot possibly—"
"I’m entering the bracket as her representative," Kara continued, ignoring his presence.
She turned her head, looking up toward the elevated boxes where the noble houses were seated.

chapters.title: Chapter 541: Daddy’s Boy [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Up in the Bloom family tier, Seraphina Bloom’s crimson eyes dilated to the size of coins with her hands flying to the grips of her twin curved daggers and her breath hitching in her throat.
Valerius Sterling meanwhile choked on his own spit as Kara’s violet gaze drifted over them with her lips curving into a slow chilling smile that made the hairs on their arms stand up straight.

"Don’t worry," Kara called out, her voice smooth and playful, yet carrying a terrifying undertone that made the noble scions shiver. "I’m going to hold myself back a bit. I’m not going to come into the ring and one-shot everyone right away... That’d make for a terrible broadcast, wouldn’t it? I’d like to see each and every one of your powers first. So make sure you bring your best, kids~"
Valerius swallowed hard, his face turning the color of chalk.
’She’s going to play with us,’ he thought with his heart hammering against his ribs. ’She’s going to dissect us like lab rats on a global livestream.’
The King’s voice broke through the murmurs with his voice sounding cold and full of disapproval.
He stared down from the dais, his sapphire eyes locking onto the small trembling girl sitting alone.

"She has no name," the King stated, his voice carrying the weight of an unmovable imperial stone. "The unawakened scions of House Castellian are not recorded on the registry... It is strictly forbidden under imperial law to bestow a formal name upon a member of the royal family who has not earned the sacred middle seal, Zel."
Kara didn’t even turn to face him.
She just strolled casually across the black flagstones with the heels of her leather dress shoes clicking rhythmically against the stone.
Click! Click! Click!

"Oh, please," Kara said, rolling her eyes toward the vaulted ceiling with an exaggerated shrug of her shoulders. "You don’t even give a damn about your own kids, so why do you care what people call her? It’s just a name... It’s not like she needs your permission to have syllables attached to her face."
She reached the lowest tier and stepped up to the small shadowed chair where the First Princess was curled in on herself.
Aki was trembling violently.
Her head was still bowed, her velvet skirts clutched tightly in her small white-knuckled fists and her chest heaving with silent breaths.

The terror of being singled out by the King, the shame of almost having to bow before Vanderbilt, and the terrifying god-like presence of the woman who had just shattered the court... it was all pressing down upon her like a mountain of lead.
Kara stopped beside the chair. She reached down with her single right hand, her fingers settling gently over Aki’s narrow trembling shoulder.
... It was warm.

"She doesn’t need to take that Zel middle name either," Kara said loudly with her voice carrying cleanly across the frozen pit toward the throne. "That name only comes with your dysfunctional, garbage family baggage anyway... Aki is more than enough."
Aki flinched, a sharp burning heat instantly rising from her chest straight into her face.
’Silas... do you have to make it embarassing~?’

A fierce brilliant blush bloomed across her pale cheeks, spreading with terrifying speed all the way to the tips of her small delicate ears, making the First Princess look impossibly flustered and unmistakably cute against the dark imposing backdrop of the hall.
Kara leaned down slightly.
She pulled her right hand back from Aki’s shoulder and extended it forward with her palm up and her calloused fingers open and relaxed.
"First Princess," Kara spoke. "I officially request to stand as your blade in the Exhibition of Succession. Will you have me?"
Aki stared at the open hand.

Her vision blurred with unshed tears with her lower lip trembling as she looked at the calloused palm, the neat cuffs of the charcoal suit, and then up... straight into those deep hypnotic violet eyes behind the clear glass lenses.
’Ah... my savior...’
And in that fraction of a second, looking deep into those glowing violet depths...
’Silas.’
Aki’s breath caught in her throat.
She could swear by everything holy and by every memory she had of Blessed Land that she could see Silas Graves looking back at her from behind the woman’s face.
’And he’s smiling too.’
Slowly, her small slender fingers reached out.
GRIP!
Her trembling hand settled into Kara’s right palm and Kara’s fingers closed firmly around hers feeling warm like an iron bracket.
With a single smooth pull that didn’t strain a single muscle, Kara hoisted the First Princess clean out of her chair, bringing her firmly to her feet on the black flagstones.
"Good girl," Kara murmured, her voice soft enough that only Aki could hear it beneath the ventilation hum.
She stepped close, her single right arm resting casually across Aki’s shoulders, pulling the red-faced princess securely against her side.

"Listen to me. There are a whole lot of pathetic people in this room who are going to try and bully you... They’re going to talk about your lack of a core, your bloodline, your standing but don’t you pay them a single second of your attention."
She squeezed Aki’s shoulder gently.
"You’re special. Remember that."
Aki’s eyes welled with hot tears spilling over her lashes and running down her burning cheeks, but she bit her lip, refusing to let out a sob.
She nodded wth her smaller hand clutching the sleeve of Kara’s charcoal suit like a lifeline.
Kara turned, dragging the First Princess along with her toward the massive double doors at the primary diplomatic exit.
As she walked, Kara raised her pinned left sleeve, waving the empty charcoal fabric back at the Grand Table with lazy mocking cheerfulness.

"Alright, folks!" Kara called out, her voice echoing off the obsidian arches. "We’re heading out to brainstorm some winning strategies! Make sure you ping us when the bracket is drawn and the arena is primed! Don’t start the party without us~!"
CREEEAK... SLAM!

The heavy star-iron blast doors groaned as the guards frantically scrambled out of their path, slamming shut behind the two women with a deafening crash that echoed down the long vaulted hallways of the Citadel.
The golden pressure that had choked the chamber evaporated completely, leaving behind only the flat stale smell of cold air and more than five hundred people who had forgotten how to breathe.
Every ruler at the table was staring at the closed iron doors in a state of disbelieving paralysis.

The Lord of Blessed Land... the miraculous untouchable Second Phase Gold Core had just bypassed all nine global superpowers, ignored trillion-credit trade offers, insulted the Supreme Monarch to his face, and formally allied herself with the nameless unawakened defect of the Royal house.
Down in the southern arc, High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva sat with her arms crossed over her broad armored chest.
Her jaw was locked tight, her sharp canine teeth grinding together with an audible crunch that made her adjutants flinch.
Beside her, Chancellor Henri de Montmirail looked like a man whose bank vault had just been swallowed by a sinkhole, clutching his treaty papers with trembling white-tipped fingers.
The greatest martial asset of the century had just walked out the door, and neither of them had gotten a piece of her.
Yet... as Da Silva exhaled through her nose, the tension in her broad shoulders began to loosen.
A tiny smile carved itself into the corner of her dark, scarred lips.
’All of this will pay off,’ Da Silva thought, her feline eyes narrowing with cool satisfaction.
Among all the arrogant nobles and blind Lords in the capital, Da Silva had been the only one who had seen value in the First Princess from the very first day she had laid eyes on her.
While the King saw an empty vessel and Alexander saw an embarrassment, Da Silva had recognized a long-term investment... A pure-blooded royal who was starved for basic human connection.
Over the last two years, Da Silva had quietly cultivated that bond.
They spoke frequently over private, encrypted comm-channels, sharing casual messages about border logistics, court gossip, and personal feelings.
Just three nights ago, Aki had texted her a long, rambling paragraph about her anxieties.
And now?
Now, that lonely neglected little princess was walking arm-in-arm with the Lord of Blessed Land, treating her like an older sister and a protector.

’You played yourself, Julian,’ Da Silva thought, casting a cold amused glance toward Vanderbilt’s trembling frame. ’You tried to corner a stray dog, and she brought back a dragon. I don’t need to beg Blessed Land for an alliance since Aki considers me a confidante... The road to that Gold Core runs straight through that little girl’s inbox.’
Up on the Royal dais, the King drew a slow shuddering breath.
His face had settled back into an impenetrable sheet of blue-tinted marble with his fingers releasing the table as he prepared to regain control of the room.
"Scribes," the King’s voice boomed. "Record the factional adjustments. The Exhibition of Succession shall proceed with—"
"Father!"
The shout was sudden and lacking any sort of court etiquette as every head in the room jerked back toward the dais.
Crown Prince Alexander had surged to his feet without asking for permission.
His star-iron slate tumbled from his hands, clattering loudly against the stone risers as he stepped forward and his tall muscular frame was trembling with hysterical outrage.
His royal uniform was stretched taut across his broad shoulders, his beautiful face was mottled with dark furious red, and his bloodshot eyes burned intensely.

"Majesty!" Alexander roared. "This assembly has been subjected to unforgivable treason! That... that gutter-trash vagrant from Europa dared to spit upon your Royal authority! She mocked the sacred blood of House Castellian, challenged your leadership before the governing bodies of the world, and dragged our name through the mud in front of foreign delegates!"
He struck his own chest with a heavy, armored fist!
THUMP!

"You are the King of the World! You are the pillar that saved this species from the ashes of the Apocalypse! I will not stand by and allow a Gold Core to treat our court like an unranked tavern brawl!"
He dropped heavily to one knee with the joint of his boot slamming into the stone with an ear-splitting crack.
CLANG!

"Authorize my entry into the Exhibition, Father!" Alexander begged, his hands clasped over his heart and his chest heaving as he looked up at the King with adoration. "I am an Awakened Prince of the Realm! I have broken through the threshold and reached the Fourth Stage of Core Advancement! If the laws of the bracket require parity, I will voluntarily wear the Star-Iron Suppression Rings! I will seal my pathways! I will drag my rank down to the Second Stage to match her refinement phase!"
His voice cracked, a plea that laid his entire soul bare before hundreds of people.
"Let me teach her a royal lesson, Father! Let me break her in the Sovereign Realm and restore the honor of your crown!"
The chamber fell into an embarrassed uncomfortable silence.
The Crown Prince of the human race was literally on his knees, offering to bind his own soul pathways with suppression collars just to avenge a minor insult leveled at his father’s pride.
The King looked down at him.
For three long seconds, the monarch’s face was a void.

He looked at his firstborn son... the boy he had sent into the northern trenches at fourteen, the prince who had slaughtered hordes without ever receiving a word of praise and slowly, the corner of the King’s thin lips curled upward into a approving smile.
"Granted," the King murmured softly. "Stand, Alexander. You shall carry the standard of the Sovereign Throne."
Alexander’s entire body shuddered with euphoric relief.
His heart skipped a frantic beat with a sickening surge of pure warmth flooding his chest as he rose.
His eyes shining with triumphant tears as he bowed his head in deep worshipful gratitude.
"Thank you, Father," Alexander breathed, his voice trembling. "I will bring you her head."
Across the table, High Marshal Valeria Da Silva watched the spectacle with unmasked revulsion, slowly shaking her head as she leaned back in her chair.

’A grown-ass man still crying for daddy’s approval,’ Da Silva thought, her lip curling in bitter contempt. ’Thirty years old, commanding thousands of soldiers in the Sovereign Realm, and he’s still begging for a pat on the head like a lapdog that brought back a dead bird... It’s pathetic... Truly pathetic... Where the hell are the real men in this world?’

She glanced toward the closed double doors where Kara White had vanished minutes earlier, remembering the fearless casualness with which that one-armed woman had looked the King in the eye and dared him to strike.
’God,’ Da Silva scoffed internally, a dark chuckle rumbling in her throat. ’If I could find a man who had even half the balls of that woman, I would have been pregnant five years ago.’
The King’s voice rose cutting through the murmurs of the court.
"The Exhibition of Succession is hereby convened! Scribes, draft the brackets! Prime the transit corridors to the Sovereign Realm! We adjourn!"
Miles to the west, in the commercial high-district of Valoria City, the midday heat rose off the asphalt in shimmering oily waves.

Evelyn stood on the crowded sidewalk near the central shopping concourse with her shoulders hunched deep inside an oversized red hoodie that swallowed her petite frame down past the hem of her black cotton gym shorts.
Her messy black hair was yanked into a lopsided, loose bun held together by a scuffed plastic stylus, and dark exhausted purple bruises hung heavily beneath her eyes.
Between her dry lips rested a slim white Silver-Leaf cigarette, the tip glowing dull orange against the bright sunlight as she dragged a deep scorching lungful of menthol smoke into her chest.
FSSSSSH.
She held it for two seconds, letting the nicotine cut through the dull chronic throb behind her temples, before blowing a long thin stream of gray smoke into the humid air.
’Date my ass,’ Evelyn thought bitterly, her thumb flicking a tiny clump of ash into the gutter.
Who the hell was she supposed to be on a date with?
[Bonus Chapter]

Crown Prince Alexander had surged to his feet without asking for permission.
His star-iron slate tumbled from his hands, clattering loudly against the stone risers as he stepped forward and his tall muscular frame was trembling with hysterical outrage.
His royal uniform was stretched taut across his broad shoulders, his beautiful face was mottled with dark furious red, and his bloodshot eyes burned intensely.
"Majesty!" Alexander roared.
"This assembly has been subjected to unforgivable treason!
That... that gutter-trash vagrant from Europa dared to spit upon your Royal authority!
She mocked the sacred blood of House Castellian, challenged your leadership before the governing bodies of the world, and dragged our name through the mud in front of foreign delegates!"
He struck his own chest with a heavy, armored fist!
THUMP!
"You are the King of the World!
You are the pillar that saved this species from the ashes of the Apocalypse!
I will not stand by and allow a Gold Core to treat our court like an unranked tavern brawl!"
He dropped heavily to one knee with the joint of his boot slamming into the stone with an ear-splitting crack.
CLANG!
"Authorize my entry into the Exhibition, Father!" Alexander begged, his hands clasped over his heart and his chest heaving as he looked up at the King with adoration.
"I am an Awakened Prince of the Realm!
I have broken through the threshold and reached the Fourth Stage of Core Advancement!
If the laws of the bracket require parity, I will voluntarily wear the Star-Iron Suppression Rings!
I will seal my pathways!
I will drag my rank down to the Second Stage to match her refinement phase!"
His voice cracked, a plea that laid his entire soul bare before hundreds of people.
"Let me teach her a royal lesson, Father!
Let me break her in the Sovereign Realm and restore the honor of your crown!"
The chamber fell into an embarrassed uncomfortable silence.
The Crown Prince of the human race was literally on his knees, offering to bind his own soul pathways with suppression collars just to avenge a minor insult leveled at his father’s pride.
The King looked down at him.
For three long seconds, the monarch’s face was a void.

He looked at his firstborn son... the boy he had sent into the northern trenches at fourteen, the prince who had slaughtered hordes without ever receiving a word of praise and slowly, the corner of the King’s thin lips curled upward into a approving smile.
"Granted," the King murmured softly.
"Stand, Alexander.
You shall carry the standard of the Sovereign Throne."
Alexander’s entire body shuddered with euphoric relief.
His heart skipped a frantic beat with a sickening surge of pure warmth flooding his chest as he rose.
His eyes shining with triumphant tears as he bowed his head in deep worshipful gratitude.
"Thank you, Father," Alexander breathed, his voice trembling.
"I will bring you her head."
Across the table, High Marshal Valeria Da Silva watched the spectacle with unmasked revulsion, slowly shaking her head as she leaned back in her chair.

’A grown-ass man still crying for daddy’s approval,’ Da Silva thought, her lip curling in bitter contempt. ’Thirty years old, commanding thousands of soldiers in the Sovereign Realm, and he’s still begging for a pat on the head like a lapdog that brought back a dead bird...
It’s pathetic...
Truly pathetic...
Where the hell are the real men in this world?’

She glanced toward the closed double doors where Kara White had vanished minutes earlier, remembering the fearless casualness with which that one-armed woman had looked the King in the eye and dared him to strike.
’God,’ Da Silva scoffed internally, a dark chuckle rumbling in her throat. ’If I could find a man who had even half the balls of that woman, I would have been pregnant five years ago.’
The King’s voice rose cutting through the murmurs of the court.
"The Exhibition of Succession is hereby convened!
Scribes, draft the brackets!
Prime the transit corridors to the Sovereign Realm!
We adjourn!"
Miles to the west, in the commercial high-district of Valoria City, the midday heat rose off the asphalt in shimmering oily waves.

Evelyn stood on the crowded sidewalk near the central shopping concourse with her shoulders hunched deep inside an oversized red hoodie that swallowed her petite frame down past the hem of her black cotton gym shorts.
Her messy black hair was yanked into a lopsided, loose bun held together by a scuffed plastic stylus, and dark exhausted purple bruises hung heavily beneath her eyes.
Between her dry lips rested a slim white Silver-Leaf cigarette, the tip glowing dull orange against the bright sunlight as she dragged a deep scorching lungful of menthol smoke into her chest.
FSSSSSH.
She held it for two seconds, letting the nicotine cut through the dull chronic throb behind her temples, before blowing a long thin stream of gray smoke into the humid air.
’Date my ass,’ Evelyn thought bitterly, her thumb flicking a tiny clump of ash into the gutter.
Who the hell was she supposed to be on a date with?
