Glad you’re all enjoying the arc.

chapters.title: Chapter 542: Cheating On Silas...?
paragraphs: The barista from sector two who looked like a twig and cried when the espresso machine jammed?
Or the corporate pencil-pusher from the trade guild who spent forty minutes talking about his index funds before asking if she had an Awakened core?
’Ah... I really am a loser.’
If she were to go on a date with anyone, it would be Silas but Evelyn herself didn’t know how that would end up.
She looked down at herself.
The red cotton of the hoodie hung like a tent over her frame while her legs on the other hand were pale and joined in a pair of beat-up canvas sneakers with torn laces.
’I have so much money and I still prefer to look like this...’

Perhaps this was one of her flaws but it was good with her, sure she looked like a tired runaway who had crawled out of a storm drain and not an elite Lord who was in the top hundred of the Classic Leaderboard.
People in this city liked tall statuesque women with long legs, curved hips, and tailored silk jackets... women who looked like they belonged on billboards for cosmetic mana-enhancement clinics.
Nobody was looking twice at a twenty-two-year-old chain-smoker who looked like she hadn’t slept at all, even if she was quite pretty.
’Whatever,’ she muttered, taking another long drag until the paper crackled. ’At the very least, I managed to dodge that godforsaken World Council meeting...’
The mere thought of that summit made her stomach knot up with cold acid.
She had actually intended to go.

For about ten minutes yesterday morning, she had stood in the armory of her territory staring at the heavy mythril plate and the translucent blue crystal rapier that made up her registered persona as Lord Sky.
But the entire cover was built on a lie.
Her helmet was sturdy enough to stay on her head through Lord wars, sure, but what about in a room where the King of the World was sitting ten paces away?
A fucking helmet! That was her disguise!
If the King released his spiritual pressure, the shockwave alone could have blown the latch clean off her head, sending the helmet rolling across the marble floor like a kicked bucket.
What then?
’Oh, hello, Your Majesty! The stoic mysterious Lord Sky is actually a depressed, foul-mouthed twenty-two-year-old girl who looks like she lives on instant ramen and stress smokes!’
They would have clapped her in anti-mana cuffs before she could even summon a water barrier.
Silas, on the other hand, had that ridiculous ring he’d gotten from Thora.

The spatial warping was bound directly to the band’s internal enchantment... It was completely portable, didn’t slip off, and turned him into a one-armed woman with glowing purple eyes who could throw hands with a lot of people.
’And the idiot didn’t even care,’ Evelyn thought, her teeth grinding down hard on the cigarette filter.
When she had shoved him out the door of the room this morning, waving her hand and blabbing about having a lunch date just to get out of the summit, she had secretly waited to see his reaction.
’I just wanted a tiny flicker...’
Maybe a pause or a raised eyebrow... Hell she would have taken a single irritated question like, "Who are you going with?" or "Since when do you date people?"
Instead?
The big idiot had just given her a cheerful thumbs-up, told her not to spend all her cash on more cigarettes to stink up the building, and stepped straight back to the Keep.
"Dense one-track-minded bastard," Evelyn grumbled under her breath, dropping the butt to the concrete and grinding it flat with the heel of her sneaker.
Her stomach gave a violent hollow growl that vibrated straight through her ribs.
GRRRRR!
"Ugh, fuck..." she winced, pressing a palm against her stomach. "I’m starving."
She looked up at the polished mahogany facade of the restaurant directly in front of her.
It was an upscale glass-fronted establishment called Le Jardin Doré... all polished brass, white marble tiling, and velvet banquettes visible through the tinted floor-to-ceiling windows.
She took two steps toward the polished brass doors, reaching into her pocket out of habit to pull out another cigarette, when her eyes caught the small silver plaque mounted beside the handle.
[STRICTLY NO SMOKING — VIOLATORS SUBJECT TO IMMEDIATE FINE]
Evelyn stopped dead.
She stared at the sign for three agonizing seconds, her left eyelid giving an involuntary violent twitch.
"Fuck," she said out loud to the empty street. "I’m too hungry for this shit."

With a sharp irritated flick of her wrist, she banished the half-empty pack of Silver-Leafs and her metal lighter straight into her Lord Inventory, the items popping out of physical space and vanishing into the dimensional pocket tied to her soul.
She pushed the heavy brass door open and stepped inside.
CHIME!
The cool lavender-scented air conditioning hit her like a bucket of iced water which was a welcome relief from the baking heat outside.
Inside, soft jazz was humming through concealed ceiling speakers, and the gentle clinking of silver cutlery against fine china filled the room.

Several wealthy patrons in tailored business suits and silk day-dresses turned their heads with their eyebrows arching in sharp collective disapproval as a girl in an oversized red hoodie and gym shorts shuffled past the maître d’ podium.
Evelyn ignored them completely.
She spotted a small secluded two-seater booth near the back of the dining room, walked over, and flopped down into the velvet seat with a heavy exhausted groan.
A nervous-looking young waiter in a crisp white shirt rushed over, clutching an embossed leather menu against his chest like armor.
"Uh... welcome to Le Jardin, miss," the waiter stammered, his eyes darting down to her scuffed sneakers. "Are you... waiting for a party, or—"

"Garlic butter pasta," Evelyn said immediately, not even opening the menu. "The largest portion you have... Side of roasted potatoes, a basket of sourdough bread with extra butter, and an iced lemon water. Bring the water right now or I’m going to pass out on this table."
"R-Right away, ma’am!"
The waiter practically sprinted toward the kitchen.
Evelyn leaned her head back against the plush velvet, closing her eyes and letting out a long shuddering breath.
Without a cigarette between her fingers, her hands felt restless with her nerves jumping under her skin.

’Hope Silas isn’t getting his ass handed to him,’ she mused silently with a smirk tugging at the corner of her mouth. ’Knowing that idiot, he probably tried to punch one of the Presidents in the face already.’
Hopefully he wouldn’t do something as dumb enough as challenging the King Of The World...
Right?
She opened her eyes, letting her gaze drift lazily across the dining room to pass the time.
And then, her breath caught in her throat.
Across the dining floor, seated at an exclusive corner booth framed by large potted palms and a panoramic view of the courtyard fountain, sat a woman.
She had long magnificent hair that fell in rich, heavy waves of deep, vibrant purple, cascading down the back of an immaculate ivory-white pantsuit cut from expensive silk.
Even from across the restaurant, her profile was unmistakable.
’Isn’t that the billionaire...?’ Evelyn’s eyes narrowed into sharp, dangerous slits. ’Harper, right? Harper Whitmore.’
That woman that owned almost all of the LAB buildings in Valoria City..

And more importantly, the very same woman Evelyn had seen standing inside Silas’s apartment not too long ago, leaning against his door and looking at Evelyn like she was an annoying stray pest that had crawled in through the window.
’What the hell is she doing in Valoria City?’ Evelyn wondered, her tactical mind immediately spinning up.
She leaned slightly to the side, peering past the marble pillar to see who was sitting across from the purple-haired CEO.
It was a young man, perhaps twenty-four or twenty-five, wearing an elaborate high-collared tunic of gold-embroidered linen and deep lapis-lazuli silk.
Around his neck hung heavy chains of solid gold and raw turquoise, and his dark kohl-lined eyes carried the distinct insufferable arrogance of eastern royalty.
’The crest on his collar...’ Evelyn analyzed, her brow furrowing. ’That’s the royal house of Khemet... The Third Prince of Khemet, isn’t it? What is this, a private contract?’
A sudden wicked realization struck her like a lightning bolt.
’Wait a second...’ she thought, her shoulders shaking with silent stifled laughter. ’Is she cheating on Silas with an Egyptian Prince?!’
The thought was ridiculous and immensely satisfying.

Silas was out in the World Council meeting sweating through a summit with the King of the World, and his billionaire sugar-mommy was up here sipping imported sparkling water with a foreign prince in broad daylight.
’Oh, this is gold,’ Evelyn chuckled under her breath. ’I am taking this video and shoving it in his face the second he steps back in Blessed Land... He is never, ever going to hear the end of this.’

Keeping her posture low and relaxed to avoid drawing attention, Evelyn reached into the deep front pocket of her red hoodie, pulled out her black mobile phone, and rested it flat against the rim of her bread plate.
With a silent flick of her thumb, she activated the high-resolution optical sensor, zooming the feed straight between the palm leaves, locking onto Harper and the Prince of Khemet.
She tapped the record button.

On the screen, Prince Malikar was talking animatedly with a condescending smirk playing across his lips as he leaned forward, gesturing with a gold-ringed hand toward a glowing digital document floating above the table.
Harper sat completely still, her purple hair obscuring her profile with her pale hands resting motionless beside her untouched glass.
Evelyn glanced down for half a second, checking to see if her waiter was bringing the bread rolls.
...Still empty.
"Where the hell is my bread..." she muttered, looking back up toward the window.
Her breath froze solid in her lungs as her pupils contracted into microscopic pinpricks.
Harper had stood up.
Her right arm was extended across the white linen tablecloth, her bare pale hand clamped directly over Prince Malikar’s face!
Her slender fingers covered his eyes, his nose, and his mouth like an iron vice with her thumb digging deep into the soft unprotected hollow behind his ear.
The prince was being lifted bodily out of the velvet booth by his skull with his heavy gold chains swinging wildly as his legs kicked out in spastic circles.
GURRRR-K!
A wet horrific sound tore from behind Harper’s palm and before Evelyn’s horrified eyes, the Prince’s body was collapsing inward.
It was drying out...?
The healthy tanned skin of his forearms wrinkled, blackening into desiccated parchment as the moisture, the blood, and the fat were violently violently ripped from his tissue!
His muscular frame shrank at a terrifying speed with his ribs jutting sharply through his linen tunic like snapped spars and his eyeballs sinking into hollow sockets beneath her grip.
SHSHSHSHSHSH!
The sound of dry rustling sand filled the quiet corner of the dining room as the Prince’s legs stopped kicking.
His knees cracked, turning gray and brittle as dry clay and then... right there beneath the crystal chandelier, his entire body disintegrated.

A torrent of pale-yellow sand poured from beneath his embroidered tunic, spilling down over the edge of the velvet chair and splashing onto the polished hardwood floor like grain bursting from a torn sack.

His arms crumbled into dust with his gold bangles clattering against the parquet with sharp hollow rings, until nothing remained in Harper’s grip except an empty silk tunic and a swirling dry cloud of sand that drifted down into the heap below.
"AAAAAAAHHHHHHH!"
A woman two tables away shrieked at the top of her lungs with her chair flying backward as she scrambled across the floor.
"HE’S DUST! HE’S TURNING INTO DUST! GUARDS! SOMEONE CALL THE GUARDS!"

The entire restaurant exploded into pandemonium with plates shattering and tables flipping as well as terrified diners lunged for the emergency exits, waiters screamed, and the sound of breaking glass echoed like gunfire across the dining floor.
Harper ignored the screaming crowd as she stood beside the pile of yellow silt, her ivory suit pristine with not a single grain of dust clinging to her silk sleeves.
Slowly... rhythmically... her head turned.
Her thick purple hair parted.
Beneath her bangs, her eyes were glowing with a terrifying green radiance and her gaze locked straight through the palm leaves.
Straight onto Evelyn.
Evelyn didn’t even have time to blink.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The floor beneath Harper’s feet detonated as a deafening eruption of thousands of tons of high-velocity pressurized sand exploded outward in an apocalyptic wave, shattering the reinforced windows into millions of shards, pulping forty tables into kindling, and tearing the plaster clean off the ceiling as the tidal wave of grinding earth roared straight at Evelyn’s booth.
’SHIT!’

chapters.title: Chapter 543: Authorized To Kill [Bonus - [
paragraphs: The shockwave began with the violent displacement of mass.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The reinforced poly-glass facade of Le Jardin Doré exploded into millions of needle-fine diamond fragments, carried outward on an ocean of pressurized sun-baked sand.
The interior of the dining hall ceased to exist in a fraction of a second.

Teakwood tables, cast-iron candelabras, high-back velvet chairs, and porcelain soup tureens were caught in the grinding circular torrent of yellow silt, shredded down to composite kindling and chalky dust before they even breached the sidewalk.

The blast blew outward across the four-lane boulevard, ripping the steel canopies off the luxury storefronts opposite the plaza, snapping the decorative light posts at their bolt plates, and drowning the entire district in a roaring blinding tidal wall of earth.
CRASH... SHSHSHSHSH!
From thirty feet above the shattered stone plaza, a ball of turbulent churning liquid ruptured straight out of the apex of the erupting dune.
SPLASH!
"Haah!"
Evelyn burst free into the open air.
She wasn’t dead, though her oversized red hoodie was soaked through at the cuffs and hem.
In that final microscopic window before the ceiling had caved in, she hadn’t tried to trade raw concussive force against thousand-ton geological pressure.
That would be stupid...

She had collapsed her mana inward, pulling every droplet of atmospheric moisture in the dining room... along with the ice water from her table and the condensation weeping along the wine coolers into a spinning hydro-barrier that had wrapped around her body like a lubricated cocoon.
The sand had scraped across the pressurized water, deflecting off the slick centrifugal skin rather than pulverizing her ribs into chalk.
It was heavy and reeked of dredged silt, but it had worked.
"Tch... fucking hell," Evelyn spat through gritted teeth, coughing out a mouthful of gritty sediment as her sneakers cleared the top of the blast.
The ground below her was a roiling pit of shifting dunes, but the sand wasn’t done.
The moment her silhouette broke free of the main geyser, the turbulent mass beneath her surged with violent intelligence.
FSSSSSH... WHIP!

Six thick whip-like tendrils of braided high-velocity sand shot skyward from the collapsing crater with their tips sharpening into rotating drill-cones that hissed through the air like screaming vipers.

Evelyn didn’t panic as her face remained set in that permanent irritated exhaustion that defined her morning shifts, but her body moved with the terrifying movement of a frontline commander who had survived years of war at the Unmovable Wall.
In mid-air, with no solid footing beneath her, she twisted her core.
SWOOSH!
The first tendril tore through empty space an inch past her shoulder with the friction singeing the frayed red cotton of her sleeve.
She kicked off the air by manifesting a paper-thin pressurized disc of surface-tensioned water beneath the sole of her scuffed sneaker for a secon.
THUMP!
The tiny platform popped, propelling her two yards to the left just as the second and third tendrils crossed in a lethal scissor-snap where her throat had been.
CRACK!

The fourth and fifth spikes converged on her descent but Evelyn pulled her knees tight against her chest, somersaulting between the twin corkscrewing drills, feeling the coarse grains graze her shins before kicking off another temporary splash-disc with her left heel.
SWISH... SLAM!
She cleared the final whip, her momentum carrying her horizontally toward the sheer glass face of an adjoining twelve-story office tower.
THUD!
Her canvas sneakers hit the vertical pane of structural glass at an angle but she didn’t slip.

A thin film of moisture anchored her rubber soles to the smooth surface with her knees bending deeply to absorb the concussive inertia before she pushed off, vaulting up five yards to plant herself sideways against the concrete mullion between the fifth-floor windows.
"Fuuu... Been a while since I had to push myself like that."
She looked down into the ruins of the plaza.

The settling dust parted like an opening curtain, revealing the center of the deep circular crater where the restaurant’s foundation had been and standing in the center of the pit was Harper Whitmore.
Except it wasn’t the untouchable multi-billion-credit CEO anymore.
The immaculate ivory-white pantsuit was still draped over the figure’s shoulders but the fabric was stiff, bloated with internal pressure, and crusted in yellow clay and the face...
Evelyn scrunched up her nose, her dark eyes narrowing with pure revulsion.
The left half of the woman’s visage was still smooth, pale, and striking, framed by rich waves of vibrant purple hair.
But the right half had completely collapsed into a sloughing nightmare.
The cheekbone had dissolved into thick, crumbling clumps of grit that slid down her jawline like drying mud, leaving behind a hollow empty crater where her right eye socket should have been.
The lips were split down the center, one side soft and painted with gloss and the other side a line of coarse sandstone grinding against itself with an audible sickening crunch.
CRUNCH! GRIND!
The creature stood motionless amidst the rubble with its left purple eye wide and glazed over with a dull luminescent yellow film.
"You’re not her, are you?" Evelyn called down. "What the hell are you...?"
However the entity did not offer a spoken reply, instead, the throat of the woman bulged outward like a swallowing serpent.
A dry rasping hiss tore from the ruin of its mouth...
HSSSSSSS!

The thousands of tons of sand drowning the plaza began to churn in violent concentric circles as the ivory suit ripped down the spine, tearing into shreds as the shape underneath began to warp, distend, and flow.
The woman’s silhouette melted away like tallow under an open flame.
The shifting dunes rushed upward, climbing the collapsing frame, packing together with speed until the silhouette thickened, broadened, and rebuilt itself into a completely different form.
Within three seconds, standing in the crater was no longer Harper.
It was Prince Malikar of Khemet.
The body was broad-shouldered, draped in the simulated likeness of his gold-embroidered linen tunic and heavy lapis sash, perfectly rendered down to the turquoise stones hanging around his neck.

But there was no living flesh on that frame... His skin was pale, grainy, and shifting constantly in tiny vibrating waves of loose silt, his kohl-lined eyes looking like blank unblinking pools of pure sulfur-yellow.
’A Rogue Awakened,’ Evelyn thought with the muscles along her jaw clenching tight.
That was the formal classification for a Lord like this...
An Awakened individual abusing the authority of Lords within the boundaries of a civilian sector.

Under the global protocols established after the Apocalypse, Lords were strictly barred from unsealing their powers inside civilian zones without direct authorization from the regional safety bureaus.

The city had defense barriers, response protocols, and designated duel grounds for a reason but to detonate a high-tier spell inside a crowded midday restaurant, butcher a foreign dignitary, and reduce thirty civilians to bone-dust wasn’t just a regular breach...
It was a Class-A atrocity!
And under the harsh unvarnished laws of the World Council, when an Awakened went completely rogue like this, there was no courtroom waiting for them.
They were an existential contagion that had to be put down like a rabid dog before the regional infrastructure collapsed.
The sand around the false Prince’s boots began to coil upward, forming four massive spiraling vortices that began grinding the asphalt of the plaza to dust.
BZZZZZZT! BZZZZZZT!

Inside the deep front pocket of Evelyn’s oversized red hoodie, her black mobile began vibrating violently with the shrill obnoxious ringtone of the local dispatch frequency cutting through the low rumble of the forming storm.
’Eh...? Not again...’
Evelyn didn’t take her eyes off the creature in the crater as she reached into her pocket, tapped the screen without looking, and held the glass to her ear.
"I’m a little fucking busy right now," she snapped into the receiver.

"This is Dispatch Officer Vuleptope, Valoria City Police Department, Central Ward," a woman’s voice barked through the speaker, sounding strained with barely contained panic. "We are tracking a seismic spike and massive unauthorized mana-discharge in Sector Seven! Our orbital surveillance grid has identified your registered transponder so you are currently the highest-ranking combat asset in the immediate perimeter!"
’Vuleptope is a crazy name though... Who does that to their kids?’
That aside, they had probably picked up on her other Lord identity which was Lord Evelyn of course. Lord Sky was done differently and she was grateful for that.
"Yeah, no shit," Evelyn muttered, watching the sand creature’s neck twist at a grotesque ninety-degree angle as its sulfur eyes tracked her up on the wall. "I’m looking right at it."

"Under Section Nine of the Metropolitan Defense Edict, the Valoria City Police Department formally invokes emergency conscription!" the officer yelled over the sound of screaming sirens in the background. "You are ordered to intercept and subdue the Rogue Awakened immediately! If non-lethal containment is impossible, you are authorized... repeat, authorized to execute the target on sight!"

"Listen to me, dispatch," Evelyn sighed, rubbing the space between her eyebrows with her left thumb. "I’m off the clock so at the very least, if you want me to... What’s the hazard pay on this? Does the department cover property damage or am I going to get another—"
BOOM!
She didn’t get to finish the sentence.
A column of compressed sand that was five feet wide and traveling at the speed of an artillery shell, pulverized the concrete directly beneath her sneakers!
SHATTER!
The entire fifth-floor facade blew inward, three plate-glass windows disintegrating into a cloud of sparkling dust as the pillar struck the structural pillar.
Evelyn was already airborne.
The instant she felt the air pressure shift beneath her feet, she had vaulted backward off the glass, pushing off with enough force to send her flying in a wide controlled arc across the open street.
"Yeah, yeah, fine, I’ll kill it," Evelyn muttered into the phone, her voice completely deadpan as she descended through the air. "Just make sure the paperwork has my name spelled right this time..."
BEEP!
She hung up, placed the phone straight into her inventory, and hit the ruined asphalt of the boulevard with a clean low crouch.
TAP!
She didn’t immediately draw a weapon.
She stayed crouched on the cracked pavement, reached into her cargo pocket with two fingers, and pulled out a fresh unlit Silver-Leaf cigarette.
She clamped it between her lips, flicked a cheap brass lighter with her thumb and took a long burning drag of smoke into her lungs.
FSSSSSSSSSH!
The yellow-and-white cylinder flared blue in the dust-choked midday light.
Across the ruined intersection, sixty yards away, the creature was losing whatever humanoid composure it possessed.
The body of Prince Malikar was spazzing out violently.
His shoulders twitched in erratic spasms and his jaw unhinging until his mouth was a dark gaping cavern from which loose silt poured like a waterfall.

The thousands of tons of sand that had erupted from the restaurant were no longer sitting dormant... they were rising, caught in a massive, spinning centrifugal vortex that was rapidly turning the entire three-block radius into a blinding howling miniature sandstorm.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The wind screamed, tearing the paint off parked vehicles, pulverizing the remaining brickwork of the storefronts, and reducing visibility to less than ten feet in every direction.
Yet Evelyn remained completely stationary, sitting back on her haunches, her hoodie flapping wildly in the gale.
She drew a second deeper lungful of smoke, letting the chemical burn steady her frayed nerves, and then blew it out smoothly through her nostrils in two neat gray streams.
’Think, you idiot,’ she told herself, her eyes tracking the shifting silhouettes in the dust. ’Don’t just swing like a brute... Use your damn head.’
The Rogue didn’t make tactical sense.
She had watched the person or was it even a person... drain Prince Malikar with her own eyes.
It had clamped its hand over his skull and violently sucked every drop of moisture, plasma, and arterial blood out of his biological frame within four seconds. But why?

A pure earth or sand-affinity entity had no use for mammalian blood as blood was full of iron and biological proteins... it fouled up earth magic, adding unnecessary weight and friction to high-velocity particle manipulation.
If it was an elemental construct, drinking blood was counterproductive.
’So what did it do with it?’ Evelyn analyzed, her gaze sweeping through the blinding yellow haze. ’It didn’t consume it for fuel so I can guess that it was an extraction.’
And then, there was the storm itself.
The miniature sandstorm wasn’t just an offensive weapon designed to grind her down... it was an impenetrable visual screen.
In a major metropolitan hub like Valoria City, with orbital satellites and police drones overhead, a three-block dust screen completely severed overhead thermal tracking.

’It’s moving the blood,’ Evelyn realized with a cold prickle of clarity settling behind her eyes. ’It drained the blood, and while it keeps me occupied in the middle of this street, it’s using the drainage or a secondary sub-construct to transport that blood out of the sector.’

chapters.title: Chapter 544: Fighting With Sand [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She couldn’t afford to waste ten minutes dancing around with a decoy.
"Ugh... I really hate this," she sighed.
Evelyn took one last sharp pull on the Silver-Leaf, pinched the burning ember between her calloused thumb and forefinger to extinguish it, and dropped the crumpled filter into her pocket.
Her right hand opened.
SHING... VUMMMMMMM!
The space directly above her palm rippled with deep cerulean distortion as she reached into her Lord Inventory.
Her fingers closed around a familiar hexagonal hilt of frosted silver, and with a clean metallic hiss as she dragged her signature weapon into the physical world.
’My rapier...’
The blade was three feet of flawless crystal, glowing with an inner, liquid luminescence that hummed at a high frequency.
Evelyn stood up straight.
Her dark eyes, normally half-lidded and drowned in chronic fatigue, snapped wide open.
BA-THUMP!
Deep within the center of her chest, nestled behind her sternum, her spiritual core ignited.
It was a Blue Core.
One that was clear and brilliant as glacial ice.

’I’m not the best or the strongest either... Silas has a Gold core and even his Heroes are stronger than me, and let’s not mention all these nobles that average at Purple cores.’ She thought with her breath wisping out. ’And not only that but in terms of core strength, I’m one of the weakest Blue cores. Anyone in my position might have stopped or given up...’
Yet she had not stopped.

Through brutal years of holding the Unmovable Wall against relentless waves of monsters, through endless sleepless nights refining her soul pathways drop by agonizing drop, she had polished that blue stone until the mana flowing through her veins possessed the cutting density of a diamond drill.
WHIRRRRRR!
A brilliant misty haze of rich cerulean mana wafted off her skin like steam rising from a hot spring but the mana did not form an armor around her body.
It surged upward, flooding directly into the neural pathways behind her eyes.
Her dark pupils contracted, ringed by concentric circles of glowing cyan light.

Instantly, the blinding sandstorm ceased to be an impenetrable wall of dust as the individual trajectories of grinding silica grains slowed to a crawl in her perception with the moisture clinging to each particle illuminating the invisible thermal drafts and mana-currents moving through the intersection.
She could see everything.
GLUG... GLUG... GLUG..!

Beneath her sneakers, the water pooled in the cracked gutters and the moisture in the humid air began to vibrate, bubbling upward in tiny suspended spheres of pure pressurized liquid that orbited her blade like miniature moons.
She raised the translucent blue rapier, resting the flat of the crystal against the side of her forearm.
"Alright, sandbox," Evelyn murmured. "Come on."
The sand entity answered with slaughter.
SKRRRRRRR-BOOM!
The false Prince’s legs dissolved into a swirling cyclone of pressurized dust, propelling him across the sixty yards of ruined asphalt in seconds.

He arrived with the concussive force of a car with his right arm morphing from a humanoid limb into a massive cleaver of compressed sandstone three feet wide, whistling through the air as it cleaved downward toward Evelyn’s skull.
SWISH... SLAM!
Evelyn didn’t try to block it as she knew her physical limitations well.

She was a mana-caster whose physical strength without reinforcement was high but not that high... If she took a direct kinetic blow from an earth-construct of that mass, her forearms would splinter into nothingness.
Instead, she used her size.
The moment the massive stone cleaver descended, Evelyn dropped her center of gravity, ducking cleanly beneath the arc of the swing with an effortless fluid slide.

The displaced wind pressure tore the hood clean off her messy bun, but her scuffed sneakers glided along the asphalt on a micro-thin layer of lubricating water, sliding her directly between the creature’s wide-set legs.
SHING!
Her translucent rapier thrust upward like a needle striking through silk.
CRACK!

The crystal tip struck the hardened sandstone skin of the entity’s thigh though the armor was tough... dense enough that an ordinary steel blade would have shattered on impact but Evelyn had already flooded the crystal with vibrating water mana.
The point vibrated at thirty thousand cycles in seconds, acting as a microscopic hydro-jet that drilled cleanly through the petrified crust, punching straight out the back of the leg.
"Hah!"
Evelyn twisted the hilt as she completed her slide, popping out behind the creature.
The false Prince whipped around with terrifying speed with its left hand stretching outward into five razor-sharp spears of hardened quartz, thrusting straight for her face.
STAB! STAB! STAB!
Evelyn’s head bobbed and weaved with precision.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! SWISH!
The stone spears grazed her cheeks, cutting stray strands of her black hair, but never finding purchase.

Her footwork was brutally efficient as she stepped inside the reach of the long clumsy construct, using her smaller frame to stay inside its guard where the massive weapons couldn’t properly accelerate.
’It’s times like this I thank the gods I’m not as tall as Silas...’
CLANG!
She deflected the fourth thrust with the forte of her rapier, spinning on her heel to redirect the force into the dirt, and brought her blade around in a horizontal slash.
SHIIIIING... CRACK!
The cerulean blade severed the creature’s neck.

The head of Prince Malikar detached cleanly from the shoulders, spinning into the air with a spray of loose yellow dust before hitting the asphalt and disintegrating into a pile of harmless sand but Evelyn didn’t celebrate.
’Decapitation doesn’t mean shit to a golem,’ she thought grimly.
Sure enough, before the headless neck could even finish crumbling, the sand within the chest cavity roared upward like a rising piston.
In the span of half a second, a new head burst forth... identical to the first, its sulfur-yellow eyes glaring down at her with mindless malice.
WHAM!
A massive flat backhand of solid stone caught Evelyn across the chest.
Even with her instinctive mana reinforcement flaring across her ribs, the shockwave sent her skipping backward across the pavement like a flat stone over a pond.
SKIDDDDDDD!

Her sneakers tore two deep grooves through the asphalt with her teeth rattling in her jaw as she came to a halt twenty yards away and a thin trail of blood trickling from the left corner of her mouth.
"Tch... yeah, that hurt," she grunted, wiping her chin with the oversized cuff of her red hoodie. "Hit like a brick wall, you ugly bastard."
The creature didn’t give her time to breathe.
It lunged forward again, the ground beneath its feet undulating like an ocean wave, launching dozens of jagged stone shards ahead of its advance.
TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT!
Evelyn’s rapier became a blur of pale blue light.
CLINK! CLANG! PING!
She parried, deflected, and shattered eighteen high-velocity stone spikes in the span of two seconds with her wrist working like an oiled piston.
Every time her blade made contact, a burst of high-pressure water erupted from the crystal tip, dampening the impact and cracking the structural integrity of the stone.
She closed the distance again.
SWOOSH!
She feinted a thrust to the chest, waited for the creature to raise its massive hammer-like forearms to catch the blow, and then vanished downward.
Evelyn dropped to her knees, sliding forward beneath the guard, her blade tracing a vicious rising diagonal arc.
SLASH... CRACK!
For the second time, the rapier cleaved through the neck, sending the newly regenerated head flying off into the dust yet as the head tumbled away, Evelyn didn’t look at the construct’s body.
Her glowing mana-enhanced cyan eyes were locked onto the ground beneath its feet.
Throughout the entire clash... the feints, the dodges and the parries, Evelyn hadn’t just been surviving.
Her blue mana had been seeping into the wet gutters, spreading through the saturated soil beneath the cracked pavement like an invisible net.
She had found it.
’There you are,’ she thought, her lips curving into a sharp grin.
The construct was indeed a hollow puppet.

Thirty yards behind it, near the shattered curb of the plaza where the storm drains emptied into the city’s underground reservoir, a tiny compact dome of wet sand... no larger than a soccer ball was crawling slowly toward the iron sewer grating.
It was moving under the cover of the howling winds, completely undetectable to an ordinary observer.
And inside that tiny, shifting sphere?
Every single liter of Prince Malikar’s extracted arterial blood, pressurized and insulated within a moisture-locked core.

"Clever parasite," Evelyn muttered, springing back to her feet as the headless torso began to sprout a third head of churning sand. "Too bad you’re dealing with someone who actually does logistics for a living."
She raised her rapier, channeling her mana to end the puppet once and for all...
WEE-WOO-WEE-WOO-WEE-WOO!
The sudden piercing shriek of sirens shattered the sandstorm.
SCREEEEEECH!
Four heavy black-and-white armored response cruisers from the Valoria City Police Department slid around the perimeter barricades, their massive runic-tread tires biting into the ruined asphalt.

The cruisers formed a defensive crescent sixty yards away with the reinforced gull-wing doors snapping open instantly as eight armored tactical officers spilled out with their assault rifles raised and their chest plates glowing with blue light.
Leading the unit was a tall, sharp-featured woman in a navy officer’s trench coat, holding a heavy scattergun against her shoulder.

"Lord Evelyn! Fall back!" the Captain’s voice boomed through an external loudspeaker mounted on the lead cruiser. "The Vanguard has established an overcharge perimeter and we are taking custody of the target!"
Evelyn stopped, lowering her rapier by half an inch, an irritated scowl spreading across her face.
"Are you serious right now?" Evelyn yelled back over the howling wind. "I literally just found the—"
"Stand back!" the Captain ordered, ignoring her completely. "Overcharge suppression rounds primed! On my mark—"
The officers raised their weapons, their barrels tracking the regenerating sand entity and then, every single officer hesitated.
The third head had finished reforming.
The face of Prince Malikar turned toward the police cruisers, his golden necklaces clinking softly in the gale, his pale noble features perfectly rendered in the sunlight.
"Wait... is that...?" one of the younger officers stammered, his finger freezing on the trigger. "The Third Prince of Khemet?! Captain, that’s a foreign dignitary! We can’t fire on—"
"He’s already dead, you idiots!" Evelyn screamed with her patience finally snapping. "It’s a fucking puppet! Shoot it or get out of my way!"
"Open fire!" the Captain roared, shaking off her shock. "Suppress, don’t execute! Light it up!"
TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT!
The tactical rifles fired in unison but they didn’t fire normal bullets.
They were high-voltage suppression rounds, designed specifically to capture rogue Awakeners without causing fatal internal trauma.
Dozens of glowing blue-and-yellow electrical slugs slammed into the sand entity’s chest, torso, and shoulders, discharging hundreds of thousands of volts of concentrated lightning upon impact.
BZZZZZZZZZT! CRACKLE!
The results were instantaneous, but completely wrong for the situation.
Under the intense heat of the electrical arcs, the loose moving sand of the construct’s outer layer began to superheat.
FZZZZZZT!
The granules fused together, vitrifying into brittle dark sheets of jagged glass as the creature’s movements seized, its arms locking in place as the glassy crust paralyzed its limbs.
"We have containment!" the junior officer cheered, lowering his rifle.
"No, don—!"
CRACK!
Right on cue, the brittle glass crust shattered outward in a violent spray of sharp shards!
The electrical charge did not shock the creature’s central nervous system... because it didn’t have one.
The loose sand beneath the street simply surged upward, sloughing off the crystallized shell and rebuilding the limbs with twice the mass and twice the aggression.
The entity’s blank yellow eyes snapped away from Evelyn and then it locked onto the squad of police officers.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The creature liquefied into a surging tidal wave of high-velocity sand, roaring straight toward the police cruisers with the unstoppable momentum of a landslide.
"SHIT! FIRE! RE-ENGAGE!" the Captain screamed, racking the slide of her scattergun, but it was already too late.
The wave crossed forty yards in a heartbeat.
The Captain blinked with her breath catching in her throat as the towering wall of yellow earth rose ten feet above her head, casting a massive suffocating shadow over the cruisers.
In the center of the wave, the gaping hollow maw of the false Prince opened wide, ready to swallow the entire squad whole and crush their bones beneath the force of pressure.
The Captain’s eyes widened in helpless terror with her finger frozen against the trigger as death loomed inches from her face—
SNAP.
A red-hooded figure appeared directly between the Captain and the falling tsunami.
Evelyn didn’t look back.
She simply planted her canvas sneakers into the cracked stone, raised her translucent blue crystal rapier horizontally with both hands, and unleashed the true depth of her mana pool.
"Dissolution Trench!"
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM... BOOM!

"Ugh...
I really hate this," she sighed.

Evelyn stood up straight.
Her dark eyes, normally half-lidded and drowned in chronic fatigue, snapped wide open.
BA-THUMP!
Deep within the center of her chest, nestled behind her sternum, her spiritual core ignited.
It was a Blue Core.
One that was clear and brilliant as glacial ice.

Silas has a Gold core and even his Heroes are stronger than me, and let’s not mention all these nobles that average at Purple cores.’ She thought with her breath wisping out. ’And not only that but in terms of core strength, I’m one of the weakest Blue cores.
Anyone in my position might have stopped or given up...’

Through brutal years of holding the Unmovable Wall against relentless waves of monsters, through endless sleepless nights refining her soul pathways drop by agonizing drop, she had polished that blue stone until the mana flowing through her veins possessed the cutting density of a diamond drill.
WHIRRRRRR!
A brilliant misty haze of rich cerulean mana wafted off her skin like steam rising from a hot spring but the mana did not form an armor around her body.
It surged upward, flooding directly into the neural pathways behind her eyes.
Her dark pupils contracted, ringed by concentric circles of glowing cyan light.

Instantly, the blinding sandstorm ceased to be an impenetrable wall of dust as the individual trajectories of grinding silica grains slowed to a crawl in her perception with the moisture clinging to each particle illuminating the invisible thermal drafts and mana-currents moving through the intersection.
She could see everything.
GLUG...
GLUG...
GLUG..!

Beneath her sneakers, the water pooled in the cracked gutters and the moisture in the humid air began to vibrate, bubbling upward in tiny suspended spheres of pure pressurized liquid that orbited her blade like miniature moons.

SWISH...
SLAM!
Evelyn didn’t try to block it as she knew her physical limitations well.
She was a mana-caster whose physical strength without reinforcement was high but not that high...
If she took a direct kinetic blow from an earth-construct of that mass, her forearms would splinter into nothingness.
Instead, she used her size.
The moment the massive stone cleaver descended, Evelyn dropped her center of gravity, ducking cleanly beneath the arc of the swing with an effortless fluid slide.

The displaced wind pressure tore the hood clean off her messy bun, but her scuffed sneakers glided along the asphalt on a micro-thin layer of lubricating water, sliding her directly between the creature’s wide-set legs.
SHING!
Her translucent rapier thrust upward like a needle striking through silk.
CRACK!

The crystal tip struck the hardened sandstone skin of the entity’s thigh though the armor was tough... dense enough that an ordinary steel blade would have shattered on impact but Evelyn had already flooded the crystal with vibrating water mana.
The point vibrated at thirty thousand cycles in seconds, acting as a microscopic hydro-jet that drilled cleanly through the petrified crust, punching straight out the back of the leg.
"Hah!"
Evelyn twisted the hilt as she completed her slide, popping out behind the creature.
The false Prince whipped around with terrifying speed with its left hand stretching outward into five razor-sharp spears of hardened quartz, thrusting straight for her face.
STAB!
STAB!
STAB!
Evelyn’s head bobbed and weaved with precision.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
SWISH!
The stone spears grazed her cheeks, cutting stray strands of her black hair, but never finding purchase.

Her footwork was brutally efficient as she stepped inside the reach of the long clumsy construct, using her smaller frame to stay inside its guard where the massive weapons couldn’t properly accelerate.
’It’s times like this I thank the gods I’m not as tall as Silas...’
CLANG!
She deflected the fourth thrust with the forte of her rapier, spinning on her heel to redirect the force into the dirt, and brought her blade around in a horizontal slash.
SHIIIIING...
CRACK!
The cerulean blade severed the creature’s neck.

The head of Prince Malikar detached cleanly from the shoulders, spinning into the air with a spray of loose yellow dust before hitting the asphalt and disintegrating into a pile of harmless sand but Evelyn didn’t celebrate.
’Decapitation doesn’t mean shit to a golem,’ she thought grimly.
Sure enough, before the headless neck could even finish crumbling, the sand within the chest cavity roared upward like a rising piston.
In the span of half a second, a new head burst forth... identical to the first, its sulfur-yellow eyes glaring down at her with mindless malice.
WHAM!
A massive flat backhand of solid stone caught Evelyn across the chest.
Even with her instinctive mana reinforcement flaring across her ribs, the shockwave sent her skipping backward across the pavement like a flat stone over a pond.
SKIDDDDDDD!

Her sneakers tore two deep grooves through the asphalt with her teeth rattling in her jaw as she came to a halt twenty yards away and a thin trail of blood trickling from the left corner of her mouth.
"Tch... yeah, that hurt," she grunted, wiping her chin with the oversized cuff of her red hoodie.
"Hit like a brick wall, you ugly bastard."
The creature didn’t give her time to breathe.
It lunged forward again, the ground beneath its feet undulating like an ocean wave, launching dozens of jagged stone shards ahead of its advance.
TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT-TAT!
Evelyn’s rapier became a blur of pale blue light.
CLINK!
CLANG!
PING!
She parried, deflected, and shattered eighteen high-velocity stone spikes in the span of two seconds with her wrist working like an oiled piston.

chapters.title: Chapter 545: Kara And Aki [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The air exploded into a roaring high-pressure attack of pressurized azure water.
WHOOSH!
A massive circular ring of dense water blades detonated outward from the tip of her rapier in a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree hemisphere but the water wasn’t flowing naturally...
’I didn’t get to use this at the Lord War but sure.’
It was pressurized to a lot of water per square inch, cutting through physical matter with the terrifying precision of an industrial laser.
SHSHSHSHSHSH... CRASH!
The colossal wave of sand exploded as though it was atomized.

The individual grains of sand were stripped of their charge, saturated instantly by the overwhelming volume of water, and reduced to a harmless sloshing slurry of thin mud that splashed heavily across the asphalt, washing over the police cruisers, the tires, and the boots of the stunned tactical officers like a gentle river.
The construct was gone and completely dissolved.
Drip! Drip! Drip!
The heavy lavender-scented rain of residual water fell softly through the cleared midday air, washing away the dust and leaving the intersection sparkling in the bright sunlight.

Behind her, the Captain sat half-collapsed against the hood of her cruiser with her face paper-white and her uniform soaked to the bone in warm water and mud, staring at the red-hooded back before her with wide disbelief.
Evelyn didn’t even turn around as she flicked her rapier downward, shedding the last droplets of water from the crystal edge with a clean sharp shlick.
"Don’t wet your pants, Captain," Evelyn said with her voice deadpan, carrying easily through the quiet street. "It’s just water."
The Captain swallowed hard, her voice trembling as she struggled to stand up straight.
"Y-You... you wiped out that Rogue in a single strike..." the Captain stuttered, her eyes darting to the massive puddles of mud drowning the street. "The... the mana power... how—"
Evelyn didn’t answer.
Her left hand rose, pointing toward the far corner of the intersection that was thirty yards away.

There, having survived the dissolution of the main body, the small dense dome of wet sand was scrambling frantically toward the iron bars of the storm drain, trying to slip beneath the city streets and vanish into the darkness.
"Did you really think I forgot about you?" Evelyn muttered.
GLUG!
A high-velocity sphere of pressurized water formed instantly around her extended left palm, no larger than a billiard ball, spinning with enough centrifugal force to whistle like a falling shell.
She flicked her wrist.
THWIP!
The water-bullet tore through the air, crossing the thirty yards in the blink of an eye.
POP!
It struck the retreating dome of wet sand dead center.
The compacted sand ruptured instantly and the moment the containment broke, the horrifying truth detonated before the eyes of the entire police squad.
SPLASHHHHH!
A massive violent explosion of thick dark-crimson blood erupted from the ruptured sphere, painting the surrounding concrete, the curb, and the iron sewer grating in a sickening shower.
The metallic stench of so much blood hit the air like a hammer, filling the clean afternoon breeze with the unmistakable reek of slaughter.
The officers gasped in collective gagging horror.
"Is that...?" the Captain choked out, clapping a gloved hand over her mouth as her stomach violently churned. "Sweet merciful gods... that’s all the blood from the victims..."
Evelyn took a long exhausted breath through her nose, feeling the strain of the mana-discharge settle into her joints.
With a soft fluid motion, she reversed her grip on the crystal rapier.
SHING!
The translucent blue blade dissolved into shimmering motes of cerulean light, returning straight into her Lord Inventory.
She reached down, pulled the hem of her oversized red hoodie straight, and ran a tired hand through her messy black bun, tucking a loose strand of hair behind her ear.
Evelyn turned around and slowly walked toward the police cruisers with her scuffed sneakers splashing softly through the puddles of mud.
The officers immediately lowered their rifles, stepping back to give her a wide reverent berth.
They looked at her petite frame, her pale face, and the dark circles under her eyes with a mixture of awe and terror.
’How high has she gone in Core Advancement...?’
The Captain stepped forward, snapping her boots together and bowing her head deeply at a sharp ninety-degree angle of military respect.

"We owe you our lives, Lord Evelyn," the Captain said, her voice shaking with genuine humility. "The Valoria City Police Department is forever in your debt. If there is anything our precinct can do to facilitate your official report—"
"Save the bow," Evelyn cut her off, stopping five feet from the cruiser and looking at the Captain with mild irritation. "First of all, I’m a Classic Lord."
The surrounding officers blinked in surprise as several of them exchanged hurried bewildered glances.
A Classic Lord... then why did she tell them to stop bowing?! Didn’t that mean they should bow even more for being in the presence of a Lord of her level?!
Evelyn reached into the deep front pocket of her red hoodie and her hand emerged holding her black mobile phone.
She tapped the screen with her thumb, turning the glowing display outward toward the Captain and the stunned tactical squad.

On the high-resolution screen, paused in crystal-clear definition, was the frozen frame from thirty minutes ago with the ivory-suited silhouette of Harper, her pale hand clamped like an iron vice over the face of Prince Malikar, whose body was visibly desiccating into dust beneath her grip.
Evelyn’s lips curved into a dangerous smirk.
"And second of all..." Evelyn said, tapping the glass with her fingernail.
Tap! Tap!
"I have... video evidence."
The heavy star-iron blast doors groaned behind them as the locks sealed with a muffled concussive thud that cut off the suffocating atmosphere of the Grand Assembly Chamber.
Kara did not break her stride.
Her right hand remained firmly clasped around Aki’s wrist, tugging the First Princess along the high, vaulted corridors of the Citadel’s inner perimeter.
The obsidian flags beneath their boots were polished to a mirrored finish, reflecting the nervous twitching silhouettes of the imperial guards stationed every ten paces.
The guards stood rigid, halberds clutched in white-knuckled grips and their breastplates humming with latent mana.
Yet as the pair approached, not a single soldier dared to step forward and not a single officer barked for credentials.

Their eyes flicked between the First Princess’s flushed tear-streaked face and the one-armed woman in the charcoal double-breasted suit whose empty sleeve swayed with lazy insolent ease against her ribs.

Everyone had felt the tremor minutes ago and everyone knew the woman walking down their corridor had looked the King of the World in the eye, called him a cowardly father, and dared him to unleash the First King’s Destruction.
...What a disrespectful woman.
Kara stopped in front of a heavy oak door reinforced with brass filigree as she turned her head toward a guard sergeant pressed flat against the wall.
"Hey," Kara said. "Is this an empty lounge?"
The sergeant swallowed so hard his adam’s apple bobbed over his iron gorget. "Y-Yes, My Lady. It is the private staging antechamber for foreign emissaries."
"Cool... We’re borrowing it."
Kara pushed the handle down with her single hand, hauling Aki inside before the guard could even stammer out a protest.
The moment their heels crossed the threshold, Kara paused as her single right hand did not leave the brass doorknob.

Her violet eyes narrowed slightly behind her wire-rimmed glasses as her senses flared outward in an invisible circular sweep, mapping every cubic inch of the lavish room... the velvet divans, the cold hearth, the ornate baseboards and the crystal sconces lining the ceiling.
Beside her, Aki pulled her wrist free with her chest heaving as she tried to catch her breath.

"W-Wait," Aki whispered frantically, reaching out to tug the sleeve of Kara’s suit and her eyes darting toward the ornate molding. "You can’t talk here... You shouldn’t even speak freely... Every single staging room in the Citadel is rigged with listening arrays and the scribes... they monitor the arrays through the floorboards to record every delegation’s private—"
Kara didn’t let her finish.
She reached out with her right index finger, pressing the pad of her flesh lightly against the plaster wall beside the doorframe.
BZZZZZZZZT!
A sharp violent web of blinding pale-blue lightning erupted from her fingertip.

It raced through the interior masonry like a swarm of starving serpents as the lightning traveled through the star-iron conduit pipes, snaked behind the baseboards, surged into the copper wiring of the ceiling chandeliers, and jumped straight through seventeen hidden runic listening stones embedded within the plaster.
POP! POP! CRACKLE! SSSSSSH!

A sequence of muffled electrical ruptures snapped behind the drywall as tiny wisps of gray acrid smoke curled out from the corners of the ceiling, accompanied by the distinctive smell of fried copper and shattered quartz.
Kara pulled her hand back, lifted her index finger to her lips, and gently blew a thin trail of smoke away from her nail.

"Thor showed me that trick," Kara muttered, clicking her tongue with satisfaction. "That lady might be a drunken couch potato ninety percent of the time, but when it comes to short-circuiting devices, she knows her stuff."
She reached behind her, grabbed the edge of the heavy oak door, and kicked it shut with the heel of her shoe.
SLAM!
The mechanical deadbolt clicked into place and the room fell into silence, insulated from the rest of the world by three feet of stone and a completely fried surveillance circuit.

Kara let out a long sigh that rattled her collarbones as she rolled her shoulders back, reaching up with her single hand to pinch the bridge of her nose, letting her head drop forward for two seconds as if shedding twenty pounds of performative arrogance.

"Man," she groaned, rotating her neck until the vertebrae popped with clean muffled clicks. "Sitting in those fancy chairs is exhausting. My lower back feels like someone hit it with a cinderblock... How do these nobles do it all day without falling asleep?"
She turned around, letting her hand drop.
"Anyway—"
Kara stopped dead.
Standing in the center of the Persian rug, Aki was trembling from her slippers to the collar of her navy velvet gown.
Her head was bowed with her shoulders shaking with violent suppressed tremors.
Her face was flushed a dark feverish crimson with her lips pressed together so tightly they were white, and her eyelashes were completely soaked with moisture.
She looked like she was desperately trying to hold in a hurricane with her hands clenched into white-knuckled balls within the heavy folds of her skirt.
DRIP!
A single fat tear spilled over her lashes and splashed onto the polished floorboards.
Kara blinked behind her glasses as she stepped forward, leaning down slightly and her violet eyes widened with genuine panic.
"Whoa, hey," Kara said, her voice dropping into a gentle tone. "What’s wrong? What happened? Did someone hit you on the way out? Is it your hand?"
She looked down at her own right palm, flexing the calloused fingers in confusion.

’Did I grip her wrist too hard?’ Kara thought, a spike of internal guilt striking her chest. ’Damn it, I keep forgetting she doesn’t have mana reinforcement to pad her joints. Did I sprain her wrist when I dragged her out of the chair?’
"Aki? Talk to me. Did I hurt you?"
At the sound of her name, the dam broke.
Aki choked and a ragged strangled sob tore out of her throat with her chest heaving as she squeezed her eyes shut.
"N-No..." Aki gasped, the words stumbling over each other as they were thick with mucus and suffocating grief. "N-No, you... you didn’t... I..."
She tried to force her mouth to form the syllables.
She tried to say thank you... She tried to say you saved my life... Aki tried to say nobody has ever stood between me and my father before...
But every time she drew a breath, the crushing weight worthlessness caught in her windpipe, turning her words into broken pathetic wheezes.
"Th-Tha... th-thank... y-you..." she stuttered, her voice cracking like dry wood. "I... I’m... I’m s-sorry... I’m s-so..."
Kara took another step, raising her single hand awkwardly.
"Hey, easy. Breathe. You’re hyperventilating. Look at me, you’re fine. Nobody’s touching you. Just take a deep—"
Aki moved.
With a desperate uncoordinated lunge, the First Princess threw her entire weight forward, launching herself straight at Kara’s chest.
"Whoa—shit!"
Kara, completely unprepared for an unawakened civilian tackling her like a wild hound, lost her footing on the slick Persian rug.
Her heels slid and her center of gravity tipped backward then with an ungraceful crash, both of them went sprawling across the floorboards.
THUD!
Kara hit the ground on her back with her single right arm instinctively coming up to protect her head, only for Aki to land squarely on top of her.
