The heavy lavender-scented rain of residual water fell softly through the cleared midday air, washing away the dust and leaving the intersection sparkling in the bright sunlight.

Behind her, the Captain sat half-collapsed against the hood of her cruiser with her face paper-white and her uniform soaked to the bone in warm water and mud, staring at the red-hooded back before her with wide disbelief.
Evelyn didn’t even turn around as she flicked her rapier downward, shedding the last droplets of water from the crystal edge with a clean sharp shlick.
"Don’t wet your pants, Captain," Evelyn said with her voice deadpan, carrying easily through the quiet street.
"It’s just water."
The Captain swallowed hard, her voice trembling as she struggled to stand up straight.
"Y-You... you wiped out that Rogue in a single strike..." the Captain stuttered, her eyes darting to the massive puddles of mud drowning the street.
"The... the mana power... how—"
Evelyn didn’t answer.
Her left hand rose, pointing toward the far corner of the intersection that was thirty yards away.

There, having survived the dissolution of the main body, the small dense dome of wet sand was scrambling frantically toward the iron bars of the storm drain, trying to slip beneath the city streets and vanish into the darkness.
"Did you really think I forgot about you?" Evelyn muttered.
GLUG!
A high-velocity sphere of pressurized water formed instantly around her extended left palm, no larger than a billiard ball, spinning with enough centrifugal force to whistle like a falling shell.
She flicked her wrist.
THWIP!
The water-bullet tore through the air, crossing the thirty yards in the blink of an eye.
POP!
It struck the retreating dome of wet sand dead center.
The compacted sand ruptured instantly and the moment the containment broke, the horrifying truth detonated before the eyes of the entire police squad.
SPLASHHHHH!
A massive violent explosion of thick dark-crimson blood erupted from the ruptured sphere, painting the surrounding concrete, the curb, and the iron sewer grating in a sickening shower.
The metallic stench of so much blood hit the air like a hammer, filling the clean afternoon breeze with the unmistakable reek of slaughter.
The officers gasped in collective gagging horror.
"Is that...?" the Captain choked out, clapping a gloved hand over her mouth as her stomach violently churned.
"Sweet merciful gods... that’s all the blood from the victims..."
Evelyn took a long exhausted breath through her nose, feeling the strain of the mana-discharge settle into her joints.
With a soft fluid motion, she reversed her grip on the crystal rapier.
SHING!
The translucent blue blade dissolved into shimmering motes of cerulean light, returning straight into her Lord Inventory.
She reached down, pulled the hem of her oversized red hoodie straight, and ran a tired hand through her messy black bun, tucking a loose strand of hair behind her ear.
Evelyn turned around and slowly walked toward the police cruisers with her scuffed sneakers splashing softly through the puddles of mud.
The officers immediately lowered their rifles, stepping back to give her a wide reverent berth.
They looked at her petite frame, her pale face, and the dark circles under her eyes with a mixture of awe and terror.
’How high has she gone in Core Advancement...?’
The Captain stepped forward, snapping her boots together and bowing her head deeply at a sharp ninety-degree angle of military respect.
"We owe you our lives, Lord Evelyn," the Captain said, her voice shaking with genuine humility.
"The Valoria City Police Department is forever in your debt.
If there is anything our precinct can do to facilitate your official report—"
"Save the bow," Evelyn cut her off, stopping five feet from the cruiser and looking at the Captain with mild irritation.
"First of all, I’m a Classic Lord."
The surrounding officers blinked in surprise as several of them exchanged hurried bewildered glances.
A Classic Lord... then why did she tell them to stop bowing?!
Didn’t that mean they should bow even more for being in the presence of a Lord of her level?!
Evelyn reached into the deep front pocket of her red hoodie and her hand emerged holding her black mobile phone.
She tapped the screen with her thumb, turning the glowing display outward toward the Captain and the stunned tactical squad.

On the high-resolution screen, paused in crystal-clear definition, was the frozen frame from thirty minutes ago with the ivory-suited silhouette of Harper, her pale hand clamped like an iron vice over the face of Prince Malikar, whose body was visibly desiccating into dust beneath her grip.
Evelyn’s lips curved into a dangerous smirk.
"And second of all..." Evelyn said, tapping the glass with her fingernail.
Tap!
Tap!
"I have... video evidence."
The heavy star-iron blast doors groaned behind them as the locks sealed with a muffled concussive thud that cut off the suffocating atmosphere of the Grand Assembly Chamber.
Kara did not break her stride.
Her right hand remained firmly clasped around Aki’s wrist, tugging the First Princess along the high, vaulted corridors of the Citadel’s inner perimeter.
The obsidian flags beneath their boots were polished to a mirrored finish, reflecting the nervous twitching silhouettes of the imperial guards stationed every ten paces.
The guards stood rigid, halberds clutched in white-knuckled grips and their breastplates humming with latent mana.
Yet as the pair approached, not a single soldier dared to step forward and not a single officer barked for credentials.

Their eyes flicked between the First Princess’s flushed tear-streaked face and the one-armed woman in the charcoal double-breasted suit whose empty sleeve swayed with lazy insolent ease against her ribs.

Everyone had felt the tremor minutes ago and everyone knew the woman walking down their corridor had looked the King of the World in the eye, called him a cowardly father, and dared him to unleash the First King’s Destruction.
...What a disrespectful woman.
Kara stopped in front of a heavy oak door reinforced with brass filigree as she turned her head toward a guard sergeant pressed flat against the wall.
"Hey," Kara said.
"Is this an empty lounge?"
The sergeant swallowed so hard his adam’s apple bobbed over his iron gorget.
"Y-Yes, My Lady.
It is the private staging antechamber for foreign emissaries."
"Cool...
We’re borrowing it."
Kara pushed the handle down with her single hand, hauling Aki inside before the guard could even stammer out a protest.
The moment their heels crossed the threshold, Kara paused as her single right hand did not leave the brass doorknob.

Her violet eyes narrowed slightly behind her wire-rimmed glasses as her senses flared outward in an invisible circular sweep, mapping every cubic inch of the lavish room... the velvet divans, the cold hearth, the ornate baseboards and the crystal sconces lining the ceiling.
Beside her, Aki pulled her wrist free with her chest heaving as she tried to catch her breath.
"W-Wait," Aki whispered frantically, reaching out to tug the sleeve of Kara’s suit and her eyes darting toward the ornate molding.
"You can’t talk here...
You shouldn’t even speak freely...
Every single staging room in the Citadel is rigged with listening arrays and the scribes... they monitor the arrays through the floorboards to record every delegation’s private—"
Kara didn’t let her finish.
She reached out with her right index finger, pressing the pad of her flesh lightly against the plaster wall beside the doorframe.
BZZZZZZZZT!
A sharp violent web of blinding pale-blue lightning erupted from her fingertip.

It raced through the interior masonry like a swarm of starving serpents as the lightning traveled through the star-iron conduit pipes, snaked behind the baseboards, surged into the copper wiring of the ceiling chandeliers, and jumped straight through seventeen hidden runic listening stones embedded within the plaster.
POP!
POP!
CRACKLE!
SSSSSSH!

A sequence of muffled electrical ruptures snapped behind the drywall as tiny wisps of gray acrid smoke curled out from the corners of the ceiling, accompanied by the distinctive smell of fried copper and shattered quartz.
Kara pulled her hand back, lifted her index finger to her lips, and gently blew a thin trail of smoke away from her nail.
"Thor showed me that trick," Kara muttered, clicking her tongue with satisfaction.
"That lady might be a drunken couch potato ninety percent of the time, but when it comes to short-circuiting devices, she knows her stuff."
She reached behind her, grabbed the edge of the heavy oak door, and kicked it shut with the heel of her shoe.
SLAM!
The mechanical deadbolt clicked into place and the room fell into silence, insulated from the rest of the world by three feet of stone and a completely fried surveillance circuit.

Kara let out a long sigh that rattled her collarbones as she rolled her shoulders back, reaching up with her single hand to pinch the bridge of her nose, letting her head drop forward for two seconds as if shedding twenty pounds of performative arrogance.
"Man," she groaned, rotating her neck until the vertebrae popped with clean muffled clicks.
"Sitting in those fancy chairs is exhausting.
My lower back feels like someone hit it with a cinderblock...
How do these nobles do it all day without falling asleep?"
She turned around, letting her hand drop.
"Anyway—"
Kara stopped dead.
Standing in the center of the Persian rug, Aki was trembling from her slippers to the collar of her navy velvet gown.
Her head was bowed with her shoulders shaking with violent suppressed tremors.
Her face was flushed a dark feverish crimson with her lips pressed together so tightly they were white, and her eyelashes were completely soaked with moisture.
She looked like she was desperately trying to hold in a hurricane with her hands clenched into white-knuckled balls within the heavy folds of her skirt.
DRIP!
A single fat tear spilled over her lashes and splashed onto the polished floorboards.
Kara blinked behind her glasses as she stepped forward, leaning down slightly and her violet eyes widened with genuine panic.
"Whoa, hey," Kara said, her voice dropping into a gentle tone.
"What’s wrong?
What happened?
Did someone hit you on the way out?
Is it your hand?"
She looked down at her own right palm, flexing the calloused fingers in confusion.
’Did I grip her wrist too hard?’ Kara thought, a spike of internal guilt striking her chest. ’Damn it, I keep forgetting she doesn’t have mana reinforcement to pad her joints.
Did I sprain her wrist when I dragged her out of the chair?’
"Aki?
Talk to me.
Did I hurt you?"
At the sound of her name, the dam broke.
Aki choked and a ragged strangled sob tore out of her throat with her chest heaving as she squeezed her eyes shut.
"N-No..." Aki gasped, the words stumbling over each other as they were thick with mucus and suffocating grief.
"N-No, you... you didn’t...
She tried to force her mouth to form the syllables.
She tried to say thank you...
She tried to say you saved my life...
Aki tried to say nobody has ever stood between me and my father before...
But every time she drew a breath, the crushing weight worthlessness caught in her windpipe, turning her words into broken pathetic wheezes.
"Th-Tha... th-thank... y-you..." she stuttered, her voice cracking like dry wood.
I’m s-sorry...
I’m s-so..."
Kara took another step, raising her single hand awkwardly.
"Hey, easy.
Breathe.
You’re hyperventilating.
Look at me, you’re fine.
Nobody’s touching you.
Just take a deep—"
Aki moved.
With a desperate uncoordinated lunge, the First Princess threw her entire weight forward, launching herself straight at Kara’s chest.
"Whoa—shit!"
Kara, completely unprepared for an unawakened civilian tackling her like a wild hound, lost her footing on the slick Persian rug.
Her heels slid and her center of gravity tipped backward then with an ungraceful crash, both of them went sprawling across the floorboards.
THUD!
Kara hit the ground on her back with her single right arm instinctively coming up to protect her head, only for Aki to land squarely on top of her.

chapters.title: Chapter 546: Kara And Aki [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Princess was sitting directly on Kara’s stomach with her navy skirts bunched around her knees and her face buried completely in her hands as she wept with reckless abandon.
Tears poured through her fingers like water through a sieve, splashing hot and wet straight through Kara’s tailored charcoal shirt.

"I-I’m sorry!" Aki wailed, her entire body jerking with each violent sob. "I’m s-sorry! I know it’s... it’s pathetic! I know I’m a mess! But I... I really just... I really wanted to cry so bad! I couldn’t... I had to hold it for so long...!"
Kara lay flat on the floor, staring up at the plaster ceiling with a dazed wide-eyed expression.
Having a weeping, royal girl straddling her midsection while soaking her bespoke collar in tears was completely outside her training but slowly, Kara raised her single right arm.
She didn’t push Aki off.
Instead, her broad calloused palm settled gently on the back of Aki’s head with her fingers threading through the soft loose strands of dark hair.
Aki gasped, her frame shivering violently and then... as if all the bone and sinew had melted out of her body, she collapsed completely forward.
Her forehead slammed into the crook of Kara’s neck, her arms wrapping desperately around Kara’s shoulders, burying her face into the warm scented skin of her throat.
SOB! SOB!
The sobs were muffled against Kara’s flesh, hot breath and wet tears pooling in the hollow of her collarbone.
Kara didn’t move.
She lay there on the cold wood with her right hand gently patting the back of the girl’s head, feeling the rapid flutter of Aki’s pulse against her own neck.

"It’s alright," Kara said softly, her voice carrying a rare quiet tenderness that had never once surfaced in the Grand Assembly. "Go ahead. Let it out... Everybody needs a good, ugly cry once in a while, even princesses... Especially princesses who have to deal with garbage families."
They stayed like that for several minutes.
The ragged gasps slowly began to slow as the violent shaking in Aki’s spine subsided into small occasional twitches, until finally, the room was quiet again, save for the rhythm of their breathing.
Aki sniffled with a wet loud sniffle that she immediately tried to swallow in embarrassment.
She slowly pushed herself up with both hands, her palms pressed against Kara’s chest as her face was burning hotter than a forge.

Aki’s eyes were swollen, puffy, and rimmed in angry crimson while her nose was bright pink, her hair was a catastrophic bird’s nest, and a damp dark patch was visibly soaked into the lapel of Kara’s charcoal suit.
She looked down at Kara, realized she was still sitting directly across the woman’s stomach, let out a tiny high-pitched squeak, and scrambled backward across the rug like a startled crab.

"I-I... I apologize!" Aki stammered, covering her swollen eyes with both forearms, her face turning an impossible shade of beet-red. "That was... that was completely unbefitting of... of anyone! I didn’t mean to tackle you! I just... my legs moved on their own and—"
Thud!
Kara sat up smoothly, resting her right wrist against her raised knee.
Her tailored jacket was wrinkled, her collar was damp, and her hair was slightly disheveled, but she had a wide amused grin plastered across her face.

"Tackle me?" Kara teased, tilting her head with a low chuckle. "You call that a tackle? I’ve been hit by monsters that had less impact, Princess. Though I gotta admit, you’ve got decent form for someone with no core reinforcement... You caught me completely off-guard."
Aki’s hands dropped an inch, revealing one puffy embarrassed blue eye glaring at her from behind her wrists.
"Don’t make fun of me..."
"I’m not making fun of you," Kara laughed, standing up and brushing a stray fleck of rug lint from her trousers.

She reached out with her single hand, grabbing Aki’s arm and hauling her gently to her feet. "I’m complimenting your initiative. Most people in this building are too busy bowing to remember how to move their feet."
Kara turned, walking over to a long plush velvet sofa resting beneath the tall lancet windows.

She didn’t sit down properly like a noblewoman as she collapsed onto it sideways, throwing her long legs over the armrest, letting her head sink deep into the cushions with an audible groan of luxury.

"Ugh, finally," Kara sighed, staring up at the gilded ceiling moldings. "If I had to listen to that old man drone on for another five minutes, I was going to lose my mind... No offense, by the way. I know he’s your father and all, but holy shit, Aki. What a piece of work."
Aki stood near the center of the rug, smoothing down the front of her navy skirts with nervous fluttering motions.
’Is it just me or are Silas and Kara different...?’
Even their mannerisms, at least Silas tried to contain himself. Kara made no such effort at all...
At the mention of the King, her lower lip poked out slightly with her eyebrows drawing together in a small genuine scowl.
"He’s..." Aki started, her throat tight.
She hesitated.
Her entire life, she had been trained under the iron laws of roya etiquette.
You did not speak ill of the Throne and you did not disrespect the progenitor.
The words in her throat felt heavy and dangerous, like trying to lift a boulder with bare hands.
"He’s a..." she tried again, her face scrunching up in intense concentration. "He’s a... a..."
Kara turned her head, watching her with an eyebrow raised in amusement.
"A what? Come on, spit it out. There are no listening arrays left to tell on you."
Aki took a sharp determined breath, puffed her cheeks out until they were round and red, and practically shouted.
"He’s an asshole!"
The word left her mouth with the force of a detonating cannon.

The instant the syllable died, Aki slapped both hands over her mouth, her eyes bulging to the size of saucers with her skin turning so violently red that Kara wondered if she was about to pass out from shock.
She looked around the empty room as if expecting the Citadel’s executioners to drop through the ceiling beams and take her head.
Kara stared at her for three seconds.
Then, slowly, Kara raised her single right hand, curling her fingers into a fist and extending her thumb straight into the air.
"Solid," Kara said, nodding with deadpan approval. "A classic with clean execution and good volume but honestly? You can do better."
Aki blinked, slowly lowering her hands from her lips, looking very lost. "B-Better how...? Isn’t that... isn’t that the worst word?"
Kara let out a loud, incredulous snort.

"The worst word? Kid, ’asshole’ is what you call a guy who cuts you off in traffic or forgets to bring napkins with the takeout... For a man who left you to rot in a dark palace for twenty-five years because your soul didn’t come with fireworks? That’s barely a greeting so what other insults do you know?"
Aki tilted her head, genuinely racking her brain.
She had grown up isolated in the inner sanctums, reading historical treatises, diplomatic registries, and poetry manuals.
Her entire social sphere consisted of cold tutors, silent handmaidens well except for Mira, and the distant polite sneers of court nobles who were too terrified of law to use vulgarity.

"Well..." Aki began, counting on her slender fingers with utmost seriousness. "There’s... scoundrel and ne’er-do-well. Once, when Alexander took my practice wooden sword and snapped it over his knee, I called him an uncouth barbarian."
Kara choked on her own spit, coughing into the sofa cushion.
"An uncouth barbarian?" Kara wheezed, her shoulders shaking with uncontrollable laughter. "Stop, please, you’re killing me. You’re actually going to break my ribs..."

"It was very harsh at the time!" Aki protested, her face burning as she stamped her foot against the Persian rug. "The maid made me copy thirty pages of the ancestral statutes as penance and... and during the winter feast, when Julian.Jr poured cold wine on my skirt and said it was an accident, I told him he was a witless popinjay!"
"A witless popinjay?!" Kara howled, wiping a tear of mirth from behind her glasses. "Oh, man. The venom! The savagery! How did Julian survive such psychological trauma?"
"Stop laughing at me!" Aki whined, her cheeks puffing out into an adorable frustrated pout. "I didn’t grow up in the lower sectors so that is the extent of my vocabulary!"
Kara pushed herself up onto her elbow, shaking her head with a wide, fond grin.
"Alright, alright, come here," Kara said, beckoning with her right forefinger. "Sit down before you hurt yourself."
Aki hesitated, but the warm relaxed atmosphere of the room was impossible to resist.
She walked over to the velvet sofa, smoothing her skirts before perching delicately on the edge of the cushions beside Kara’s hip with her hands clasped neatly in her lap.
Kara leaned closer, dropping her voice to a conspiratorial murmur.

"Repeat after me," Kara instructed, her violet eyes gleaming with pure mischief. "Your father is an arrogant, self-important, crusty old bastard who wouldn’t know real leadership if it bit him on his royal ass..."
Aki gasped with her jaw dropping open. "I can’t say that!"
"Yes, you can. Come on. Say it. It’s therapeutic."
"I... I shouldn’t! It’s treason!"
"The listening bugs are fried, Aki. Say it. Arrogant... crusty... old bastard."
Aki looked at Kara’s wide encouraging grin as she looked down at her own hands, taking a slow trembling breath.
"He’s an... an arrogant..." she squeaked, her voice trembling like a frightened mouse. "A cr-crusty... old... b-bastard..."
The syllables felt bizarre and utterly terrifying on her tongue, but the moment they left her lips, a strange electric thrill shot straight through her chest.
Kara beamed, ruffling Aki’s messy blue hair with her knuckles.
"Look at that! Natural talent. Memorize that one and use it whenever you look at his portrait in the gallery."
Aki swatted Kara’s hand away with a soft pout, but the tension that had gripped her jaw for years was completely gone.
She looked at Kara, taking in the elegant cheekbones, the flawless pale skin, and the rich dark bangs falling across the wire-rimmed glasses.
"Your... your female form," Aki murmured softly, her fingers tracing the hem of her sleeve. "It looks... really amazing. It suits you."
Kara chuckled, leaning her head back against the sofa.

"Thanks. Honestly, it’s pretty convenient. The disguise ring does most of the heavy lifting. It alters the skeletal perception, shifts the voice, masks the core signature completely... Which is a massive relief, because if people figured out what was actually under the hood, the entire summit would have turned into a circus."
Aki tilted her head, curious. "What do you mean?"
"Well," Kara said, tapping her chin with a lazy smirk, "in my male body? Right now? I’m completely naked."
Aki froze as her eyes dilated to the size of dinner plates.
"What?" Aki whispered, the word barely carrying through the air.

"Yeah," Kara said, nodding with nonchalance. "I was in such a rush to come here early this morning that I literally just hopped out of the bath, slipped the ring onto my finger, and let the illusion weave the suit over my bare skin so underneath the disguise, I don’t have a stitch of clothes on."
Aki’s brain short-circuited.
’N-Naked...?!’
The thought hit her with the concussive force of a blast to the face.
Instantly, an unbidden detailed image flashed behind Aki’s eyes.

Silas... his tall broad-shouldered frame, the lean muscle cut across his chest, the water droplets glistening along his collarbones and steam rising from his skin as he stepped out of a porcelain tub with nothing on standing right there in the room, separated from her by only a thin translucent film of disguise magic.

’Wait... wait... wait...’ Aki’s thoughts screamed in hysterical panic, her hands flying to her burning cheeks. ’If he’s naked underneath... and I just tackled him... and I was sitting directly on his stomach... that means... that means I was basically...?!’
Her breath hitched.
Her heart was hammering so fast, so hard against her ribs that she genuinely thought she was going to faint right there on the velvet upholstery.
Her imagination ran wild, visualizing the line of his hips, the broad expanse of his back, the scars running down his—
"Pfft... hahahaha!"
A loud wheezing laugh shattered the fantasy as Aki snapped out of it, blinking frantically.
Kara was clutching her side with her single hand, laughing so hard tears were prickling in the corners of her eyes.

"Oh, man, you should see your face!" Kara cackled, pointing at Aki’s beet-red visage. "I was totally lying! I’m wearing full under-armor underneath the suit! I would never walk into an imperial fortress without layered gear! You actually believed me?!"
Aki’s mouth dropped open.
The realization hit her, followed immediately by an overwhelming wave of mortification.

"You... you jerk!" Aki yelled, her voice pitching up a bit as she grabbed a plush velvet throw pillow and slammed it against Kara’s shoulder. "You’re terrible! You’re an awful person! That wasn’t funny at all!"
POOF!
Kara caught the pillow easily with her single hand, still chuckling softly under her breath.
"Alright, alright, I’m sorry," Kara grinned, tossing the pillow aside.

Kara let out a loud, incredulous snort.
"The worst word?
Kid, ’asshole’ is what you call a guy who cuts you off in traffic or forgets to bring napkins with the takeout...
For a man who left you to rot in a dark palace for twenty-five years because your soul didn’t come with fireworks?
That’s barely a greeting so what other insults do you know?"
Aki tilted her head, genuinely racking her brain.
She had grown up isolated in the inner sanctums, reading historical treatises, diplomatic registries, and poetry manuals.
Her entire social sphere consisted of cold tutors, silent handmaidens well except for Mira, and the distant polite sneers of court nobles who were too terrified of law to use vulgarity.
"Well..." Aki began, counting on her slender fingers with utmost seriousness.
"There’s... scoundrel and ne’er-do-well.
Once, when Alexander took my practice wooden sword and snapped it over his knee, I called him an uncouth barbarian."
Kara choked on her own spit, coughing into the sofa cushion.
"An uncouth barbarian?" Kara wheezed, her shoulders shaking with uncontrollable laughter.
"Stop, please, you’re killing me.
You’re actually going to break my ribs..."
"It was very harsh at the time!" Aki protested, her face burning as she stamped her foot against the Persian rug.

"The maid made me copy thirty pages of the ancestral statutes as penance and... and during the winter feast, when Julian.Jr poured cold wine on my skirt and said it was an accident, I told him he was a witless popinjay!"
"A witless popinjay?!" Kara howled, wiping a tear of mirth from behind her glasses.
"Oh, man.
The venom!
The savagery!
How did Julian survive such psychological trauma?"
"Stop laughing at me!" Aki whined, her cheeks puffing out into an adorable frustrated pout.
"I didn’t grow up in the lower sectors so that is the extent of my vocabulary!"
Kara pushed herself up onto her elbow, shaking her head with a wide, fond grin.
"Alright, alright, come here," Kara said, beckoning with her right forefinger.
"Sit down before you hurt yourself."
Aki hesitated, but the warm relaxed atmosphere of the room was impossible to resist.
She walked over to the velvet sofa, smoothing her skirts before perching delicately on the edge of the cushions beside Kara’s hip with her hands clasped neatly in her lap.
Kara leaned closer, dropping her voice to a conspiratorial murmur.
"Repeat after me," Kara instructed, her violet eyes gleaming with pure mischief.
"Your father is an arrogant, self-important, crusty old bastard who wouldn’t know real leadership if it bit him on his royal ass..."
Aki gasped with her jaw dropping open.
"I can’t say that!"
"Yes, you can.
Come on.
Say it.
It’s therapeutic."
I shouldn’t!
It’s treason!"
"The listening bugs are fried, Aki.
Say it.
Arrogant... crusty... old bastard."
Aki looked at Kara’s wide encouraging grin as she looked down at her own hands, taking a slow trembling breath.
"He’s an... an arrogant..." she squeaked, her voice trembling like a frightened mouse.
"A cr-crusty... old... b-bastard..."
The syllables felt bizarre and utterly terrifying on her tongue, but the moment they left her lips, a strange electric thrill shot straight through her chest.
Kara beamed, ruffling Aki’s messy blue hair with her knuckles.
"Look at that!
Natural talent.
Memorize that one and use it whenever you look at his portrait in the gallery."
Aki swatted Kara’s hand away with a soft pout, but the tension that had gripped her jaw for years was completely gone.
She looked at Kara, taking in the elegant cheekbones, the flawless pale skin, and the rich dark bangs falling across the wire-rimmed glasses.
"Your... your female form," Aki murmured softly, her fingers tracing the hem of her sleeve.
"It looks... really amazing.
It suits you."
Kara chuckled, leaning her head back against the sofa.
"Thanks.
Honestly, it’s pretty convenient.
The disguise ring does most of the heavy lifting.
It alters the skeletal perception, shifts the voice, masks the core signature completely...
Which is a massive relief, because if people figured out what was actually under the hood, the entire summit would have turned into a circus."
Aki tilted her head, curious.
"What do you mean?"
"Well," Kara said, tapping her chin with a lazy smirk, "in my male body?
Right now?
I’m completely naked."
Aki froze as her eyes dilated to the size of dinner plates.
"What?" Aki whispered, the word barely carrying through the air.
"Yeah," Kara said, nodding with nonchalance.

"I was in such a rush to come here early this morning that I literally just hopped out of the bath, slipped the ring onto my finger, and let the illusion weave the suit over my bare skin so underneath the disguise, I don’t have a stitch of clothes on."
Aki’s brain short-circuited.
’N-Naked...?!’
The thought hit her with the concussive force of a blast to the face.
Instantly, an unbidden detailed image flashed behind Aki’s eyes.

Silas... his tall broad-shouldered frame, the lean muscle cut across his chest, the water droplets glistening along his collarbones and steam rising from his skin as he stepped out of a porcelain tub with nothing on standing right there in the room, separated from her by only a thin translucent film of disguise magic.

’Wait... wait... wait...’ Aki’s thoughts screamed in hysterical panic, her hands flying to her burning cheeks. ’If he’s naked underneath... and I just tackled him... and I was sitting directly on his stomach... that means... that means I was basically...?!’
Her breath hitched.
Her heart was hammering so fast, so hard against her ribs that she genuinely thought she was going to faint right there on the velvet upholstery.
Her imagination ran wild, visualizing the line of his hips, the broad expanse of his back, the scars running down his—
"Pfft... hahahaha!"
A loud wheezing laugh shattered the fantasy as Aki snapped out of it, blinking frantically.
Kara was clutching her side with her single hand, laughing so hard tears were prickling in the corners of her eyes.
"Oh, man, you should see your face!" Kara cackled, pointing at Aki’s beet-red visage.
"I was totally lying!
I’m wearing full under-armor underneath the suit!
I would never walk into an imperial fortress without layered gear!
You actually believed me?!"
Aki’s mouth dropped open.
The realization hit her, followed immediately by an overwhelming wave of mortification.
"You... you jerk!" Aki yelled, her voice pitching up a bit as she grabbed a plush velvet throw pillow and slammed it against Kara’s shoulder.
"You’re terrible!
You’re an awful person!
That wasn’t funny at all!"
POOF!
Kara caught the pillow easily with her single hand, still chuckling softly under her breath.
"Alright, alright, I’m sorry," Kara grinned, tossing the pillow aside.

chapters.title: Chapter 547: Gift From Thora [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She looked at Aki, watching the First Princess cycle through five different expressions of outrage, embarrassment, relief, and frustration in the span of ten seconds.
There was something genuinely addictive about it.
In a world full of cold sociopaths like Vanderbilt and the King, Aki was honest and completely incapable of hiding what was happening in her heart.
’...Cute.’
Was she trying to steal his heart? Because it was working... a lot actually.
Aki pulled her knees up to her chest on the sofa, wrapping her arms around her shins and resting her chin on her knees.
The blush slowly receded from her cheeks, leaving behind a quiet pensive stillness.
"Silas..." Aki said quietly with the name slipping out softly.
Kara’s smile softened. "Yeah?"
"Why did you help me?"
Aki didn’t look up. Her eyes were fixed on the intricate patterns of the Persian rug below.

"My father... he’s the strongest man on this planet," she continued, her voice trembling slightly. "He holds Destruction. He commands the nine regional garrisons, the planet’s defense grids, the entire world military. Angering him... publicly humiliating him in front of the World Council... it puts Blessed Land in terrifying danger. You could have just taken the trade treaty and you could have walked away with billions in credits and full recognition."
She turned her head, resting her cheek against her knee, looking at Kara with wide searching blue eyes.
"Why throw all of that away for me?"
Kara leaned back against the armrest, looking up at the high lancet windows where the midday sun was casting long pale beams through the glass.

"Honestly?" Kara murmured, remembering something from her past life. "I just really hate shitty parents. That’s it... When an adult treats a kid like an expendable asset because they didn’t inherit the right genetic lottery, it pisses me off. I grew up with nothing, Aki so seeing people who have everything still act like selfish cold-blooded monsters just grates on my nerves."
Aki’s gaze dropped slightly.
’Oh,’ she thought, a quiet cold hollow opening up in the pit of her stomach. ’So that was it. Just... moral outrage. Just a good person feeling sorry for a stray dog.’
It was a noble reason, of course.
Anyone would be grateful for it.
But deep down, beneath the fear and the relief, a tiny childish part of her had hoped stupidly that there was something more.
That she, as an individual, meant something to the man behind the violet eyes.
Kara glanced down, catching the subtle downward curve of Aki’s lips as a small knowing smirk touched Kara’s face.
"Besides," Kara added, her voice dropping into a low, teasing cadence, "you’re an official member of Blessed Land now, aren’t you?"
Aki blinked, looking back up. "I... I am?"

"Of course you are," Kara said, leaning forward, resting her single elbow on her knee. "Remember that night in the Sovereign Realm? When I gave you that name? You looked me dead in the eye and told me that if I named you, I had to take responsibility for it..."
Aki’s breath caught.

"Well," Kara shrugged, her violet eyes crinkling with warmth, "I’m a man of my word. Even if I’m currently wearing a skirt and high heels. I took responsibility. So right now, in my book? You’re my responsibility and nobody gets to mess with what’s mine."
Aki’s entire body went rigid.
A brilliant wave of heat surged from the base of her neck straight to her forehead.
’Responsibility...? What’s... what’s mine...?!’
The words bounced around inside Aki’s skull like ricocheting bullets with her hands gripped her shins so tightly her knuckles cracked.
"D-Does that mean..." Aki stammered, her voice barely a squeak and her eyes darting frantically away from Kara’s face, "does that mean we’re... like... uhm... friends?"
Kara let out a soft snort, shaking her head.
"Friends?" Kara echoed, tilting her head with a teasing glint in her eyes. "Nah. It’s definitely much deeper than just friends, Aki."
BOOM.
Aki’s internal reality shattered into a million sparkling pieces.
’DEEPER THAN FRIENDS?!’
Her mind spiraled into pandemonium.
’Deeper than friends is... is a relationship! That’s romance! That’s courting! That’s... that’s betrothal!’
Her hands flew to her face with her cheeks burning so hot she felt like she could fry an egg on her cheekbones.

’Does that mean we’re dating?! Are we in a relationship right now?! In this room?! But... but I haven’t even had my first kiss! I don’t know how to be a girlfriend! What do girlfriends do?! Do they make lunches?! Do they hold hands in public?! What about the imperial protocols?! What about his female disguise?! Can two women be betrothed under Europa law?!’
She was hopelessly overwhelmed by the weight of what she assumed was a formal romantic commitment.
But beneath the terror, beneath the embarrassment, a fierce stubborn warmth bloomed in her chest.

’I’m not ready,’ Aki thought frantically, puffing out her cheeks and squeezing her eyes shut. ’I’m not ready for all the responsibilities that come with being Silas’s partner! But... but I’m going to try! I will become the most reliable girlfriend in the world!’
Kara, entirely unaware of the catastrophic five-layer romantic drama unfolding inside the First Princess’s head, stood up from the sofa.
"Anyway," Kara said, stepping close.
She reached out with her right hand, her long slender fingers gently brushing against the collar of Aki’s navy gown.
... It was warm again.

Aki jumped slightly with her breath hitching as Kara’s fingertips traced the cold metal of the Star-Iron necklace resting against her collarbone... the very necklace Silas had forged for her, its surface embedded with glowing mana diamonds.
"Thanks for keeping this on," Kara murmured softly, her violet eyes meeting Aki’s with genuine gratitude. "I know it’s heavy."
The proximity was suffocating.
Kara was standing inches away, her scent washing over Aki’s senses with her fingers lingering against the metal at her throat.
Aki felt her knees turn to water, her blush deepening until she thought her skin might actually catch fire.
"I... I never take it off," Aki whispered, her voice barely audible.
Kara smiled, stepping back and letting her hand drop.
"Good. Because we’ve got work to do."
Kara’s posture shifted.
The teasing warmth vanished, replaced instantly by the focused edge of a Lord preparing for war.
"So," Kara said, crossing her single arm over her chest, "we’re going to be fighting the representatives of the other nations in this Exhibition."
Aki swallowed hard, forcing her runaway thoughts to grind to a halt. She straightened her back, nodding seriously as the reality of the situation came rushing back.

"Yes," Aki said. "The King framed it as an exhibition to resolve the contested drilling rights for the Northern Corridor and the Nine Major Powers have been squabbling over the border for years... Whoever wins the tournament secures the exclusive extraction permits."
Kara stroked her chin with her right thumb with her eyes narrowing in calculation.

"So..." Kara mused, a slow, predatory grin curling across her lips, "if we win the tournament... we get the northern mining rights and by imperial decree, the territory itself has to be ceded to the winning faction’s banner. Which means... we get the land too."
Aki blinked, flustered by the sheer scale of the ambition. "All... all of that land? The entire northern land?"

"Of course," Kara said naturally, waving her hand. "Why the hell would we fight in a death tournament just to hand the dirt back to the Council? It’s only natural that we take the land rights. You’re going to own an entire sector under your own name, Aki... A real, recognized territory in the real world so we need a bit of a backer too."
She let out a dry dismissive scoff, looking toward the closed oak door.
"It’ll be ten times better than whatever that bum Alexander has... He’s thirty years old and still thrives on his daddy’s praise just to survive the week. We’re going to build something real."
Aki’s chest swelled with pride at the words, but then... just as quickly, a cold sickening dread clamped around her throat as she looked down at her small soft hands.
"Silas..." Aki whispered, her voice dropping, heavy with shame. "How... how can I be of use to you?"
Kara stopped, looking down at her.

"The Exhibition requires two combatants," Aki said, her eyes welling up again as she gripped the fabric of her skirt. "The rules state both representatives must fight in the arena and the other factions... they’re sending their prodigies. Seraphina Bloom has slaughtered monsters of high ranks with her daggers and Valerius Sterling commands the wind but even if I wear high-tier enchanted armaments, I don’t have mana to activate the runes. In an active Sovereign Realm zone... I’m just a liability! I’ll just get in your way!"
Kara didn’t look worried.
Her grin merely widened, splitting her face into a confident razor-sharp smile.
"Chill out, Princess," Kara said, stepping toward the center of the room. "You really think I’d drag you into a meat grinder without bringing the right tools?"
Aki looked up, confused. "What tools...?"

"Thora’s been working on something for you all week," Kara explained, rolling her right sleeve back slightly. "She stayed up in the workshop until three this morning just to finish the final stabilization rune before I left for the summit."
Kara extended her right hand with her palm reaching upward.
VUUUUUUUM!
A soft brilliant pulse of deep blue light erupted from her palm.
The air temperature in the room dropped by three degrees as a pair of slender exquisite combat gloves materialized in the glow.
They were stunning.
Crafted from supple, midnight-blue beast leather that shimmered with an inner liquid luminescence, the gloves were reinforced along the knuckles with thin overlapping scales of polished void-steel.
Runic circuits, so delicate they looked like silver thread, were woven across the back of the hands, converging into a single circular socket directly over the palm.
"What are they...?" Aki whispered, her breath catching as she stared at the glowing blue fabric.
"Try the right one on first," Kara instructed, tossing it lightly toward her.
Aki caught the glove clumsily against her chest but she didn’t hesitate and she didn’t ask about safety warnings either.
’I trust in Silas...’
Without a second thought, she slipped her slender right hand into the cool, silk-like interior of the midnight-blue leather.
SNAP!
The moment her fingers cleared the seams, the glove contracted as it snapped tight against her skin, fitting her hand like a second layer of living flesh.
And then...
SHK-SHK-SHK-SHK!
A sharp electric shock ripped straight from her knuckles, shot through her wrist, and traveled up the nerves of her arm, detonating straight into her spinal column.
"Ah!" Aki gasped, her knees buckling as her back arched and her spine sparking with tiny microscopic needles of internal friction.
Before she could fall, Kara’s single hand caught her wrist.
"Steady," Kara said calmly. "It’s going to cause a bit of trembling... The glove doesn’t draw from your dormant core but it creates an external bypass along your nervous system."
Kara’s eyes flared with sudden intense focus.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A controlled current of raw mana flowed from Kara’s fingertips, surging directly through the Star-Iron weave of the glove and impacting Aki’s physical channels.
"Gah—!"
Aki let out a dry cough as the foreign energy slammed into her lungs with the power making her teeth rattle in her skull and then, the glove reacted.
The deep cool blue of the leather did not stay blue.
FZZZZZZT!
The silver runic circuits across the knuckles flared with crimson light.
The midnight-blue fabric flushed a deep volcanic red, the air around Aki’s fist warping with intense shimmering heat waves that made the edges of the sofa blur.
"What is this...?" Aki stammered, staring at her own glowing, crimson-lit hand in pure wide-eyed disbelief. "It feels... it feels so hot..."
Kara stepped back, crossing her single arm over her chest with her grin wider than ever.

"It’s a converter," Kara said proudly. "It takes external mana, stabilizes the volatile frequencies through Thora’s invention, and lets an unawakened host trigger high-tier spells through physical nerve-pulses so test it out."
Aki blinked, looking from her glowing red glove to Kara’s face. "Test it? How?!"
"Just test it," Kara encouraged, gesturing with her chin. "Aim it at the wall... Twitch your fingers and do whatever comes naturally."
Aki swallowed hard.
Her heart was hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
She looked at her fist.
For so many years, that hand had been useless... It had held embroidery needles, diplomatic tea cups, and books of dead history but it had never once felt the hum of power.
She raised her arm.
Her hand trembled slightly, but she gritted her teeth, locking her slippers firmly into the Persian rug.
She pointed her extended fingers straight toward the reinforced stone wall on the far side of the room.
"I... I don’t know what to do..." Aki whispered.
"Don’t think," Kara’s voice came from behind her,. "Just squeeze."
Aki’s knuckles twitched as her fingers curled into a fist—
CLICK!
The socket in the palm aligned.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!

"Steady," Kara said calmly.
"It’s going to cause a bit of trembling...
The glove doesn’t draw from your dormant core but it creates an external bypass along your nervous system."
Kara’s eyes flared with sudden intense focus.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A controlled current of raw mana flowed from Kara’s fingertips, surging directly through the Star-Iron weave of the glove and impacting Aki’s physical channels.
"Gah—!"
Aki let out a dry cough as the foreign energy slammed into her lungs with the power making her teeth rattle in her skull and then, the glove reacted.
The deep cool blue of the leather did not stay blue.
FZZZZZZT!
The silver runic circuits across the knuckles flared with crimson light.
The midnight-blue fabric flushed a deep volcanic red, the air around Aki’s fist warping with intense shimmering heat waves that made the edges of the sofa blur.
"What is this...?" Aki stammered, staring at her own glowing, crimson-lit hand in pure wide-eyed disbelief.
"It feels... it feels so hot..."
Kara stepped back, crossing her single arm over her chest with her grin wider than ever.
"It’s a converter," Kara said proudly.
"It takes external mana, stabilizes the volatile frequencies through Thora’s invention, and lets an unawakened host trigger high-tier spells through physical nerve-pulses so test it out."
Aki blinked, looking from her glowing red glove to Kara’s face.
"Test it?
How?!"
"Just test it," Kara encouraged, gesturing with her chin.
"Aim it at the wall...
Twitch your fingers and do whatever comes naturally."
Aki swallowed hard.
Her heart was hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
She looked at her fist.
For so many years, that hand had been useless...
It had held embroidery needles, diplomatic tea cups, and books of dead history but it had never once felt the hum of power.
She raised her arm.
Her hand trembled slightly, but she gritted her teeth, locking her slippers firmly into the Persian rug.
She pointed her extended fingers straight toward the reinforced stone wall on the far side of the room.
I don’t know what to do..." Aki whispered.
"Don’t think," Kara’s voice came from behind her,.
"Just squeeze."
Aki’s knuckles twitched as her fingers curled into a fist—
CLICK!
The socket in the palm aligned.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Thanks a lot and more Chapters coming once I wake up, let’s get this arc started.

chapters.title: Chapter 548: Gift From Thora [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: FZZZZZZT... CRASH!
The volcanic plume of searing superheated crimson mana detonated outward from the palm socket of the blue glove in an expanding deafening cone of combustion.

The air inside the private chamber violently vaporized into an eye-watering shockwave of dry heat and pressurized ozone, slamming the heavy brocade drapes against the ceiling and rattling the lead-glass windowpanes until they vibrated with high-pitched screams.
BOOOOOOOM!
The fire crashed head-on into the reinforced stone wall on the far side of the room.
Yet, contrary to the terrifying roar that had preceded it, the masonry of the Citadel did not collapse.
The wall shuddered, groaning beneath the impact as a three-yard-wide circle of bubbling black vitrification seared into the plaster.

Sheets of persistent clinging red fire writhed across the charred mortar like hungry liquid parasites, spitting fat droplets of incandescent slag onto the edge of the Persian rug where the wool instantly smoked and blackened to ash.
Aki flinched violently, staggering backward on her velvet slippers with her hands flying up to shield her face from the boiling wash of air.

Her blue hair whipped across her cheeks with her knuckles pale and her chest heaving as she pressed her spine flat against the side of the sofa, staring at the still-burning stone in paralyzed wide-eyed horror.
Kara on the other hand didn’t flinch.
She stood with her single right hand buried casually in her trouser pocket, leaning back on her heels, letting out a long low whistle that carried cleanly over the hiss of dying embers.

"Damn," Kara murmured, tilting her head to inspect the black smoking crater. "Didn’t even crack the exterior mortar... Say what you want about the old man’s taste in interior decorating, but the stone in this fortress is basically unbreakable. You could park an artillery battery in here and the neighbors down the hall wouldn’t hear a damn thing."
She turned her chin with her violet eyes glinting behind her clear wire-rimmed lenses and looking down at the First Princess.
Aki had frozen completely.

Her right arm remained stiffly outstretched with the midnight-blue leather glove now cooling down releasing thin tendrils of gray smoke that curled lazily from the runic silver circuits etched across the knuckles.
Her jaw hung slightly loose with her blue eyes darting frantically between the scorched wall and the palm of her hand and she stared at her own fingers as if they had suddenly grown claws.
"I-I..." Aki stammered, her voice catching high in her throat.
She blinked rapidly, her breath coming in shallow disbelieving gasps.
"I... I just... I used..."
"Magic," Kara finished for her, a smug satisfied grin stretching across her face. "You cast a flame lance and a pretty damn dense one, too."
THUD! THUD! THUD!
The violent hammering of iron gauntlets against the exterior oak door shattered the quiet.

"Your Highness! Lord Vespera!" the guard sergeant’s muffled, terrified voice shouted from the corridor, followed by the clatter of halberds and drawn sidearms. "We registered a catastrophic spike within your antechamber! Are you under assault?! Open the hatch immediately! We are authorized to breach—"
Kara rolled her eyes, turned toward the sealed oak door, and shouted at the top of her lungs.
"Go away! We’re doing breathing exercises! If one of you touches that brass handle, I’m turning this entire hallway into an ashtray!"
The hallway instantly went dead silent.

A frantic scuffle of boots retreating at top speed echoed through the floorboards, followed by the sound of two guards whispering in panicked hushed tones as they established a cordon thirty paces away from the door, terrified of provoking the one-armed Gold Core.
Kara snorted, shaking her head.
"Idiots."
She walked over to Aki, stopping right in front of the princess.
Reaching down with her single right hand, she tapped the back of the midnight-blue glove with her fingernail.
CLINK!
The metal scale socket in the center of the palm flickered once with a crimson ember fading out of the rune as it cooled down to temperature.

"You can use magic now," Kara said, her voice dropping into a matter-of-fact tone. "Though, before you start thinking you’re about to solo the nine royal houses, let’s manage your expectations... It’s strictly temporary, and the capacity is pretty damn small. Each glove can only store and convert one elemental type at a time. For that right one, it’s dialed into Fire and with the internal compression rune Thora slapped into it, you’ve got maybe five, six of those burst shots before the mana cells burn out and need a recharge..."
Aki blinked, staring at her glove as if it were an alien organism grafted onto her wrist.
She flexed her slender fingers inside the supple beast leather, feeling the soft inner lining shift against her skin.

"That tingly feeling you got earlier?" Kara continued, crossing her single arm over her chest and nodding toward Aki’s shoulder. "That’s because the array doesn’t just hold mana like a battery... The moment it detects a neural command from your brain, it sends a pressurized micro-current backward through your wrist, artificially carving out temporary mana pathways through your muscle tissue. It tricks your physical nervous system into acting like an Awakened conduit."
Aki’s eyes widened, her mouth parting in pure fascination. "It... it creates mana pathways in my body...?"

"Temporary ones," Kara clarified, reaching up to adjust the bridge of her glasses with a finger. "Emphasis on temporary... The second you strip those gloves off, the simulated pathways collapse and your channels go completely dormant again. Every time you lace them up, it has to burn those temporary bridges all over from scratch."
Kara paused with her violet eyes lingering on Aki’s flushed earnest face.
Beneath her casual exterior, a familiar quiet ache settled into Silas’s chest.

’I really wish I could help her awaken properly,’ Silas thought, looking at the delicate woman who had spent twenty-five years being treated like dirt by her own bloodline. ’It would be unbelievable to see the look on the King’s face if she actually unlocked a real core... To watch her stand in front of that arrogant prick Alexander, ignite her own pathways, and prove every single one of those court parasites dead wrong.’
Yet the reality of this world was brutal.
In modern human history, a failed awakening was an immutable medical sentence.
If your soul didn’t ignite during the Awakening ceremony at 18 or rather 16 for nobles, you were inert forever.

Even Thor... the first daughter of Asgard, a bona fide deity who had spent the last week lounging on the chairs of Blessed Land didn’t know of a clean reproducible way for a regular human who had failed their trial to ignite a core after the fact.
’Well...’ Kara corrected herself, her mouth twitching as a vivid memory from yesterday afternoon flashed behind her eyes. ’Thor did technically mention one method...’

Silas had cornered the goddess in the courtyard of Blessed Land while she was chewing her way through an entire roasted wild boar, asking her directly if Asgardian divinity had any rites for dormant mortals.
Thor had paused, wiped grease from her jaw with the back of her wrist, burped loudly enough to shake the leaves off the cherry trees, and casually said.

"Oh, that’s easy, Silas~ Just take a direct bolt of pure divine lightning from the highest terrace of Asgard, slam it straight into their spinal column, and hope their soul doesn’t explode into pink mist before the pathways fuse. Works about twenty percent of the time...!"
’Yeah... no,’ Kara thought grimly, shivering slightly at the memory. ’We are definitely not trying that. I’m trying to keep Aki alive, not vaporize her into a smear on the carpet.’
Kara cleared her throat, pushing the dark thought aside, and pointed at the glove again.

"Thora wasn’t the only one who worked on this, by the way," Kara explained. "Her sister helped tune the frequencies, and that dwarven smith Thor dragged down from Asgard spent three days hammering the void-steel scales on the knuckles to make sure the recoil wouldn’t shatter your wrist when the spell fired..."
Aki blinked, overwhelmed by the names of craftsmen being tossed around as if they were neighborhood tailors.
"O-Okay..."

"And here’s the best part," Kara added, stepping in and tapping the collar of Aki’s gown. "The gloves don’t just rely on their internal cells... The temporary neural pathways they carve through your arms connect directly to the Star-Iron necklace around your neck. The mana diamonds I set into that pendant act as a reservoir so as long as the necklace has juice, you can siphon power into the gloves without needing a native core in your chest. You’re set..."
Aki looked up, her blue eyes shining with overwhelming emotion.

"Silas... I... I don’t even know what to say," she whispered with her hands coming up to clutch the midnight-blue leather against her heart. "Thank you. Truly, thank you so much! I never thought I’d ever feel magic with my own hands. I never thought I’d be able to—"

"Alright, alright, stop, please," Kara groaned, reaching up with her single hand to vigorously rub the side of her face, wincing as Aki’s breathless rapid-fire gratitude began to make her ears ring. "My ears are going to bleed if you keep thanking me like that. If you actually want to look grateful, you can do it on the battlefield. You just have to win this damn tournament today..."
She lowered her hand, her expression turning serious as her violet eyes narrowed with clarity.

"I’m going to be in the ring with you," Kara said firmly. "I’ll handle the heavy hitters but you heard what the King said out there... The moment we step into the Sovereign Realm, my presence is going to be monitored, and I’m going to be suppressed most probably. I can draw their fire, but I can’t be in two places at once... You’re going to have to rely on yourself, Aki."
Kara reached out, taking Aki’s gloved right hand in hers.

"What about the times I’m not right beside you?" Kara asked, her voice dropping into a deep, steady cadence that brooked no argument. "You can’t spend your life hiding behind other people’s backs. You have to be able to stand up for yourself. You have to be able to back yourself up when the room turns ugly..."
She squeezed Aki’s fingers, stepping closer until their boots were barely inches apart.

"So what if you don’t have an Awakened core in your chest? Who gives a damn? You spent time in Blessed Land... You watched how we fight, you learned how to move, you absorbed every scrap of training we threw at you and you have the tools now. Go into that ring and prove everybody in this building wrong."
Aki looked directly into Kara’s eyes.
Beneath the wire-rimmed glasses, the dark bangs, and the feminine features of the disguise, the burning passion behind those violet irises was unmistakable.
Silas wasn’t just handing her weapons... he was handing her his unshakable trust.
He truly believed without an ounce of pity or condescension that she could stand in a ring against the greatest prodigies of humanity and hold her ground.

’He believes in me this much,’ Aki thought, her chest tightening with an emotion so fierce it made her head spin. ’Silas has so much trust in me... I can’t disappoint him. I won’t. I’d rather die in that dirt than let him look at me and see a failure...’
Then, she realized how close they were standing.

Kara was leaning forward with her breath warm against Aki’s cheek and her single hand firmly clutching Aki’s fingers with her slightly taller frame casted a dark shadow over the First Princess’s petite silhouette.
FLUSH!
Aki’s face turned the color of a ripe bursting tomato.
"Y-You’re..." Aki squeaked, blinking frantically, her words tumbling out in a hurried embarrassed rush. "You’re... t-too close!"
Kara blinked.
She looked down at their tangled hands, looked at Aki’s glowing red face, and immediately took a step backward, clearing her throat with an awkward chuckle.
"Right. My bad," Kara muttered, letting go of her hand. "Got a little carried away with the coach speech... Anyway."
Kara reached into her inner jacket pocket, pulling out a second, folded bundle of leather, and held it up.
It was the left glove crafted from midnight-black beast leather, studded with identical void-steel scales, but completely inert with its runic channels waiting for a charge.
Kara held it out, tilting her head.
"So, what element do you want for the off-hand? We did Fire for the right. What do you want in the black one?"
Aki blinked, taking a deep breath to steady her hammering heart as she looked at the second glove.
"How many elements can you actually put in it?"
Kara didn’t hesitate.
She raised her single right hand, counting off on her fingers. "Fire, Water, Earth, Lightning, Wind—"
She stopped.

chapters.title: Chapter 549: Valeria Da Silva [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Her right hand was out of fingers.
She looked at her open palm, realized she didn’t have a second hand to keep counting on, stared blankly at her empty left sleeve pinned flat to her ribs, and blinked in mild irritation.
Aki stared at her for a second, and then...
"Pfft—!"
A soft musical giggle escaped Aki’s lips, quickly dissolving into bright clear laughter that filled the quiet room.
Kara let out an exaggerated sigh, crossing her single arm over her chest and looking at Aki with a deadpan unimpressed smirk.
"Yeah, yeah, laugh it up, Princess," Kara scoffed, though the corner of her mouth twitched with genuine amusement. "Very funny... A top-tier one-armed joke, you’re a regular comedian."
"I’m sorry!" Aki laughed, covering her mouth with her gloved hand as her eyes crinkled with unrestrained delight. "It was just... the way you stopped and stared at your thumb! It was adorable!"
"Whatever," Kara muttered, tossing the black glove into the air and catching it cleanly. "Pick an element before I decide to charge it with raw slime and make your fingers glow green."
Aki smoothed down her skirts, composing herself, though a fond smile remained on her lips.
"Wind. Please. If the right hand is for direct destructive power, I want the left hand to have mobility and deflection."
"Smart girl," Kara approved.
She held the black glove in her palm, her violet eyes flaring slightly as a swirling pale-green vortex of concentrated wind-mana gathered at her fingertips.
FSSSSSH.
The miniature cyclone hissed as it was forcibly compressed, sinking directly into the silver runes etched along the seams of the black leather.
The runes flared with a soft jade brilliance for two seconds before settling down into a metallic sheen.
Kara handed it over.
"Put it on."
Aki took the black glove and slid her left hand into the silk lining.
SNAP!
The leather contracted instantly as the same sharp electric spark traveled up her left arm and jolted her spine but this time, she was prepared.
She gritted her teeth, planted her slippers, and absorbed the shock without stumbling, letting the cold, light feeling of wind-mana settle comfortably into her fingers.
She looked at her hands.
"Silas," Aki asked, looking up curiously. "Do I have to use them strictly for elemental spells? Like shooting fireballs or wind blades?"
Kara shook her head.

"Nope. That’s the beauty of Thora’s design... You don’t just have to sling projectiles. You can take the raw mana stored inside your necklace and cycle it straight into your outer skin then you can form a mana shield over your forearms to block blows, or pour it directly into your quadriceps and calves to give yourself three times your normal sprint speed."
Kara stepped forward, reaching up with her single hand to lightly touch the Star-Iron pendant resting against Aki’s throat.
Her fingers paused and her violet eyes narrowed behind her lenses.
’Wait a second,’ Kara thought with her thumb tracing the surface of the three mana diamonds set into the metal.
The reservoir was light.
Nearly twenty percent of the compressed mana Silas had personally poured into the stones days ago was missing...
Kara slowly lowered her hand, looking down at Aki.
Aki’s eyes immediately darted to the right, studiously inspecting a completely unremarkable brass wall sconce with sudden intense fascination.
Her lips were pressed into a tight guilty line with her cheeks faintly pink.
Kara’s eyebrow arched.

"Aki," Kara said slowly, her voice dripping with deadpan suspicion. "Did you... as a completely Unawakened civilian with zero internal channels... try to siphon raw mana out of that necklace and force it into your own physical body?"
Aki kept her gaze locked entirely on the wall sconce and she didn’t move a muscle.

"Only a suicidal idiot would try to convert unrefined external mana into a body without mana channels," Kara continued. "That’s how people rupture their spleen and spend two weeks vomiting black bile in an intensive care ward."
Aki slowly shifted her eyes back toward Kara, looking like a scolded puppy that had been caught chewing on the leg of an antique dining table.

"I... I was careful..." Aki whispered defensively with her voice barely audible. "I only took a tiny microscopic sip... I just wanted to see what it felt like to have energy moving through my arms..."
Kara stared at her.
Deep down, Silas couldn’t even be genuinely angry.
The girl had spent years living in a country where personal worth was entirely dictated by the hum of mana in your chest.
To be handed a necklace holding radiant power and be expected to just let it sit there like a piece of dead jewelry... of course she had tried to touch it.
It was stupid, reckless, and insanely dangerous, but it was completely human.
"You’re an idiot," Kara sighed, shaking her head. "A cute idiot, but an idiot nonetheless."
"I’m not an idiot," Aki mumbled under her breath, pouting. "I survived, didn’t I?"
"Because you have royal blood," Kara muttered.

Kara stepped close, placing her single palm against the pendant, channeling a dense golden-blue stream of refined mana back into the three diamonds until the crystals hummed with deep satisfied sound.
As the energy flowed, Kara pulled back slightly with her thoughts drifting inward.
’All of this is only possible because of her bloodline,’ Silas mused silently, watching the diamonds absorb the charge.
As much as Silas despised the King of the World, the reality of House Castellian was undeniable.
Aki’s royal blood was an extraordinary miraculous catalyst.
When Silas had forged the necklace and woven the prototype mana circuits back in Blessed Land, they had used several drops of Aki’s own blood to key the whole thing.
Her blood had adapted to the foreign mana with effortless fluidity... almost identical to the way Talira’s ancient dragon blood absorbed energy and adapted.

During the grueling physical training Aki had endured over the past months, whenever she had scraped her knees or bled through her bandages, the mana in the air had subtly gravitated toward the wounds, accelerating her recovery.
’Hopefully, we can figure out a way to help her condense a real Lord Core at least...’ Silas thought, staring at her delicate profile.
A Lord Core was different from a standard combat core.
It was anchored to a territory but even then, without a random celestial artifact, the chances of an Unawakened mortal condensing a core from scratch were astronomically low.
Still, Silas refused to drop the project.
’Eluned said she could do it,’ Kara recalled with her brow furrowing slightly.

Eluned had casually mentioned during an evening meal that she once possessed a skill capable of reconstructing a shattered or awakening a dormant spiritual core but the moment the thought crossed Kara’s mind, an irritated bitter scowl twisted her lips.
’Except the System stripped it away,’ Kara thought, clicking her tongue in sharp frustration.
Silas despised that specific restriction.

Every time he summoned a legendary Hero into Blessed Land, the overarching System mechanics forced them to undergo a reset... stripping away their legendary skills, sealing their masteries, and forcing them to start their progression from square one under his territorial banner.
Eluned remembered that she had the skill centuries ago, but the actual pathways to cast the spell were locked behind her personal progression tiers.
’Stupid game mechanics...’ Kara grumbled internally. ’One of these days I’m going to find the entity behind that interface and punch it in the jaw.’
Suddenly, the air shifted and Kara’s eyes snapped toward the heavy oak door.
Across the threshold, approaching with exceptionally heavy footsteps, an unmistakable presence had just cleared the corridor checkpoint.

It was a tempered aura that was not the scuffling of the guards. Kara stepped away from Aki, strolling casually toward the entrance and she turned the brass handle, pulling the heavy oak door open with a single effortless tug.
Standing on the polished obsidian flagstones outside was Valeria Da Silva.
’Is it just me or does she look a bit different...? I can’t place it.’

The High Marshal-President of Amazon stood tall and imposing, her broad muscular shoulders draped in a pristine tailored military trench coat cut from dark olive wool, adorned with gold bullion aiguillettes and high-ranking campaign ribbons across her left breast.
Her dark scarred skin was taut, her sharp amber-brown eyes radiating the cool authority of a woman who had butchered horrors with her bare hands.

Flanking her half a step behind were two female military attendees in matching olive service dress with their posture rigid as iron bars and their hands resting formally on the pommels of their side-arms.
Da Silva stopped.
She looked at Kara with her lips parting as she adopted the formal, diplomatic greeting customary among the sovereign warrior-clans of Amazon.
She tilted her head forward by a measured respectful three inches, raising her right fist across her breastplate in a salute.
"I am High Marshal-President Valeria Da Silva of the Amazonian—"
SLAM!
The heavy oak door was violently shoved shut right in her face.
CLICK!
The brass latch locked into place and outside in the corridor, the silence was deafening.

Da Silva remained frozen in mid-salute with her fist pressed against her coat and her head still slightly tilted forward, staring at the polished brass door knocker resting three inches from her nose.

Behind her, the two military attendees inhaled sharply with their eyes nearly bulging out of their skulls and their fingers instinctively tightening around the hilts of their blades in horrified shock.
How rude! the thought screamed through Da Silva’s mind.
Nobody on the face of the Earth... not the King of the World, not the Grand Tsar of Borealis, not the masked of the World Council had ever slammed a door in Valeria Da Silva’s face.
Yet... before the heavy wood had snapped shut, Da Silva had caught the expression on the one-armed woman’s face.
Kara hadn’t closed the door out of fear.

She had closed it with a wide entertained grin plastered across her sharp features... It was a look of childish glee that said she had deliberately shut the door simply because she knew how utterly absurd and disrespectful it was.
A tiny involuntary shiver ran down Da Silva’s spine.
’She really takes pride in people’s suffering,’ Da Silva thought with a mixture of disbelief and dark admiration warring in her chest.

Unlike most of the political figureheads sitting at the Grand Table.. bureaucrats like Julian Vanderbilt Senior who hid behind balance sheets, artillery contracts, and corporate security details, Da Silva was an authentic martial prodigy.
She was an accomplished Lord in her own right, commanding a vast blood-soaked territory deep within the lower rims of the Sovereign Realm.
She knew violence intimately.
Yet as Da Silva stared at the heavy oak door, an honest cold realization settled in her gut.
’Would I be able to survive on the battlefield of Blessed Land?’
Blessed Land wasn’t a simple territory at all.
’On the stream... they had a Red Dragon.’

Red Dragons were terrifying beings that were extinct... except for that one, Kara had the only dragon of that kind known as of right now and now, she was standing on the other side of this wooden door as humanity’s only active Gold Core.
Da Silva shook her head, letting out a soft dry breath through her nose.
’No,’ she concluded honestly. ’I wouldn’t last five minutes.’
Before her attendees could draw their sabers to demand satisfaction, the brass latch clicked again.
CREEEAK!
The oak door swung open once more.
Kara was standing in the threshold with her single right hand rubbing the back of her neck, offering a lazy half-assed grimace that barely passed for an apology.
"Sorry about that," Kara grumbled. "Force of habit. I saw uniforms and my hands moved on their own but you’re Aki’s friend, right? Come on in."
Da Silva recovered her composure in a fraction of a second.
She lowered her fist, offering a calm nod. "Thank you, Lord Vespera."
She stepped across the threshold, her heavy military boots clicking cleanly on the floorboards.
Her two attendees followed with their heads bowed low and their movements stiff with reverent caution.
They kept their gazes locked strictly onto the Persian rug, terrified of doing anything that might draw the attention of the black-haired woman leaning casually against the doorframe.
Inside the chamber, Aki had already stepped forward.
The moment Aki saw the High Marshal, the lingering tension on her face vanished, replaced by a soft genuine smile of pure relief.
"Valeria!" Aki called out softly, stepping forward with open arms.
Da Silva’s sharp features softened instantly.
The cold persona of the Amazonian warlord melted away as she stepped into the embrace, wrapping her muscular arms gently around Aki’s smaller frame in a warm protective hug.
Kara stood near the closed door, leaning her shoulder against the wall with her violet eyes watching the two women with a mixture of curiosity and mild surprise.
’They’re that close?’ Kara thought, her eyebrows raising slightly.
